  of [authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-028 included, so the request is resolved and
  authorized against a state that knows the repository ([architecture.md](architecture.md)
  R-ARCH-011 step 2, cross-page). A project key or repository key that does not match its pattern (INV-5) answers `404`
  without a query; concurrent lookups of one repository share one query, and concurrent polls share one
  poll. A script that creates a repository and then publishes to it through the Service
  therefore never meets a `404` from a replica that has not heard of it yet. This matters because
  npm does not retry a `404` (its fetch layer retries `408`, `420`, `429` and `5xx` only), so a
  bounded delay would fail the publish instead of slowing it down. The one exception: a key that
  was requested and missed on a replica shortly before it was created may still answer `404` there
  within the bound of the previous bullet, because repeated misses for one key are answered from a
  short-lived negative entry that the creation's change evicts. The negative entries are a
  registered, size-bounded per-replica cache (R-ARCH-018), so a flood of requests for unknown keys
  costs at most one indexed query per distinct key and entry lifetime, as an unknown token does
  (R-AUTH-023), and never more memory than the cache's bound.
- Deletions and changes of existing repositories follow that bound: for up to that bound, another
  replica may still serve a deleted repository. Grant changes follow it too for every client that
  does not send the header of the next bullet; such a client may meet a refusal of an action a new
  policy allows, or an allow of one a removed grant refused, and waits for the bound or retries.
- **Waiting for one's own permission change** ([authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-032,
  Q-AUTHZ-12). Two headers carry the authorization epoch, the epoch of the `authz` change area
  (R-AUTHZ-028), so that a client can see its own grant change on whichever replica answers next,
  without affinity:
  - Response header `Trove-Authz-Epoch: <n>`: sent by the writes that change grants, which are
    policy writes and role bindings (R-API-033), project writes with their members and roles, and
    the move of a repository to another project (R-API-047). `n` is the epoch the write's transaction
    produced.
  - Request header `Trove-Authz-Min-Epoch: <n>`: honoured on every authenticated request on the
    client listener, `/api/v1/`, `/files/` and the package protocols alike. It is read only after
    authentication succeeded, so an invalid or revoked credential gets its `401` first, and a
    request without a credential ignores it, which keeps anonymous callers from probing the epoch.
    The replica then decides the request on a grant index whose epoch is at least `n`, waiting for
    a build if needed, and answers `412` `authz_epoch_unknown` when the database has
    not reached `n`, `503` `authz_stale` with `Retry-After` when the wait runs out, and `400`
    `invalid_header` for a value that is not a decimal integer between 1 and 2^63 − 1 (R-API-009).
  - The header covers added and removed grants alike. It does not cover a new repository reached
    through a pattern grant, which the lookup of the previous bullets handles.
  - A `412` is a hint, not a proof: the client stops sending that epoch, because the database may
    take long to reach it, and re-reads the changed object; its `ETag` tells whether the change is
    stored (R-API-012). Epochs from before a restore lie below every restored one and pass at once
    ([backup-and-restore.md](backup-and-restore.md) R-BAK-022).
  - The OpenAPI document (R-API-002) declares `Trove-Authz-Min-Epoch` as an optional header
    parameter of every authenticated operation, and `Trove-Authz-Epoch` on the responses of the
    writes above. The UI sends the request header after its own permission changes (R-UI-042).

Acceptance criteria:

- In the e2e profile `scatter` with Valkey stopped and `cluster.epoch_poll_interval: 10s` (a test
  setting that makes a stale snapshot visible), 100 runs of `POST /api/v1/projects/web/repositories` creating
  `npm-new-<n>` followed at once by `npm publish --registry "$TROVE_URL/api/npm/web/npm-new-<n>/"`
  through the Service all succeed on the first attempt.
- In the same profile, a `PATCH` of a repository followed at once by a `GET` through another
  replica returns the new `ETag` in 100 of 100 trials.
- With Valkey running, a policy change made through one replica is enforced by every replica
  within 1 s (p99 over 100 trials), as R-ARCH-018's criterion measures.
- In the same profile, with an existing policy that grants `deploy` on `web/npm-*` to the publishing
  token, the publish of the first criterion succeeds although the replica it reaches learns of the
  new repository only through the lookup. 10,000 requests for random unknown keys on one replica
  cause at most 10,000 repository lookups and no change-log poll beyond the scheduled ones.
- In the profile `scatter` with the test settings of [authorization.md](authorization.md)
  R-AUTHZ-032's acceptance criteria (Valkey stopped, a long change-log poll interval), a
  `PUT /api/v1/permission-policies/{name}` that grants a group `deploy` on a local repository
  answers `Trove-Authz-Epoch: n`; 20 uploads of a member to `/files/…` through the Service with
  `Trove-Authz-Min-Epoch: n` all succeed on the first attempt. The value `abc` answers `400`
  `invalid_header`, the current epoch plus 1,000 answers `412` `authz_epoch_unknown`, and the same
  header without a credential gets the answer it would get without the header.

Routes are registered on the HTTP stack of R-ARCH-005 with method-qualified patterns. The browser
login flow under `/auth/` is not part of `/api/v1/`; the exchange endpoint
`/api/v1/auth/oidc/token` is fixed by INV-10.

**One path per function for maintenance work** (Q-API-9). Every singleton maintenance task of
R-OPS-019 in [operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) is started only
through `POST /api/v1/system/tasks/{name}/run` and stopped only through
`POST /api/v1/system/jobs/{id}/cancel`, and its runs are listed by
`GET /api/v1/system/jobs?kind=<task>`. The page that owns a task's semantics defines its
parameters and job result, MAY add a read-only domain view of its runs that references the job,
and owns the read paths of its results (`GET /api/v1/storage/summary` and
`GET /api/v1/storage/damaged-blobs` in [storage.md](storage.md)). No page adds a second start,
stop or refresh path for a task. Per-resource actions (`/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/{repoKey}/reindex`,
`/storage/damaged-blobs/{sha256}/recheck`, from M4b `/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/{repoKey}/vulnerabilities/rescan`) and the runs of retention policies, which have their own
run model with queueing and per-policy runs ([storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-041), are not
singleton tasks and keep their resource paths.

Acceptance criteria:

- The route-parity check of R-API-002 passes.
- A request to every prefix in the table without credentials answers 401 or the documented
  anonymous result, never 500.
- Each function in this table has exactly one path in the OpenAPI document: the document contains
  no `/api/v1/maintenance/…` start or stop path, no `POST /api/v1/storage/summary/refresh` and no
  `/api/v1/system/storage/summary`, and `POST /api/v1/system/tasks/gc/run` starts a run.

### R-API-021 · Current caller and UI preferences
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: trove-only

| Method | Path | Purpose | Permission | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/v1/auth/whoami` | Principal and credential of the caller | authenticated | R-AUTH in [identity-and-authentication.md](identity-and-authentication.md) |
| GET | `/api/v1/auth/login-options` | Providers, auto-redirect, break-glass visibility, `publicContent`; the sign-in screen renders only from it | anonymous | [identity-and-authentication.md](identity-and-authentication.md) |
| GET | `/api/v1/users/me` | Own user record | authenticated user | [identity-and-authentication.md](identity-and-authentication.md) |
| GET | `/api/v1/users/me/sessions`, DELETE `/api/v1/users/me/sessions…` | Own sessions; end one or all | `self`, `x-trove-owner-rights` | R-AUTH-010 in [identity-and-authentication.md](identity-and-authentication.md) |
| GET | `/api/v1/authz/me` | Effective capabilities, scope summary, principal set and the caller's project memberships with their roles (`projects`: `{key, role}`); drives navigation | authenticated | R-AUTHZ-022, R-AUTHZ-026 in [authorization.md](authorization.md) |
| POST | `/api/v1/authz/check` | Up to 100 permission checks for the caller's own credential; drives per-control rendering | authenticated | R-AUTHZ-023 in [authorization.md](authorization.md) |
| GET, PATCH | `/api/v1/users/me/preferences` | UI preferences | `self`; PATCH with `x-trove-owner-rights` | this page |

**Own-account operations and token scopes.** A token's scope is a ceiling on its owner's rights (R-AUTH-024), and
a profile resource is no repository right a scope can name. The operations that change, or expose beyond the
user record, the caller's own account therefore declare `x-trove-owner-rights: required` and the shared
authorization step refuses a token whose scope does not inherit the owner's rights (`scope.inherit` false) with
`403 forbidden`, before the handler runs; a session, the break-glass session and a token with `inherit: true` pass
(Q-API-214). The set is: `setAvatar`, `removeAvatar`, `updatePreferences`, `listOwnSessions`, `endOwnSession`,
`endOwnSessions` and `revokeOwnTokens`. The reads `getCurrentUser`, `getPreferences`, `getWhoami` and `getAuthzMe`
are not in it: they return what the credential itself is allowed to know about its principal, and the UI of a restricted
token needs them. `403` also answers a service account and a CI token (they have no profile). A new unsafe operation
that declares `authenticated: true` must either declare `x-trove-owner-rights` or be named, with the reason, in the
list `ownerRightsExempt` of `TestR_API_021_EveryAuthenticatedWriteDeclaresItsTokenRule`.

Preferences are owned here:

```json
{"locale": "de", "theme": null, "keyboardShortcuts": true, "revision": 2}
```

`keyboardShortcuts` turns the UI's single-key shortcuts on and off; on by default (R-UI-095,
[Q-API-280](#q-api-280--keyboardshortcuts-is-true-by-default-and-the-migration-sets-it-on-every-stored-row)). `locale` is `en`, `de` or `null` (browser decides); `theme` is `light`, `dark` or `null` (system). The project is not a
preference: it is the context of the screens ([Q-UI-129](#q-ui-129--the-project-is-the-context-of-the-content-chosen-from-your-projects)),
and a member `projectFilter` in a patch is refused as an unknown member. PATCH takes a merge patch with
`If-Match`. `user_preferences.revision` is the `ETag` and is registered with
`meta.RegisterRevisionColumn` (R-API-012, [backup-and-restore.md](backup-and-restore.md)
R-BAK-022).

Data model:

```sql
CREATE TABLE user_preferences (
  user_id            uuid PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES app_user (principal_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,  -- Q-API-15
  locale             text CHECK (locale IN ('en', 'de')),
  theme              text CHECK (theme IN ('light', 'dark')),
  keyboard_shortcuts boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true,  -- Q-API-280, migration 00077
  revision           bigint  NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  updated_at         timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
```

Acceptance criteria:

- `curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TROVE_TOKEN" "$TROVE_URL/api/v1/auth/whoami" | jq -r .credential.type`
  names the token type.
- `PATCH /api/v1/users/me/preferences` with `{"locale": "de"}` makes the next visit of `/ui/`
  open the German UI (R-UI-045).
- Service-account and CI tokens get 403 on `/api/v1/users/me/preferences`.

### R-API-022 · Repositories
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: API-052, API-054, API-057, API-058, API-059, API-060, API-061, API-063

Semantics, payloads and status codes: [repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md).

| Method | Path | Purpose | Permission |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/v1/formats` | Format descriptors with classes (generated from `Descriptor().Classes`), clients (`clients`: `{id, displayName}` from `Descriptor().Clients`, empty for generic; Q-API-177), settings schema (`settingsSchema`, a JSON Schema 2020-12 or `null`; R-ARCH-008, R-ARCH-010, Q-ARCH-229) and `mirror` (the format's remote can be a mirror, [repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-050), and `baseUrl`: the configured base URL of the endpoint the request arrived on, or `null` (Q-UI-75) | authenticated; anonymous while `publicContent` is true (R-AUTH-037) |
| GET | `/api/v1/repositories` | Instance-wide list over every project; each item carries `project` and `visibility`; filters `class`, `format`, `q`, `state`, `project`, `visibility` (R-API-057); `view`; the cursor orders by project and key | readable repositories, by a grant, a role or a level; configuration fields only with `repositories:read-config`, or as an Owner of the repository's project |
| GET | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories` | The repositories of one project; the same filters but `project` | as the instance-wide list, within the project |
| POST | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories` | Create in the project; the key is unique within the project | `admin` or `repository-admin` role (`repositories:write-config`), or Owner of the project (R-AUTHZ-026) |
| GET | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/{repoKey}` | Read; full configuration for `repositories:read-config`, an Owner of the project and `manage` | `read` |
| PUT, PATCH | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/{repoKey}` | Replace or merge patch, with `If-Match` | as create, or `manage` |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/{repoKey}?detach=` | Delete configuration and content; 202 with a job | as create; recent authentication |
| POST | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/{repoKey}/move` | Move the repository to the project named in the body (`{"project": "<target>"}`); its address changes ([repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-060, [Q-REPO-217](repositories-and-proxy.md#q-repo-217--a-repository-moves-to-another-project-through-an-operation-of-its-own-and-only-while-nothing-of-its-project-names-it)) | `repositories:write-config`, or Owner of both projects; recent authentication |
| POST | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/{repoKey}/upstream-test` | Probe the saved upstream configuration | as update |
| POST | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/upstream-tests` | Probe an unsaved remote configuration | as create |
| GET | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/{repoKey}/resolution?path=` | Explain how a virtual repository resolves a client path | `read` |
| GET | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/{repoKey}/mirror` | The status of a remote repository's mirror ([repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-056) | as the full configuration read |
| POST | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/{repoKey}/mirror/run` | Request a pass of the mirror now; 202 with the job, 409 while one is queued or running (R-REPO-056) | as update |

`POST /api/v1/repositories` and the item routes `/api/v1/repositories/{key}…` do not exist: a repository is created
in its project and addressed inside it ([Q-REPO-212](repositories-and-proxy.md#q-repo-212--a-repository-is-addressed-inside-its-project-and-no-repository-is-shared)).

Mapping of catalog operations: API-058 (format-filtered configuration) is the regular read, which
contains only fields that apply to the class and format; API-059 (configurations by key) and
API-060 (all configurations) are the list with `view` and the batch read of R-API-023.

Acceptance criteria:

- Creating an npm remote repository with
  `curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TROVE_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @npm-remote.json "$TROVE_URL/api/v1/projects/web/repositories"`
  answers 201; then `npm view lodash version --registry "$TROVE_URL/api/npm/web/npm-remote/"`, sent
  at once through the Service to whichever replica it reaches, prints a version (R-API-052).
- A reader without `repositories:read-config` gets no upstream configuration in the answer.
- Projects `web` and `mobile` each create a repository `npm-remote` (201 twice); a second create of `npm-remote` in
  `web` answers 409 `already_exists`.

### R-API-023 · Repository batch operations and quick setup
Priority: **P1** · Covers: API-053, API-055, API-064

Owned by [repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md):

| Method | Path | Purpose | Permission |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/batch-create` | Create several repositories of the project, all or nothing | as create |
| POST | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/batch-update` | Merge-patch several repositories of the project with per-entry `ifMatch` (required per entry, R-API-012), all or nothing | as update |
| POST | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/batch-get` | Read several configurations of the project | as read, per key |
| POST | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/batch-delete` | Delete several repositories of the project, best effort; 202 with per-key job references | as delete |
| POST | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/quick-setup` | Create local, remote and virtual repositories of the project per format from a prefix (R-UI-023) | as create |

The sub-path verbs follow R-API-004 (Q-API-7); `batch-create`, `batch-update`, `batch-get`,
`batch-delete` and `quick-setup` are therefore reserved repository keys in every project. All of them accept
`Idempotency-Key` (R-API-014).

Acceptance criteria:

- A `batch-create` whose third document is invalid answers 422 with a pointer into that document
  and creates nothing.

### R-API-024 · Repository maintenance actions
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: API-028, API-040, API-041, API-043, API-045, API-050

The requirement is MVP because cache invalidation is:
[operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) R-OPS-021 and
[repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-045 are MVP, and
invalidation is the one way to cut a wrong or forged negative entry in Valkey short without a
Valkey credential (H-49 in [architecture.md](architecture.md)). The other rows keep the priority
of their owners:

| Method | Path | Purpose | Permission | Priority | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/{repoKey}/reindex` | Rebuild the format's index and metadata from stored packages (npm package documents, NuGet indexes; later Maven metadata, PyPI simple index, Helm `index.yaml`); 202 with a job; 409 when the format has no index | `manage` | P1 | R-OPS-022, format pages |
| POST | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/{repoKey}/cache/invalidate` | Mark cached metadata (`scope` `metadata`), cached misses (`negative`) or both (`all`) of a remote or virtual repository under a path prefix as stale, on every replica within `cluster.epoch_poll_interval` plus 1 s, with or without Valkey; binaries stay cached (INV-11); `400` on a local repository | `manage`, or `admin` | MVP | R-OPS-021, [repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-045 |
| GET | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/{repoKey}/cache/entries` | Cached metadata entries for diagnosis | `repositories:read-config` or `manage` | MVP | [repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-032 |
| POST | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/{repoKey}/vulnerabilities/rescan` | Re-evaluate every stored version of the repository against the advisory data; 202 with the `vuln-rescan` job, 409 with the running one | `manage`, or `settings:write` | MVP (M4b) | [vulnerability-scanning.md](vulnerability-scanning.md) R-VULN-011, R-VULN-019 |
| POST | `/api/v1/system/caches/flush` | Installation-wide: flush every registered in-process cache on every `web` and `worker` replica and invalidate the negative entries of every remote repository; deletes no Valkey key; a synchronous action, not a task of R-OPS-019 | `admin` | P1 | R-OPS-047 |

Acceptance criteria:

- After a test removes a computed npm package document, `POST …/web/repositories/npm-local/reindex` restores it and
  `npm view @team-a/ui versions` lists every stored version.
- `POST …/web/repositories/npm-remote/cache/invalidate` followed by `npm view lodash` makes trove fetch the package
  document from the upstream again (visible in the upstream mock's request log). With Valkey
  stopped, the same holds on another replica within `cluster.epoch_poll_interval` plus 1 s.
- The same invalidation with the token of a user who holds `read` and `delete` but not `manage` on
  `npm-remote` answers 403.

### R-API-025 · Items and raw file transfer
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: API-003, API-004, API-005, API-013, API-016, API-022, ART-027, ART-028

Semantics, payloads and status codes: [storage.md](storage.md) (R-STOR-007 and the item
requirements) and the request paths of R-ARCH-011 and R-ARCH-014 in
[architecture.md](architecture.md).

| Method | Path | Purpose | Permission |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/{repoKey}/items?path=` | Metadata of a file or folder (digests, size, media type, creation, download statistics) | `read` on the path |
| GET | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/{repoKey}/children?path=&recursive=&maxDepth=&folders=` | Paginated children | `read` on the path |
| GET | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/{repoKey}/stats?path=` | Download statistics | `read` on the path |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/{repoKey}/items?path=` | Delete a file or folder | `delete` on the path |
| GET, HEAD | `/files/{projectKey}/{repoKey}/{path}` | Download, `Range`, conditional requests, `Repr-Digest` | `read` |
| PUT | `/files/{projectKey}/{repoKey}/{path}` | Raw deploy; `Repr-Digest` verified; trailing `/` with empty body creates a folder | `deploy`; `overwrite` to replace different content |
| DELETE | `/files/{projectKey}/{repoKey}/{path}` | Same as the item DELETE | `delete` |
| GET, HEAD, PUT | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/{repoKey}/content/{path}` | The UI's content transfer (Q-UI-106, Q-API-195): the semantics of the `/files/` row with the same method, for a request that the session cookie authenticates; served by the role `api` | as the `/files/` row |

API conventions that apply on top:

- A remote repository's items answer from the cache only; the metadata routes never trigger an
  upstream fetch.
- **The content routes** (`/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/{repoKey}/content/{path}`, Q-UI-106) exist because the session cookie
  reaches only the role `api` after the cut into roles ([architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-001,
  [endpoints.md](endpoints.md) R-EP-010), while `/files/` and the package protocols are served by `packages`. They run
  the files transfer of `/files/` (path cleaning, the decision of every request, `Range`, conditional requests,
  `Repr-Digest`, the content headers of R-ARCH-007 and the resource policy of Q-ARCH-86, blocking of R-VULN-015, the
  download statistics) through the same item store, with three differences: a request that is not authenticated by the
  session cookie answers the `404` problem of an unknown path, so token clients keep their bulk traffic on `packages`; a
  `PUT` larger than `ui.deploy.max_upload_bytes` (when it is not 0) answers `413` before the body is spooled; and a path
  that is not stored answers `404` without contacting an upstream, also in a remote repository. A `PUT` needs the
  session's CSRF token as every unsafe request of a session does. Every `Item` of a file and every file of a
  `PackageVersion` carries `contentUrl`, the relative URL of its content route, next to `downloadUrl`, the protocol URL
  for clients. The routes offer `GET`, `HEAD` and `PUT` and no `DELETE` (the UI deletes through the items operation);
  a path that ServeMux would redirect (an empty, `.` or `..` segment) is redirected as on every route of `/api/v1/`,
  where `/files/` answers `400 invalid_path` (Q-API-195); `ui.deploy.max_upload_bytes` is a configuration key of the
  `ui` section (default `100MiB`).
- npm and NuGet repositories refuse raw deploys of files and folders (`409` `conflict` before the body
  is read, with a reason naming the format's protocol address, where `npm publish` or `dotnet nuget push`
  sends), because a raw upload would bypass their metadata generation
  ([architecture.md](architecture.md) Q-ARCH-223).
- The items operations decide a path of a package format on the package and the version the format gives
  it, as `/files/` does ([authorization.md](authorization.md) Q-AUTHZ-160); the delete asks the ownership
  question of every package whose files it removes (Q-AUTHZ-161) and applies the repository's patterns and
  disabled flag to every caller but a holder of `content:bypass` (Q-AUTHZ-162).

Acceptance criteria:

- After `npm publish` of `@team-a/ui@1.4.0` to `npm-local`,
  `GET /api/v1/projects/web/repositories/npm-local/items?path=@team-a/ui/-/ui-1.4.0.tgz` returns the SHA-256
  that `shasum -a 256 ui-1.4.0.tgz` prints.
- `curl -s -X PUT -T app.tgz -u "ci:$TROVE_TOKEN" -H "Repr-Digest: sha-256=:$(openssl dgst -sha256 -binary app.tgz | base64):" "$TROVE_URL/files/web/generic-local/app/1.0/app.tgz"`
  answers 201 (generic format, P1); `curl -s -r 0-99 -u "ci:$TROVE_TOKEN" "$TROVE_URL/files/web/generic-local/app/1.0/app.tgz" | wc -c`
  prints `100`.
- Paging the children of a folder with 1,000 files at `limit=100` returns ten pages.

### R-API-026 · Deploy by checksum and item properties
Priority: **P1** · Covers: API-007, API-009, API-010, API-011, API-014

Owned by [storage.md](storage.md):

| Method | Path | Purpose | Permission |
|---|---|---|---|
| PUT | `/files/{projectKey}/{repoKey}/{path}` with `Trove-Deploy-By-Checksum: ?1` and `Repr-Digest`, empty body | Create a file from content already stored; 404 when the content is unknown **or** not readable by the caller (R-STOR-008) | `deploy` on the target and `read` on an item holding the content |
| GET | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/{repoKey}/properties?path=&keys=` | Read properties | `read` |
| PATCH | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/{repoKey}/properties?path=&recursive=` | Merge patch of properties | `annotate` |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/{repoKey}/properties?path=&keys=&recursive=` | Remove properties | `annotate` |

`keys` follows the repeated-parameter rule of R-API-011 (`keys=qa.status&keys=build.number`), like
every other multi-value parameter, so one parser and the generated clients' array form (OpenAPI
`style: form`, `explode: true`) serve every endpoint; a comma-separated list is not accepted.

Acceptance criteria:

- `curl -X PATCH -H 'Content-Type: application/merge-patch+json' -d '{"qa.status": "passed"}' "$TROVE_URL/api/v1/projects/web/repositories/generic-local/properties?path=app/1.0/app.tgz"`
  answers 200, and `GET /api/v1/search/items?property=qa.status%3Dpassed` finds the file.
- A user without read on any item holding the content gets 404 for a deploy by checksum, and the
  same answer for a random digest.

### R-API-027 · Copy, move and trash can
Priority: **P1** · Covers: API-023, API-024, API-111

Owned by [storage.md](storage.md):

| Method | Path | Purpose | Permission |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/v1/content/copy` | Copy a file or folder to another path or repository; dry run | `read` on the source, `deploy` on the target (`overwrite` when replacing) |
| POST | `/api/v1/content/move` | Move a file or folder; dry run | as copy, plus `delete` on the source |
| GET | `/api/v1/trash-can/items` | Trash entries the caller may see | visibility rule of [storage.md](storage.md) |
| POST | `/api/v1/trash-can/restorations` | Restore by IDs, by deletion job or by source path, optionally to another target | as [storage.md](storage.md) |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/trash-can/items` | Purge entries | `delete` or `manage` on the original path |
| POST | `/api/v1/trash-can/purge` | Empty the trash can; 202 | `admin` |

Acceptance criteria:

- A copy of `@team-a/ui/-/ui-1.4.0.tgz` from `npm-local` to `npm-release` makes
  `npm view @team-a/ui@1.4.0 --registry "$TROVE_URL/api/npm/web/npm-release/"` succeed.
- A deleted file appears in `GET /api/v1/trash-can/items?repository=web/generic-local`, and after a
  restoration it downloads again with the same SHA-256.

### R-API-028 · Artifact search
Priority: **P1** · Covers: API-092, API-095, API-096, API-098, API-099, API-100, API-101

No other page specifies the search operations; this page does. `GET /api/v1/search/items` returns
item descriptions as defined in [storage.md](storage.md), with cursor pagination.

| Parameter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `name` | Case-insensitive substring of the file name |
| `pathGlob` | Glob over the path: `*` within a segment, `**` across segments, `?` one character |
| `checksum` | Lowercase hex; the length selects MD5 (32), SHA-1 (40), SHA-256 (64) or SHA-512 (128) |
| `property` | `key=value`, or `key` alone for any value; repeat for AND |
| `repository`, `class`, `format` | Restrict the scope; `repository` takes the qualified name `<projectKey>/<repoKey>`; a virtual repository expands to its members |
| `project` | Restrict the scope to the repositories of one project |
| `createdFrom`, `createdTo`, `modifiedFrom`, `modifiedTo`, `lastDownloadedFrom`, `lastDownloadedTo` | Date ranges (R-API-011) |
| `notDownloadedSince` | Never downloaded, or last downloaded before this time |
| `sort` | `name`, `createdAt`, `modifiedAt` and their descending forms |

At least one of `name`, `pathGlob`, `checksum`, `property` or a date filter is required (400
`filter_required`). Results are filtered by `read`. The indexes the search needs (trigram index on
names, B-tree indexes on digests, property index) are defined in [storage.md](storage.md); the SQL
predicate form of the permission filter comes from [authorization.md](authorization.md).

Acceptance criteria:

- `GET /api/v1/search/items?checksum=<sha256 of app.tgz>` returns every readable copy of the file.
- `GET /api/v1/search/items?pathGlob=app/**/app.tgz&repository=web/generic-local` returns
  `app/1.0/app.tgz`.
- A file in a repository the caller cannot read never appears, and the result count does not
  change when such a file is added.

### R-API-029 · Packages, versions and README
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: ART-048, ART-049, API-094, API-109, API-110

This page owns the cross-repository package view the UI needs; package and version metadata are
stored as [storage.md](storage.md) and the format pages define. (The npm checksum lookup
`/api/v1/npm/{projectKey}/{repoKey}/packages/{name}/versions/{version}` of [formats/npm.md](formats/npm.md) and
the package-ownership endpoints of [authorization.md](authorization.md) are per repository and
remain as their owners define them.)

| Method | Path | Purpose | Permission |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/v1/packages` | Packages; filters `format`, `repository` (both repeatable; the qualified name `<projectKey>/<repoKey>`), `project`, `q` (name and description), `namePrefix`, `keyword`, `createdFrom` / `createdTo` (first visible version); `sort` `name`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt` and their descending forms (default `name`); `include=vulnerabilities` (R-UI-052) | visible versions (below); anonymous where allowed |
| GET | `/api/v1/packages/lookup?format=npm&name=@team-a/ui` | Resolve a name to the package | as list |
| GET | `/api/v1/packages/{packageId}` | Package summary | as list |
| GET | `/api/v1/packages/{packageId}/versions` | Versions; filters `prerelease`, `repository`; `sort` `-publishedAt` (default), `publishedAt`, `-version`, `version` (the format's version precedence); `include=digest` (R-UI-052) | as list |
| GET | `/api/v1/packages/{packageId}/versions/{version}` | Version details | as list |
| GET | `/api/v1/packages/{packageId}/versions/{version}/readme` | Sanitized README HTML; wiki content (`x-trove-part: wiki`, R-API-058) | as list, then the wiki check ([authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-034) |
| GET | `/api/v1/packages/{packageId}/versions/{version}/docs`, `…/docs/entries/{type}/{name}`, `…/docs/files/{file}` | The documentation of a version of a format that has one (Ansible Galaxy: the tree with search, one plugin's page, a Markdown file): `getPackageVersionDocs`, `getPackageVersionDocEntry`, `getPackageVersionDocFile`, [formats/ansible.md](formats/ansible.md) R-ANS-036; wiki content (Q-API-260, Q-API-261); 404 for a format without documentation | as list, then the wiki check of R-AUTHZ-034 ([formats/ansible.md](formats/ansible.md) R-ANS-037) |

- A package is identified by format plus normalized name (npm names as stored; NuGet IDs
  case-insensitive, displayed in their original casing). Version strings are percent-encoded in the
  path.
- A version is visible to a caller who holds `read` on a repository containing it, by a grant, a role or the repository's
  artifacts level ([authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-035), with the package-name narrowing of INV-9 applied. A package is listed when at least one version is
  visible, and `latestVersion` is computed from visible versions only, so a hidden newer version
  leaks neither its number nor its existence. The filter runs in SQL.
- A virtual repository in the `repository` filter expands to its members. Remote repositories
  contribute only cached versions; this endpoint never queries an upstream.
- Version details contain `packageId`, `format`, `name`, `version`, `prerelease`, `publishedAt`, `licenses`
  (declared SPDX identifiers or expression, `[]` when none), `sizeBytes`, `downloadCount`, `hasReadme` (whether
  the `readme` answer is 200 for this caller, so the UI chooses its default tab without a probing request; `false` for a caller
  who may read the version but not the wiki of the repository that holds it, [authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-034),
  `metadata` (a
  format-specific object whose schema the format page owns), `repositories`
  (`[{"project", "key", "class", "publishedAt"}]`) and `files` (`[{"path", "sizeBytes", "sha256", "downloadUrl"}]`).
  The members of npm's `metadata` that the UI reads are `distTags`, `dependencies`, `devDependencies`,
  `peerDependencies`, `optionalDependencies`, `engines` (name to string), `authors`, `homepage`,
  `repositoryUrl`, `bugsUrl` and `deprecated`; a member that does not apply is absent (Q-API-159).
  NuGet's `metadata` has `id` (the casing of this version's `.nuspec`), `listed`, `title`, `summary`, `releaseNotes`,
  `copyright`, `language`, `minClientVersion`, `licenseUrl`, `homepage`, `repositoryUrl`, `authors`, `tags`, `packageTypes`,
  `dependencyGroups` (per target framework) and, when true, `requireLicenseAcceptance` and `developmentDependency`; its
  README is the file the `.nuspec` names, read out of the stored package (Q-NUGET-48).
- `sizeBytes` of a version, in the list and in the details, is the sum of the sizes of the version's files unless the format
  has the optional `ViewSizer` ([ADR-177](../decisions.md#adr-177--the-format-contract-gains-the-optional-viewsizer-for-the-size-of-a-version-that-is-not-the-sum-of-its-files)),
  which reports the size of its versions: an OCI tag's file is the manifest document, so its `sizeBytes` is the image's (R-OCI-031,
  Q-OCI-130). The UI shows the value as received.
- The `versions` list entries hold `version`, `prerelease`, `publishedAt`, `sizeBytes`, `repositories`
  (the qualified names `<projectKey>/<repoKey>` of the repositories the caller may read) and `downloadCount`; with `include=digest` also
  `digest`, the content digest the format's version metadata names (an OCI tag: `sha256:…` of its manifest, R-UI-052), absent for a format without one.
  With `include=vulnerabilities`, `GET /api/v1/packages` adds `vulnerabilityGrade` to each entry for a signed-in caller of an installation
  that scans: the grade of the entry's `latestVersion` over the repositories the filter names ([vulnerability-scanning.md](vulnerability-scanning.md)
  R-VULN-038, R-VULN-039), in a fixed number of statements per page; a caller who is anonymous or a failure to read the grades leaves the
  member absent and the list is answered anyway. The details and the README answer carry a strong `ETag`
  and honour `If-None-Match`; the README tag covers the README source, the renderer version and the hash of
  the image origin list.
- The visibility filter is decided per repository by the decision point and passed into the statements that
  count (Q-API-165): a caller who may read only some versions of a package sees a `versionCount`,
  `downloadCount`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `repositories` and `latestVersion` computed from those, in the list, in
  the package summary and in the version list. A request that would need the decision point to decide more than
  200 000 versions one by one answers `400` and asks for a narrower filter; it never answers a partial set. On an
  endpoint with exposure rules (R-EP-014) the same rule applies to the exposed packages and versions, and a
  dist-tag in the `metadata` names a version only when the caller may read it. A version of a name that the
  include and exclude patterns of its repository do not admit (R-REPO-005) is not served, and so is not listed
  or counted for any caller. A package, a version or a
  README the caller may not read answers the `404` of one that does not exist, and so does an id that is none.
- The package `id` is `pkg_` and the lower-case base32 of the format, a NUL and the normalized name (Q-API-164):
  opaque to clients, no secret and no capability. `lookup` resolves a name by the format's name rule; a name the
  rule refuses is a `404`. A sort or a filter the document does not list answers `400`; a cursor of another sort
  or filter answers `400 invalid_cursor` (R-API-010). Package names order bytewise, so the order and the keyset of
  a cursor do not depend on the locale of the database. The order and the cursor use the normalized name, the key
  the statement compares, never the display name of a format that keeps the case of a name (Q-API-170). Remote repositories contribute their cached versions only,
  and a version the format withholds (npm: a tombstoned one, R-NPM-047) is not counted anywhere.
- What the generic rows do not hold - description, keywords, licenses, the README and the `metadata` - comes from
  the format's view adapter over its data port (Q-API-166); the order of versions and the pre-release rule are the
  format's (SemVer precedence for npm). `latestVersion` is the highest visible stable version, or the highest visible
  pre-release while no stable version is visible. The `downloadUrl` of a file is the protocol URL of the repository
  that holds it where the format has a protocol, else its `/files/` URL, built on the configured base URL of the
  endpoint and never on the `Host` of the request. Its `contentUrl` is the relative URL of the content route of R-API-025
  for the item that holds the file (Q-UI-106): `PackageFile.path` is the path of the file item in the repository that
  holds it (`PackageFile.contentUrl` is built from the pair, and so is `downloadUrl`).
- The package summary, the version details and the README carry a strong `ETag` (a hash of the representation sent
  for the details and the summary, so two callers who see different versions never share one) and answer `304`
  for `If-None-Match`. The README tag is computed from its source, the renderer version and the hash of the
  origin list before the rendering, so a request that holds it costs no rendering (Q-API-167).
- README answer: `{"contentType": "text/markdown", "html": "<h1>…</h1>", "truncated": false, "externalImagesBlocked": 2}`;
  404 when the version has none, with the answer of a version that is not visible, and the same 404 when the caller may read
  the version but not the wiki of the repository that holds it: the README is wiki content (R-AUTHZ-034). Rendering and sanitizing follow R-UI-008; README extraction (npm
  `readme` field or `README.md` in the tarball, NuGet `<readme>` file in the package) is owned by
  the format pages.
- Formats added in P1 use the same endpoints: Maven coordinates as `name=group:artifact`
  (API-094), container images as packages with tags as versions (API-109, API-110).

```json
{
  "id": "pkg_01JBQ6V7S3K9",
  "format": "npm",
  "name": "@team-a/ui",
  "description": "Shared UI components",
  "latestVersion": "1.4.0",
  "keywords": ["ui", "components"],
  "repositories": ["web/npm-local", "web/npm-all"],
  "createdAt": "2026-09-02T08:00:12.201Z",
  "updatedAt": "2026-10-20T09:12:44.512Z",
  "versionCount": 3,
  "downloadCount": 1832
}
```

`createdAt` is the publication time of the first visible version, `updatedAt` that of the latest visible one;
`versionCount` and `downloadCount` count visible versions only (Q-API-159).

Data model (not built: the README is rendered on demand and its tag is computed from the three inputs below, Q-API-167;
the table is added when a profile asks for it):

```sql
CREATE TABLE package_readme_cache (
  version_id       uuid PRIMARY KEY,           -- references the version table of storage.md
  source_sha256    bytea       NOT NULL,
  renderer_version integer     NOT NULL,       -- bumped when renderer or sanitizer policy changes
  image_policy_sha256 bytea    NOT NULL,       -- hash of ui.readme.external_image_origins (R-UI-008)
  html             text        NOT NULL,
  truncated        boolean     NOT NULL,
  rendered_at      timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
```

Acceptance criteria:

- After `npm publish` of three versions of `@team-a/ui`,
  `GET /api/v1/packages?format=npm&q=team-a` lists the package with `latestVersion` `1.4.0`.
- A user who can read only the repository containing `1.3.0` sees `latestVersion` `1.3.0`.
- `GET …/versions/1.4.0/readme` for a README containing `<script>` returns HTML without it.
- `@team-a/ui` is in a repository whose artifacts are `public` and whose wiki is `internal`: an anonymous `GET
  …/versions/1.4.0` answers `"hasReadme": false` and `GET …/versions/1.4.0/readme` 404; an internal user gets `true` and 200.

### R-API-030 · Client setup snippets
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-023

`GET /api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/{repoKey}/client-setup` returns the snippets of a repository (permission `read`;
publish snippets only with `deploy` on the target). Query: `client` (required; the clients a format offers, for
npm `npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn` for Yarn 2 and later, `yarn-classic`; an unknown value answers `400 malformed_request`
naming the clients the format serves, Q-UI-77),
`credentials` (`placeholder`, the default, `env` or `none`), `package` and `version` (the install snippets name
them), `scope` (an npm scope; adds the scoped registry variant). The answer holds `repository`, `format`,
`client`, `credentials`, `registryUrl`, `endpointPath`, `username`, `publishTarget`, `tokenTtlSeconds` and
`snippets` of `{id, tab, fileName, language, content}`, `tab` being `configure`, `install` or `publish`
(Q-API-160). This page owns the endpoint; the format registry of R-ARCH-010 in
[architecture.md](architecture.md) feeds it, and the format pages contribute the templates. Rules the UI relies
on:

- The server fills the public base URL, the project key and the repository key, the package-manager endpoint URL of
  INV-6 (`/api/<format>/<projectKey>/<repoKey>/`), the scheme-less endpoint path (npm's per-registry credential key) and the caller's name.
  With `package` and `version` the install snippets are specific to that version.
- The server never fills a token. With `credentials=placeholder` snippets contain the placeholder
  `{{token}}`, replaced in the browser (R-UI-016); with `credentials=env` they hold the
  environment-variable reference of the client's syntax (`${TROVE_TOKEN}` for npm and Yarn,
  `%TROVE_TOKEN%` for `nuget.config` and cmd, `$env:TROVE_TOKEN` for PowerShell, Q-API-187); with `credentials=none` they hold no authentication line (an
  anonymous caller, and the install command panel of R-UI-009). The variable name is
  `ui.client_setup.token_env_var`. `tokenTtlSeconds` is `ui.client_setup.token_ttl` in seconds, the lifetime
  the setup dialog asks for when it creates a token.
- Every snippet has a stable `id`; the human-readable explanation lives in the UI, translated per
  `id` (R-UI-045). The `id` is `<client>.<tab>[.<name>]`; the scoped variant of a configure snippet appends
  `-scoped` to its name. A scoped variant exists only for a configure template that reads the scope (the npm clients);
  `scope` for a client without one answers `400 malformed_request` whose detail names `scope` (Q-API-235).
- The credential mode, the package and the quoting are the API's, not the template's (Q-API-168): the template
  spells the token as `${TROVE_TOKEN}` (POSIX shell), `%TROVE_TOKEN%` (a `nuget.config` value or cmd) or
  `$env:TROVE_TOKEN` (PowerShell), whichever the syntax of its file or shell expands, and the package as `<package>`,
  and receives the functions `shell`, `powershell`, `cmd` and `xml` (quoting) and `schemeless` (a URL without its scheme, the
  key of a keyed credential line; Q-ARCH-257) and `hostname` (the host name of a URL without port and path, the key of a
  credential line that binds to a host name alone, such as a `~/.netrc` line; Q-ANS-48). An install template may carry a `VersionSpec`, the
  form in which the version follows the package (default `@<version>`, dotnet ` --version <version>`; Q-API-188). Its
  language fixes the quoting of what the API substitutes: `shell`, `powershell`, `cmd` or `xml` (Q-API-189).
  A `package`, `version` or `scope` above 256 bytes, with a control character or in the shape of a token is
  refused with `400`, and so is a `package` or `version` that starts with `-` (a client reads it as an option,
  quoted or not) and a `package` that the format's name rule does not take; the snippet holds the normalized
  name ([formats/npm.md](formats/npm.md) Q-NPM-50). The operation answers `503` while no base URL is configured for the endpoint, because
  an address built from the `Host` of the request would end in a file the user copies. The publish snippets and
  `publishTarget` need `deploy` on the repository that receives the publish: the repository itself when local, the
  deployment target of a virtual one, none for a remote one. Whether the snippets send the credential before
  being challenged (`RequiresAuth`) follows whether an anonymous caller on the same endpoint may read the
  repository; it is off for `credentials=none`. The npm templates contribute the configure, install and publish snippets
  (R-NPM-041, Q-API-180); the CI snippets of R-UI-017 are not templates yet. The generic templates contribute curl's
  configure, install and publish snippets ([formats/generic.md](formats/generic.md) R-GENERIC-016).
- A virtual repository without a default deployment target has no publish snippets and `publishTarget: null`;
  a caller without `deploy` on the target gets no publish snippets either.
  A publish snippet names the registry URL of the repository the caller chose (Q-API-180); `publishTarget`
  names the repository that receives the publish.
- Values substituted into shell commands (package names, versions, project and repository keys) MUST be
  single-quoted, with embedded single quotes escaped, unless they match
  `^[A-Za-z0-9@/._+:=][A-Za-z0-9@/._+:=-]*$` (a value that starts with `-` is quoted); values
  substituted into PowerShell commands are single-quoted by the same rule, with an embedded single quote doubled, and
  into cmd commands double-quoted with `"` and `%` doubled; values
  substituted into XML snippets MUST be XML-escaped. Legacy npm
  names served through remote repositories may contain `'`, `(`, `)`, `!` and `*`, which a shell
  interprets when a user pastes the command.

Configuration:

```yaml
ui:
  client_setup:
    token_env_var: TROVE_TOKEN   # default; an environment variable name, at most 64 characters
    token_ttl: 720h               # default; expiry of tokens created by the setup dialog, at most auth.tokens.pat.max_ttl
```

Acceptance criteria:

- The answer for `npm-all` of project `web`, client `npm`, `credentials=env` contains
  `//trove.example.com/api/npm/web/npm-all/:_authToken=${TROVE_TOKEN}`.
- No answer of this endpoint, for any format, client and credential mode, matches
  `trv_(pat|sat|cit)_` (R-ARCH-010 kit check 8).
- The npm install snippet for version `1.0.0` of a legacy remote package named `a(b)` reads
  `npm install 'a(b)@1.0.0'`.

### R-API-053 · Guides of the formats
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: trove-only

The owner's requirement of 2026-10-31 (Q-UI-83): the guide of R-UI-049 for every registry variant (format × repository
class × client). The format contributes the text (`Guide()` of the format contract, [architecture.md](architecture.md)
R-ARCH-008, Q-ARCH-235); this page owns the operations (Q-API-175).

| Method | Path | Purpose | Permission |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/{repoKey}/guide?client=` | The guide of a repository for one of its format's clients | `read` on the repository (`404` otherwise, like a missing repository) |
| GET | `/api/v1/formats/{format}/guide?class=&client=` | The guide of a class of a format, without a repository | as `GET /api/v1/formats`: authenticated; anonymous while `publicContent` is true (R-AUTH-037) |

- The answer holds `format`, `class`, `client`, `repository` (`null` for the guide of a format), `registryUrl`,
  `publishTarget`, `credentials`, `exposureRules` and `sections` of `{id, topic, title, html, snippets}`. The sections are
  those of the format's guide that are written for the class and the client, in the topic order `what`, `configure`,
  `authenticate`, `install`, `publish`, `maintain`, `audit`, `lockfiles`, `endpoint`, `troubleshooting`; a section that
  renders to nothing is left out.
- A section's Markdown is a template over the data of the setup templates plus the class, the client, the publish target
  the caller may deploy to, whether the caller is anonymous, whether the endpoint has exposure rules, and the name of
  `ui.client_setup.token_env_var` (`GuideData`); it has no credential field. The server renders it with the renderer and
  the sanitizer of R-UI-008, with a source bound of its own (256 KiB) instead of `ui.readme.max_source_bytes`, which
  bounds untrusted READMEs (Q-API-178).
- A section that names a setup section carries the snippets of R-API-030 for the same repository, client and credential
  mode, rendered by the same code, so the guide's configure and install snippets are the client setup's. The credential
  mode is `env` for a signed-in caller and `none` for an anonymous one; the guide never carries a token or the placeholder
  of one, and the reference `${TROVE_TOKEN}` of a section's text is rewritten like a snippet's (Q-API-176).
- The guide of a format writes `<project>` and `<repository>` where the project key and the repository key go and names
  no target. The guide of a virtual repository
  names its deployment target only to a caller who may deploy there and never lists the members, which are configuration
  (Q-API-179). Both operations answer `503` while no base URL is configured for the endpoint, like R-API-030.
- An unknown format answers `404`; a client or class the format does not have, or a format without clients, `400
  malformed_request`. No answer matches `trv_(pat|sat|cit)_`.

Acceptance criteria:

- For each npm client, the snippets of the `configure` and `install` sections of `GET …/repositories/npm-local/guide`
  equal the snippets of the same tabs of `GET …/repositories/npm-local/client-setup?credentials=env` byte for byte
  (`TestR_API_053_TheGuideShowsTheSnippetsOfTheClientSetup`, and through the stack
  `TestR_API_053_TheGuideThroughTheStack`).
- The guide of a remote repository has no `publish` and no `maintain` section; for an anonymous caller the guide of a
  local repository has neither, and its snippets hold no credential line.
- On an endpoint with exposure rules the guide carries the `endpoint` section and the endpoint's own addresses; on the
  default endpoint it does not (`TestR_API_053_TheGuideOnAnEndpointWithRules`).
- No answer, for any class, client and caller, matches `trv_(pat|sat|cit)_`.

### R-API-054 · The manual
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: trove-only

The owner's requirement of 2026-11-01: the documentation for the people who use trove and the people who run it is
delivered by trove itself, behind the Documentation link of the UI (R-UI-050). The manual is Markdown in
[docs/manual/](../manual/README.md), embedded into the binary (`docs/manual/embed.go`), so an installation always shows the
manual of the version it runs; [internal/manual](../../internal/manual/) loads and renders it once at start-up (Q-UI-89).

| Method | Path | Purpose | Permission |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/v1/manual` | The sections (`user`, `admin`) in reading order with each page's id, title and summary | as `GET /api/v1/formats`: authenticated; anonymous while `publicContent` is true (R-AUTH-037) |
| GET | `/api/v1/manual/{section}/{page}` | One page: `title`, `summary`, `html`, `headings` (levels 2 and 3, with their anchors), `previous` and `next` | as above |

- A page starts with a `# Title` line and a summary paragraph of plain text; the HTML is the page below the title, rendered
  by the renderer and the sanitizer of R-UI-008 with a source bound of 1 MiB. A relative link to another page
  (`access-tokens.md#create-a-token`, `../admin/endpoints.md`) becomes `help/<section>/<page>` with
  `#user-content-<slug>` for a heading, a link inside the page `#user-content-<slug>`; every other relative link is removed
  as in a README.
- The contents are fixed in `internal/manual`; a page that is missing, a file outside the contents, a page without a title
  or summary and a link to a page or a heading that does not exist stop the load, so start-up fails rather than serve a
  broken manual. The test of the package loads the embedded files, so such a manual never passes CI.
- Both answers carry the same strong ETag, a hash over every rendered page and the renderer version; a matching
  `If-None-Match` answers `304`. An unknown section or page answers `404`. The text is English (Q-UI-86 applies).

Acceptance criteria:

- The embedded manual loads; `docs/manual/README.md` lists the same sections and pages in the same order with the same
  titles (`TestR_API_054_EmbeddedManualLoads`, `TestR_API_054_ReadmeListsTheContents`).
- A link to another page with a heading becomes `help/<section>/<page>#user-content-<slug>`; a link to a missing page or
  heading, a link into the repository and a page outside the contents stop the load
  (`TestR_API_054_LinksBecomeHelpRoutes`, `TestR_API_054_DefectsAreRefused`, `TestR_API_054_LinkedRenderingResolvesRelativeLinks`).
- The contents list `user` before `admin`; a page carries its headings and neighbours; both answer `304` for the ETag and
  an unknown page `404`; an anonymous caller gets `200` while `publicContent` is true and `401` otherwise
  (`TestR_API_054_TheManualOperations`, `TestR_API_054_AnonymousReadersFollowPublicContent`).

### R-API-055 · User avatars
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: trove-only

The owner's requirement of 2026-11-07, in two parts. A user who has not uploaded an avatar gets a generated robot avatar in
the UI (R-UI-051); the UI bundles the generator and loads nothing from outside trove's origin. A user can upload an avatar,
and the owner fixed its shape: only PNG, JPEG and WebP and never SVG; the server decodes the image and stores a new one; at
most 1 MiB is accepted; the image is stored as a blob; the `api` role serves it from trove's origin. Everything below that
the owner did not say is the development agent's decision, recorded as Q-API-207 to Q-API-210, Q-AUTH-195 to Q-AUTH-197 and
Q-STOR-166, Q-STOR-167.

| Method | Path | Purpose | Permission |
|---|---|---|---|
| PUT | `/api/v1/users/me/avatar` | Set the caller's avatar; the body is the image, `Content-Type` is `image/png`, `image/jpeg` or `image/webp`; answers the user record | authenticated; a user or the break-glass account |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/users/me/avatar` | Remove the caller's avatar; `204` also when there is none | as above |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/users/{username}/avatar` | Remove another user's avatar (moderation); `204` also when there is none | `identities:write` (`admin`) |
| GET | `/api/v1/avatars/{digest}` | The image, named by the lower-case hexadecimal SHA-256 of its bytes | authenticated |

- **The user record names the image.** `User.avatarUrl` (R-AUTH-016) is `/api/v1/avatars/<sha256>` or `null` for a user
  without an avatar; the UI shows the generated avatar for `null`. It is on `GET /api/v1/users/me`, `GET /api/v1/users/{username}`
  and every item of `GET /api/v1/users`. Nothing else is needed to find another user's avatar: the digest is in the record.
- **The input is untrusted and is never stored or served.** The server decides the format from the bytes, not from the
  declared type (Q-API-208). In this order: the declared media type must be one of the three, else `415`; the body is read
  through a reader that stops at 1 MiB (1,048,576 bytes), a longer body is `413 payload_too_large` and is not held; the first
  512 bytes must sniff as PNG, JPEG or WebP, else `415`, and as the declared one, else `415` (an SVG, an HTML page, a GIF or
  a polyglot never gets this far); an animated PNG or WebP is `422`; the size in the header is read before any pixel is
  allocated and must be at least 32 x 32 and at most 4,194,304 pixels in all, else `422` (a header that declares 100,000 x
  100,000 pixels in a few bytes costs nothing); a JPEG with more than 64 scans, or whose scans add up to more than 3,145,728 block visits (Q-UI-174), is `422` `too_complex`, and one whose estimated
  decode memory (Q-API-211) is above 48 MiB is `422` `invalid_dimensions`; the image is decoded with the Go decoders
  (`image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `golang.org/x/image/webp`, decoder only) under a deadline of 5 s, which on expiry is `422`
  `too_complex`, and one that does not decode, a truncated one included, is `422`.
- **The result is a new image.** The centre square of the decoded pixels is scaled to 256 x 256 (Catmull-Rom) and encoded as a
  PNG from the pixels alone: no metadata (EXIF, GPS position, ICC profile, text chunks), nothing appended, one frame. The
  EXIF orientation of a JPEG is applied first, because the result has no EXIF to apply it later. Transparency is kept. The
  same image always gives the same bytes, so it gives the same digest.
- **Bounded cost.** A replica decodes two images at a time (`avatar.MaxConcurrent`); a request that finds no free slot within
  2 s is `503 server_busy` with `Retry-After: 1`. The memory of one decode is estimated from the header and bounded to 48 MiB,
  so the decoding of a replica holds at most 96 MiB, which the admission guard does not charge (H-563). The decode stops at its
  next read after 5 s or when the client leaves; the reads of its input are 16 bytes at most, so a file of few bytes and many scans is
  stopped too (Q-UI-174). The slowest image the checks accept costs about 0.5 s of CPU for the whole of `Process` (Q-UI-173). The management API's rate limits (R-API-016) apply as to any write.
- **The image answer.** `Content-Type: image/png`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Content-Security-Policy: default-src
  'none'; sandbox`, `Content-Disposition: inline; filename="avatar.png"`, `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin`,
  `ETag: "<sha256>"` and `Cache-Control: private, max-age=31536000, immutable`: the answer is for a signed-in caller and the
  URL never changes its content (Q-API-209). These replace the headers R-API-017 gives a JSON answer. A digest that is no
  user's avatar, a replaced or removed one included, is `404`; the route reads no other blob of the store. The page's CSP
  (`img-src 'self' data:`, R-UI-001) admits the URL, which is on trove's origin.
- **Storage.** The PNG is a blob of the object store, committed by the protocol of R-STOR-005 and deduplicated; the table
  `user_avatars` names it for the user, with `ON DELETE CASCADE` from the user (Q-STOR-166, Q-STOR-167). A replaced or removed
  avatar's blob is queued for collection by the reference triggers (R-STOR-024); deleting a user does the same. The
  table is exported by a backup (R-BAK-004, `data`).
- **Audit.** `user.avatar.set` (`details.source` `self`, `sha256`, `size`) and `user.avatar.removed` (`source` `self` or
  `admin`, `sha256`), transactional with the change (Q-AUTH-197). An upload of the image the user already has records nothing.
- **Who.** A user changes only their own avatar. A service account and a CI token have no avatar and answer `403` on the two
  `me` routes, and so does a token whose scope is narrower than its owner's rights (`x-trove-owner-rights`, R-API-021, Q-API-213, Q-API-214); a session
  and a token that inherits the owner's rights may. An administrator removes, never sets, another user's avatar (Q-AUTH-196). Any authenticated caller reads an
  image (Q-AUTH-195).
- **Writes from the browser** are session writes: `X-CSRF-Token` is required (R-API-006), `If-Match` is not (the image is
  replaced as a whole and addressed by its digest, R-API-012).

| Status | `code` | When |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | `malformed_request` | The body is empty |
| 403 | `forbidden` | The caller is a service account or a CI token, or a token limited to part of its owner's rights; or lacks `identities:write` for another user's avatar |
| 403 | `csrf_failed` | A session write without the CSRF header |
| 404 | `not_found` | `GET`: no avatar has this digest; `DELETE` of another user: no such user |
| 413 | `payload_too_large` | The body is longer than 1 MiB |
| 415 | `unsupported_media_type` | The declared type is not PNG, JPEG or WebP; the content is not; the content is another of the three than declared |
| 422 | `validation_failed` | `errors[0].code` `animated_image`, `invalid_dimensions` (under 32 x 32, over 4,194,304 pixels, or above the decode memory bound), `too_complex` (more than 64 JPEG scans, or a decode over 5 s) or `undecodable_image` (damaged or truncated) |
| 503 | `server_busy` | No decoding slot became free within 2 s; `Retry-After: 1` |
| 503 | `unavailable`, `object_store_unavailable` | The store or the object store cannot take the request |

Acceptance criteria:

- A PNG, a JPEG and a WebP (lossy, lossless and with alpha) each come out as a PNG of 256 x 256 pixels, the corner of the
  source in the corner of the result; a 96 x 64 image is cropped to its centre square; the same input gives the same bytes
  (`TestR_API_055_ReEncodesToTheFixedSquare`).
- A JPEG with an EXIF block holding a position and a comment, and a PNG with a text chunk and an HTML page after `IEND`, come
  out with no such byte, with the chunks `IHDR`, `IDAT` and `IEND` only and nothing after `IEND`
  (`TestR_API_055_ResultCarriesNoMetadataAndNoAppendedData`); the orientation of a photo is applied
  (`TestR_API_055_AppliesTheExifOrientationOfAPhoto`, `FuzzR_API_055_ExifOrientation`).
- An SVG, an HTML page, a GIF and a GIF-and-script polyglot are refused whatever type they declare, and an image of another
  accepted format than declared is refused (`TestR_API_055_RefusesWhatIsNotAPNGJPEGOrWebP`).
- A body of 1 MiB + 1 byte is refused and one of 1 MiB is not (`TestR_API_055_RefusesABodyAboveTheLimit`); an image whose
  header declares 100,000 x 100,000 pixels, or a canvas of 16,000 x 16,000, is refused by its size and not by a failed decode
  (`TestR_API_055_RefusesTheDimensionsBeforeDecoding`); a truncated image (`TestR_API_055_RefusesAnImageThatDoesNotDecode`) and
  an animated PNG or WebP (`TestR_API_055_RefusesAnimatedImages`) are refused; a replica with no free slot answers busy
  (`TestR_API_055_BoundsTheImagesDecodedAtOnce`).
- On a running `api` replica: an upload, the read with the headers above by the owner, another user and an administrator, the
  `304` for the ETag, the replacement (the old URL is `404` and its blob queued), the removal by the owner and by an
  administrator, the refusal for another user and for a service account, the cascade when the user is deleted, the refusals
  of every error row, and the CSRF header for a session
  (`TestR_API_055_AvatarLifecycle`, `TestR_API_055_AvatarRefusals`,
  `TestR_API_055_AvatarWritesNeedTheCSRFHeaderOfASession`).

### R-API-056 · The installation's visibility settings
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: trove-only

Owned by [authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-033 (the installation's default level, Q-AUTHZ-264):

| Method | Path | operationId | Purpose | Permission |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/v1/settings/visibility` | `getVisibilitySettings` | The default level, whether `public` is available, and the objects that are `public` | `settings:read` |
| PATCH | `/api/v1/settings/visibility` | `updateVisibilitySettings` | Change the default level (JSON Merge Patch, R-API-013; `If-Match`, R-API-012) | `security-settings:write`; recent authentication |

```json
{
  "defaultLevel": "private",
  "publicAvailable": true,
  "publicObjects": {"projects": ["web"], "repositories": ["web/npm-public"], "truncated": false}
}
```

*(example answer; `defaultLevel` `private` is the default)*

- `defaultLevel` (`private`, `internal`, `public`) is the level a project takes when it is created and the upper bound of the
  levels a repository takes when it is created (R-AUTHZ-033). A `PATCH` is `{"defaultLevel": "internal"}`; the other two
  members are read-only and ignored in a `PATCH` body, so a `GET` body can be sent back (Q-AUTH-45).
- `publicAvailable` is the default endpoint's `auth.anonymous` ([endpoints.md](endpoints.md) R-EP-010). While it is `false`,
  a `defaultLevel` of `public` answers 409 `public_not_allowed`.
- `publicObjects` lists the projects and the repositories whose artifacts are `public`, at most 100 of each in key order,
  `truncated` when there are more; the UI shows it as the summary of what anyone can read (R-UI-032, R-UI-053).
- A change writes `settings.visibility.changed` with the default before and after; it is not journaled, because it decides
  only objects created later ([authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-036). The value is read in the transaction that
  creates a project or a repository and is cached nowhere.

Schemas in `api/openapi.yaml`: `VisibilityLevel` (enum `private`, `internal`, `public`), `VisibilitySettings`,
`VisibilitySettingsPatch`, `PublicObjects`.

Acceptance criteria:

- `PATCH /api/v1/settings/visibility` with `{"defaultLevel": "internal"}` and the `ETag` of the `GET` answers 200; a project
  created afterwards reads back `"visibility": "internal"`, and the projects that existed keep their levels.
- With `endpoints.default.auth.anonymous: false`, `GET` answers `"publicAvailable": false` and a `PATCH` to `public` answers
  409 `public_not_allowed`.
- A caller with `settings:read` and without `security-settings:write` (the `auditor`) reads the settings and gets 403 on the
  `PATCH`.

### R-API-057 · The visibility of projects and repositories in the API
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: trove-only

Owned by [authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-033 and R-AUTHZ-035:

| Method | Path | operationId | Purpose | Permission |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PUT | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/visibility` | `setProjectVisibility` | Set the project's level: `{"level": "internal"}`; `If-Match` with the project's `ETag` | `projects:write`; recent authentication |
| POST | `/api/v1/projects` | `createProject` | `visibility` in the body, default the installation's `defaultLevel` | `projects:write`; recent authentication for a level above `private` |
| PATCH, PUT | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/{repoKey}` | `updateRepository`, `replaceRepository` | the member `visibility` of the document ([repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-004) | as for the document; the project's Owner or `repositories:write-config`; recent authentication when a level rises |

- **The project's answer.** `setProjectVisibility` answers 200 with the project and a member `lowered`: the qualified names of
  the repositories whose levels the change lowered, with their levels before (`[{"repository": "web/npm-public", "before":
  {"artifacts": "public", "wiki": "internal"}}]`), empty when it lowered none. The answer carries `Trove-Authz-Epoch`
  (R-AUTHZ-032). 409 `public_not_allowed` while the default endpoint admits no request without a credential; 412 for a
  stale `If-Match`; 403 for an Owner without `projects:write`.
- **The repository's member.** `visibility` is `{"artifacts": "<level>", "wiki": "<level>"}` in every view of the document,
  the reduced consumer view of R-REPO-010 included, so every reader sees how open a repository is. A merge patch may name one
  part. The answers are 422 `validation_failed` with `visibility_above_project` or `visibility_wiki_above_artifacts` at
  `/visibility/artifacts` or `/visibility/wiki`, and 409 `public_not_allowed`; a write that opens a remote repository with
  `cacheFillAction: read` to the public carries the warning `public_populates_remote`
  ([authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-008).
- **Lists.** `GET /api/v1/repositories` and the project's list accept `visibility=` (one or more levels, comma-separated),
  matched against the artifacts level, and carry `visibility` in the summary view; `GET /api/v1/projects` carries each
  project's `visibility` and accepts `membership=true` (R-API-047).
- Schemas: `VisibilityLevel`, `RepositoryVisibility` (`artifacts`, `wiki`), `ProjectVisibilityRequest`,
  `ProjectVisibilityResult` (the project and `lowered`), the member `visibility` of `Project` and `Repository`.

Acceptance criteria:

- `PUT /api/v1/projects/web/visibility` with `{"level": "private"}` while `web/npm-public` is `public` answers 200 with
  `lowered` naming `web/npm-public`; `GET /api/v1/projects/web/repositories/npm-public` then shows `{"artifacts": "private",
  "wiki": "private"}`.
- `GET /api/v1/repositories?visibility=public` lists exactly the repositories whose artifacts are `public` among those the
  caller may read.
- A merge patch `{"visibility": {"wiki": "internal"}}` on a repository whose artifacts are `public` answers 200 and leaves the
  artifacts `public`.

### R-API-058 · Operations that serve wiki content
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: trove-only

An operation of the management API that serves only wiki content ([authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-034) carries
the extension `x-trove-part: wiki` in `api/openapi.yaml`. The document validator accepts the extension only on a `GET`
operation whose permission is the read of a repository's content (the declaration of R-API-029's operations) and refuses it
elsewhere; it is read into `Operation.Part`, as `x-trove-maintenance` is read into `Operation.MaintenanceAllowed`
([Q-API-247](#q-api-247--the-wiki-part-of-an-operation-is-an-extension-of-the-document-read-into-the-operation)).

- The shared authorization step admits such an operation as it admits the other reads of R-API-029, whose read is decided per
  repository in the handler; the handler then asks the wiki of the repository that holds the version through
  `authz.ReadScope.MayReadWiki` and answers the 404 of a missing README when it is refused. Like the filter of a listing, the
  question writes no `authz.denied` (R-AUTHZ-029): the caller may read the package and asked about a member of it. Nothing tells
  the caller that a README exists.
- A member of a management answer that carries wiki content (`hasReadme` of R-API-029, `metadata.docs` of the Ansible format)
  is decided with `MayReadWiki` and is `false` or absent when refused. The format's view adapter returns the wiki members
  marked, so that the API, not the format, drops them.
- Today's operations with `x-trove-part: wiki`: `getPackageVersionReadme`; the documentation operations of
  [formats/ansible.md](formats/ansible.md) (T-19) join with their requirement.
- A test walks the document and fails when an operation whose response schema holds a README or a documentation body lacks
  the extension (`TestR_API_058_WikiOperationsAreMarked`).

Acceptance criteria:

- `getPackageVersionReadme` carries `x-trove-part: wiki`; a document with the extension on a `PUT` operation fails to load.
- For a caller who reads the artifacts of `web/npm-public` and not its wiki, `GET …/readme` answers 404 with the body of a
  missing README.

### R-API-060 · One operation answers the suggestions of the search field
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: trove-only

The owner's task T-22 (2026-11-12): one search field with live suggestions for every caller (R-UI-095 to R-UI-099).
`GET /api/v1/search/suggestions` answers, in one request, the best matches of a text for each kind the field shows
([Q-API-270](#q-api-270--one-operation-answers-the-suggestions-and-the-results-page-reads-the-three-lists)):

| Parameter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `q` | Required. The text, trimmed: 2 to 100 characters, else `400 malformed_request` with the pointer `q` |
| `kind` | `repository`, `package`, `project`, `user`, `group`; repeated or comma-separated; default `repository,package,project`. An unknown kind answers `400 malformed_request` |
| `limit` | Suggestions per kind, 1 to 10, default 5 |

```json
{
  "repositories": {"items": [{"project": "web", "key": "npm-local", "format": "npm", "class": "local"}], "more": false},
  "packages": {"items": [{"id": "pkg_nzyg2acao5swel3vnewww2lu", "format": "npm", "name": "@web/ui-kit", "project": "web", "repository": "npm-local"}], "more": true},
  "projects": {"items": [{"key": "web", "displayName": "Web platform"}], "more": false}
}
```

- One member per kind asked (`repositories`, `packages`, `projects`, `users`, `groups`), absent for a kind not asked; `items` in the
  order of R-API-062, `more` by R-API-061. A user is `{"id", "username", "displayName", "disabled"}`, a group `{"name",
  "description"}`; a package's `name` is its display name and `id` the identifier of `GET /api/v1/packages/{packageId}`
  ([Q-API-271](#q-api-271--the-answer-holds-one-typed-member-per-kind-and-no-cursor)).
- Not a list of R-API-010: no `cursor`, `nextCursor` or `Link`. The results page reads the lists (R-UI-098).
- Permission: any caller (`x-trove-permission: public: true`), decided in the handler by R-API-061. Without a credential `401`
  while no repository's artifacts are `public`, as the lists answer. `kind` `user` or `group` needs `identities:read`; without it
  the answer is `403`, before any lookup and the same for every `q`
  ([Q-API-272](#q-api-272--users-and-groups-need-identitiesread-checked-before-any-lookup)).
- Rate limit: the class `read` with a credential, `anonymous` without (R-API-016); no class of its own
  ([Q-API-281](#q-api-281--the-suggestions-use-the-read-and-anonymous-classes-and-q-is-2-to-100-characters)).
- Freshness: the repositories are matched over the grant index of the request (R-AUTHZ-028), on which they are decided anyway, so a
  repository created through another replica is suggested within the propagation bound of R-API-052; projects, packages, users and
  groups are read from PostgreSQL. `Trove-Authz-Min-Epoch` (R-AUTHZ-032) applies as on every operation.
- `Cache-Control: no-store` (R-API-017).

Acceptance criteria:

- `GET /api/v1/search/suggestions?q=n` and a `q` of 101 characters answer `400 malformed_request`; `kind=file` `400`; `limit=11`
  `400`.
- `GET /api/v1/search/suggestions?q=npm&kind=repository` answers only the member `repositories`.
- The answer carries `RateLimit-Policy: "read";q=200;w=4` with the defaults.

### R-API-061 · A suggestion names only what the caller may read
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: trove-only

The suggestions are a listing in the sense of [authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-016: they hold only what the caller may
read, and nothing in the answer depends on an object it may not read. Per kind the rule is the one of that kind's list, on the same
decision point and the same index of the request:

| Kind | Suggested when | Decided by |
|---|---|---|
| repository | the caller may read it, by a grant, a role or its artifacts level (R-AUTHZ-035), or, holding `repositories:read-config`, the endpoint of the request exposes it; a repository being deleted is never in the index | `acc.Readable`, `acc.Exposed` for `repositories:read-config`, as `GET /api/v1/repositories` |
| package | in a physical repository the caller reads whole (read shape `ReadAll`), one version is live and served; in one it reads in part (`ReadRows`), the caller may read the package's document and the repository's include and exclude patterns admit the name ([Q-API-275](#q-api-275--a-package-in-a-repository-read-in-part-is-decided-on-its-document)) | the read scope of `GET /api/v1/packages` (`authz.ReadScope`) |
| project | the caller is a member, holds `projects:read`, or the project's level admits it (R-AUTHZ-035 rule 8) | the rule of `GET /api/v1/projects` |
| user, group | the caller holds `identities:read` | the capability, checked before any lookup |

- **Hidden existence holds.** `hideExistence` (R-AUTHZ-017) changes only the status of a refused read. A repository with
  `hideExistence: false` that the caller cannot read is suggested no more than any other. A virtual repository is suggested by its own
  gate (R-AUTHZ-009 rule 1); its members are not suggested through it.
- **Levels, users and tokens.** The level `internal` admits an internal subject only (R-AUTHZ-030): a user flagged external, a
  service account, a CI token and a request through a Bastion get what grants, roles and `public` give them. A token's scope narrows
  what grants and `internal` give, not what `public` gives (R-AUTHZ-035 rule 3).
- **A project is named by its key** in a repository's or a package's entry
  ([Q-API-277](#q-api-277--an-entry-names-the-project-of-a-repository-or-a-package-by-its-key)). Its display name appears only in a
  project entry, which the project rule admits.
- **Filtered before it is cut** ([Q-API-276](#q-api-276--more-reports-only-readable-matches-the-answer-left-out)). Each kind is ranked
  among the readable matches (R-API-062) and then cut at `limit`. `more` is `true` when the kind left out a readable match it found.
  The work per request is bounded (R-API-064), so `more` may be `false` while the results page holds more; it is never `true` because
  of an object the caller cannot read.
- **The same for every text.** `400`, `401` and `403` do not depend on `q`.

Acceptance criteria, each a test of the integration area `search` on the worked rows of R-AUTHZ-035 (project `web`, `public`;
`npm-public` with artifacts `public` and wiki `internal`; `npm-internal`, both `internal`; `npm-private`, both `private`, with
`hideExistence: false`; the virtual `npm-all`, `internal`, over the three; each local repository holds `@web/button`; Erin flagged
external with `read` on `npm-private`; Frank internal without grants):

- Without a credential, `q=npm` answers the repository `web/npm-public` alone and `@web/button` with `repository: npm-public`.
- Frank: `npm-all`, `npm-internal` and `npm-public`, never `npm-private`. Erin: `npm-private` and `npm-public`, never `npm-internal`
  or `npm-all`.
