- Routes with slash-containing parameters (npm scoped names, file paths) use a router `UrlMatcher`
  that captures the remaining segments.
- A repository is named in a route by the project of the route and its key, and in a query parameter (`?repository=`)
  by the qualified name `<projectKey>/<repoKey>`. The content routes live under `/projects/{project}/…`
  ([Q-UI-129](#q-ui-129--the-project-is-the-context-of-the-content-chosen-from-your-projects)); `/projects/{project}`
  answers with the repositories (Q-UI-216), so that the step of the project in the breadcrumb links to a route that exists. A route
  that existed before the project was the context (`/packages`, `/browse`, `/vulnerabilities`,
  `/admin/repositories/{project}/{key}`, `/admin/projects/{project}`) is not found.
- Route guards only shape navigation; the API decides (R-UI-005). When a screen's first API call
  answers 403, the screen shows a "no access" state with the missing permission and, for callers
  with `policies:read`, a link to the explainer.
- Every route sets a page title ("Packages – trove") through a `TitleStrategy`.

Acceptance criteria:

- Opening `/ui/en/projects/web/packages/npm/@team-a/ui?version=1.3.0` in a fresh tab shows that version.
- Copying the URL of a filtered packages list into another browser reproduces the filters.

### R-UI-004 · Sign-in, session and sign-out
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-006, AUTHN-037, AUTHN-038

The flow and its security properties are owned by
[identity-and-authentication.md](identity-and-authentication.md); the UI side:

- The UI never shows a username and password form for regular users (INV-7).
- On load the UI calls `GET /api/v1/auth/whoami`. Success starts the application. 401 while
  `publicContent` is false navigates to `/login?returnTo=<current route>`; while it is true
  (from `login-options`), the application runs anonymously with a "Sign in" button (R-UI-057).
- `/login` renders only from `GET /api/v1/auth/login-options`: one button per provider, each
  navigating (full page) to the provider's `startUrl` with `return_to` set to the UI route under the path of the page's
  resolved base (`document.baseURI`, so a relative `<base href>` counts as the browser resolves it): `/ui/en/…` and `/ui/de/…` in
  the builds per locale, `/ui/…` on the development server (UI-A-49). With
  `autoRedirect` set, the page navigates at once unless the URL carries `?auto_sign_in=false`. The
  break-glass form appears when `localLogin` is true or the URL carries `?auto_sign_in=false`, and
  posts to the local login endpoint of the owning page. The screen stands alone, without the shell,
  in one column: the form first, then the providers below "or sign in with" (Q-UI-125).
  A login notice is P2 ([operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md)).
- A 401 during use (expired or revoked session) opens a dialog "Your session has ended" with "Sign
  in again"; editors with unsaved changes first offer "Copy draft as JSON".
- Sign-out: `POST /auth/logout` with the CSRF header, then navigation to the returned
  `redirectTo`, or to `/logged-out`.
- `/logged-out` is where the post-logout redirect URI `<baseURL>/ui/logged-out` lands. R-AUTH-003
  and R-AUTH-013 register that URI at the identity provider, and the locale redirect of R-UI-001
  takes it to `/ui/{locale}/logged-out`. Because the URI is registered at the IdP, the route name
  is a contract: it does not follow the UI wording, whose visible text stays "Signed out". The
  page needs no session. A 401 from `whoami` on this route does not navigate to `/login`, and the
  page never sends the browser to an identity provider on its own; otherwise auto-redirect would
  sign the user straight back in while the IdP session is still alive. The page offers "Sign in
  again", which opens `/login`.
- Sign-out in one tab signs out every other tab of the same browser (`BroadcastChannel`).
- Command-line login approval (P1). The flows, the `cli_login` record and the texts are owned by
  R-AUTH-034 and R-AUTH-036 in [identity-and-authentication.md](identity-and-authentication.md).
  Both screens need a session; without one the UI starts the sign-in with `return_to` set to the
  screen. Approve and deny send the CSRF header and need recent authentication (R-API-007).
  - `/cli-login/{publicId}` is the `loginUrl` that `npm login` opens. It renders
    `GET /api/v1/auth/cli-logins/{publicId}`: the client kind and registry URL; the requesting
    address, user agent and request time; the resulting token's lifetime and scope; the warning to
    approve only a login the user just started; a prominent warning when the browser's address
    differs from the requesting address; and every refused poll with its address, its time and
    the text of R-AUTH-034. While the screen is open it refreshes the record every 2 seconds, so a
    refusal before or after the decision appears without a reload; leaving the screen stops the
    refresh. "Approve" (with an optional narrower scope or shorter lifetime) and "Deny" are final.
  - `/device` is the `verification_uri` of the device flow; `verification_uri_complete` adds
    `?code=`. The screen takes the user code as R-AUTH-036 requires, then shows the same record
    plus the tool's `client_id`. When the tool asked for `self_rotatable=true`, the screen shows
    that request, explains that the token could then renew itself, and lets the approver decline
    it; the issued PAT records the outcome as `selfRotatable`.

Acceptance criteria:

- With one provider and auto-redirect, opening `/ui/en/packages` unauthenticated lands at the
  identity provider and, after login, back on `/ui/en/packages`.
- Signing out in tab A shows `/logged-out` in tab B within two seconds.
- With one provider, auto-redirect on, nothing public and `rp_initiated_logout` false,
  signing out lands on `/ui/{locale}/logged-out` and stays there. The browser sends no request to
  the identity provider until the user selects "Sign in again".
- (P1) With `/ui/en/cli-login/{publicId}` open, a poll of the login's `doneUrl` from outside the
  starting network appears on the screen as a refused poll with its address within 4 seconds,
  without a reload.
- (P1) On `/ui/en/device`, approving a request with `self_rotatable=true` and declining the
  self-rotation issues a PAT whose `POST /api/v1/tokens/current/rotate` answers 403.

### R-UI-005 · Permission-driven rendering
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-005

- Authorization is enforced by the API alone; the UI adapts what it shows for convenience.
- Data: capabilities and project memberships with their roles from `GET /api/v1/authz/me` for navigation and global
  actions; per-control
  decisions from `POST /api/v1/authz/check` (up to 100 checks per call, batched per screen, cached
  for 60 seconds, dropped on any 403 and on sign-out).
- Primary actions on a screen that the caller lacks are shown disabled with the reason ("Needs
  deploy on npm-local"); menu entries the caller lacks are hidden. Lists show what the API returns.
- On a screen of a project the reason names whom to ask, the project's Owners by name ("Read only. Ask priya, an Owner of
  web-frontend, to change this."), and no capability (Q-UI-318); the administrator's screens name the capability ("Read only:
  changing this needs the permission `settings:write`").
- Self-lockout guards are shown before the API refuses them: the last administrator binding cannot
  be removed, a user cannot disable themselves, the last Owner of a project cannot be removed or demoted except by an
  administrator (R-UI-041).
- An authenticated user who can read nothing sees an empty state that names their identity and
  groups, so they can ask for access.

Acceptance criteria:

- A user without `deploy` on `npm-local` sees the deploy action disabled with its reason; forcing
  the request from the browser console answers 403.

### R-UI-006 · Packages list
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-008, ART-048

- The list uses the shared data table and the shared filter panel of R-UI-002 (Q-UI-68): the
  filters below are the panel's categories, the sort control is a column header, "Load more" is the
  table's.
- Backed by R-API-029 (the start page of a project is its repositories, R-UI-052, Q-UI-216). Filters, as the categories of the panel: package type (multi-select),
  repository (multi-select), name or description (`q`), keyword, created period (last 7, 30, 90 days,
  custom; a custom end day is included). Applied filters appear as removable chips and live in the URL.
- Table (Q-UI-314): the package (its name, with its description as the muted second line, never cut), its format (icon plus
  text, never icon alone; the icon is the format owner's logo where the owner's terms allow it, else the neutral package
  glyph, Q-UI-225), the latest version, updated (relative, with the absolute time in a `<time datetime>` element and its
  title). The number of versions, of repositories, the downloads and the first publication are on the package's page (its
  Details). Sortable by the package and updated in the headers; the sort by first created stays the API's and a saved view's
  (`sort=createdAt`). Every sort is the server's (R-API-029).
- Paging with an explicit "Load more" button; no infinite scroll.
- Tabs: all packages; recently opened (last 10 opened, browser storage keyed by user, Q-UI-323); saved views
  (at most 8, browser storage; rename, delete, make default; a list opened without any query applies the
  default view once). Browser storage access is wrapped so that blocked storage only hides these tabs.
  The tab is the `tab` query parameter.
- Each row is a link, so it opens in a new tab with the usual browser gestures.
- Empty states: no packages at all (link to client setup); no match (clear filters).

Acceptance criteria:

- After publishing three npm packages and one NuGet package, `format=nuget` shows one row, and
  reloading the page keeps the filter.
- With browser storage disabled, the page works and the two browser-storage tabs are hidden.

### R-UI-007 · Package details and versions
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-009, ART-049

- `/packages/{format}/{name…}` resolves through `GET /api/v1/packages/lookup`; the name keeps its slash
  as a path separator (`/packages/npm/@team-a/ui`) and is one breadcrumb step (Q-UI-73). The selected
  version is the `version` query parameter, the open tab the `tab` parameter, the pre-release switch
  `prerelease=true`.
- Header: name, format (its icon of Q-UI-225 and its name), selected version (default: the latest stable visible version; the latest
  pre-release when no stable one exists), published time, licenses, download count, the
  repositories that contain it.
- Version selector: a select of the versions, newest first (it looks like the choice it is, Q-UI-315), and an "include
  pre-releases" switch that follows the format's version rules (npm SemVer pre-release tags, NuGet SemVer 2.0 pre-release
  labels). An "All versions" tab lists versions with published time, size, repositories and downloads.
- Tabs: README (default when the version has one for the caller, `hasReadme`; a version without one, or whose wiki the
  caller may not read, has no README tab and the README is not requested, R-UI-008, R-UI-057; for the format `ansible` the tabs **Documentation**, **Contents** and, on a local repository, **Import log** replace and extend it: [Q-UI-240](#q-ui-240--an-ansible-package-has-a-documentation-tab-and-a-contents-tab-the-readme-tab-is-its-first-page) to Q-UI-244, shown by `metadata.docs` of the version details); Metadata (format-specific: npm dist-tags and
  dependency kinds, NuGet target frameworks and dependency groups, authors, project URL as a text
  link with an external-link marker; the members the page reads are in Q-UI-93, among them the unlisted state; OCI the digest, media type, artifact type and
  size of the tag and the platforms of an index, Q-UI-177); Files (files of the version with size, SHA-256 copy button,
  download); Repositories (each with "show in browser"); Owners (R-API-048, P1); Builds (P1).
- From M4b ([vulnerability-scanning.md](vulnerability-scanning.md) R-VULN-023): a Vulnerabilities
  tab (`tab=vulnerabilities`) with the selected version's grade card (R-UI-093), evaluation state, block and findings per
  readable repository, its label carrying the count of open findings; in the "All versions" tab the
  grade of each version (R-UI-094); in the header the selected version's grade and "Blocked in <repository>"
  when the selected version is blocked in a repository the caller can read.
- Layout (Q-UI-3): the header spans the full width. When the content area is at least 960 CSS px
  wide, two columns follow: the tabs on the left, the install panel (R-UI-009) on the right, which
  stays in view while the README scrolls (`position: sticky`). Narrower, one column: header,
  install panel, then the tabs, so the install command never sits below a long README.
- Opening the page records it in "recently opened" (Q-UI-323).
- Links taken from package metadata (npm `homepage`, `repository.url`, `bugs.url`; NuGet
  `projectUrl`, `licenseUrl`, the `repository` URL) MUST be rendered as links only when their
  scheme is `http` or `https`, with `rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer"`; any other value is shown
  as text. Package authors set these values, and Angular's URL sanitizer is a second layer, not
  the rule.

Acceptance criteria:

- For `@team-a/ui` with versions `1.3.0`, `1.4.0` and `1.5.0-beta.1`, the page opens on `1.4.0`;
  switching on pre-releases offers `1.5.0-beta.1`.
- The Files tab's SHA-256 equals `shasum -a 256` of the downloaded tarball.
- A package whose `homepage` is `javascript:alert(1)` shows the value as text, and no `a` element
  carries it.
- At a viewport of 390 CSS px the install command is visible without scrolling past the README; at
  1440 CSS px it stays visible after scrolling to the end of a long README.

### R-UI-008 · Sanitized README rendering
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-009

Rendering happens on the server (R-API-029), so one renderer and one sanitizer policy serve every
client.

- Markdown is CommonMark plus GitHub-style tables, strikethrough, autolinks and task lists. Raw HTML
  inside Markdown passes through the sanitizer.
- Sanitizer allowlist (normative minimum):

| Allowed | Rule |
|---|---|
| Elements | `h1`–`h6`, `p`, `br`, `hr`, `blockquote`, `ul`, `ol`, `li`, `dl`, `dt`, `dd`, `pre`, `code`, `kbd`, `samp`, `em`, `strong`, `del`, `ins`, `sup`, `sub`, `a`, `img`, `table`, `thead`, `tbody`, `tfoot`, `tr`, `th`, `td`, `details`, `summary`, and disabled task-list checkboxes |
| `href` on `a` | Schemes `http`, `https`, `mailto`, and in-page `#` fragments; relative links that cannot be resolved are reduced to their text; links get `rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer"` and no `target` |
| `img` | `src` per the image policy (Q-UI-6): an `https` image whose origin is listed in `ui.readme.external_image_origins` is kept (the UI document's `Referrer-Policy: same-origin` of R-UI-001 keeps the page URL, which names the package, from reaching that host); every other external image is replaced by a link "External image: <alt>"; `data:` sources dropped; sources that resolve to trove's own origin, relative or absolute, dropped as well, except image URLs the renderer itself generates for files embedded in the package, so a README cannot make the viewer's browser send authenticated requests to package or file endpoints ([authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-008). The renderer builds those URLs only through `LinkBuilder` ([architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-007), never from strings, so from P1 a content origin (R-ARCH-029) receives them without a renderer change; `alt`, `width`, `height` |
| `id`, `name` | Kept only when prefixed `user-content-` (prevents DOM clobbering) |
| `class` | Only `language-*` on `code` |
| Table attributes | `align` with `left`, `center`, `right`; `colspan`, `rowspan` |
| `open` on `details` | Kept |

  Everything else is removed: `script`, `style`, `iframe`, `object`, `embed`, `form`, `input` (except
  the checkboxes above), `svg`, `math`, `base`, `meta`, `link`, `style` attributes, event-handler
  attributes, and `javascript:`, `vbscript:` and `data:` URLs.
- Limits: source at most `ui.readme.max_source_bytes`, rendered HTML at most 1 MiB, rendering at most
  2 seconds; beyond that the README is truncated with a notice. These limits come on top of the
  limits for untrusted package content of R-ARCH-028.
- The client binds the HTML with `[innerHTML]`, so Angular's sanitizer runs a second time; the
  Trusted Types CSP of R-UI-001 is the third layer. That second layer removes every `id` and `name`
  and does not know `vbscript:`; the component therefore finishes the job after binding: it drops a link
  target that is not a fragment, `http`, `https` or `mailto`, drops an image whose source is neither
  `https` nor a path of this origin, sets `rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer"` and no `target` on every
  link that leaves trove, and derives the anchor `user-content-<slug>` of every heading itself, with the
  rule of the server's renderer (lower case, punctuation removed, spaces to hyphens, a repeated name
  numbered `-1`, `-2`), so that the table-of-contents links the server wrote resolve (Q-UI-71). The server
  and the component implement one rule, JavaScript's `trim`, `\s` and `toLowerCase`, and test one corpus
  (Q-UI-76).
- In-page links to `#user-content-…` scroll within the README and never navigate (the document's
  `<base href>` would turn a bare fragment into a navigation to the UI root); code blocks scroll
  horizontally and take focus.
- Libraries (pinned once in `go.mod`): [goldmark](https://github.com/yuin/goldmark) for Markdown
  and [bluemonday](https://github.com/microcosm-cc/bluemonday) for sanitizing.
- External image origins (Q-UI-6) are exact `https` origins (scheme, host, optional port; no
  path, no wildcard), validated at start-up; an invalid entry stops start-up, and so does an entry that
  is an origin of this installation (`server.base_url`, `additional_base_urls`, an endpoint's `base_url`):
  an image from it would make the viewer's browser send authenticated requests to trove. Images of files
  embedded in the package (rendered through `LinkBuilder`) are P1 (R-ARCH-029) and not built. The same list feeds
  the sanitizer and the CSP `img-src` of R-UI-001, so the two can never disagree. Because the
  rendered HTML depends on the list, the README cache of R-API-029 stores the list's hash and
  re-renders when it changes.
- Package images (P1, R-ARCH-029): with `server.content_base_url` set, a browser's request for an
  image the renderer generated is redirected to the content origin, which the CSP `img-src` of
  R-UI-001 then lists. The list of external image origins above is unaffected; the content origin
  is never entered there.

Configuration:

```yaml
ui:
  readme:
    max_source_bytes: 512KiB          # default; 1KiB to 16MiB
    external_image_origins: []        # default: every external image becomes a link
    # external_image_origins: ["https://img.shields.io", "https://gitlab.example.com"]   # example
```

Acceptance criteria:

- A fixture corpus of XSS vectors (script tags, event-handler attributes, `javascript:` links, SVG
  with script, `<form>`, `<base>`, `<style>`, `id="__proto__"`) rendered by the server contains none
  of them in executable form; a Playwright test displays each fixture and observes no dialog, no
  request to a foreign origin and no CSP violation.
- A README with a badge image from `https://img.shields.io` shows "External image: build status" as
  a link while `external_image_origins` is empty; with that origin listed, the image loads, the
  UI's CSP names exactly that origin in `img-src`, and an image from an unlisted host in the same
  README is still a link.
- A README containing `![x](/api/npm/web/npm-remote/left-pad)` or
  `<img src="https://trove.example.com/files/web/generic-local/x.png">` renders without an `img`
  element for either source, and viewing it causes no request to those paths.

### R-UI-009 · Install command panel
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-010

- Client picker per format (npm, pnpm, Yarn; .NET CLI, NuGet CLI, `PackageReference` XML); a
  repository picker when the version exists in more than one repository (default: a virtual
  repository containing it, else the first local one).
- The command comes from the install snippet of R-API-030 with package and version, requested with
  `credentials=none` (the install command carries no credentials). A command of one line is an address field of R-UI-065
  with its joined copy button; a command of several lines is a code block with its copy button (Q-UI-320); either way a
  live region announces "Copied". The client picker lists the clients of the format that the UI has instructions for
  (Q-UI-70).
- The panel's selects (client, repository) stack and share the panel's width (Q-UI-320).
- npm and NuGet install commands carry no credentials; the panel links to client setup for
  configuring the client once.
- Commands longer than three lines are collapsed with an expander.

Examples: `npm install @team-a/ui@1.4.0`, `dotnet add package Contoso.Logging --version 2.3.1`,
`<PackageReference Include="Contoso.Logging" Version="2.3.1" />`.

Acceptance criteria:

- Copying the npm command for `@team-a/ui@1.4.0` and running it in a project configured by the
  client setup installs that version.

### R-UI-052 · Repository content page
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: trove-only

`/projects/{project}/repositories/{key}` is what a repository holds, on the logical level (Q-UI-216); its settings moved to
`…/settings`. One shell serves every format; what differs per format is a small table of words and columns, not a screen per format
([content-shape.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/content-shape.ts)).

- Header (the shared page header of R-UI-067): the key (the `h1`), one muted sentence (the repository's description, else what
  the class means), the format and the class as badges (and **disabled** for a disabled repository), the repository's client
  address as an address field (its first address; the others are in Details, Q-UI-320), and at the right the primary action
  **Set up client** (not for a disabled repository), **Settings** for a caller who can read the configuration
  (`repositories:read-config`, or the Owner of the project) and a `more_vert` menu with **Browse files** (not for generic, whose
  content is its files) and **Vulnerabilities** (not for generic and virtual).
- No tabs: the content (captioned Images, Packages or Files) follows the header. **Set up client** opens the client setup of
  R-UI-016 for this repository (`/setup?repository=<project>/<key>`), which shows the format and the repository as one line with
  **Change** (Q-UI-316); it is the page's one way to the setup (Q-UI-321).
- A package format (npm, NuGet, OCI, Debian, every format with a view adapter) lists its items from `GET /api/v1/packages` with
  `repository=<qualified name>` and `format=<format>`, the filter `q` (query, server-side, name and description) and the sort `name`
  or `updatedAt`, paged with "Load more". The column **Vulnerabilities** appears only for a format whose versions are matched against
  advisories (`FormatDescriptor.vulnerabilityScanning`, a format with the vulnerability adapter, R-VULN-009, or the image scanning, R-VULN-033)
  and only when the answer carries grades (Q-UI-377); for a format that is not scanned a muted sentence says so (Debian today). It shows
  the grade of the item's latest version in this repository (`vulnerabilityGrade` from `include=vulnerabilities`, R-VULN-039, Q-VULN-154)
  as `<trove-grade>` (R-UI-094) and sorts by grade (`sort=grade`, worst first as `-grade`, in the browser, Q-UI-373). The versions list
  of an item is `…/versions?repository=…` with its `…/vulnerabilities?repository=…` report, one request each per opened item.
- The row of an item opens in place (`collapse-region`) to its versions: for an image, the tags with digest (`include=digest`), size and
  pushed time; for a package, its versions with size and published time; each with the grade of the version in this repository.
  Above the versions, the install command of the version chosen in the list (default: the item's latest version) from the install
  snippet of R-API-030 for this repository and the client picked in the panel (`credentials=none`, so it never holds a token): `docker
  pull`/`podman pull` with this installation's real address for OCI, the install command of the format elsewhere. The item's name links
  to the package details (R-UI-007), a version's name to the details at that version.
- A generic repository lists its files through `GET …/children` (R-API-025): folders open in place (query `path`, with a trail back up), a
  file links to its detail in the file browser (R-UI-010) and offers a copy of its download address; the filter narrows what is loaded,
  because children have no name filter on the server.
- A virtual repository shows what it resolves: the same list, whose `repository` filter expands to its members (R-API-029). A remote repository
  lists what it holds: what the format has stored for it (a cached npm or NuGet version, for example); a note says that only what
  clients have fetched appears. An OCI remote lists the images and tags its cache holds, from the same list API as a local one
  (R-OCI-036, Q-OCI-215): the note says that only the cached tags appear (those clients pulled and those a mirror pass fetched), the
  column of the tag's time is **Fetched** and not Pushed, and an empty remote says that it has cached no images yet (Q-UI-217).
- **Details** at the end of the page, closed (the disclosure of Q-UI-322), when the repository has one of these: the raw file
  address, labelled **Address for downloads by path (curl, wget)** (the API's `addresses` list the format's protocol address
  first and the raw file address after it where the two differ, R-REPO-002; the UI labels by that order and names no path of
  its own, R-ARCH-007), the upstream a remote repository caches (its URL), and the members a virtual repository resolves from,
  each linked to its content page as far as the caller may read them (the consumer view of R-REPO-010 has neither).
- An empty repository says how it is filled ("This repository holds no packages yet. Publish a package with your client.",
  for OCI images and generic files the same) and offers **Set up client** under it (the empty state of Q-UI-309), except for
  a disabled repository. Without a description the header's sentence says what the class means; for a local repository
  "Holds what is published to it."
- Opening the page records it in the recently opened repositories of the browser (R-UI-020), which the start page shows
  (Q-UI-311, Q-UI-323).

Acceptance criteria:

- `/projects/web` opens the repositories of the project; the sidebar lists Repositories first; the project switcher and the start page lead there.
- `/projects/web/repositories/<oci-key>` lists the images; opening one shows its tags with digest, size and pushed time and a
  `docker pull <host>/web/<oci-key>/<image>:<tag>` copy; Podman in the client picker switches it to `podman pull`.
- `/projects/web/repositories/<oci-remote-key>`, after a pull through it, lists the pulled image with its tag, the digest and a **Fetched** time; before any pull it says
  that the repository has cached no images yet (R-OCI-036, Q-UI-217).
- `/projects/web/repositories/<npm-key>` lists the packages with the grade of their latest version, and the open version
  row shows `npm install <name>@<version>`; a reader without `repositories:read-config` sees no Settings action.
- The Edit action of the repository list and the Settings action of the content page open `…/settings`, and leaving it with unsaved changes asks first.
- A generic repository shows Files, a folder opens in place and a file links to its detail.

### R-UI-010 · File tree browser
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-011, ART-040, ART-041

- Two bordered panes that fill the height of the content area, each with its own scroll: the tree on the
  left, the details on the right; one pane at a time with back navigation on narrow screens
  ([Q-UI-98](#q-ui-98--the-file-browser-is-two-panes-with-a-toolbar-and-a-details-header)). The selection is the
  URL (`/browse/{project}/{repo}/{path…}`); a deep link expands the ancestors.
- Tree toolbar: one filter field that narrows the repositories by key text as the user types (no search button; the
  query parameter `q` follows after a short pause), the shared filter panel for class and format with the applied
  filters as removable chips and "Clear all", a sort menu (class, then key; or key), and the number of repositories
  shown. Tree root: the readable repositories of the project, each labelled with its key (`npm-local`; a repository of
  another project, a member of a virtual one, with its qualified name). The screen is **Browse** at its root and with a
  selection: one screen, one name (UI-A-18). Children load lazily through
  `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/{repoKey}/children` (R-API-025) in pages of `ui.browser.page_size` with a "Load more" entry.
  A row shows an icon by class (folder and file icons below), the key, a badge with the format and, where it applies,
  the labels below.
- A virtual repository's children are its members in resolution order, labelled "resolves from"; a member leads to
  that repository, and the tree does not merge member contents. A remote repository shows its cached content,
  labelled as cache.
- Details header: the path of the selection as a breadcrumb and the actions of R-UI-011 as a toolbar. Content by
  selection: a repository shows its summary (class, format, description, and for a caller who may read the
  configuration the upstream, project, creation and last activity), links to its configuration and to the client
  setup, and its content as the shared data table (a virtual repository lists its members instead); a folder shows
  its children as the shared data table (name, size, last change) so it is browsed from the right pane too, tabs
  Contents, General and API; a file shows tabs General (path, kind, size, creation, digests with copy buttons,
  media type, download), Statistics (downloads) and API (the item's JSON and the equivalent `curl` command, INV-17).
  Properties (P1, R-API-026) and Effective permissions (P1, R-API-034, for callers with `policies:read` or
  `manage`) are not built yet. The link from a file to its package version appears when the API reports one; it
  reports none today (`package` is always null).
- Empty states: nothing selected (a short text and a link to the manual page), no readable repository (an
  administrator is offered "Create repository", anyone else is told to ask for access, both get the manual link),
  and a filter that matches nothing ("Clear all filters").
- The tree follows the WAI-ARIA tree pattern (roles `tree` and `treeitem`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-level`,
  `aria-setsize` and `aria-posinset` with lazy loading, arrow keys, Home and End, type-ahead), built on the tree
  pattern of `@angular/aria` (R-UI-001, Q-UI-1).

Configuration:

```yaml
ui:
  browser:
    page_size: 200   # default (proposed)
```

Acceptance criteria:

- With the keyboard only, a user expands `npm-local`, reaches `@team-a/ui/-/ui-1.4.0.tgz`, opens its
  details and downloads it.
- A folder with 1,000 files shows the first page and loads the rest with "Load more".

### R-UI-011 · Item actions
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-012, UI-016

| Action | Applies to | Needs | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|
| Download | File | `read` | MVP |
| Copy path, copy download URL | File, folder | `read` | MVP |
| Delete | File, folder | `delete` | MVP |
| Client setup | Repository | `read` | MVP |
| Reindex | Repository | `manage` | P1 |
| Invalidate cache (scope metadata, negative or all, R-API-024) | Remote or virtual repository | `manage` | MVP |
| Copy, move | File, folder | R-API-027 | P1 |
| Edit properties | File, folder | `annotate` | P1 |
| Deploy | Toolbar | `deploy` | P1 |

- Actions are reached through the toolbar of the details header and through the keyboard (context-menu
  key, Shift+F10 on the tree move focus to it), never through right-click alone (Q-UI-17, Q-UI-98). "Copy
  path" and a copy button for the address (the download URL of a file, the listing URL of a folder) sit beside
  Download. "Upload files" and "New folder" appear on a repository or folder of a local repository whose format
  is served below the files path (the raw-files family, R-API-025) and only for a caller who holds `deploy`
  there; "Client setup" on a repository opens the setup page for it. "Invalidate cache" has no control yet.
- Deleting a file asks for confirmation naming the path. Deleting a folder shows the number of
  items; above 100 items the user types the folder name to confirm. When the trash can is enabled,
  the dialog says the items go there for the retention period. Folder deletion shows the job's
  progress (R-UI-042).

Acceptance criteria:

- Deleting a folder with 150 items requires typing its name; the tree no longer shows it after the
  job succeeds.

### R-UI-012 · Deploy dialog
Priority: **P1** · Covers: UI-013

- Target repository: those where the caller holds `deploy` and raw deploys are accepted
  (R-API-025). For npm and NuGet repositories the dialog explains native publishing and links to
  the publish tab of the client setup.
- Fields: target path (prefilled with the selected folder), files (a drop zone plus a "Choose files"
  button, so dragging is never required), overwrite (only with `overwrite`).
- The size limit `ui.deploy.max_upload_bytes` is checked before the upload starts; larger files are
  pointed to native clients or `curl`.
- Uploads use `PUT /api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/{repoKey}/content/{path}` on the UI's own origin (R-API-025, Q-UI-106), built by the `files` client of `web/src/app/api/` (R-UI-001), never by the dialog. Because the fetch backend reports no upload
  progress, uploads go through an XHR-based `HttpClient` instance (`withXhr()`) to show progress.
  This is the only XHR use for content, and it writes; the UI never reads package content with
  `fetch` or XHR (R-UI-001).
- Files up to 256 MiB are hashed in the browser (Web Crypto SHA-256) and sent with `Repr-Digest`;
  larger files rely on the server's own digest.
- Several files upload one after another with per-file status; "Cancel" aborts the current one.
- An upload cut without an answer (a drain that reaches the shutdown deadline, R-API-051, Q-ARCH-18
  in [architecture.md](architecture.md)) has stored nothing ([storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-004).
  The dialog sends it once more from the start through the Service, from the `File` object it
  still holds; a raw deploy of identical content to the same path is idempotent. If the retry
  answers that the path exists, the dialog compares the item's SHA-256 with the digest it computed
  and reports success when they match.

Configuration:

```yaml
ui:
  deploy:
    max_upload_bytes: 100MiB      # default; 0 = unlimited
```

Acceptance criteria:

- Uploading a 10 MiB file shows progress and ends with the file in the tree; a file above the limit
  is refused before any request.

### R-UI-013 · Copy and move dialog
Priority: **P1** · Covers: UI-014

- Target repository picker (same format; local, or virtual with a default deployment target;
  `deploy` required), target path (default: the source path) with a live preview of the resulting
  full path, conflict handling, "Dry run" showing the report of `/api/v1/content/copy` or `/move`,
  then "Copy" or "Move".
- Large operations show job progress (R-UI-042).

Acceptance criteria:

- The preview shows `npm-release/@team-a/ui/-/ui-1.4.0.tgz` before execution, and that is where the
  file ends up.

### R-UI-014 · Trash can
Priority: **P1** · Covers: UI-018

- `/trash` and, when the trash can is enabled and the caller sees entries, a last "Trash can" node in
  the tree.
- Table: path, original repository, deletion time and actor, time until purge; filters by repository
  and path.
- Restore dialog: original location by default, optional other repository and path, conflict
  handling (`/api/v1/trash-can/restorations`). Purge of selected entries with confirmation. "Empty
  trash can" (administrators) requires typing `empty`.

Acceptance criteria:

- A deleted file appears in the trash can and downloads again after restore.

### R-UI-015 · Search
Priority: **P1** · Covers: UI-019, UI-020, SRCH-048, SRCH-058

- The header search is R-UI-095 to R-UI-099. What stays here is the file search: when R-API-028 is built, **Files** becomes a
  kind of the field's filter, and Enter under it opens the file search form below.
- File search form: name, path glob, checksum, property, repositories, date ranges, "not downloaded
  since"; each field maps to one parameter of R-API-028 and to the URL.
- Results table: path, repository, size, modified; actions "show in browser", download, copy URL.
- From the browser, a search starts scoped to the selected repository and folder (a removable scope
  chip).

Acceptance criteria:

- Searching files by the SHA-256 of a known tarball, under the field's kind **Files**, lists it with a working "show in
  browser" link.
- With shortcuts off, typing `/` in the page body does not move focus.

### R-UI-016 · Client setup dialog
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-021, UI-022, UI-023

- Route `/setup` (`?format=&client=&repository=`, so a link opens the page prepared), reachable from the
  user menu, a repository row, a repository node in the browser, the package details (the install panel
  links to it with the repository and client chosen there) and empty states.
- The shared page header (**Client setup**, one sentence, **Read the guide** as its action). Opened by a link that names a
  repository the caller may read, the page does not ask the format and the repository again: they are one line with
  **Change**, and the client is its one choice (Q-UI-316). Otherwise one page with progressive steps:
  1. format (generic, npm and NuGet in the MVP; further formats appear as they ship, from
     `GET /api/v1/formats`, in its order, the first preselected);
  2. client (curl; npm, pnpm, Yarn Berry, Yarn classic; .NET CLI, NuGet CLI, Visual Studio,
     `nuget.config`; Docker CLI with Buildx, Podman);
  3. repository: readable repositories of that format, each named with its project (`web/npm-all`), virtual
     repositories marked as recommended, publish availability shown per repository.
- The credential is one line under the choices: by default "The snippets read your token from the variable TROVE_TOKEN."
  with **Create a token to put into the variable**. The ways to give it, and the place to install from where a Bastion can be
  chosen (R-BAS-007), are a closed **More options** (the disclosure of Q-UI-322). The credentials, one of:
     - **Reference an environment variable** (default): snippets reference `TROVE_TOKEN`
       (R-API-030 `credentials=env`); no secret appears on screen; a link leads to creating a token.
     - **Create a token for this setup**: creates a personal token (R-API-032) described as "Client
       setup: <client>, <repository>, <date>", scoped to the chosen repository with `read` (plus
       `read` and `deploy` on the `publishTarget` of the setup answer when the user ticks the publish
       option, which exists only while the answer names a target), expiring after `tokenTtlSeconds` of
       the setup answer, which is `ui.client_setup.token_ttl` (bounded by the PAT maximum of R-AUTH-040).
       Recent authentication applies. The token is shown once and embedded in the snippets; choosing
       another repository or another way of signing in discards it (Q-UI-74).
     - **Use a token I already have**: a password-type field with a reveal toggle; pasting is
       allowed. The value stays in the browser; the UI checks its prefix, its length, its alphabet
       and its CRC32 checksum (INV-8, R-AUTH-022) locally, says which check failed, writes only a value
       that passes into the snippets, and never sends it to the server.
- Tabs Configure, Install and Publish with the snippets; each snippet shows its target file name
  and has a copy button; whole configuration files (`.npmrc`, `nuget.config`) can be downloaded.
  For npm, the Publish tab also holds the GitLab CI snippet in its two labelled variants
  (R-UI-017). The Publish tab is offered to who may publish (the answer holds publish snippets only for a caller with
  `deploy` on the target, R-API-030); a caller who may not has no Publish tab (Q-UI-316), and a Bastion's banner says that
  it is read only.
- Anonymous viewers of anonymously readable repositories get no credential choice and snippets
  without authentication lines.
- The browser replaces `{{token}}` in the component only; the composed text is never stored in a
  service, browser storage or the URL and is discarded when the route is left (R-UI-043).
- A virtual repository without a default deployment target shows, on the Publish tab of a caller who can read its
  configuration and so change it, an explanation and a link to its local members.
- The page links to the guide of R-UI-049 for the chosen format, client and repository, and the guide links back
  (Q-UI-84).

Acceptance criteria:

- Playwright: choosing npm, `npm-all` and "Create a token for this setup", downloading `.npmrc` and
  running `npm install @team-a/ui` with it in a `node:24` container succeeds.
- The default choice produces a `.npmrc` containing the literal `${TROVE_TOKEN}`.
- Pasting a token with a wrong checksum shows a validation error and sends no request.

### R-UI-017 · npm client instructions
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-024

Snippets for `npm-all` at `https://trove.example.com` (# example). The registry URL keeps its
trailing slash; the credential key is the same URL without scheme, which is how npm matches
credentials to a registry ([npmrc](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/configuring-npm/npmrc)); npm
expands `${…}` in `.npmrc`. The protocol behind the URLs is owned by
[formats/npm.md](formats/npm.md), which contributes these templates.

Project `.npmrc` for npm, pnpm and Yarn classic:

```ini
registry=https://trove.example.com/api/npm/web/npm-all/
//trove.example.com/api/npm/web/npm-all/:_authToken=${TROVE_TOKEN}
```

Scoped variant (only `@team-a` packages from trove):

```ini
@team-a:registry=https://trove.example.com/api/npm/web/npm-all/
//trove.example.com/api/npm/web/npm-all/:_authToken=${TROVE_TOKEN}
```

User-level configuration through the CLI (the shell expands the variable, so the token is written
into `~/.npmrc`):

```shell
npm config set registry=https://trove.example.com/api/npm/web/npm-all/
npm config set "//trove.example.com/api/npm/web/npm-all/:_authToken=${TROVE_TOKEN}"
```

Yarn Berry `.yarnrc.yml` ([yarnrc](https://yarnpkg.com/configuration/yarnrc); Yarn expands
`${…}`):

```yaml
npmRegistryServer: "https://trove.example.com/api/npm/web/npm-all/"
npmAlwaysAuth: true
npmAuthToken: "${TROVE_TOKEN}"
```

| Client | Install | Publish (local repository, or virtual with default deployment target) |
|---|---|---|
| npm | `npm install <package>` | `npm publish --registry https://trove.example.com/api/npm/web/npm-all/`, or `"publishConfig": {"registry": "…/api/npm/web/npm-all/"}` in `package.json` (the guide) |
| pnpm | `pnpm add <package>` | `pnpm publish --registry https://trove.example.com/api/npm/web/npm-all/` |
| Yarn Berry | `yarn add <package>` | `npmPublishRegistry: "…/api/npm/web/npm-all/"` in `.yarnrc.yml`, then `yarn npm publish` |
| Yarn classic | `yarn add <package>` | `yarn publish --registry …/api/npm/web/npm-all/` |

The registry in the publish column is the repository the snippets are for (`npm-all` here, a virtual repository
with a deployment target, or a local repository), not the deployment target (Q-API-180).

GitLab CI publishing. The Publish tab shows the GitLab CI snippet of
[formats/npm.md](formats/npm.md) R-NPM-041 in two variants, each labelled with the client versions
it serves, so the user picks by the client in the job image:

| Variant | Label | ID token | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|
| Native exchange | "npm 11.5.1 and later, pnpm 11 and 12, Yarn 4" | `NPM_ID_TOKEN` with `aud: "npm:<host>"` (here `npm:trove.example.com`); the client exchanges it itself (R-NPM-022) | P1, with R-NPM-022 |
| Generic exchange | "npm 10, pnpm 10 on npm 10, Yarn 1" | `TROVE_ID_TOKEN` with `aud` set to the base URL; a pipeline step exchanges it at `POST /api/v1/auth/oidc/token` ([gitlab-ci-oidc.md](gitlab-ci-oidc.md) R-CI-007), and the job revokes the token as its last step | MVP |

The dialog offers both variants for every installation and never chooses between them by the base
URL's path: `server.base_url` is an origin without a path (R-OPS-005 in
[operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md)), so trove owns the host root
that npm's native exchange posts to ([formats/npm.md](formats/npm.md) Q-NPM-1). Until R-NPM-022
ships, the native variant is not shown.

Acceptance criteria (CI end-to-end, `node:24` container, real token in `TROVE_TOKEN`):

- With the project `.npmrc`, `npm view <package> version` and `npm install <package>` succeed;
  `npm publish` of a fixture to `npm-local` succeeds.
- With `.yarnrc.yml`, `yarn add <package>` (Yarn Berry) succeeds; `pnpm add <package>` succeeds with
  the `.npmrc`.
- The generic-exchange variant, pasted into a GitLab CI job on a `node:22` image whose ID token a
  CI identity mapping accepts, publishes a fixture to `npm-local` and ends with the CI token
  revoked. From P1, the native variant does the same on `node:lts`.

### R-UI-018 · NuGet client instructions
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-025

.NET CLI (`--store-password-in-clear-text` is required on Linux and macOS, where NuGet cannot
encrypt stored passwords):

```shell
dotnet nuget add source "https://trove.example.com/api/nuget/web/nuget-all/v3/index.json" \
  --name trove --username trove --password "${TROVE_TOKEN}" --store-password-in-clear-text
```

The snippets of the UI write the credential part only for a repository that is not anonymously readable, and the fixed user
name `trove`; the exact shapes per client and shell are in [formats/nuget.md](formats/nuget.md) R-NUGET-026 (Q-NUGET-49).

Repository `nuget.config`. `%VAR%` references work on every operating system, and `<clear />`
removes other sources, so every package resolves through trove (the virtual repository includes a
nuget.org remote) and a same-named package on a public source cannot slip in
([nuget.config reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/nuget/reference/nuget-config-file)):

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<configuration>
  <packageSources>
    <clear />
    <add key="trove" value="https://trove.example.com/api/nuget/web/nuget-all/v3/index.json" />
  </packageSources>
  <packageSourceCredentials>
    <trove>
      <add key="Username" value="trove" />
      <add key="ClearTextPassword" value="%TROVE_TOKEN%" />
    </trove>
  </packageSourceCredentials>
</configuration>
```

NuGet CLI: `nuget sources add -Name trove -Source "https://trove.example.com/api/nuget/web/nuget-all/v3/index.json" -Username trove -Password "<token>"`.
Visual Studio: add a package source with name and service-index URL in the NuGet package manager
options; at the credential prompt enter any user name and the token as password.

| Task | Command |
|---|---|
| Install | `dotnet add package <id> --version <version>`; `dotnet restore` |
| Publish | `dotnet nuget push <id>.<version>.nupkg --source "https://trove.example.com/api/nuget/web/nuget-local/v3/index.json" --api-key "${TROVE_TOKEN}"` (the token travels as `X-NuGet-ApiKey`, INV-8; a `.snupkg` next to the package is pushed with it, [formats/nuget.md](formats/nuget.md)) |

The username is not checked (INV-8); the snippets use the fixed name `trove`.

The UI's client table offers three clients for NuGet: `dotnet`, `nuget` (nuget.exe) and `visual-studio` (Q-UI-94). Visual Studio
has a configure and an install snippet and none for publishing.
PowerShellGet and Chocolatey instructions need NuGet v2, which is P2 (INV-14), and are not offered in
the MVP; the `dotnet` and `nuget.exe` commands also come in PowerShell syntax.

Acceptance criteria (CI end-to-end, .NET SDK container, real token in `TROVE_TOKEN`):

- With the generated `nuget.config`, `dotnet restore` of a fixture project that references a package
  from `nuget-local` and one from nuget.org succeeds.
- `dotnet nuget push` of a fixture package to `nuget-local` succeeds, and the package is listed by
  `GET /api/v1/packages?format=nuget`.

### R-UI-019 · Instructions for further formats
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-026

Each format that ships, in whichever phase, ships in that phase its snippet templates (R-API-030), its guide
(R-UI-049) for every class and client it supports, and acceptance commands for its native clients (for example
`docker login`, Maven `settings.xml` with `${env.TROVE_TOKEN}`, `pip` index configuration, `GOPROXY` with `.netrc`,
`helm repo add` and OCI registry login). The guide is not a later step: the conformance kit fails a format with
clients that lacks it (R-ARCH-010 check 8). The setup page and the guides area are data-driven: a new format needs no
new screen, and the guides area offers it as soon as `GET /api/v1/formats` lists it with clients; the setup page still
takes its clients from the UI's table and the translated snippet explanations (Q-UI-70).

Raised from P1 to MVP by the owner's decision of 2026-10-31 (Q-UI-83): the rule binds NuGet in M3 and every later
format. What stays P1 is the list of further formats itself; each brings its templates, its guide and its acceptance
commands when it ships.

Acceptance criteria: per format, on its page; the setup page lists a format as soon as its templates are registered and
the UI's table names its clients, the guides area as soon as the format registers clients; the kit refuses a format
whose guide misses a class or a client.

### R-UI-049 · Guides for every registry variant
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: trove-only

The owner's requirement of 2026-10-31 (Q-UI-83): the UI offers documentation and setup help for every package registry
variant, which is a format × a repository class (local, remote, virtual) × a client (for npm: npm, pnpm, Yarn Berry,
Yarn Classic). A guide tells a developer, accurately for trove as built, what the repository is and how the client
configures, signs in, installs, publishes, changes tags, unpublishes, audits and keeps lockfiles through it, what an
endpoint with exposure rules changes, and what each answer of the protocol means. The text is the format's
(R-ARCH-008 `Guide()`, kit check 8), rendered by the server (R-API-053); the UI adds no format knowledge.

- **Where.** A side bar entry **Guides** in the area Artifacts, route `/guides`
  (`?format=&client=&repository=&class=`); a tab **How to use** on the repository screen (and the same guide below the
  facts of the consumer view) for the repository's class and the client the reader picks; links between the guide and
  the client setup page of R-UI-016 in both directions, carrying the choice (Q-UI-84).
- **Choice.** The guides area offers the formats of `GET /api/v1/formats` that list `clients`, in its order and the
  first preselected, their clients, the readable repositories of the format (virtual first), and, without a
  repository, the format's classes (virtual preselected). A repository opens its guide
  (`GET /api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/{repoKey}/guide`), a class the guide of the format (`GET /api/v1/formats/{format}/guide`),
  whose addresses show `<project>` and `<repository>`.
- **Content.** A contents list (a `nav` landmark) whose links move focus to the section heading without navigating; one
  region per section with its heading; the section's HTML bound like a README (R-UI-008, the same component and its
  finishing pass); the setup snippets of the section with a copy button each (Q-UI-85). The guide's text is the format's
  and English, marked `lang="en"`; the frame of the page is translated (Q-UI-86).
- **Addresses** are the server's (the base URL of the endpoint the page is served from, R-API-053), never the page's
  location (Q-UI-69).
- **Anonymous readers** of anonymously readable repositories get the guide without credential steps: snippets without
  an authentication line and no publishing, tag or unpublish sections.
- Accessibility as R-UI-044: headings in order, landmarks, every control reachable by keyboard.

Acceptance criteria:

- Playwright (`09-guides.spec.ts`): the side bar opens the guides with generic and curl preselected, and offers npm
  with its four clients; the How to use tab of
  a virtual npm repository shows the virtual repository's sections and names its deployment target; its configure
  snippet equals, character for character, the configure snippet the client setup page shows for the same repository
  and client with "Reference an environment variable"; the setup page links back to the same guide; axe finds no
  serious or critical violation (E2.13, Q-UI-87).
- For every class and client of npm the guide has the sections `what`, `configure`, `authenticate`, `install` and
  `troubleshooting` (kit check 8), and every code its troubleshooting table names is a code of the problem catalog,
  under the status trove answers it with (`TestR_UI_049_TheTroubleshootingCodesAreTroves`).

### R-UI-050 · Help area and the manual
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: trove-only

The owner's requirement of 2026-11-01: a "?" at the top right behind which the user and administrator documentation of
trove is found, delivered by the frontend. The text is the manual of R-API-054; the UI renders no Markdown.

- **Entry.** The Documentation link of the top bar (R-UI-002) links to the manual page of the current screen: the longest route
  prefix of `HELP_TOPICS` in [core/help-topics.ts](../../web/src/app/core/help-topics.ts) (for example `/admin/endpoints`
  to the administrator guide's endpoints page), or the overview `/help` where none matches (Q-UI-90). The lint
  (`web/scripts/check-rules.mjs`) fails when a page named there is not a file of `docs/manual/`.
- **Overview** (`/help`): both guides with every page's title and summary, each a link to the page, and a link to the
  guides of R-UI-049 for the commands of a package client. For a plain user (R-UI-067) the administrator guide is a closed
  section at the end (Q-UI-324).
- **Page** (`/help/<section>/<page>`): the contents of both guides beside the page with the current page marked
  (`aria-current`), the page title as the heading and the document title, "On this page" from the page's headings, the
  page's HTML bound like a README (R-UI-008, the same component and finishing pass), and links to the previous and the
  next page. A link of the text to another page stays a link and opens the page in the application (a modified click
  opens it in a new tab through the browser); a fragment in the address scrolls to its heading. On narrow content the
  contents give way to a link back to the overview.
- The manual's text is English and marked `lang="en"`; the frame is translated (Q-UI-86). The area sits behind the same
  guard as the guides: signed-in callers, anonymous ones while `publicContent` is true.
- **Width** (Q-UI-97). The page takes the width of its column, which grows with the viewport; the prose keeps a measure
  of 80 characters, tables and code use the full width. A table sits in a container of its own that scrolls sideways
  when it is wider; its cells break at spaces only, code in a cell stays whole, and the first column has a minimum width.
- Accessibility as R-UI-044: one `h1`, landmarks for the contents, "On this page" and the page navigation.

Acceptance criteria:

- The Documentation link leads to `/help/admin/endpoints` on the endpoints screen, to `/help/user/files` on the file browser,
  to `/help/admin/operations` on the jobs screen and to `/help` on the signed-out screen (`app.spec.ts`).
- The overview lists both guides with every page linked; a page shows its title, its headings, the contents and its
  neighbours; a link to another page navigates in the application to that page and heading, a link inside the page
  scrolls; an unknown page and a failed read show the error with a retry; axe finds no serious or critical violation
  ([help.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/help/help.spec.ts), `app.routes.spec.ts` for both routes).
- A table of the manual sits in a focusable `.readme-table` container, and wrapping twice does not nest
  ([package-readme.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/packages/package-readme.spec.ts), help.spec.ts).

### R-UI-020 · Repository list
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-030, REPO-007

- The columns come from the job of the list's kind of user (R-UI-067, [Q-UI-330](#q-ui-330--a-list-takes-its-columns-from-the-job-of-its-kind-of-user-the-important-properties-are-columns-and-the-address-takes-no-more-than-its-share)); under the key stands only its
  description ([Q-UI-302](#q-ui-302--the-repository-list-names-a-repository-by-key-and-description-in-its-first-column-and-puts-the-rows-actions-in-a-menu)), every other property is a column, and below 48 rem of the list's width the rows stack (Q-UI-306).
  - The project's own list (`/projects/{project}/repositories`, Q-UI-129), the plain user's (find a repository, copy its

    address** (the address field, one width for the column: what is left after the repository's 20 rem and the least widths of

    whose name and tooltip carry the client address, beside the menu, which has **Copy client address** too. The address is no
    field there. A column **Visibility** (T-18) fits beside them at 1440 px.
- Filters in the filter panel: project, format, class, text, disabled only. The list is ordered by key; the API takes
  no `sort` parameter yet, so the table has no sort control (sorting by creation arrives with the
  API, and the creation time with the summary, Q-UI-18). "Recently opened" (browser storage, 20) is the start page's: neither
  list shows it ([Q-UI-329](#q-ui-329--recently-opened-is-the-start-pages-only-the-admin-areas-repository-list-leaves-it-out-too)); a project's list says under its heading what the project is and, to a plain user,

  from M4b vulnerabilities (local and remote repositories of a format with the vulnerability
  adapter: the repository's view of the report, `/projects/<projectKey>/vulnerabilities?repository=<projectKey>/<repoKey>`,
  [vulnerability-scanning.md](vulnerability-scanning.md) R-VULN-022),
  move to another project (for a caller who holds `repositories:write-config` or is Owner of both projects; R-REPO-060),
  delete. Delete requires typing the key, offers the `detach` choice of

### R-UI-021 · Repository creation wizard and edit form
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-031

- Steps: format, class, basic settings, class-specific settings, review. The format comes first
  because some features are technically impossible for some formats (Q-UI-112). The basic settings hold the artifacts'
  visibility level (R-UI-055). The project is chosen in the basic
  settings, from the projects in which the caller may create repositories (every project for
  `repositories:write-config`, the projects it owns otherwise); inside a project (`/projects/{project}/repositories/new`) the
  project is given, shown as text and not chosen. It is read-only on the edit form, where a move to another project is its
  own action (R-UI-020). After the create the wizard opens the new repository's content page (R-UI-052); its settings are `/projects/{project}/repositories/{key}/settings`.
- The format step is a grid of tiles from `GET /api/v1/formats`, each with the format's icon (its owner's logo where
  the owner's terms allow it, else the neutral package glyph, Q-UI-225) and its
  name, under a search field ("Search by package type") that filters the tiles by name, a title and
  a one-line hint. Only the formats the installation has appear. The grid is a single-choice listbox
  of `@angular/aria` (R-UI-001, Q-UI-1): one tab stop, arrow keys, Home and End, Enter or Space to
  choose, one click to choose, a visible focus ring (Q-UI-114, Q-UI-115). Next is disabled until a
  format is chosen.
- The class step offers only the classes in the chosen format's `classes` in
  `GET /api/v1/formats`. Those `classes` are generated from each format's `Descriptor().Classes`
  (R-ARCH-008, R-ARCH-010 in [architecture.md](architecture.md)); the UI holds no list of classes
  per format of its own (FMT-001). A class the format lacks is shown disabled with one sentence of
  reason, and cannot be chosen (Q-UI-113). Going back to the format step and choosing another format
  keeps the class when the new format has it, clears it when not, and starts the format settings and
  the mirror section afresh (Q-UI-116). A create that names a class the format lacks still fails on
  the server with 422.
- Settings forms render from the format's settings JSON Schema (R-ARCH-004, R-ARCH-008) into the
  format member of the repository document that is named after the format (`npm`, `nuget`;
  [repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-004), never into a generic
  `formatSettings` member. A format adds a panel only for interactions a schema cannot express.
  The form shows the members whose `x-trove-classes` contain the class, in the class-specific step
  of the wizard and on a tab of the edit form, and writes a setting only where it differs from the
  schema's default (Q-UI-78 to Q-UI-81).
- NuGet local repositories: the settings view, in the wizard's review and on the edit form, shows
  the effective `nuget.deleteMode`, `unlist` (the default) or `delete`, with one sentence on what
  `dotnet nuget delete` and `nuget delete` do in this repository: unlist the version, or delete it
  for good with a tombstone ([formats/nuget.md](formats/nuget.md) R-NUGET-007). Deletes through
  the UI and the management API are hard deletes whatever the mode (R-NUGET-007).
- A setting that is an array of strings is a **list control** (Q-UI-200): one entry per line, or, when its items are an enum, one
  checkbox per option; an empty list leaves the setting to its default. A string setting that may be longer than 1 KiB (a pasted key
  block) is an area. A read-only member of the document that is not in the schema (`deb.upstreamKeyFingerprints`) is shown by the
  format's own panel and never written back.
- Ansible Galaxy repositories ([formats/ansible.md](formats/ansible.md) R-ANS-009, R-ANS-012, R-ANS-026): the operations `listAnsibleImportTasks`
  (`read`; the import tasks of a local repository, of the deployment target for a virtual one, 405 `not_applicable` for a remote one),
  `listAnsibleTombstones` and `clearAnsibleTombstone` (`manage`; local only, the clearing writes the journaled event
  `ansible.tombstone.cleared`) are in `api/openapi.yaml` and answer 501 `ansible_not_implemented` until the local class builds them; the
  `ansible` member of the repository document holds `authUrl` and `clientId` for remote repositories.
- Ansible Galaxy documentation ([formats/ansible.md](formats/ansible.md) R-ANS-033 to R-ANS-037): the three operations above, and `listAnsibleImportTasks` gains the optional query parameters `package` and `version` (the Import log tab of a version, Q-UI-240).
- Debian (APT) repositories ([formats/debian.md](formats/debian.md) R-DEB-030, Q-DEB-100 to Q-DEB-102): a local or virtual repository
  has the tabs **Signing keys** (the keys in every state with fingerprint in groups of four, state in words, type, origin, times and
  the public certificate; **Generate a next key**, **Import a key** with a write-only secret key and passphrase, **Promote**,
  **Remove**, **Reinstate** and **Confirm retirement**; a private key is never shown) and **Index** (the state of each suite and
  **Rebuild all indexes**). The calls act at once and are not part of "Save changes"; the destructive ones ask first.
- Key: live check of the INV-5 pattern and of availability within the chosen project (a `GET` of
  `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/{repoKey}` answering 404); the same key may exist in another project.
- Remote: an **Upstream** section, in the class-specific step of the wizard above the format's settings and on a tab
  **Upstream** of the edit form (Q-UI-122): the upstream URL with the format's preset (`defaultUpstreamUrl`:
  `https://registry.npmjs.org/`, `https://api.nuget.org/v3/index.json`; the wizard starts with it, an empty field means it, and a
  format without one needs the URL), the authentication (none, username and password, bearer token) with a write-only password
  (Q-UI-123), the metadata and negative cache periods with the format's defaults (`defaultMetadataTtlSeconds`,
  `defaultNotFoundTtlSeconds`), the offline switch (INV-11), and "Test connection" (`POST /api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/upstream-tests`) with the
  result inline, in words (Q-UI-124). A member is written only where it differs from its default (Q-UI-80); the rest of the
  `remote` section (extra hosts, limits, integrity, `sourceNetwork`, the other cache members) is set through the API.
- Virtual: member editor (R-UI-022) and default deployment target.
- From phase 6b, on remote repositories of a format whose upstream can be discovered (`mirror: true` in
  `GET /api/v1/formats`, from the format's registration; the UI holds no list of such formats): a **Mirror**
  section with the mode (`pullThrough` or `mirror`) and the members of `remote.mirror`
  ([repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-050), the warning or refusal `mirror_unbounded` at the
  mode with the sentence of R-REPO-052, and for an Owner without `repositories:write-config` the section read-only except
  **Pause** and **Turn off** (Q-REPO-142). The section is in the wizard's class-specific step and on the edit form's tab **Mirror**
  (Q-UI-117); the members show in mode `mirror` and are written only where they differ from their defaults, and a create in
  mode `pullThrough` writes no `remote` member; the early notice at the mode applies the server's bound rule to the upstream
  URL entered and the server decides (Q-UI-118, Q-UI-122). On the edit form of a remote stored in mode `mirror`, the **Mirror**
  tab shows, above the settings (Q-UI-119), the status of `GET /api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/{repoKey}/mirror`: the state in words (off,
  paused, scheduled, running, waiting, bound reached, failing; green only for a scheduled mirror after a complete pass), the pass
  in progress with its counts and its job, the last complete pass, the next pass, the last error, the rate-limit waits and the
  bound. While a pass is in progress (`running`, `waiting`) the status is read again every 5 s, and no longer once the tab is
  left. A caller who may change the repository (the permission of Save, Q-UI-120) has **Pause** and **Resume**, which `PATCH`
  `remote.mirror.paused` with `If-Match` and nothing else of the form (a 412 opens the conflict dialog of R-UI-042), and **Run a
  pass now** (`POST …/mirror/run`, and **Run a full pass** from its menu), which shows the queued job with a link to the jobs of
  the kind `mirror-pass`; `409 mirror_pass_running` shows the running job instead of an error, and `mirror_off` and
  `mirror_paused` are shown in words (Q-UI-104, Q-UI-105, Q-UI-121).
- From M4b, on local and remote repositories of a format with the vulnerability adapter: the
  `vulnerabilities` member ([vulnerability-scanning.md](vulnerability-scanning.md) R-VULN-002), and
  on the edit form a link to the repository's view of the vulnerability report (R-VULN-022).
- Review: summary plus "Show as API request" with the JSON body and the equivalent `curl` command
  (INV-17).
- Create sends the `Idempotency-Key` generated when the wizard opened.
- Edit form: the same sections as tabs; key, class and format read-only; save sends PATCH with
  `If-Match`; 412 opens the conflict dialog (R-UI-042); unsaved changes are guarded on navigation. For a
  format with clients, a tab **How to use** shows the repository's guide (R-UI-049).
- Server field errors (`errors[].pointer`) are shown at their fields and in an error summary.

Acceptance criteria:

- Creating `npm-remote` with the npm preset and "Test connection" succeeds; double-clicking "Create"
  creates one repository.
- Saving an edit after another administrator saved first opens the conflict dialog.
- With a test build that registers a format whose `Classes` lack `Virtual`, choosing that format
  does not offer the class `virtual`, or shows it disabled with the reason, and `local` can be
  chosen. Choosing the class `virtual` for npm, going back and choosing that format leaves no
  class chosen.
- The format step lists the installed formats as tiles, typing `nu` in the search field leaves the
  NuGet tile, and the tiles can be reached, moved over and chosen with the keyboard alone.
- A remote npm repository in the wizard shows the Upstream section with the preset URL, authentication none, empty periods
  (their defaults in the hints) and the offline switch off, and a create that changes none of them sends no `remote` member.
  A create with another URL, username and password and a metadata period sends
  `remote: {url, authMode: "basic", username, password: {value}, cache: {metadataTtlSeconds}}` and nothing else of `remote`;
  the value of the password is nowhere on the page, in the request shown in the review, in browser storage or in a read of the
  repository, which shows `password: {set: true}`. On the edit form its field is empty and says that one is stored, and a save of
  another member does not touch it. "Test connection" posts the unsaved section and shows the answer: reachable and the credentials
  accepted, or the reason of an upstream that could not be reached.
- A remote npm repository in the wizard shows the Mirror section in mode pull-through; choosing
  mirror shows its members with their defaults, and a create with only `intervalSeconds` changed
  sends `remote: {mode: "mirror", mirror: {intervalSeconds: …}}` and nothing else of `remote`.
  An Owner of the project without `repositories:write-config` sees the section read-only except Pause and Turn off.
- The Mirror tab of a remote stored in mode `mirror` shows the state and the facts of `GET …/mirror`; **Pause** sends
  `{"remote": {"mirror": {"paused": true}}}` with the loaded `If-Match` and the state reads Paused, **Resume** reverts it, a
  caller who neither holds `repositories:write-config` nor is Owner of the project sees the status and no button, and **Run a
  pass now** answers with the job of its 202 or, after a 409 `mirror_pass_running`, with the running job. While the state is
  running or waiting the status is read every 5 s, and no read follows once another tab is open.
- The edit form of `nuget-local` without a `nuget.deleteMode` shows "unlist"; after
  `PATCH /api/v1/projects/web/repositories/nuget-local` with `If-Match` and `{"nuget": {"deleteMode": "delete"}}`
  it shows "delete".
- Creating a local npm repository in the wizard with `latestGuard` turned off stores
  `{"npm": {"latestGuard": false}}`; turning it on again on the edit form removes the `npm` member,
  and the wizard offers no `latestGuard` for a virtual repository.

### R-UI-022 · Virtual repository member editor
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-032

- Two lists: available (repositories of the virtual repository's own project and the same format, excluding the
  repository itself and anything that would create a cycle; a virtual repository never lists a repository of another
  project, [Q-REPO-212](repositories-and-proxy.md#q-repo-212--a-repository-is-addressed-inside-its-project-and-no-repository-is-shared))
  and selected (ordered). Buttons Add, Remove, Move up, Move down, Move to top work with
  keyboard and single pointer (WCAG 2.5.7); drag and drop is an optional extra. Both lists are
  listboxes of `@angular/aria` (R-UI-001, Q-UI-1).
- An "Effective resolution order" view flattens nested virtual repositories per
  [repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md); `GET …/resolution?path=` explains a sample
  path.
- Default deployment target: picker over the selected local repositories, or none.
- A live region announces each change ("npm-remote moved to position 2 of 3").
- A cycle reported by the server (422 with pointer) is shown on the offending member.

Acceptance criteria:

- With the keyboard only, a user adds two members, reorders them and saves; the API shows that order.

Built as [Q-UI-210](#q-ui-210--the-member-editor-is-a-tab-with-its-own-save-offers-what-the-api-accepts-and-explains-the-saved-order); the journey is `R-UI-022` in [18-virtual-members.spec.ts](../../web/e2e/tests/18-virtual-members.spec.ts).

### R-UI-023 · Quick repository setup
Priority: **P1** · Covers: UI-033, REPO-008

Administrators and the project's Owners pick a project, formats and a prefix; the preview shows the keys that
`POST /api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/quick-setup` ([repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md))
will create in the project (local, remote with the public upstream preset, virtual over both), then creates them in
one request and offers client setup for the virtual repository.

Acceptance criteria:

- Quick setup for npm with prefix `team-a` creates the three repositories of the owner's naming
  rule, and `npm install` through the virtual one fetches a public package.

### R-UI-024 · Users and system roles
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-035, UI-036

- List: username, display name, email, origin (identity provider, administrator-created, SCIM,
  break-glass), status, the badge External (R-UI-056), last login; filters text, status, origin, group, administrator,
  external (filter panel); the user name column sorts (`sort=username`, `-username`).
- Detail ([Q-UI-223](#q-ui-223--the-user-the-endpoint-and-the-service-account-and-group-lists-follow-the-guide)): display name and email edited in place with "Save changes" (an administrator's correction lasts until the next login), ID and origin as
  read-only fields; identities (provider and subject, read-only and copyable); attributes from the identity
  provider, read-only and labelled as such; status with "Disable" (choice to revoke tokens) and
  "Enable"; group memberships (identity-provider-sourced read-only with a badge, manual ones
  editable); system roles through role bindings (R-API-033) with the last-administrator guard; the
  user's tokens (a quiet section **Tokens** like the page's others, open while the user holds a token, [Q-UI-333](#q-ui-333--a-pages-sections-are-quiet-disclosures-tokens-too-open-while-there-is-a-token-the-profile-follows); **Revoke all
  tokens** a danger button in the page's section **Advanced**, last on the page) and sessions (list, end all); "Explain permissions" (P1); "Audit"
  (audit log filtered on this actor). The break-glass account shows its lock state and "Unlock".
- "Add user" pre-provisions a user linked to an identity-provider identity (R-API-031). No password
  fields exist.
- `/admin/roles` lists the fixed roles of `GET /api/v1/roles` with their bindings and offers bind
  and unbind.

Acceptance criteria:

- Disabling a user with "revoke tokens" makes that user's API calls with a token fail with 401 on
  every replica within 2 s (R-API-052), and the audit log shows the change.

### R-UI-025 · Groups
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-037

- List: name, description, origin, member count; filters name and origin (filter panel); the name
  column sorts (`sort=name`, `-name`).
- Editor: name (rename allowed where the owner allows it), description, auto-join, members with
  their sources (manual, identity provider, SCIM) where only manual ones are editable, role bindings
