Acceptance criteria:

- Adding a manual member through the editor makes `GET /api/v1/groups/{name}/members` list the user
  with source `manual`.

### R-UI-026 · Service accounts
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: trove-only

- List and editor: project (none for an account of no project), name, description, owners (P1), groups (accounts of
  no project only: a project's account is never a group member), status with disable and enable. The list of the admin
  area is the instance-wide list with a project column; a project's screen (R-UI-041) lists the project's accounts.
  A name is unique within its project, or among the accounts of no project, and is shown as `sa:<projectKey>/<name>`
  or `sa:<name>` ([Q-AUTHZ-209](authorization.md#q-authz-209--a-projects-policies-and-service-accounts-are-named-within-the-project-administrators-keep-instance-wide-ones)).
- Tokens, a quiet section of the page open while the account holds a token
  ([Q-UI-333](#q-ui-333--a-pages-sections-are-quiet-disclosures-tokens-too-open-while-there-is-a-token-the-profile-follows)):
  issue (scope and expiry as in R-UI-029, one-time display, recent authentication), list, revoke one, and revoke all in the
  page's section **Advanced**. The server lets the administrator role, and for a project's account the project's Owners, issue
  and rotate the tokens of a service account ([identity-and-authentication.md](identity-and-authentication.md)
  R-AUTH-027, R-AUTH-030, [authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-026); the tab offers **Create token** and
  **Rotate** to those callers only (`authz/me` `roles` and `projects`), not to a holder of `identities:write` alone,
  who would get 403. An Owner's form offers no non-expiring lifetime, no `admin` and no `system` item. Revoking follows
  `tokens:revoke` or the role `owner`.
- The token form offers the binding to endpoints where the caller may read them (Q-UI-91). It offers **Administrator: everything on this installation**
  to a caller with the administrator role for an account of no project that holds the role itself (`ServiceAccount.isAdmin`); the choice sends
  `{"inherit": true, "admin": true}` ([Q-UI-220](#q-ui-220--the-form-of-a-service-account-token-offers-the-administrator-choice-for-an-account-that-holds-the-role)).
- The page is one column, as the style guide's settings pages are ([Q-UI-222](#q-ui-222--which-settings-pages-are-one-column-now-and-what-a-sections-save-button-is-called)):
  the description and the ID at the top with **Save changes**, **Details** (status, the administrator role, created) and **Advanced** (disable or enable, delete) as sections.
- A hint explains when to use one: CI systems without OIDC exchange, long-running automation.

Acceptance criteria:

- A token issued on the Tokens tab authenticates `npm view` against a repository the service account
  may read.

### R-UI-027 · Permission policy list and editor
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-039, UI-040

- List: project (none for a policy of no project), name, description, principal summary ("3 groups, 1 CI mapping"),
  resources summary, actions; filters by principal (picker), repository and project. The list of the admin area is the
  instance-wide list; a project's screen (R-UI-041) lists the project's policies.
- Layout (Q-UI-4): one page for create and edit, no step-by-step wizard. The sections run down the
  left with an in-page table of contents; the preview panel is a sticky right column while the
  content area is at least 960 CSS px wide and a collapsible region above the save bar when it is
  narrower. The explainer (R-UI-028, P1) is its own screen, reached from the editor through "Test
  this policy" (saved policies only, once the explainer ships), which opens it in a new tab with the policy's first principal and
  repository filled in, so the draft in the editor stays untouched.
- Editor sections, following the policy model of
  [authorization.md](authorization.md): general (name on create only, description); principals
  (users, groups, service accounts, CI identity mappings) through
  searchable pickers; resources with a live "covers 4 repositories" preview, whose selectors take the form of the
  policy's context: `<projectGlob>/<keyGlob>[:<format>]` or a class for a policy of no project, bare keys, key globs
  and classes of the project for a project's policy ([authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-004,
  [Q-AUTHZ-216](authorization.md#q-authz-216--repository-selectors-name-the-project-in-instance-contexts-and-a-bare-key-inside-a-project)); include and exclude
  patterns of package names and paths with syntax help and a tester field ("Does `@team-a/ui` match?") in a closed section
  **Limit to package names or paths**, open when one of them holds a value (details on demand); actions with a one-line
  explanation each. Every section is the quiet disclosure of Q-UI-322.
- Preview panel fed by `POST /api/v1/authz/validate-policy` (debounced 500 ms): covered repositories,
  errors, warnings. An error of a field shows once the field holds a value or a save was tried, as next to the field, and names
  the field by its label ("Name: …"), never its JSON pointer. "Try it" answers from the draft alone; its **Explain** is a
  secondary button that says what is missing when a principal or a repository is not named yet; the answer adds what the repository's visibility level gives the principal
  (`internal` covers users who are not external, never service accounts, CI identities or anonymous; R-AUTHZ-030,
  R-AUTHZ-035), and says so.
- The one-line help of the actions says what each covers; `manage` is the administration of content
  (package owners, the override of the shadowing check, namespace claims, cache operations), and
  the settings of a repository need the capability `repositories:write-config`.
- Save shows a diff against the loaded revision (principals, resources and actions added or removed),
  then sends PUT with `If-Match`; recent authentication is handled as in R-UI-042.
- Delegated managers (P1) see only the entries the API lets them change.

Acceptance criteria:

- Creating the policy of R-API-033's acceptance test through the editor yields the same stored
  document as creating it through the API.
- The diff before saving lists exactly the added principal when only one was added.

### R-UI-028 · Effective-permission explainer
Priority: **P1** · Covers: IAM-030

- `/admin/permissions/explain` for callers with `policies:read`; the item details tab of R-UI-010
  for repository managers.
- Question form: "Why can [principal] [action] on [repository] [path or package]?", principal kinds
  user, group, service account and CI identity mapping, or a token ID.
- Answer from `POST /api/v1/authz/explain` (R-API-034):
  - decision as icon plus text ("Allowed" or "Denied"), never colour alone, with the reason code;
  - the trace steps as an ordered list (for example: grant from policy `team-web-publish` via group
    `team-web` → ownership check → denied, owned by project 4711), each step linking to the policy,
    mapping or owner list it names;
  - the scope intersection when a token was given.
- "Copy as text" and "Copy as JSON" for support tickets.
- Entry points: user and group details, the policy editor ("Test this policy"), the no-access state
  (R-UI-003), the claim tester.

Acceptance criteria:

- For the deny example of R-AUTHZ-024, the screen names the ownership step and its owners.
- A screen reader reads the steps as an ordered list in evaluation order.

### R-UI-029 · Profile, personal tokens and sessions
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-053, AUTHN-039, AUTHN-040

- Profile (`GET /api/v1/users/me`): one column ([Q-UI-333](#q-ui-333--a-pages-sections-are-quiet-disclosures-tokens-too-open-while-there-is-a-token-the-profile-follows)): the avatar, the identity as read-only fields (from the identity
  provider), then the quiet sections **Preferences** (language, theme, keyboard shortcuts; R-API-021; open), **Groups** with
  source (open while the group claim notice stands) and **System roles**.
- Missing group claim (R-AUTH-008 in [identity-and-authentication.md](identity-and-authentication.md)):
  while the record carries `groupClaimMissing` (`{"provider", "reason"}`), a notice next to the
  groups names the provider and the reason (`absent`, `wrong_type` or `overage`). It says that the
  last login through that provider carried no usable group claim, so the groups synchronized from
  it may be missing (the default `clear` removes them) and the identity provider's group mapping
  needs an administrator. The notice is `role="status"` text, not a dialog, and disappears after a
  login that delivers the claim.
- What the profile does not have (settles UI-053's open point on password changes): no unlock step,
  because the session already proves the login (R-AUTH-017 in
  [identity-and-authentication.md](identity-and-authentication.md)); no password section, because
  users have no password in trove (INV-7) and the break-glass password is changed by replacing its
  Kubernetes Secret (R-AUTH-014); no editable email or display name, because both come from the
  identity provider at every login (R-AUTH-016 maps the catalog's "profile updatable" option to
  this). Nobody changes a password through trove. An administrator's correction of email or
  display name through `PATCH /api/v1/users/{username}` (R-API-031) lasts until the user's next
  login. SSH keys and linked accounts are P2 on the identity page and not shown.
- The profile's three pages (Profile, Personal tokens, Sessions) have the shared page header and are the tab strip of links
  under it; **Create token** and **End all other sessions** are the header's actions (Q-UI-307, UI-A-20). An empty token list
  says what is missing: "No active tokens." while the revoked and expired ones are hidden, "No tokens yet." with them (the
  administrator's filtered list keeps "No tokens match.").
- Personal tokens: list with the token (description and hint), scope summary, expires and last used, and, from 64 rem of the
  list, created and created via; the row ends with **Revoke** and a quiet **Rotate**, or the state of a token that is no longer
  active ([Q-UI-332](#q-ui-332--a-token-list-shows-token-scope-expiry-last-use-and-its-action-created-and-created-via-give-way-first)); tokens
  expiring within 7 days are marked, and a token with `admin: true` whose owner does not hold the administrator role now says that
  its administrator rights are inactive. Create dialog: description (required), expiry (presets and a
  custom date, bounded by R-AUTH-040), scope (three choices, Q-UI-213: administrator rights, only for a caller who holds the
  administrator role; all repository permissions of the owner without administration, the preselected one; or restricted to
  repositories and actions; grammar of R-AUTH-024) and, for a caller with `endpoints:read`, the endpoints the token
  is bound to (Q-UI-91). Recent authentication applies. The result is shown once with a
  copy button and the notice that it cannot be shown again. Revoke and rotate with confirmation;
  rotate is P1 and, like creation, needs recent authentication (R-AUTH-030).
- Sessions (`/api/v1/users/me/sessions`): list with created, last seen, address, user agent and
  "this session"; end one, or end all others.

Acceptance criteria:

- A created token works in `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer …" "$TROVE_URL/api/v1/auth/whoami"`;
  reopening the profile never shows it again; revoking it makes the same call answer 401 on every
  replica within 2 s (R-API-052).
- Ending all other sessions signs out a second browser.
- The profile page contains no password field, no unlock control and no editable email or display
  name; after the identity provider changes the user's email, the next login shows the new value.
- After a login whose ID token and userinfo carry no group claim, the profile shows the notice with
  the provider and `absent`; after a later login that carries the claim, the notice is gone.

### R-UI-030 · Token administration
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-041, TOK-026

- All tokens (`tokens:read`): the token (description and hint, which names its type), owner, scope, expires, last used, and
  **Revoke** or the state of a token that is no longer active; below 64 rem of the list the rows stack ([Q-UI-332](#q-ui-332--a-token-list-shows-token-scope-expiry-last-use-and-its-action-created-and-created-via-give-way-first)); filters type,
  owner, state, expiring before, unused since; revoke single and selected
  with confirmation. An active token with `admin: true` whose owner does not hold the administrator role says that its
  administrator rights are inactive (`Token.ownerIsAdmin`, [Q-UI-221](#q-ui-221--the-token-administration-marks-administrator-tokens-whose-owner-no-longer-holds-the-role)).
- CI tokens come from `/api/v1/ci/issuances` with job context (project, pipeline, job, mapping) and
  "Revoke matching" by project or pipeline.
- "Revoke by value": a field to paste a leaked token; the value is sent once to
  `POST /api/v1/tokens/revoke` and cleared. The screen says only what the answer supports (Q-UI-92):
  after a `200` (administrator) which token of which owner was revoked, after the empty `202`
  that the request was accepted and that the answer does not say whether the value was a token.

Acceptance criteria:

- Filtering "unused since 90 days" lists a token never used since its creation 91 days ago (test
  clock).

### R-UI-031 · Authentication settings
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-043

`/admin/settings/auth` (the sidebar's **Settings › Authentication**, Q-UI-326) renders `GET /api/v1/settings/auth`: **New users are external** (`newUsersExternal`, a checkbox with
the sentence "Users created from now on start as external users; existing users keep their flag.", R-AUTH-044), token default
and maximum lifetimes per token type, expiry notices, and the read-only status block (providers and discovery state, break-glass state, session
timeouts, client switches including Basic, the command-line login poll binding mode, SCIM state).
YAML-pinned and ceiling-bounded values show their source. Hiding unauthorized resources
(`authz.hide_existence`) is shown read-only. Save sends `PATCH` with `If-Match`; recent
authentication applies. The page is one column ([Q-UI-222](#q-ui-222--which-settings-pages-are-one-column-now-and-what-a-sections-save-button-is-called)):
**New users are external** is open at the top, the token lifetimes and the read-only status are sections, and each group with a
save button sends the members of its own group only. Who may read without signing in is the visibility of the general settings
(R-UI-053).

The status block shows the two poll-binding warnings that the answer carries (R-AUTH-034,
R-AUTH-040 in [identity-and-authentication.md](identity-and-authentication.md)) as warnings next to
the mode, each with icon and text:

- mode `off`: any poll of an approved `npm login` receives the token, wherever it comes from;
- mode not `off` while `server.trusted_proxies` is empty: behind an edge proxy every poll carries
  the proxy's address, so the binding cannot tell the user's network from anyone else's.

Acceptance criteria:

- Ticking **New users are external** and saving makes the next user who signs in for the first time an external user.
- With the default poll binding and an empty `server.trusted_proxies`, the screen shows the
  trusted-proxy warning; with `poll_binding.mode: off`, it shows the `off` warning.

### R-UI-032 · Sign-in protection and public content
Priority: **P1** · Covers: UI-038, UI-042

- Break-glass lockout state and threshold (read-only, R-AUTH-038) with "Unlock".
- A summary of what anyone can read without signing in: the `publicObjects` of `GET /api/v1/settings/visibility` (R-API-056),
  linked to the general settings' Visibility section (R-UI-053).
- Multi-factor authentication, password expiry and password rules belong to the identity provider
  (INV-7); the screen says so instead of offering controls.

Acceptance criteria:

- After the configured number of failed break-glass logins the account shows as locked, and
  "Unlock" unlocks it.

### R-UI-033 · General settings
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-044

`/admin/settings/general` (the sidebar's **Settings › General**, where `/admin/settings` leads, Q-UI-326) shows the public base URL and its source (`GET /api/v1/system/info`,
read-only field, R-OPS-005) at the top, then the visibility (R-UI-053), the banner and the maintenance mode as sections with a **Save changes** each
([Q-UI-222](#q-ui-222--which-settings-pages-are-one-column-now-and-what-a-sections-save-button-is-called)); the maintenance section opens by
itself while the mode is on. The banner is `/api/v1/system/banner` (enabled, severity, plain text) and the

Acceptance criteria:

- An enabled banner appears on every screen for every user within one minute after saving.

Built as [Q-UI-211](#q-ui-211--general-settings-save-the-banner-and-the-mode-separately-ask-before-read-only-and-the-shell-reads-both-every-30-seconds); the journey is `R-UI-033` in [19-general-settings.spec.ts](../../web/e2e/tests/19-general-settings.spec.ts).

### R-UI-034 · Storage and proxy settings
Priority: **P1** · Covers: UI-045

`/admin/settings/storage` renders `/api/v1/settings/storage` (trash can and the other runtime
storage settings of [storage.md](storage.md)) and the global offline mode of
`/api/v1/system/proxy-offline` (confirmation: every remote repository stops fetching), and links to
outbound proxies and client certificates ([repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md)).
The UI-only limits (`ui.deploy.max_upload_bytes`, `ui.browser.page_size`) are shown read-only.

Acceptance criteria:

- With offline mode on, `npm view` of an uncached public package through `npm-remote` fails while
  cached packages still install.

### R-UI-035 · CI identity
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-049, CIOIDC-024

- Issuers: name, type, issuer URL, audiences, number of mappings, key status (last fetch or error)
  with "Refresh keys".
- Issuer editor per [gitlab-ci-oidc.md](gitlab-ci-oidc.md); creation validates discovery and keys.
- Mappings per issuer in evaluation order, with conditions summary (`namespace_path in [4711]`,
  `ref_protected = true`), grants summary and maximum token lifetime.
- Mapping editor: conditions with suggestions of GitLab claim names (`project_path`,
  `namespace_path`, `ref`, `ref_type`, `ref_protected`, `environment`, `pipeline_source`,
  `user_login`, …); grants, where the policies and the groups are each a text field that suggests the names as they are typed,
  held and saying so while the list loads ([Q-UI-334](#q-ui-334--a-picker-is-one-control-from-the-start-held-while-its-list-loads-and-a-field-is-as-wide-as-its-kind-of-input));
  options; "Test with claims" opens the claim tester prefilled. Warnings returned on save are shown.
- Per mapping, "CI snippet" shows the text of `GET /api/v1/ci/issuers/{issuer}/snippets/gitlab-ci`
  (for a project's mapping `GET /api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/ci/issuers/{issuer}/snippets/gitlab-ci`, which an Owner of the
  project may read) for the chosen format (npm or NuGet) with a copy button. This covers the GitLab counterpart of
  CIOIDC-024 ([GitLab ID tokens](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/secrets/id_token_authentication/)).
- Delegations (P1) and issuances (R-UI-030) are tabs of the issuer.
- An Owner of a project reaches the project's CI mappings from the project (the project route family of
  R-API-035): the mapping list and editor, the claim tester over the project's tier and the issuances of its mappings, with
  the issuers as a read-only choice (Q-CI-26). A mapping's name is unique within the project and the issuer, without a
  prefix, and shown as `ci:<issuer>/<projectKey>/<name>`
  ([Q-AUTHZ-214](authorization.md#q-authz-214--a-projects-ci-mappings-are-named-within-the-project-like-its-policies-and-service-accounts)).
  The editor offers the project's repositories as bare keys and its policies, and no groups. The
  screens and routes are those of [Q-UI-99](#q-ui-99--the-ci-screens-sit-under-identity-and-a-projects-ci-screens-are-the-same-components-under-the-project);
  the bulk revoke and the detail of an issuance are Q-UI-100; the bulk revoke is offered only while every applied filter is one
  the request carries, and the day filters are the local day (Q-UI-102).

Acceptance criteria:

- The snippet copied from the screen, used in a GitLab CI job of project `team-a/ui` on a protected
  branch against the test environment, publishes `@team-a/ui`.

### R-UI-036 · Claim tester
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: trove-only

- `/admin/ci/{issuer}/test`. Input: a text area accepting claims as JSON or a compact JWT.
- A pasted JWT is decoded in the browser (base64url header and payload, no signature check). The UI
  replaces the text with the pretty-printed claims, discards the token, and states that only the
  claims are used. If `exp` lies in the future, a warning says the token is still a valid credential
  until then.
- "Insert sample GitLab claims" fills a realistic payload (`iss`, `aud`, `sub` such as
  `project_path:team-a/app:ref_type:branch:ref:main`, `namespace_id`, `namespace_path`,
  `project_id`, `project_path`, `ref`, `ref_type`, `ref_protected`, `pipeline_source`,
  `environment`, `user_login`, `job_id`, `iat`, `nbf`, `exp`) that the user edits, as JSON or in a
  form view.
- "Evaluate" calls `POST /api/v1/ci/issuers/{issuer}/evaluate` and shows the decision trace of the
  owning page: the matched mapping or "No mapping matches; the exchange would fail", every
  candidate with each condition's expected and actual value and a pass or fail mark (icon plus
  text), the resulting grants with templates resolved, the token that would be issued.
- "Explain resulting permissions" opens the explainer (P1) with the mapping as principal.
- Claims are never put into browser storage and are gone when the route is left.

Acceptance criteria:

- Pasting a signed test ID token shows its claims, and the network log shows that only the claims
  JSON was sent.
- Changing `ref_protected` to `false` switches the result to no match and marks that condition.

### R-UI-037 · Audit log
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: OPS-023

- Table from `GET /api/v1/audit/events`: time, actor, action (a short plain name of its own for every event type of the audit
  registry, in English and German, with the event name under it; an unknown name is shown as sent), target (actor and target wrap in their
  column and are never cut, UI-A-46), outcome,
  source address; filters time range (presets and custom), actor, action, category, project, repository,
  outcome (filter panel); "Load more". The log is always newest first and has no sort control. The action filter suggests every
  prefix of the registry's event types at every level (`ci.*`, `ci.issuer.*`) and every type with its name, from the registry.
- Detail panel with the full event and links to actor and target.
- Times in the user's locale with a UTC toggle; export of the current filter as CSV or JSON Lines
  (`/api/v1/audit/events/export`).

Acceptance criteria:

- Changing a policy and filtering the audit log by it shows the event with the before and after of
  the grants.
- Every event type the registry holds has a name in the audit log: a unit test walks the registry (the fixture
  `audit-actions.fixture.ts`, which a Go test writes from `internal/audit` and keeps current) and fails on a type without one.

### R-UI-038 · System status
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: OPS-008

The screen is MVP because every endpoint it renders from is MVP (the replica registry API of
R-OPS-003, R-OPS-004, the task and job API of R-OPS-019, R-API-049, R-API-050), and it is the only
UI view of the replicas per role, of Valkey, of the backup job, of the scheduled tasks and of the
key ring. It needs a little backend work beyond those endpoints: the registry's `node` and its
nested `valkey` view (R-OPS-003, adopted by R-API-038), the per-role counts and the `backup` block
of the system information (R-OPS-004), and the backup summary of R-API-050, which are MVP because
INV-12 makes roles, drains and Valkey MVP and INV-19 the backup job (Q-UI-7).

- **Admin dashboard** (Q-OPS-175, owner 2026-11-06): the first screen of the admin area at
  `/admin/dashboard`, where `/admin` and the Admin button of the top bar lead a holder of
  `settings:read`. One page of cards: the instance bar (overall state, version, base URL, ready
  replicas, a link to the status screen); one card per role with its ready and live replicas, nodes,
  requests and server errors per second, the worst p95 latency, requests in flight, CPU and memory
  against the limits, summed from the runtime snapshots of R-OPS-003 (lost replicas left out; a role
  without a replica says so); PostgreSQL, Valkey and the object store with their readiness check over
  the live replicas (connected with the slowest `durationMs`, or how many replicas fail), their facts
  of R-OPS-004, and the stored content of the overview; the counts of the overview with links to
  their screens and "New repository" for `repositories:write-config`; and the job queue with the
  active key. It refreshes every 15 seconds with a pause control (WCAG 2.2.2), like the status screen,
  and a failing overview leaves the rest readable with a retry.
- Cards from `GET /api/v1/system/info` and `/system/replicas`: version and revision, with a link to the notices of the
  bundled software of the same build (Q-UI-144); base URL and
  source; the maintenance mode, as a row only while it is not `normal` (Q-OPS-156); database (server version, schema version against the supported ones);
  scheduled tasks (`/system/tasks`: next run, last outcome) with "Run now", which runs on a
  `worker` replica; recent jobs (`/system/jobs`) with cancel.
- **Jobs** (`/admin/system/jobs`, and the recent jobs of the status screen, one table for both): kind, state, enqueued,
  progress, replica, result and cancel. The result cell of a job whose `error` is set shows its `code`, under it the `detail`
  as the server wrote it, untranslated and wrapping at any character, and "Attempt *n* of *m*" with *n* the error's `attempt`
  (the job's `attempt` when the error has none) and *m* the job's `maxAttempts`; an error without a detail shows its code
  alone. The result of a succeeded job is summarised as before (Q-UI-172).
- **Replicas by role** (Q-UI-7, Q-UI-107). One group per role in the order `api`, `packages`, `worker`, taken from the replica's `roles`
  (Q-ARCH-341); a group `web` while a replica of that role is live, during the
  upgrade across the cut ([ha-and-helm.md](ha-and-helm.md) R-HA-064); a replica with roles
  `["all"]` of the development role forms a group `all`, and while one is live it serves every role (R-HA-001), so a group
  `api`, `packages` or `worker` without a replica of its own is left out with its warnings (UI-A-45); within a group, one sub-group per pool of R-HA-062 and per
  endpoint pool, each with its own counts and drain safety,
  headed with the role's `live`, `ready` and `degraded` counts from `replicas.roles` of
  `/system/info`, each listing its replicas with name, node, version, state (`starting`, `ready`,
  `unready`, `draining`, `lost`), heartbeat age and Valkey view. Each group states whether the role
  is drain-safe right now: its `ready` replicas, not `lost`, run on at least two distinct nodes, so
  draining any one node leaves a ready replica (INV-12, R-HA-059). The group shows, with icon and
  text:
  - "Fewer than two ready replicas": a node drain or the loss of one pod interrupts this role;
  - "All ready replicas on one node": a drain of that node interrupts this role (shown only when
    every replica reports a node);
  - for `worker`, "No live worker replica": jobs and scheduled tasks are queued but nothing runs
    them (R-API-015); for a pool, "No live replica in the pool `<pool>`", shown while every row of the pool is `lost` (Q-UI-108: the registry holds the pool's name and not its queues, and a pool whose rows were pruned is not known);
  - for `packages`, "No live packages replica": package clients and raw downloads get no answer from the edge, while the
    UI keeps working (Q-UI-107);
  - while replicas of two versions are live, an information notice naming both versions, because N
    and N-1 run side by side during every rolling upgrade (INV-3); it is not a warning.

  The screen says what it cannot see: disruption budgets, free capacity on other nodes and whether
  the remaining replicas carry the peak (the N + 1 rule of R-HA-059), because trove holds no
  Kubernetes permissions (R-HA-033).
- Readiness checks per replica, from the `checks` of `/system/replicas` (R-OPS-001, R-OPS-003; Q-OPS-2
  in [operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md)), in two kinds that the
  screen never merges:
  - **failing**: a gating check fails (for example `database`, `schema` or `invalidation`) and the
    replica is `unready`; shown as an error with the check names;
  - **degraded**: the replica is `ready` while a reported check fails. Two checks can be in this
    state; `/readyz` answers `200` and lists them under `degraded`, and
    `trove_health_check_passing{name=…}` shows `0`:
    - `objectStore`, after the first readiness unless `health.require_object_store` is set: blob
      requests on that replica fail with a retryable `503`, everything else keeps working;
    - `valkey`, whenever Valkey is unreachable from that replica ([architecture.md](architecture.md)
      R-ARCH-031, [ha-and-helm.md](ha-and-helm.md) Q-HA-13): no request fails, but remote fetches
      are collapsed per replica only, the negative cache is per replica, rate limits fall back to
      per-replica shares of the budget (R-API-016), and changes reach that replica through the
      change-log poll instead of within milliseconds.

    Each is shown as a warning that names the check and says, in the words above, what it means.

  Both kinds use icon plus text, never colour alone (R-UI-044). The page header summarises the
  service as "all ready", "degraded" or "replicas unready"; a role that is not drain-safe adds
  "not drain-safe" to the summary.
- **Valkey card**, from the `valkey` block of `/system/info` (installation facts: mode, primary
  name, configured Sentinels, TLS mode, key prefix and keyspace) and each replica's nested `valkey`
  view of `/system/replicas` (R-API-038): per replica its state with the reason in R-OPS-001's
  vocabulary, each reason translated, the circuit (an open circuit is shown as such), the primary
  address, the reachable against the configured Sentinels and the server version. The card
  summarises with icon and text:
  - "Available on every replica", or "Degraded on k of n replicas" with the reasons, where k is
    `valkey.degradedReplicas` and n is `replicas.live`;
  - "Replicas disagree about the primary" when replicas whose `valkey.state` is `available` report
    different `valkey.primary` addresses for longer than `valkey.sentinel.refresh_interval` plus
    one heartbeat: a replica bound to a demoted primary, the case R-ARCH-031's reconciliation
    bounds;
  - "Sentinels unreachable" when a replica's `valkey.sentinelsReachable` is below a majority of its
    `valkey.sentinelsConfigured`, the condition on which `TroveValkeySentinelsDegraded` fires
    ([ha-and-helm.md](ha-and-helm.md) R-HA-007): no failover can happen while it lasts, so the next
    primary failure would leave trove degraded until someone acts. The `valkey` check stays `pass`
    meanwhile, because the primary still answers (R-HA-056 step 6);
  - the time of the last primary change (the newest `valkey.lastPrimaryChangeAt` of the
    replicas);
  - the server version, or each version with its replicas when the replicas report different ones,
    as an information notice.
- **Backups card**, from `GET /api/v1/system/backups/summary` (R-API-050): the last success and its
  age, an "Overdue" mark under the rule of R-API-050 (1.5 × the expected interval), "No backup
  yet", the last failure when it is newer than the last success, the active run with its phase and
  progress, and a link to the backups screen (R-UI-048).
- **Vulnerability data card** (from M4b), from the `vulnerabilityData` block of `/system/info`
  ([operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) R-OPS-004,
  [vulnerability-scanning.md](vulnerability-scanning.md) R-VULN-024): per source and ecosystem its
  mode, state, age and consecutive failures, with icon and text for data that is stale, never
  imported completely or failing to sync, and a link to the sources screen (R-VULN-022).
- Jobs (`/admin/system/jobs`): the list of `GET /api/v1/system/jobs` with filters for `kind` and
  `state`. The state filter offers every job state of R-ARCH-016: `queued`, `running`,
  `succeeded`, `failed`, `cancelling`, `cancelled`. A cancelled job shows `cancelling` until it
  stops at its next checkpoint (R-OPS-019), and "Cancel" is offered only for `queued` and
  `running` jobs.
- A "Stored-secret keys" card from `GET /api/v1/system/encryption` (R-API-049): the active key ID
  and the key IDs of each replica, sealed values per key ID, the canary state labelled with the
  replica that reported it, and whether the rings are compatible (icon plus text). A key ID that is no longer active but still seals values is marked
  "re-encryption pending" with "Re-encrypt now" for administrators (the task trigger of
  R-API-049), disabled with its reason while the rings are incompatible. The card names the next
  rotation step of R-HA-027 that the state allows, for example "No values left under 2026-04: its
  key file can be removed."
- Automatic refresh every 15 seconds with a visible pause control (WCAG 2.2.2).

Acceptance criteria:

- Stopping one of two replicas changes its status on the screen within 40 seconds without a reload.
- After a rotation to a new key, the card shows the old key ID as "re-encryption pending"; after
  "Re-encrypt now" finishes, it shows zero values under the old key ID and the removal hint.
- Blocking object storage after both replicas became ready shows both as degraded with
  `objectStore` within 40 seconds, and neither as unready (default `health.require_object_store`).
- Cancelling a running `gc-full` job lists it under the state filter `cancelling` until it stops,
  then under `cancelled`.
- With two `web` and two `worker` replicas, stopping Valkey shows every replica as degraded with
  `valkey` and the explanation within 40 seconds, the header reads "degraded", no replica is shown
  unready, and the Valkey card reads "Degraded on 4 of 4 replicas".
- `SENTINEL FAILOVER trove` updates the last primary change on the Valkey card within 40 seconds,
  and every replica reports the new primary.
- Scaling `worker` to 0 shows "No live worker replica" within `system.heartbeat_stale_after` plus
  15 seconds. A test that pins both `web` replicas to one node shows "All ready replicas on one
  node" and "not drain-safe" in the header.
- With `backup.expected_interval: 1h` and the last successful backup two hours old (test clock),
  the Backups card shows "Overdue"; at 80 minutes it does not.
- With two of three Sentinels stopped, the Valkey card shows "Sentinels unreachable" within
  40 seconds, while every replica's `valkey` check stays `pass` and the header does not read
  "degraded".

### R-UI-039 · Webhooks
Priority: **P1** · Covers: UI-046, UI-047, EVT-034

List; editor (key, URL, handler kind standard or templated, for templated handlers the method,
the body template and header templates of R-OPS-041 and named write-only secrets, otherwise the
signing secret with rotation; event types from `/api/v1/webhooks/event-types`, repository
selectors, outbound proxy, custom headers, enabled); "Test" with the receiver's status, latency
and body excerpt; status (`/{key}/status`); deliveries with request and response details and
"Redeliver". Project-scoped subscriptions and a project column come with EVT-022 (P2). Semantics:
[operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md).

Template validation (R-OPS-041, Q-OPS-11 there): a template is checked when the subscription is
saved or tested unsaved, and a refusal answers `422`. The editor shows each error at the template
field it belongs to (`errors[].pointer`, R-API-009) and in the error summary, with the server's
text, which names the rejected construct: `define`, `template` or `block`; a `range` inside
another `range`; a `range` over a literal, a function result or a variable; more than 16 `range`
actions in one template, header templates included; the `call` function; a reference to an
unknown secret; a template that fails to render against the sample event of a subscribed type.
The editor does not check templates itself, so its rules never drift from the server's.

Acceptance criteria:

- "Test" against a receiver that answers 500 shows the status and body excerpt.
- Saving a template with 17 `range` actions keeps the editor open and shows, at the template
  field, the error naming the 16-range cap; a template with `{{ define "x" }}` shows an error
  naming `define`.

### R-UI-053 · The installation's visibility in the general settings
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: trove-only

`/admin/settings/general` gains the section **Visibility** (`<trove-disclosure>`, closed by default) below the public base
URL, with its own **Save changes**, reading and writing `/api/v1/settings/visibility` (R-API-056):

- **Default visibility level** is a radio group of the three levels, each with its icon and one muted sentence
  ([Q-UI-228](#q-ui-228--a-level-is-chosen-in-a-radio-group-of-three-each-with-its-icon-and-a-sentence)): Private ("Only
  members and the principals a policy names read new projects."), Internal ("Every signed-in user who is not external reads
  new projects."), Public ("Anyone, also without signing in, reads new projects."). The help line under the group says that the
  default applies to projects and repositories created later.
- While `publicAvailable` is false, the option Public is shown disabled, muted, with the sentence "The installation's
  configuration admits no request without a credential (`endpoints.default.auth.anonymous`)."
- Below the group, read-only: what is public now (`publicObjects`), the projects and repositories each linked to its settings,
  or "Nothing is public."
- The section is editable for a holder of `security-settings:write`; for a holder of `settings:read` alone it is read-only
  with the reason. Saving needs recent authentication (R-API-007), and a `409 public_not_allowed` is shown at the group.

Acceptance criteria:

- An administrator opens the section, chooses Internal and saves; a project created afterwards shows the Internal icon in the
  project list.
- With `endpoints.default.auth.anonymous: false` the option Public is disabled and says why.

Built as [Q-UI-228](#q-ui-228--a-level-is-chosen-in-a-radio-group-of-three-each-with-its-icon-and-a-sentence): [general-settings.ts](../../web/src/app/features/settings/general-settings.ts), [visibility-level.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/visibility-level.ts); tests [visibility-settings.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/settings/visibility-settings.spec.ts) and the journey [21-visibility.spec.ts](../../web/e2e/tests/21-visibility.spec.ts).

### R-UI-041 · Projects
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-003, UI-050, UI-051

Raised from P1 on 2026-11-02 with R-AUTHZ-026 (beta phase 5a). Follows the project model of R-AUTHZ-026 in
[authorization.md](authorization.md): every repository belongs to exactly one project, and users and groups are members
with the role `reader`, `developer`, `maintainer` or `owner`
([Q-AUTHZ-206](authorization.md#q-authz-206--every-repository-belongs-to-exactly-one-project),
[Q-AUTHZ-208](authorization.md#q-authz-208--four-project-roles-reader-developer-maintainer-owner)). The content
screens live inside the project, `/projects/{project}/…`
([Q-UI-129](#q-ui-129--the-project-is-the-context-of-the-content-chosen-from-your-projects)); this requirement fixes what
the model gives the screens:

- The project is chosen, not filtered: the start page (`/projects`) lists the caller's projects (`GET /api/v1/projects`: the
  memberships of `authz/me`, every project for a holder of `projects:read`) and then the projects whose level admits the caller
  (R-UI-054), and a caller with exactly one project starts in it; inside a project the project switcher at the top of the side bar changes it. There is no project filter in the top
  bar, and no list of a project's content is narrowed by a stored choice.
- Start page: key, display name, description, the caller's role (for a member), the number of repositories and of members.
  The admin area's list of projects (`/admin/projects`, `projects:read`) keeps the owners, has a column with the logical size the project is
  charged (`logicalBytes`, [R-STOR-049](storage.md#r-stor-049--the-storage-of-a-project)) and creates and edits projects.
- Create dialog (administrators, `projects:write`): key (`^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(?:-+[a-z0-9]+)*$`, immutable), display name,
  description, the visibility level (R-UI-054), and the first Owner; repositories are created in the project afterwards. Edit dialog: display name and
  description, for administrators and the project's Owners. Delete is offered to administrators only, and only for
  projects without repositories, service accounts and CI mappings.
- The project's settings show the logical size the project is charged (`logicalBytes`, in binary units, with the exact byte count as its
  tooltip), for every member and every holder of `projects:read`. The physical size of the object store is a figure of the admin
  dashboard only.
- Members screen (`/projects/{project}/members`, Q-UI-214): the users and groups of the project with their roles, read for every member; an Owner and an
  administrator add a member through the principal lookup (Q-AUTHZ-182), change a role and remove a member. The last
  Owner cannot be removed or demoted except by an administrator: the action is shown disabled with the reason, and a
  `409 last_owner` from a concurrent change is reported as such
  ([Q-AUTHZ-217](authorization.md#q-authz-217--the-last-owner-of-a-project-is-removed-or-demoted-only-by-an-administrator-of-trove)).
- For an Owner of a project, also without any capability, the project's side bar holds the project's administration (as
  for the delegates of Q-AUTHZ-181): its repositories (create in the project, edit, delete and move to another project
  it owns; R-UI-020, R-UI-021), its policies (`/projects/{project}/policies`, named within the project; the editor offers the
  project's repositories as bare keys, key globs and classes, and the principal lookup), its service accounts
  (`/projects/{project}/service-accounts`, named within the project, shown as `sa:<projectKey>/<name>`, listed through the
  project's route `GET /api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/service-accounts`, which admits the Owner, as the policies are, never
  through the instance-wide list, which needs `identities:read`; the admin area's filter by project takes the same route; create, enable, disable and delete) and their tokens (issue, with the lifetime cap and without a `system` scope, and revoke), its CI
  mappings (`/projects/{project}/ci`, R-UI-035) and its settings (display name and description, edited in place, Q-UI-215). An Owner without a
  capability has no admin area (Q-UI-129). A member with another role sees the project's settings and members read-only. An
  action the caller's role does not allow is not offered; the policies, service accounts and CI identity are listed in the
  side bar only for the holder of their capability and for the Owner.
- The `auditor` and the other holders of `projects:read` see every project, its members and its screens read-only.
- The admin area's lists (repositories, service accounts, permission policies, audit log) name the project of each item in a
  column and link to the project's screen; the project is also a filter of the repository and policy lists.

Acceptance criteria:

- An administrator creates project `team-a` with `user:alice` as its first Owner; alice adds `group:team-a-devs` as
  `developer`; a member of that group finds `team-a` on the start page with the role `developer`, and the project's members
  read-only.
- alice, without any system role, has no admin area; in `team-a` she sees the project's side bar and none of the global
  screens; she creates a policy `npm-read` and a service account `partner` in `team-a`, and the account is shown as
  `sa:team-a/partner`.
- The remove action of alice's own membership is disabled while she is the only Owner.

### R-UI-042 · Errors, conflicts and feedback
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: trove-only

- One HTTP interceptor (R-ARCH-004 `core/http`) maps problem `code` values to translated messages and
  `errors[].pointer` to form controls. Unknown codes show the English `detail` and the `requestId`
  with a copy button ("give this ID to your administrator").
- 412 `precondition_failed`: a conflict dialog "Changed by someone else since you opened it",
  showing their version against yours field by field, with "Reload (discard mine)", "Overwrite"
  (re-sends with the new ETag after showing the diff) and "Copy my changes".
- **Own permission changes** (INV-17, R-API-052, [authorization.md](authorization.md)
  R-AUTHZ-032). After a write that answers `Trove-Authz-Epoch` (a policy, a role binding, a project, its members, the
  move of a repository), the session store (R-UI-046) keeps the highest such epoch of the tab, and the
  interceptor sends it as `Trove-Authz-Min-Epoch` on every request that follows, so the next
  screen, the `authz/me` and `authz/check` refresh included, shows the change on whichever replica
  answers. The epoch lives in memory only, never in browser storage, and is cleared on 401 and on
  sign-out.
  - 412 `authz_epoch_unknown`: the UI drops that epoch at once (otherwise every later request
    would fail the same way), re-reads the changed object by its `ETag` (R-API-012), and tells the
    user that the change may not have been saved, showing the object as now stored; when the
    stored object matches the user's draft, as for a retried write below, the message says that
    the change is stored. A GET that met the `412` is sent again without the header; any other
    request is offered again with "Retry".
  - 503 `authz_stale`: a GET is retried once after `Retry-After`; any other request shows the 503
    notice below with "Retry".
- 401 `reauthentication_required`: a dialog explains why, keeps the draft of non-secret forms in
  session storage keyed by route, and starts the re-authentication flow of R-AUTH-011; after return
  the draft is restored and the action can be repeated. Forms holding secrets are not kept.
- 429: idempotent GETs retry once after `Retry-After`; otherwise a message with the wait time.
- The UI sends an `Idempotency-Key` on every request that accepts one (R-API-014): creates, job
  starts and job-starting deletes. The key is generated when the form or dialog opens and kept
  until it closes.
- A network error without an answer (for example a request cut at the end of a replica's drain,
  R-API-051) is retried once through the Service, which picks another replica: a GET as it is; a
  request that carries an `Idempotency-Key` with the same key (R-API-014), so it cannot create or
  start twice; a PUT or PATCH with the same `If-Match`. A retried write that answers 412 because
  its first attempt did commit is recognised by comparing the current resource with the user's
  draft: when they match, the UI reports success instead of opening the conflict dialog. A retried
  DELETE that answers 404 counts as done. Any other unsafe request (a POST action without an
  idempotency key, such as a revocation or a rotation) is not retried automatically: the UI says
  that the action may or may not have run, reloads the affected resource, and offers "Retry".
- 409 `idempotency_in_progress`: the UI waits `Retry-After` and sends the same request with the same
  key once more, which replays the first request's outcome.
- 409 `token_already_issued` on a retried token creation: the first attempt created a token whose
  secret was lost with its answer. The UI revokes it (`DELETE /api/v1/tokens/{tokenId}`), creates
  the token again with a new key, and shows only the new one, so no unseen token stays valid.
- 503: a page-level notice with "Retry"; in maintenance mode the notice shows the operator's
  message.
- Confirmations use a polite live region (`role="status"`), errors `role="alert"`; notifications
  with actions stay until dismissed.
- Jobs show a progress component that polls the job (R-API-015) and announces progress at most every
  10 seconds.

Acceptance criteria:

- A forced 412 `precondition_failed` in a Playwright test opens the conflict dialog, and
  "Overwrite" stores the user's version.
- After saving a policy in the e2e profile `scatter`, the network log shows
  `Trove-Authz-Min-Epoch` with the epoch of the `PUT` on the requests that follow it. A test proxy
  that answers one of them `412` `authz_epoch_unknown` makes the UI show "may not have been saved",
  re-read the policy, and send no `Trove-Authz-Min-Epoch` on later requests until its next
  permission change; the conflict dialog does not open.
- An unknown `code` shows the request ID.
- A test proxy resets the connection of the wizard's `POST /api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories` after the server
  has committed it. The UI retries with the same `Idempotency-Key`, reports success, and exactly one
  repository exists. The same with a `PATCH` of the edit form reports success without the conflict
  dialog.
- The same proxy resets the connection of a token creation after the commit. The UI ends with one
  displayed token; `GET /api/v1/tokens` lists it and the first token as revoked.
- The same proxy resets a `POST /api/v1/users/{username}/disable`. The UI sends it once only and
  shows the user's state as reloaded afterwards.

### R-UI-043 · Secrets in the browser
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: trove-only

- Token values (created or pasted) live only in component-local signals. They never enter shared
  services, the URL, `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, IndexedDB, the browser history, console output
  or error reports, and are cleared when their dialog closes or the route changes.
- Secret inputs are `type="password"` with a reveal toggle, `autocomplete="off"` and
  `spellcheck="false"`; copying uses the Clipboard API on an explicit click only.
- Write-only fields (upstream passwords, webhook secrets) show whether a value is set and a "Replace"
  action; they are never prefilled.
- Configuration files with an embedded token are offered for download through a Blob URL that is
  revoked right after the click.
- API answers carry `Cache-Control: no-store` (R-API-017), which keeps secret-bearing answers out of
  the browser's caches.

Acceptance criteria:

- After creating a token and closing the dialog, a test inspects `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`,
  IndexedDB, the URL history and the console log and finds no `trv_` value.

### R-UI-044 · Accessibility
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: trove-only

Every screen meets [WCAG 2.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/) level AA. Design rules that follow from
specific criteria:

| Criterion | Rule in trove |
|---|---|
| 1.3.1 Info and relationships | Data tables are `<table>` with `<th scope>`; landmarks; one `h1` per screen, no skipped heading levels |
| 1.4.1 Use of color; 1.4.3 and 1.4.11 contrast | Status, decision and diff marks carry icon and text; contrast verified in both themes |
| 1.4.10 Reflow | Usable at 320 CSS px; code blocks and wide tables scroll inside their own region |
| 1.4.13 Content on hover or focus | Tooltips are dismissible and hoverable; no information exists only in a tooltip |
| 2.1.1 Keyboard | Tree, member editor, reordering, file selection ("Choose files" button) and action menus work by keyboard |
| 2.1.4 Character key shortcuts | Single-key shortcuts (`/`, R-UI-095) are on by default and turned off in the profile (`keyboardShortcuts`, R-API-021); they never act while the focus is in a text field ([Q-UI-401](#q-ui-401--slash-focuses-the-field-and-is-on-by-default-the-preference-turns-it-off)) |
| 2.2.1 Timing adjustable; 2.2.2 Pause | Session expiry warning (R-UI-002); auto-refresh can be paused (R-UI-038) |
| 2.4.2 Page titled; 2.4.3 Focus order | Title per route; focus moves to the new `h1` on navigation and into dialogs on open, and returns to the trigger on close |
| 2.4.11 Focus not obscured | `scroll-padding-top` keeps focused elements clear of the sticky header |
| 2.5.7 Dragging movements | Every drag interaction has a button alternative (R-UI-022) |
| 2.5.8 Target size | Interactive targets at least 24 × 24 CSS px |
| 3.3.1 and 3.3.3 Errors | Field errors as text next to the field plus a summary at the top |
| 3.3.7 Redundant entry | The wizard never asks twice for what was entered in an earlier step |
| 3.3.8 Accessible authentication | No cognitive tests; pasting allowed in every token field; login happens at the identity provider |
| 4.1.2 Name, role, value; 4.1.3 Status messages | Custom widgets built on `@angular/aria` or the CDK accessibility patterns ([Angular Aria](https://angular.dev/guide/aria/overview)); status messages through live regions |

Process:

- Automated checks with axe-core in Playwright
  ([Playwright accessibility testing](https://playwright.dev/docs/accessibility-testing)) on every
  route, in both themes and both locales; violations of impact "serious" or "critical" fail the
  build, others are triaged.
- Before each release, a manual screen-reader pass (NVDA with Firefox, VoiceOver with Safari) of
  five journeys: sign in; find a package and copy its install command; client setup with a new
  token; create a remote repository; edit a policy.

Acceptance criteria:

- The axe run reports zero serious or critical violations on all routes.
- The five manual journeys are recorded as passed in the release checklist.

### R-UI-045 · Internationalization
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: trove-only

- English (source and default) and German ship with the MVP. Every UI text is translatable; no
  sentence is concatenated from fragments; counts use ICU plural and select messages ("1 Version",
  "3 Versionen").
- Mechanism (Q-UI-5): Angular's compile-time i18n (`@angular/localize`,
  [Angular i18n](https://angular.dev/guide/i18n)) with one build per locale, served at `/ui/en/` and
  `/ui/de/` (R-UI-001). No runtime translation library is used; switching the language reloads the
  route under the other locale.
- Locale choice: the user's preference (R-API-021), then `Accept-Language`, then
  `ui.default_locale`. Switching the language in the user menu stores the preference and reloads the
  same route under the other locale. The preference applies to a request for `/ui/` or a UI route
  without a locale from a browser that holds a valid session cookie; the redirect reads the cookie
  itself, read-only, because the authentication stage ignores it on `/ui/` (Q-API-184). A request without a
  session, with an ended one, or whose preference cannot be read follows `Accept-Language`.
- Dates, numbers, file sizes (binary units such as MiB with the locale's decimal separator) and
  relative times are formatted with Angular's locale data and `Intl`.
- API texts stay English; the UI translates problem codes (R-UI-042) and shows the English `detail`
  for unknown ones.
- Not translated: user content (READMEs, descriptions), identifiers, and snippet code, which is
  marked `translate="no"`.
- `<html lang>` matches the locale (WCAG 3.1.1). Layouts tolerate 35 % longer German text.
- A missing translation fails the build (`i18nMissingTranslation: error`).
- An English–German glossary of product terms (for example "permission policy" →
  "Berechtigungsrichtlinie"; "repository" stays "Repository") is kept with the translation files.

Configuration:

```yaml
ui:
  default_locale: en      # default (proposed)
  locales: [en, de]      # default (proposed)
```

Acceptance criteria:

- A browser with `Accept-Language: de-DE` opening `/ui/` lands on `/ui/de/packages` with German
  texts and German number formatting.
- A user whose stored locale is `de`, signed in, opening `/ui/` with `Accept-Language: en` is
  redirected to `/ui/de/`; the same request without the session cookie, or with a cookie that is
  not a valid session, is redirected to `/ui/en/`.
- Removing one German translation unit makes the build fail.

### R-UI-046 · State management with signals
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: trove-only

Builds on the workspace rules of R-ARCH-004 (standalone, zoneless, signals; generated types and
thin hand-written clients in `src/app/api/`):

- Signals are the reactive state primitive in components and services. RxJS is used only where
  Angular APIs emit observables (router events, `HttpClient` internals) and is converted with
  `toSignal` at that edge.
- Server state is read with `httpResource()` (stable since v22,
  [Angular guide](https://angular.dev/guide/http/http-resource)) keyed by signals (route parameters,
  filters), using request descriptors built by the clients in `src/app/api/`. Mutations call those
  clients from a feature service and then reload the affected resources. There is no global cache of
  server data.
- The clients use `HttpClient` with the types openapi-typescript generates (R-API-002, Q-API-1),
  so the interceptors (CSRF,
  problem mapping, request ID) apply to every call, and no component calls `/api/v1` directly.
- URL state (filters, sort, tab, version) lives in query parameters and reaches components as signal
  inputs through the router's component input binding; changing a filter navigates with
  `replaceUrl`.
- Shared state of a feature lives in an injectable store service exposing read-only signals and
  methods; no third-party state library in the MVP. A session store holds `whoami`, `authz/me`, the
  check cache and the authorization epoch of the tab's last own permission change (R-UI-042), and
  is reset on 401, on 403 for a cached decision, and on sign-out; a reset on 403 keeps the epoch,
  so the reload it causes still carries it. A permission change made in the tab also reloads
  `authz/me` and clears the check cache, with that epoch sent.
- Forms use Signal Forms (stable since v22,
  [Angular guide](https://angular.dev/guide/forms/signals/overview)) with validators derived from the
  OpenAPI constraints (patterns, lengths) where the generator emits them.
- `computed` and `linkedSignal` derive state; `effect` is reserved for side effects at the boundary
  to non-Angular APIs (browser storage, focus, clipboard).
- Lint rules enforce: no `subscribe(` in components, no `NgZone`, no `bypassSecurityTrust*`, no direct
  `localStorage` access outside the storage wrapper.

Acceptance criteria:

- The lint configuration contains the four rules and CI fails on a violation.
- Changing a filter on the packages list issues exactly one API request and updates the URL.

### R-UI-047 · Testing
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: trove-only

| Tier | Tool | Scope | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| Unit | Vitest through Angular's unit-test builder | Pure logic: token substitution, JWT decoding, token checksum validation, pattern preview, problem mapping, stores | Every pull request |
| Component | Vitest browser mode with `TestBed`; API answers from the OpenAPI examples | Screens and widgets including keyboard behavior | Every pull request |
| Contract | TypeScript compile against the generated types; mock answers validated against the document | Drift between UI and API | Every pull request |
| End-to-end | Playwright against the chart-installed build in the local profile of [ha-and-helm.md](ha-and-helm.md) R-HA-051: two `web` and two `worker` pods, PostgreSQL with a standby, Valkey with a replica and three Sentinels, an S3-compatible store (SeaweedFS), the backup CronJob, plus a test OIDC provider and a test CI token issuer | Journeys: sign-in, client setup followed by real `npm` and `dotnet` commands, repository wizard, policy edit, claim tester, token create and revoke, audit entry, system status and backups screens | Smoke on every pull request; full nightly, once in the `scatter` profile (three `web` replicas, round robin per request, R-ARCH-032), once with Valkey stopped, and once while the node drain of R-HA-059 variant A runs, where no journey may fail |
| Accessibility | axe-core in Playwright, plus the manual pass of R-UI-044 | Every route × theme × locale | Every pull request; manual per release |
| Internationalization | Build with missing-translation error | Both locales | Every pull request |
| Security | README XSS corpus; any `securitypolicyviolation` event fails an end-to-end test | Renderer, CSP | Every pull request |
| Renders | `make ui-renders`: Playwright against the UI development profile with a seed through the API ([Q-UI-304](#q-ui-304--make-ui-renders-renders-the-working-tree-through-the-dev-server-signs-the-three-kinds-of-user-in-through-a-provider-of-the-profile-and-seeds-through-the-api)) | Every screen as each kind of user of R-UI-067, both schemes, 1440, 1024 and 390 px, every tab, the whole length; a screen with an error notice, a 4xx or 5xx of the app's own API or a console error fails | Locally, before a UI change is committed (rule 11 of the plan); no CI job |

- End-to-end tests prepare data through the API, not through the UI (INV-17), and run in Chromium on
  pull requests and, in the full run of Test and Release on the commit that closes the phase, in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.
- Line coverage of services and pure logic at least 80 % (# default (proposed)).
- Test tool versions are pinned once in the lockfile and used by local runs and CI alike.

Acceptance criteria:

- The CI workflow runs every tier at the stated cadence, and a deliberately broken snippet template
  fails the end-to-end client-setup test.

The second half is proved by [Q-UI-212](#q-ui-212--a-broken-snippet-template-is-proved-to-fail-by-a-test-on-the-apis-renderer-beside-the-journey-that-holds-the-page-against-the-written-out-text).

### R-UI-048 · Backups
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: OPS-032

`/admin/system/backups`, for callers with `settings:read` (as R-API-050), renders R-API-050. It shows the backup job
of INV-19 and changes nothing: backups are started by the CronJob or by hand with `kubectl`,
configured through the chart and the configuration file, and restored by a Helm hook Job
([backup-and-restore.md](backup-and-restore.md) R-BAK-011, R-BAK-012; Q-API-10).

- **Status.** Last success with its age, the expected interval, "Overdue" (R-API-050's rule) or
  "No backup yet", and
  the last failure with its translated `code` when it is newer than the last success. A run in
  progress shows its phase (`starting`, `snapshot`, `copying`, `finalizing`, `pruning`), tables
  exported, blobs and bytes copied against the totals, its pod and its start time, refreshed with
  the status screen's interval and pause control (R-UI-038). A run whose lease has expired is
  shown as "stopped without finishing; the next run marks it abandoned".
- **Runs.** The list of `GET /api/v1/system/backups` with filters for operation and state and
  "Load more": start, operation, pod, state, backup ID, snapshot time, duration, database bytes,
  blobs copied and warnings. State labels carry icon and text. `interrupted` reads "interrupted by
  a drain or eviction; the Job retries it" and is not shown as a failure (R-BAK-012). A detail panel
  shows the result and the error.
- **Stored backups.** The complete backups that the newest listing run found in the target, with
  backup ID, snapshot time, trove version, schema step, database and blob sizes and a "damaged"
  mark, headed "as recorded by run <id> at <time>" and the note that `trove backup list` reads the
  target itself (Q-API-11). Next to it, read-only: the target, `keep_last` and `keep_within` as
  that run applied them, and the expected interval.
- **Start a backup now.** No button starts one. A panel shows the command with a copy button,
  filled from `manualRun`:
  `kubectl -n trove create job --from=cronjob/trove-backup trove-backup-manual-<timestamp>`
  (# example), with `<timestamp>` (Unix seconds) filled in by the browser when the panel opens.
  A Job name may have at most 63 characters
  ([Job](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/controllers/job/)), so the browser shortens
  the CronJob part when a long release name would exceed it. Without `manualRun`, the namespace
  and CronJob name appear as placeholders. The panel says that the run appears in the list once its
  pod has started, that it records `trigger: schedule` and is told apart by its pod name
  (R-BAK-012), and that one backup runs at a time (R-BAK-010).
- **Restore.** When `restoredFrom` is set, a notice names the backup ID and snapshot time this
  installation was restored from. Restoring is a Helm operation on an empty installation
  (R-BAK-020, R-BAK-021); the screen links to the operator documentation and offers no restore
  action.

Acceptance criteria:

- During a run, the screen shows phase `copying` and a growing count of copied blobs without a
  reload.
- A run ended `interrupted` by a drain, then completed by the Job's next pod, shows the first as
  interrupted, not failed, and the status shows no failure.
- After two runs with `keep_last: 1`, "Stored backups" lists one backup, recorded by the second
  run.
- The network log of a visit to the screen, including a click on the copy button, contains no
  request with a method other than GET or HEAD.
- With `manualRun.cronJob` set to a 52-character name, the copied command, run with `kubectl`,
  creates the Job, and its name has at most 63 characters.

### R-UI-051 · Avatar upload
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: trove-only

The owner's decision of 2026-11-07: "Upload jetzt mitbauen: nur PNG/JPEG/WebP, serverseitig neu kodiert, max. 1 MiB, als Blob
gespeichert, vom api-Pod ausgeliefert; Spec, Security-Seite und Tests dazu." The API is R-API-055; this requirement is the
screens. The robot that a user without an image gets is R-UI-002. The development agent decided what the owner did not say
(Q-UI-169 to Q-UI-171).

- **Where a user manages their own avatar.** The profile (R-UI-029) opens with a card **Public avatar**, the place the
  reference puts it: the current avatar at 96 px (the uploaded image, or the robot), a **Choose file…** button, **Remove
  avatar** while an image is set, and the help text: PNG, JPEG or WebP, at most 1 MiB, at least 32 by 32 pixels, not animated,
  and that the server cuts the picture to a centred square and stores it again as a 256 by 256 pixel PNG, so there is no
  cropper. Choosing a file sends it at once (`PUT /api/v1/users/me/avatar`; the body is the file, `Content-Type` its type, the
  CSRF header as for every session write); there is no second save step (Q-UI-170). **Remove avatar** asks first, then
  sends `DELETE /api/v1/users/me/avatar`. Both give a status message.
- **Checks before sending.** The browser refuses, with the text of the matching server refusal and without a request, an empty
  file, a type other than `image/png`, `image/jpeg` and `image/webp`, a file over 1,048,576 bytes, a file the browser cannot
  decode, and an image under 32 pixels on a side or over 4,194,304 pixels in all (read with `createImageBitmap`). The server
  repeats every check and decides the format from the bytes; only it can tell an animated image (Q-UI-171).
- **The answers.** `415 unsupported_media_type`, `413 payload_too_large`, `400 malformed_request`, `422` with
  `errors[0].code` `animated_image`, `invalid_dimensions` or `undecodable_image`, and `503 server_busy` (which the UI does not
  retry: the user chooses again) each have a sentence in English and German next to the form (R-UI-042, R-UI-045); any other
  answer, `403` included, is the general error notice with the request ID. A refused upload changes nothing on screen.
- **The new URL.** The answer of the upload is the user record; its `avatarUrl` replaces the image everywhere in the page. The
  shell keeps the signed-in user's `avatarUrl` (it reads `GET /api/v1/users/me` once per signed-in principal, because
  `whoami` does not carry it), so the top bar changes without a reload, and a removal puts the robot back. A principal
  that is not a user or the break-glass account (a service account, a CI token) has no avatar and the shell does not ask. The
  old URL is `404` after a replacement and is never requested again. The seed of the robot stays the principal's ID.
- **Moderation.** On the administrator's user screen (R-UI-024) the **Attributes** show the user's avatar (48 px) and, for a
  holder of `identities:write` while an image is set, **Remove avatar**, which asks for a confirmation that names the user and then
  sends `DELETE /api/v1/users/{username}/avatar` (R-API-055). An administrator never sets another user's image.
- **Accessibility and security.** The avatar images are decoration (`alt=""`, hidden from assistive technology): the name is
  next to them. The file input is hidden and its button carries the name; a refusal is announced as an alert. The images
  are same-origin URLs, which the CSP (`img-src 'self' data:`) admits; the UI renders nothing from the uploaded bytes but an
  `<img>`.

Acceptance criteria:

- A signed-in user without an image sees the robot on the profile and in the top bar. After choosing a valid PNG, the top bar
  and the profile show the uploaded image without a reload, and a reload keeps it; **Remove avatar** and its confirmation
  bring the robot back.
- A GIF, an empty file, a file over 1 MiB and an image of 31 by 400 pixels are each refused with a sentence and no
  `PUT` leaves the browser; an animated WebP is refused with the sentence for `animated_image` after the server answers `422`.
- Every refusal code above has an English and a German sentence.
- An administrator with `identities:write` sees **Remove avatar** on the user screen of a user who has an image, after a
  confirmation the image is gone and the robot is shown; without the capability the button is not shown.
- While the profile and the top bar are used, no request leaves trove's origin.

### R-UI-060 · The Documentation tab of an Ansible collection
Priority: **P1** · Covers: trove-only

The package page (R-UI-007) of a version of the format `ansible` shows the tab **Documentation** instead of README when `metadata.docs.state` is not `none` or
the version has a README, and makes it the default tab then. The data is that of [R-ANS-036](formats/ansible.md#r-ans-036--the-documentation-operations-of-the-screens-their-rendering-and-the-search);
the tab is wiki content and follows the wiki check of [R-ANS-037](formats/ansible.md#r-ans-037--the-documentation-is-wiki-content-which-routes-documents-and-fields-the-wiki-check-gates).

- **Layout** (Q-UI-241): two panes. Tree pane (`clamp(18rem, 30%, 26rem)`): the search field in its head ([Q-UI-243](#q-ui-243--the-search-field-filters-the-tree-through-the-server-and-keeps-the-counts)),
  below it the tree, rows of 32 px: **Documentation** (the README, the other Markdown files as children), **Modules (n)**, **Plugins (n)** (children by type, collapsed at first with
  their counts, opened when they hold the open page or a match) and **Roles (n)**, each group with its count as a neutral badge; an entry row shows its name, the short description
  as the tooltip; an entry without documentation is muted and labelled "no documentation". Page pane: the open page. Under 48 rem of content width one pane shows at a time with a back action.
- **Addressing.** The open page is the query parameter `doc` of the package URL (`README.md`, `module/<name>`, `filter/<name>`, `role/<name>`, `file/<name>`); the search text is `q`;
  a link, a reload and the back button restore both. Changing the version or the repository resets `doc` and `q`. An unknown `doc` shows the first page and no error.
- **Requests.** The tree is one call of `getPackageVersionDocs` per version, repeated only for a search (300 ms after the last key, at least 2 characters); a page is one call of
  `getPackageVersionDocEntry` or `getPackageVersionDocFile`; nothing is requested for a tab that is not shown, and `include` of the version details is not used to learn the state.
- **Pages** are R-UI-061. **States**: `pending` shows "The documentation of this version is being fetched." and a refresh action; `unavailable` shows the reason in words
  (upstream error, too large, invalid document); `none` shows no tab. A search with no match shows "No entries match" in the pane, never an empty tree.

Acceptance criteria:

- The tab for `hans_fischer.common`-like data shows the groups Modules (8) and Plugins (24) with their counts, the README first, and keeps the counts while a search narrows the tree.
- A reload of `…?doc=module/check_host_reachable&q=host` shows the same page and the same narrowed tree.
- A version without a README and with state `none` has no Documentation tab and the page requests none of the operations.
- Keyboard: the tree is a `role="tree"` of links; arrow keys move, Enter opens, `aria-current="page"` marks the open entry; the search field has the label "Search the documentation" and Escape clears it.

### R-UI-061 · An entry page and a file page
Priority: **P1** · Covers: trove-only

An entry page (Q-UI-242) shows, in the order ansible-doc prints, a head (the full name `<ns>.<name>.<entry>` with a copy button, the short description, "added in", a `warn` badge for a
deprecated plugin) and the sections Synopsis, Parameters, Notes, Requirements, Attributes, See also, Examples, Return values and Authors, each only when it has content. **Parameters** is the shared data
table (no frame, hairlines) with the columns Name (with aliases), Type (and element type), Required (a text badge), Default, Choices and Description; a suboption row is indented 16 px per level
with a "suboptions of <name>" label for the screen reader, and a parameter with suboptions is collapsible (open at first, [Q-UI-252](#q-ui-252--the-parameters-of-a-page-are-open-at-every-level-at-first-each-parameter-with-suboptions-folds-on-its-own)). Defaults, choices and samples are text as written. Examples and a sample are a `<pre>` in the code block
control of the README with a copy button, no highlighting. A role shows its README only. A page whose entry has `hasDocs` false shows the head and "This plugin has no documentation in its source." (generated) or "The upstream sent no
documentation for this plugin." (upstream). A muted line below says where the documentation comes from ("Generated by trove from the archive, 2026-11-11 09:41" or "Taken from the upstream") and names
the repository when the version is in more than one. A file page is the README renderer's output (R-UI-008) for a Markdown file.

- **Safety.** The HTML an operation returns is bound with `[innerHTML]` as the README component binds it (Angular's sanitizer and Trusted Types stay on); **every other value of an entry is bound as text**, so a
  hostile default or sample cannot become markup. The lint rule that forbids `bypassSecurityTrust*` (R-UI-046) covers the new components.

Acceptance criteria:

- A module whose parameters nest three levels deep renders three indented levels; a parameter named `<img src=x onerror=1>` appears as that text.
- An entry with `hasDocs` false shows the head and the line, no empty sections.
- A role page shows the README HTML and no Parameters section.

### R-UI-062 · The Contents tab
Priority: **P1** · Covers: trove-only

The tab **Contents** (shown with the Documentation tab, with the count as a neutral badge) is the flat list of what the version contains: a data table with the columns Name, Type and Short description, a type
filter (a select of the types present with their counts), sorted by type then name, one request (the tree of `getPackageVersionDocs`, shared with the Documentation tab so the two never disagree). A row whose entry has documentation links to
`?tab=documentation&doc=<type>/<name>`; one without is plain text. A version with 5,000 entries (the bound) shows the list in pages of 100 with "Load more".

Acceptance criteria:

- The table lists the 32 entries of the owner's collection with their types; selecting `module` shows 8 and the badge on the tab stays 32.
- A row with documentation opens the entry in the Documentation tab.

### R-UI-063 · The Import log tab and the other tabs of the reference
Priority: **P1** · Covers: trove-only

The tab **Import log** is shown on a version held by a **local** repository (not for a remote or a virtual repository's remote member): the import task of that version, newest first, through `listAnsibleImportTasks` with the optional query
parameters `package` and `version` (Q-API-262), state as a badge, the time, and the messages as text (level, message); the warnings of the generator (R-ANS-034) are among them. It is readable by whoever reads the repository, as the task is (R-ANS-009), and is
**not** wiki content.

The other tabs and facts the reference shows are the page's existing ones; nothing is duplicated (Q-UI-240, Q-UI-245):

| Reference | trove | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Install: description, license, install command, download, Requires Ansible | The install panel (the command of R-API-030 with the real address), the Metadata tab (description, **Requires Ansible**, licenses, tags), the Files tab (the archive with its SHA-256 and download) | R-UI-007, R-ANS-026 |
| Dependencies | A **Dependencies** section of the Metadata tab: the collections the version needs with their ranges, each a link to that package's page when the installation holds it (muted text otherwise) | Q-UI-245 |
| Distributions | The **Repositories** tab (the repositories that hold the version) | R-UI-007 |
| Docs site, Website, Issue tracker, Repo | The links of the Metadata tab: "Docs site" (`documentationUrl`, so named for this format), "Homepage", "Issue tracker" and "Source repository", shown as text links with the external-link marker and only for `http` and `https` | Q-UI-245 |
| Contents, Import log, Documentation | New tabs: R-UI-062, this requirement, R-UI-060 | |

Acceptance criteria:

- A local version shows its import task with the warning of a documentation bound; the same version through a virtual repository over it shows the task of its target, and a remote version has no Import log tab.
- A version with `dependencies` shows the Dependencies section with a link for a collection the installation holds; a link with another scheme than `http` or `https` is not rendered as a link.

### R-UI-064 · States, the wiki check, responsiveness and tests of the documentation screens
Priority: **P1** · Covers: trove-only

- **The wiki check.** `metadata.docs` absent means no Documentation and no Contents tab and no request (Q-UI-244); a 404 or a refusal of an operation removes the tab without a message. The Import log and the other tabs are unaffected.
- **Responsiveness.** At 390 px the tree and the page are one pane at a time; at 1440 px both; the parameter table scrolls horizontally inside its region, never the page.
- **Accessibility and style.** Controls are the GitLab-style controls of Q-UI-126 (the tab group, the data table, the text input, the badges), the tree follows R-UI-007's keyboard rules, colours are the tokens of the design language (green only for positive status).
