- **Tests.** Web unit tests: the tab choice from `metadata.docs` and `hasReadme`, the tree grouping and counts, the search debounce, minimum length, live region and empty state, the entry sections, text-only binding of hostile values, keyboard, the narrow layout. Browser journeys named in R-ANS-046 (local, remote, virtual, wiki), each asserting the first page's content.

Acceptance criteria: the tests above exist and run in `make web-test`; the journeys run in the e2e set `ansible`; `make web-lint` is green.

### R-UI-065 · One read-only address field with a joined copy button for every client address
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: trove-only

The owner's task of 2026-11-11 (T-20): the column **Client address** of the repository list cut the address with an ellipsis
(`https://trove.k8s-main.…`), so it could not be read. Every address that trove shows for a client to put into its
configuration looks like the field **Clone with SSH** of the owner's GitLab: the whole address in a read-only, bordered field
in a monospace font, with the copy button joined to the field's right edge. It is one shared component,
`<trove-address-field>` ([ui-style-guide.md](../developer/ui-style-guide.md#address-field)); no screen draws its own
`<code>` plus copy button for a client address. The development agent decided what the owner did not say (Q-UI-272 to Q-UI-274);
the widths are Q-UI-300 and Q-UI-301 since the owner's task of 2026-11-12 (T-21), which replaced Q-UI-270 and Q-UI-271 after
the list showed a field of a different width in every row and scrolled sideways.

- **The field.** A read-only `<input type="text">` holding the address, 32 px high, the text in `--trove-font-mono` at 0.875rem,
  a 1 px border in `--trove-control-border`, the fill of an editable control (`--trove-control-bg`), not the grey fill of a
  read-only value (Q-UI-274). The copy button sits in the same row, attached to the right edge: no gap, one border between
  them, the field's right corners and the button's left corners square, the outer corners rounded by `--trove-control-radius`.
  The button is the existing `btn btn-icon` copy button with the glyph `content_copy`.
- **Never cut.** The address is never cut with an ellipsis, never wrapped, and its `title` is not the only way to read it.
  Where the field is shorter than the address, the address scrolls inside the field (an input does so natively), and the
  copy button stays joined to it.
- **One width per place.** A field takes the width of its line, not of its address. In a list every field has the same
  width: the column is as wide as the list's longest address, but never more than its share: in a project's repository list what
  is left after the repository's preferred 20 rem and the least widths of the others, elsewhere 46 characters and what the other
  columns leave at their least widths, so the properties beside it are not squeezed; the field fills the cell and
  shows the address from its start, a longer address scrolls inside it (Q-UI-300, Q-UI-330); below 48 rem of the list's width
  the rows stack and the field takes the row's width (Q-UI-306). A list whose kind of user does not copy addresses as its job
  shows none: the admin area's repository list and the search results have a copy button in the row instead (Q-UI-330). A field
  alone on its line fills the line up to a measure of 70 characters, so stacked fields are one width too (Q-UI-301).
- **Selectable.** A click or focus in the field selects the whole address; the user can also select a part of it and copy
  with the keyboard. The address is the field's value, so the browser's find, drag and copy work as on any input (Q-UI-273).
- **Copy button.** `aria-label` and `title` name what is copied (**Copy client address**; in a list the label names the row,
  **Copy client address of npm-internal**). A click writes the address to the clipboard and the polite live region says
  **Copied to the clipboard.**; where the clipboard is not available an alert says so and the field stays selectable (the
  behaviour of `trove-copy-button`, which the component reuses). There is no other visual confirmation, and no green
  (owner rule).
- **Name.** The field has an accessible name: `aria-label` = the label of the place (**Client address**, in a list **Client
  address of npm-internal**).
- **Keyboard.** Tab reaches the field, then the button; Enter or Space on the button copies. The field takes the focus ring of
  the other controls; arrow keys, Home and End move inside it. Nothing traps the focus.
- **Colour schemes.** Light and dark both use the control tokens; the border has at least 3:1 against the surface in both
  (R-UI-044).
- **No address, no field.** An empty address renders nothing; the caller decides what stands in its place (a server without a
  configured base URL shows no address, R-REPO-002).
- **Scope (Q-UI-272, Q-UI-320).** The field holds one line to copy: an address (a URL, or a registry host with a path,
  `trove.k8s-main.wds18.de/docker-hub-remote`) or a command of one line (the install command of a package). A configuration
  file or a snippet of several lines keeps the code block with its copy button.

Acceptance criteria:

- Component unit tests: the field's value is the full address for `https://trove.k8s-main.wds18.de/api/npm/npm-internal/`,
  for `trove.k8s-main.wds18.de/docker-hub-remote` and for a 300-character address; the input is `readonly` and has an
  accessible name; no element of the component has `text-overflow: ellipsis`; the field sets no width of its own from its
  address; a field shorter than its address shows its start; a click on the button writes exactly the address to the clipboard
  and sets the status message; a failed write sets the alert; focus in the field selects all of its text; an empty address
  renders nothing; axe finds no violation.
- The lists of R-UI-066 size their address column to their longest address, and every field of a list is in that column.
- Rendered (rule 11 of the plan, `make ui-renders`): in a project's repository list every address field has one width, an address of 57 characters shows whole in a project's list at 1920 px beside the open filter panel, and no
  repository list scrolls sideways at 1920, 1440, 1280, 1024 or 390 px, in both schemes, with the filter panel open or closed
  (Q-UI-330).
- Every screen of R-UI-066 shows its address through the component, and no template of those screens gives a client address
  the class `ellipsis`.
- Playwright: on a project's repository list the cell of a row holds an input whose value equals the address the API gave, and a
  click on the row's copy button puts that value on the clipboard; on the admin area's list the row's copy button, named with the
  address, does the same.

### R-UI-066 · The screens that show a client address use the address field
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: trove-only

Each screen shows its client addresses through `<trove-address-field>` (R-UI-065):

| Screen | Place | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Repository list (R-UI-020), `/projects/{project}/repositories` | The column **Client address**, one field per row | The first address of the repository; one width for the column, the list's longest address up to what is left after the repository's 20 rem (Q-UI-300, Q-UI-330); the label names the row. The admin area's list (`/admin/repositories`) and the search results (`/search`) have no field: a copy button in the row (Q-UI-330) |
| Repository page (R-UI-021), settings view | The fact **Client address** | The field fills the fact up to the measure (Q-UI-301) |
| Repository page, consumer view | The fact **Client address**, one field per address of the repository, stacked | Stacked fields are one width (Q-UI-301) |
| Repository content page (R-UI-052) | The header: the repository's first address; **Details**: each further address with its label | Q-UI-320 |
| Start page (Q-UI-311), recently opened repositories | One field per repository: its first address | Q-UI-320 |
| Repository wizard (R-UI-021), review step | The line **Client address** | |
| Client setup page (R-UI-016), Bastion banner | The Bastion's repository address | The sentence stays; the address is a field below it (Q-UI-272) |
| Guides (R-UI-049), Bastion section | **Address of the repository on the Bastion** | As above |
| Endpoint page, the address of an exposure rule | No field: the row's copy button, whose name and tooltip carry the address ([Q-UI-331](#q-ui-331--an-endpoints-rules-are-the-shared-data-table-and-a-rules-client-address-is-the-rows-copy-button)) | The administrator manages the rules; the address is handed out with the button |

Not in scope: the text of a guide (server-rendered HTML, where an address is prose in `<code>`), the snippets and commands of
the setup page and the guides, a command of several lines (an install command of one line is a field, Q-UI-320), the
**Base URL** and **Hosts** columns and field of the
endpoint (configuration of an endpoint, not an address given to a client), and digests and fingerprints (a hash is not an
address).

Acceptance criteria:

- A unit test per row of the table finds `trove-address-field` with the full address as its value.
- A test that read an address from text content reads the field's value instead (an input's value is not text content).

### R-UI-067 · Three kinds of user: the plain user, the power user and the administrator
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: trove-only

The owner's task T-21 of 2026-11-12: "Easy access to the product for simple users. Optional details for power users and
admins." The UI serves three kinds of user. A kind is not a role of its own: it is read from the roles and capabilities the
caller already has (R-AUTHZ-010, R-AUTHZ-026, `GET /api/v1/authz/me` of R-UI-005), per project
([Q-UI-310](#q-ui-310--the-kind-of-user-is-read-from-the-roles-in-force-per-project-and-is-no-role-of-its-own)):

| Kind | Who | The job the screens serve first |
|---|---|---|
| **Plain user** | In the project of the screen at most the role `reader`, or a reader through the project's visibility level (R-UI-054); no system role | Find a repository or a package, copy its client address, set up the client, install |
| **Power user** | In the project of the screen the role `developer`, `maintainer` or `owner`; no system role | Publish, maintain the project's repositories and, as its Owner, its members, policies, accounts and settings |
| **Administrator** | A system role (`admin`, `repository-admin`, `security-admin`, `auditor`, `webhook-admin`); each opens the admin area with the screens of its capabilities | All of the above in every project, and the admin area |

One person can be a plain user in one project and a power user in another; outside a project (the start page, the client setup,
the guides) the highest kind of the caller's memberships counts.

- **The main view is the plain user's.** Every screen of the main path (the start page, a project's repository and package
  lists, the repository page, the package page, the client setup) shows first what the plain user's job needs, in the same
  layout for every kind. The decisions per screen are Q-UI-311 to Q-UI-316.
- **Details behind one disclosure.** What only power users and administrators need (configuration facts, statistics, owners and
  claims, internal names) is not in the main view: it sits in one closed section **Details** at the end of the screen's main view,
  the same quiet disclosure on every screen (Q-UI-322), which remembers per user and screen whether it was opened
  ([Q-UI-319](#q-ui-319--the-details-are-one-closed-section-per-screen-that-remembers-whether-the-user-opened-it)). Changes stay on
  the screen's **Settings**, which is offered only to who may change (R-UI-005).
- **Nothing in the way.** The plain user is not offered a read-only copy of a settings page, a sidebar entry of an administration
  screen, or a disabled control of an administrator's action
  ([Q-UI-317](#q-ui-317--the-plain-users-project-sidebar-holds-the-content-the-projects-members-and-settings-move-into-its-about-section)).
  Its main views name no internal terms: no capability names (`projects:write`), no stored-format names, no UUIDs, no request
  IDs outside an error notice ([Q-UI-318](#q-ui-318--the-plain-users-main-views-name-no-internal-terms-a-refusal-says-who-can-do-it)).
- **The power user's work in place.** The power user sees the main view of the plain user plus the actions of its role in the
  screen's header and row menus (publish, create, settings, delete) and the Details; the administrator in addition the admin area
  behind the top bar's Admin button.
- **Simple by default, details on demand** (the owner's rules of 2026-11-12,
  [CLAUDE.md](../../CLAUDE.md#product-simple-by-default-details-on-demand)). The power user's flows follow the same rule as the
  plain user's views: creating and configuring a repository asks only what the repository needs to work, for every format and
  class; access in it is the members and the visibility level (R-UI-055); every other setting (patterns, disabling, hiding
  existence, administrator notes, mirror and protocol tuning) is in a detail view or behind an advanced-settings section, never a
  step; a remote's connection is tested where its upstream is entered; a default is a field's value, a field is as wide as its
  input, a title names the format, and a field shows an error only after it was touched or on submit, in words and never as a
  pattern (the shared text and select fields hold the rule for every form: an error waits until the field was left once or a
  submit of its form was attempted, UI-A-42). The creation flow and the
  repository settings are planned on T-18's tree (T-21, "Creating and configuring a repository") and are not decided on this page;
  their defects are in the audit.

This page specifies the kinds and the decisions; the screens follow them in the fix waves of the audit
([ui-audit.md](../projektplan/ui-audit.md)), each change rendered under rule 11 (R-UI-047, `make ui-renders`).

Acceptance criteria:

- `make ui-renders` renders every screen of the main path as `sam` (plain user), `priya` (power user) and `ada` (administrator)
  of its seed, and the pictures show for each kind what Q-UI-311 to Q-UI-319 say; the audit lists every difference until it is
  fixed.
- The plain user reaches a repository's client address from the start page in at most two steps and the client setup of that
  repository in at most three, without passing a settings page.
- No main view of the plain user shows a capability name, a UUID or a settings page it cannot change.

### R-UI-090 · The grade shield
Priority: **P1** · Covers: trove-only

The owner's task of 2026-11-12 (T-21): "Vulnerabilities shall be shown as we realised it in cogpit." A version's grade
([vulnerability-scanning.md](vulnerability-scanning.md) R-VULN-038) is drawn as cogpit draws an image's: a crest with its letter.
`<trove-grade-shield>` ([grade-shield.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/vulnerability/grade-shield.ts)) is the one drawing of it; no
screen draws its own.

- **The crest.** An inline SVG in a box of 100: two shallow arcs across the top that meet in a point at its middle, the sides
  straight down to half the height, then curving to a point at the bottom (cogpit's geometry). Its fill runs from 25 % lighter at
  the top to 25 % darker at the bottom of the grade's colour; S has a gold rim. N/A is flat and quiet.
- **The letter** is SVG text in the sans face at weight 700, 54 % of the side, centred at 46 % of the height (the point takes room
  below); "N/A" at 56 % of that size.
- **Sizes.** 20 px in a list, a header and a tab, the size of a format's icon in a list
  ([Q-UI-381](#q-ui-381--the-shield-in-a-list-is-20-px-the-size-of-a-format-icon)); 32 px on the card.
- **Colours** ([Q-UI-370](#q-ui-370--the-grades-take-cogpits-colours-and-s-a-and-b-are-the-greens-of-a-good-grade)): the tokens
  `--trove-grade-s` to `--trove-grade-e`, `--trove-grade-na`, the rim `--trove-grade-rim` and the letters' inks
  `--trove-grade-s-ink`, `--trove-grade-ink`, `--trove-grade-ink-on-dark`, `--trove-grade-na-ink`; S to E are the same in both
  schemes, N/A is the scheme's quiet grey. The letter keeps 4.5:1 on its fill (`palette.spec.ts`).
- **Never by colour alone.** The letter says the grade, and the grade's text stands beside the shield wherever it is shown; there
  the shield is decorative (`aria-hidden`). Alone, it is `role="img"` named **Grade E**
  ([Q-UI-371](#q-ui-371--the-shield-is-an-inline-svg-whose-letter-is-text-and-it-is-decorative-beside-its-text)).

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit: for each grade the SVG carries the letter as text and the grade's class; `size` sets 20 or 32 px; with a label it is an
  image with that name, without one it is hidden from the accessibility tree; axe finds no serious violation.
- The contrast of every letter on its fill and of N/A's crest and letter is held by `palette.spec.ts`.

### R-UI-091 · The grade's text and rule
Priority: **P1** · Covers: trove-only

- **The text** is the grade and the count that decides it, as R-VULN-038 words it: "E · 13 Critical", "C · OS end of life",
  "S · no known vulnerabilities", "N/A · not scanned"; the letter at weight 600. **The rule** is the sentence of R-VULN-038's
  table; for S of an image "No known vulnerabilities, and the OS is supported", for N/A the evaluation state in words.
- `<trove-grade>` ([grade.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/vulnerability/grade.ts)) is the shield of 20 px and the text on one line,
  for a list cell, a header and a tab. Its tooltip (`[troveTooltip]`) names every count, "13 Critical · 160 High · 113 Medium ·
  16 Low · 843 Unknown", and "OS end of life" when it is; the text stays the accessible name of the cell.
- The words are the UI's, translated (`vuln.grade.*`); the grade is the server's (R-VULN-039). `gradeText`, `gradeRule` and
  `gradeRank` ([grade-words.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/vulnerability/grade-words.ts)) derive them from the grade, its counts and
  its end of life and never decide the grade again.

Acceptance criteria:

- A table test of the text, the rule and the rank over the boundaries of R-VULN-038 (0, 10 and 11 Low, 1, 5 and 6 Critical, the
  end of life, N/A) and of the order E · 13 > E · 6 > D · 4 > D · 2 > C · 120 > S > N/A.
- Unit: `<trove-grade>` shows the shield and the text, its tooltip names every count; axe finds no serious violation.

### R-UI-092 · The severity bar
Priority: **P1** · Covers: trove-only

`<trove-severity-bar>` ([severity-bar.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/vulnerability/severity-bar.ts)) draws open findings by severity
as cogpit draws an image's:

- **Five segments** in one row, Critical, High, Medium, Low and Unknown, `none` counted in Low (Q-VULN-153); 22 px high, 4 px apart,
  rounded by `--trove-radius-s`; each segment's count inside it, centred, at 12 px and weight 700, in tabular figures.
- **Width by share** ([Q-UI-372](#q-ui-372--the-bars-segments-are-as-wide-as-their-share-with-room-for-their-number)): each
  segment first gets the room of its number and its padding, then the rest of the row is shared by the segments' shares of all
  findings, each share at least 7 %. A count is never cut and the row never scrolls sideways.
- **Colours**: `--trove-sev-critical` (dark red), `--trove-sev-high` (red), `--trove-sev-medium` (orange), `--trove-sev-low`
  (yellow), the count in `--trove-sev-ink-on-dark` on the first two and `--trove-sev-ink` on the next two; Unknown hatched in
  diagonal stripes of `--trove-sev-unknown` and `--trove-sev-unknown-light`, its count in the text colour. A severity without
  findings is drawn faint (its fill at 28 % over the surface), and its 0 stays readable in the text colour (4.5:1; the muted tone
  would not be, `palette.spec.ts`).
- **Name.** The bar is `role="img"` with the name "Open findings: 13 Critical, 160 High, 113 Medium, 16 Low, 843 Unknown"; the
  numbers inside are hidden from the accessibility tree. With `[queries]` (the report's header and the grade card of the package
  page, R-UI-094) each segment is a link that applies its severity filter, named by its count and severity ("13 Critical"), in a
  list named "Open findings"; on the package page the link keeps the page's other query parameters (`merge`) and the segment of
  the filter in force is marked (`aria-current`).

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit: the five counts in order, None added to Low; a larger count gives a larger share and a zero count a faint segment that
  still shows 0; the Unknown segment is hatched; the accessible name lists every count; with links each segment links to its
  filter; axe finds no serious violation.
- Rendered: the counts 13, 160, 113, 16 and 843 fit their segments at 1440 and 390 px in both schemes.

### R-UI-093 · The grade card
Priority: **P1** · Covers: trove-only

`<trove-grade-card>` ([grade-card.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/vulnerability/grade-card.ts)) is a version's grade in one
repository with its details, as cogpit's card:

- The shield of 32 px on the left, centred on the card's lines; on the right, one below the other: the text (weight 600), the rule
  (muted, 12 px), the severity bar of R-UI-092 and the line of facts (muted, 12 px). No frame: the card sits in its section.
- **The line of facts**, its parts separated by " · ": for an image **OS** and its name, **end of life** in the warning colour
  when it is, and **Scanned** with the time of its oldest scan ("Scanned 1 h ago (Nov 12, 2026, 12:31:51 PM)"); for every other
  format **Checked** with the time of the advisory data it was checked against ("Checked 3 min ago (…)", Q-VULN-156); the time is
  `<trove-time-ago>`, one relative time ("just now", "3 min ago", "1 h ago", "4 d ago") with the absolute time in brackets
  ([Q-UI-378](#q-ui-378--a-time-on-the-grade-card-is-one-relative-time-with-the-absolute-time-in-brackets-from-one-component));
  last, the link **Findings in web-frontend/images**, which opens the project's vulnerability report filtered by the repository,
  the package and the version (R-VULN-022) ([Q-UI-374](#q-ui-374--a-list-shows-the-shield-and-the-text-the-bar-and-the-facts-are-the-cards)).
- On the package page the card's bar filters the findings below it ([Q-UI-379](#q-ui-379--the-vulnerabilities-tab-pages-the-open-findings-of-a-version-from-the-findings-api-filtered-by-the-cards-bar)).
- **N/A** shows the shield, the text and the rule only: there are no counts to draw.

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit: an image's card with "OS alpine 3.24.1", the end of life and the scan time; a package's with the data's time; the link's
  query names the repository, the package and the version; N/A has no bar and no line of facts; axe finds no serious violation.

### R-UI-094 · Where the grade shows
Priority: **P1** · Covers: trove-only

Every screen that showed the highest severity of a version or a package shows its grade instead; the findings themselves keep
their severity (R-VULN-022). The list shows the grade; the bar and the facts are on the card (R-UI-067: details on demand,
[Q-UI-374](#q-ui-374--a-list-shows-the-shield-and-the-text-the-bar-and-the-facts-are-the-cards)).

| Screen | Place | What |
|---|---|---|
| Repository content (R-UI-052) | The column **Vulnerabilities** of the items | `<trove-grade>` of the item's latest version (`vulnerabilityGrade`, R-VULN-039); the column sorts by grade ([Q-UI-373](#q-ui-373--the-list-sorts-by-grade-in-the-browser-over-the-whole-list-up-to-1000-entries)) |
| Repository content, the opened row | The column **Vulnerabilities** of the versions | `<trove-grade>` of each version in this repository |
| Package page (R-UI-007) | The header's facts | `<trove-grade>` of the selected version (the worst of its repositories), a link to the tab **Vulnerabilities** ([Q-UI-375](#q-ui-375--the-package-page-shows-the-versions-grade-in-its-header-and-a-card-per-repository-on-its-tab)) |
| Package page, tab **Vulnerabilities** (R-VULN-023) | Each repository's section | `<trove-grade-card>` above the block banner, its bar's segments the severity filter of the findings below (`severity` in the URL); then the open findings, 25 at a time from the findings API, worst first, with their number from the grade's counts ([Q-UI-379](#q-ui-379--the-vulnerabilities-tab-pages-the-open-findings-of-a-version-from-the-findings-api-filtered-by-the-cards-bar)) |
| Package page, tab **All versions** | The column **Vulnerabilities** | `<trove-grade>` of each version |
| Vulnerability report (R-VULN-022), a project's and the admin area's security dashboard | The header | `<trove-severity-bar [links]>` of the open findings in scope in place of the five severity counts; the counts **Malicious**, **Needs triage** and **Blocked versions** stay ([Q-UI-376](#q-ui-376--the-reports-header-shows-the-severity-bar-whose-segments-are-its-filter-links)) |

- A caller who gets no grades (signed out, an installation that does not scan, Q-VULN-158) sees no grade column, no card and no
  header grade, not a column of dashes ([Q-UI-377](#q-ui-377--a-list-without-grades-has-no-grade-column)).

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit: the repository content list shows `<trove-grade>` for each row and sorts by grade, worst first, on its second click; the
  opened row grades each version; the package page's header grade links to the tab, the tab shows one card per repository and
  *All versions* a grade per version; the tab asks the findings API for 25 open findings of the version, worst first, says their
  number, and a segment of the card's bar narrows them to its severity; the report's header shows the bar with five filter links;
  without grades no column.
- Rendered (rule 11, `make ui-renders`): the repository content of `npm-internal`, `npm` and `images`, the package pages of the
  npm package and the image with the tabs **Vulnerabilities** and **All versions**, and the vulnerability report of the project
  and of the admin area, as plain user, power user and administrator, light and dark, at 1440, 1024 and 390 px; the seed holds
  versions of the grades S, A, B, C, D, E and N/A.

### R-UI-095 · One search field in the top bar for every caller
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: trove-only

The owner's task T-22 (2026-11-12): "A sensible search, with suggestions and everything." The top bar's field (R-UI-002) is the one
search of the UI.

- **Who gets it.** Every signed-in caller, whatever its roles, and an anonymous caller while the UI runs without a session, which it
  does only while some repository's artifacts are `public` (`publicContent`, R-UI-004,
  [Q-UI-400](#q-ui-400--every-signed-in-caller-gets-the-field-and-an-anonymous-one-while-something-is-public)).
- **The field.** The placeholder "Search or go to…", with " (/)" while `/` is on; a `search` icon at its start; at its end the filter
  button (`filter_list`, accessible name "Filter: <kind>"); while a kind is chosen, a chip with the kind's name and a remove button at
  the field's start. The field fills the top bar's middle column up to 40 rem.
- **The filter** ([Q-UI-402](#q-ui-402--the-filter-is-a-menu-button-at-the-fields-end-and-the-chosen-kind-a-chip-at-its-start)). A
  menu of radio items: **All** (the default), **Repositories**, **Packages**, **Projects**, and for an instance administrator
  (R-UI-099), after a divider, **Users** and **Groups**, each marked **Admin area**. Backspace in an empty field, or the chip's remove
  button, returns to **All**. The kind lasts until the page is reloaded and is part of the results page's address (R-UI-098).
- **Keyboard** ([Q-UI-401](#q-ui-401--slash-focuses-the-field-and-is-on-by-default-the-preference-turns-it-off)). `/` moves the
  focus into the field while the preference `keyboardShortcuts` is on (R-API-021, on by default) and the focus is not in a text
  field, a text area, a select or an editable element; the key is not typed. Ctrl+K, and ⌘K on macOS, does the same whatever the
  preference. An anonymous caller has no preferences and gets Ctrl+K and ⌘K only.
- **Below 36 rem** ([Q-UI-403](#q-ui-403--below-36-rem-a-search-button-opens-the-field-as-a-sheet)). The field gives way to an icon
  button (`search`, accessible name "Search") among the top bar's actions. The button, `/` and Ctrl+K open the search as a sheet: a
  panel over the top bar's full width, `role="dialog"` named "Search", with the field and the filter at its top, a **Close** button,
  and the suggestions below it down to the bottom of the window. The focus stays in the sheet; **Close**, or Escape while no list is
  open, closes it and returns the focus to the button.
- The field asks the server for nothing before it has the focus (R-UI-096) and a text (R-UI-097).

Acceptance criteria:

- The plain user `sam` (`reader` of two projects, no system role) sees the field at 1440 px and the button at 390 px; an anonymous
  visitor of an installation with one public repository sees them too; with nothing public, an anonymous visitor sees the sign-in
  page and no field.
- With `keyboardShortcuts` on, `/` typed on the page body focuses the field and is not typed into it; typed into another text field
  it is typed there; with the preference off, `/` does nothing; Ctrl+K focuses the field either way.
- At 390 px the button opens the sheet with the focus in its field; Escape closes it and the focus is on the button again.

### R-UI-096 · What the opened field offers before anything is typed
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: trove-only

When the field gets the focus without a text, a list opens under it, in this order
([Q-UI-404](#q-ui-404--the-empty-field-offers-the-references-parts-in-its-order-and-the-admin-pages-last)):

1. **Places**: Projects (`/projects`), Guides (`/guides`), Profile (`/profile`), Personal tokens (`/profile/tokens`), each with its
   side-bar icon; an anonymous caller gets Projects and Guides.
2. **Frequently visited repositories**: up to five, each with its format's icon, the key, and "· <project key>" muted.
3. **View all my projects** (`/projects`).
4. **Frequently visited projects**: up to five, each with the project's letter mark (as the project switcher's), the display name,
   and "· <key>" muted.
5. For an instance administrator only (R-UI-099), after a divider: **Admin area**, with Dashboard, Repositories, Users, Groups and
   Settings, each the admin side bar's entry (icon and label, R-UI-002) where the administrator may use it, and each marked
   **Admin area**.

Groups 2 to 4 are not shown to an anonymous caller.

- **Where "frequently visited" is kept**
  ([Q-UI-405](#q-ui-405--frequently-visited-is-kept-in-the-browser-per-principal-by-visits-and-recency)). In browser storage
  (non-secret, R-UI-043), one key per signed-in principal ID, `trove.frequent.<principal ID>`: per repository its qualified name,
  per project its key, each with the number of visits and the time of the last one, at most 20 per kind. A visit is the opening of a
  repository's page or content page, or of a project's screen, and counts once per entry in 15 minutes. The order is the number of
  visits, halved for every 14 days since the last visit, then the last visit. The same store, ordered by the last visit, is the start
  page's **Recently opened** and the project switcher's recent list; it replaces `trove.recent-repositories` and
  `trove.recent-projects.<name>`, which are removed when first read. A route under `/admin` is never recorded. With storage blocked,
  groups 2 and 4 are left out.
- **Only what the caller may still read**
  ([Q-UI-406](#q-ui-406--a-stored-entry-is-shown-after-the-server-confirms-that-the-caller-still-reads-it)). The stored repositories
  are shown after one `GET /api/v1/repositories?name=…` (R-API-063) has returned them, and only those it returned; the stored projects
  when the project list the UI reads once (Q-UI-129) holds them. An entry that is not returned is left out and stays stored. The
  request runs when the list first opens after sign-in, and again after the stored repositories or the caller's authorization epoch
  changed.

Acceptance criteria:

- `sam`, who opened `web-frontend/npm-vendor` three times and `platform/collections` once, sees them in that order; after he loses
  `read` on `platform`, `platform/collections` is not shown and its entry stays stored.
- `ada` (system role `admin`) sees the **Admin area** group last, each entry marked; `sam` and the power user `priya` see no such
  group.
- A second user signed in in the same browser sees none of `sam`'s entries; with storage blocked the list holds Places and **View
  all my projects** only.
- Opening the empty list sends at most the one request of the repositories.

### R-UI-097 · Live suggestions while typing
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: trove-only

- **When** ([Q-UI-408](#q-ui-408--one-request-per-settled-text-250-ms-after-the-last-key-an-anonymous-caller-waits-longer)). A
  signed-in caller's text of two or more characters is sent 250 ms after the last key; an anonymous caller's of three or more after
  500 ms, and at most four times in 4 s. One request per settled text, `GET /api/v1/search/suggestions` (R-API-060) with the kinds of
  the filter; a request a newer text supersedes is cancelled; the answers of the last ten texts are reused for 30 s while the list is
  open. Below the minimum the list shows R-UI-096.
- **Groups and order** ([Q-UI-407](#q-ui-407--the-main-areas-groups-come-first-and-the-admin-areas-last-five-in-each)).
  Repositories, Packages, Projects, Pages; then, for an instance administrator only and after a divider, Admin pages, Users and
  Groups, each group heading and each entry marked **Admin area** (R-UI-099). Five per group, three for Pages and Admin pages; with a
  kind chosen, that group alone with ten. A group without a match is left out. A group of the main area whose answer says `more` ends
  with **All repositories for "<text>"** (packages, projects), which opens the results page on that tab (R-UI-098).
- **An entry** shows: a repository the format's icon, the key and "· <project key>" muted; a package the format's icon, the name
  and "· <project key> / <repository key>" muted; a project the letter mark, the display name and "· <key>" muted; a page its
  side-bar icon and label; a user the avatar (R-UI-002), the display name or the username, "· <username>" muted and **Disabled**
  where it is; a group the `group` icon and the name. Keys and names carry `translate="no"`.
- **Where it leads**: a repository `/projects/<project>/repositories/<key>`; a package its page in the project of the answer's
  repository (`/projects/<project>/packages/<format>/<name>`); a project `/projects/<key>`; a page its route; a user
  `/admin/users/<username>`; a group `/admin/groups/<name>`.
- **Pages** are matched in the browser, in the UI's language, by the project rule of R-API-062 over the labels of the Places of
  R-UI-096 and of Client setup (`/setup`), Sessions (`/profile/sessions`) and Documentation (`/help`); **Admin pages** over the labels
  of the admin side bar's entries the administrator may use.
- **Highlighting** ([Q-UI-409](#q-ui-409--the-matched-text-is-bold-marked-by-the-client)). Every occurrence of each term of the text
  in the shown name is bold (weight 600), case-insensitively; overlapping marks merge. Nothing else is coloured.
- **States.** While a text's first answer is pending, the previous list stays with a quiet "Searching…" line. No match in any group:
  "Nothing you may read matches "<text>". Press Enter to search everything." A `429`: "Too many searches. Suggestions return in
  <n> s.", and no request is sent before its `Retry-After` has passed. Another error: "Suggestions are not available."; Enter still
  works.
- **Keyboard and ARIA** ([Q-UI-410](#q-ui-410--the-field-is-an-aria-combobox-with-a-grouped-listbox)), after the WAI-ARIA Authoring
  Practices' combobox with a listbox popup: the field is `role="combobox"` with `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`,
  `aria-autocomplete="list"` and `aria-activedescendant`; the popup is a `listbox` named "Suggestions" whose groups are `role="group"`
  named by their headings. The focus stays in the field. Down and Up move the active entry: Down from the field enters the list, Up
  from the first entry returns to the text, nothing wraps. Enter opens the active entry; Escape closes the list and, with the list
  closed, empties the field; Tab leaves the field and closes the list; Alt+Down opens the list without moving. After each answer a
  polite live region says how many suggestions are shown, or that none matches.

Acceptance criteria:

- `sam` types `vend`: after 250 ms one request `GET /api/v1/search/suggestions?q=vend&kind=repository,package,project&limit=5`;
  the list shows `npm-vendor · web-frontend` under Repositories with `vend` in bold.
- `ven`, `vend` and `vendo` typed within 200 ms send one request, for `vendo`.
- With the keyboard only: Down, Down, Enter opens the second entry; Escape closes the list and a second Escape empties the field.
- A `429` with `Retry-After: 3` shows the notice, and no request is sent for 3 s.
- axe reports no serious or critical violation with the list open, in both schemes.

### R-UI-098 · Enter opens the results page of the main area
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: trove-only

Enter in the field with no active entry opens `/search?q=<text>&kind=<kind>`
([Q-UI-411](#q-ui-411--enter-without-a-picked-suggestion-opens-search-whose-tabs-read-the-three-lists)), a page of the main area with
the start side bar (R-UI-002); it never opens a route under `/admin` (R-UI-099).

- **Header**: the `<h1>` **Search** and the description "What you may read that matches "<text>"." The top bar's field keeps the text
  while the page is open; the page has no field of its own.
- **Tabs**: **Repositories**, **Packages**, **Projects**, without counts. `kind` chooses the tab; without it, or with `user` or
  `group`, the tab is the first group that had a suggestion when Enter was pressed, else **Repositories**. The tab is part of the
  address.
- **A tab is the list of its kind with `q`**, 25 rows at a time with **Load more** (R-API-010): Repositories, `GET
  /api/v1/repositories?q=`, with the plain user's columns of the repository list (Q-UI-312: the key with the project key as its
  second line, format and class, the client address in the address field of R-UI-065); Packages, `GET /api/v1/packages?q=`, with
  the columns of Q-UI-314 and the project and repository of each; Projects, `GET /api/v1/projects?q=`, with the start page's columns
  (Q-UI-311). A row leads to its object's page in the main area.
- **Empty**: "Nothing you may read matches "<text>"." on the tab. A text of fewer than two characters shows "Type at least two
  characters." and asks nothing.
- The page has no users, groups or admin pages and no link into the admin area. It takes over the page of the stopgap that replaced
  `/admin/repositories?q=` ([Q-UI-415](#q-ui-415--the-stopgaps-results-page-becomes-r-ui-098s)).

Acceptance criteria:

- As `ada` (system role `admin`), `test` and Enter open `/search?q=test`; the page holds no link whose path starts with `/admin`.
- `/search?q=vend&kind=package` opened directly shows the Packages tab, and **Load more** after 25 rows.
- As `sam`, the Repositories tab lists only what `sam` may read; a repository of `platform` with `hideExistence: false` on which
  `sam` holds nothing is not listed.

### R-UI-099 · The search leads into the admin area only by an administrator's choice of a marked suggestion
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: trove-only

The owner (2026-11-12, after typing "test" in the top bar and landing on the admin area's repository list with Enter): a search on
the main page must never end in the admin area, unless live suggestions are shown, some of them are explicitly marked as pages of the
admin area, and the user is an instance admin; then and only then may a search result lead there
([CLAUDE.md](../../CLAUDE.md#product-simple-by-default-details-on-demand)).

- **Instance administrator** ([Q-UI-412](#q-ui-412--an-instance-administrator-is-the-holder-of-the-system-role-admin)): a caller
  whose `GET /api/v1/authz/me` lists the system role `admin` in `roles`, directly or through a group. The other system roles, which
  open the admin area too (R-UI-067), get no admin suggestions and reach their screens through the Admin button.
- **Admin suggestions** are the admin pages, users and groups of R-UI-096 and R-UI-097, shown only to an instance administrator.
  Each shows the mark **Admin area**, the Admin button's icon `build` and the words, which are part of its accessible name ("Users,
  Admin area"); so does each of their group headings. They come after every group of the main area, behind a divider.
- **Only by an explicit choice**: a click on such a suggestion, or Enter while it is the active entry. Enter without an active
  entry, the results page, the filter, the frequently visited entries and every other way out of the field open a route of the main
  area. With the filter on Users or Groups, Enter without an active entry opens nothing and the live region says "Choose a user from
  the list." ("a group") ([Q-UI-413](#q-ui-413--under-a-users-or-groups-filter-enter-without-an-active-entry-opens-nothing)).
- **One gate.** The field opens every target through one function, which refuses a route under `/admin` unless the target is an
  admin suggestion and the caller is an instance administrator at that moment.
- The rule is navigation, not access control: what the admin area shows is decided by the API as before (R-UI-005).

Acceptance criteria:

- As `ada`: `users` shows **Users · Admin area** under Admin pages; Enter without an active entry opens `/search?q=users`; moving to
  that entry and Enter opens `/admin/users`.
- As the holder of `security-admin` alone: `users` shows no admin group, and Enter opens `/search?q=users`.
- A unit test drives every way out of the field (Enter with and without an active entry of each kind, a click on each kind, the
  **All … for** lines, the empty list's entries, the filter) as `ada`, `priya` and `sam` and asserts that only `ada`'s choice of a
  marked entry reaches `/admin`.

## Deferred

P2, Later and Out-of-scope entries of the three catalog pages this page draws on, plus P1 entries
whose owning page defers them. None has a requirement here.

<details>
<summary>P1 catalog entries deferred by an owning page</summary>

- ADMAPI-019 · Global role operations — custom global roles are P2 per R-AUTHZ-026; the fixed system
  roles are listed by `GET /api/v1/roles` (R-API-033)
- ADMAPI-066 · Project role operations — custom project roles are P2 per R-AUTHZ-026; the four fixed project roles
  (reader, developer, maintainer, owner) are assigned through the members operations of R-API-047
- ADMAPI-068 · Environment operations — P2 per R-AUTHZ-026

</details>

<details>
<summary>Content operations (API)</summary>

- API-006 · Last-modified item under a path — P2
- API-012 · Compute SHA-256 for legacy items — P2 (trove computes SHA-256 on every upload, INV-4)
- API-015 · Deploy and extract an archive — P2
- API-017 · Download a single entry from an archive — P2
- API-018 · Download all artifacts of a build as an archive — P2
- API-019 · Download a folder or repository as an archive — P2
- API-020 · Server-side download (cache warm-up) — P2
- API-021 · RubyGems version list — P2
- API-025 · Create a signed download URL — P2
- API-026 · Rotate the signed-URL key — P2
- API-029 · List background tasks — P2 (the job list of R-API-015 covers trove's own jobs)

## Security notes

- **Session versus token.** Session-authenticated writes need the CSRF token, fetch-metadata and
  origin checks of R-AUTH-012 (R-API-006); token-authenticated requests ignore the cookie
  (R-API-005). CORS never allows credentials (R-API-018). Minting tokens and changing grants through
  a session requires recent interactive authentication (R-API-007), so a hijacked session cannot
  quietly produce long-lived credentials.
- **README rendering** has three layers: server-side sanitizing with a strict allowlist, Angular's
  sanitizer, and a CSP with Trusted Types and no inline scripts (R-UI-008, R-UI-001). External
  images are blocked unless an operator lists their exact origin, which then also appears in the
  CSP (Q-UI-6); this keeps viewer addresses and internal package names away from hosts nobody
  chose.
- **Package content in the browser.** The UI builds no content URL from strings and never reads
  package content with `fetch` or XHR (R-UI-001); content reaches the browser only by navigation or
  `img`, under the content headers that the core sets (R-ARCH-007). From P1, an optional content
  origin (R-ARCH-029) keeps the session cookie away from that content, and the UI's CSP names that
  origin in `img-src` only, never in `connect-src`.
- **Lost updates of grants.** PUT and PATCH of revisioned resources require `If-Match`, with
  `If-Match: *` as the explicit blind write (R-API-012), so a stale editor or script cannot
  silently revert a permission policy, a CI identity mapping or the member order of a virtual
  repository. A restore lifts every revision column (R-API-012), so an `If-Match` taken before it
  cannot match a record its sender never saw.
- **Key-ring status without pod access.** Rotation of the stored-secret key ring can be checked and
  finished through the API (R-API-049), which reports key IDs and counts only; operators need no
  shell in a pod, where the key files are readable.
- **Token secrets** appear once, in answers that are `no-store`, uncompressed and never stored for
  idempotency replay (R-API-014, R-API-017, R-API-032), and never leave component state in the
  browser (R-UI-043). Client setup defaults to environment-variable references and generates
  repository-scoped, short-lived tokens (R-UI-016).
- **Claim tester.** The browser decodes pasted ID tokens and sends claims only (R-UI-036); the owning
  page's evaluation endpoint takes claims, not tokens (R-API-035).
- **Information disclosure.** Unreadable repositories, items and packages answer like missing ones
  when hiding is on (R-API-008); `latestVersion` ignores hidden versions (R-API-029); deploy by
  checksum answers the same for missing and unreadable content (R-API-026). A project the caller is no member of
  answers its project routes like a missing project (R-API-008), so the address of a repository does not reveal that
  its project exists. The explainer and effective permissions are limited to `policies:read` and repository managers
  (R-API-034).
- **Error bodies** never carry stack traces, SQL, internal host names, secrets or raw upstream errors
  (R-API-009).
- **Dependency confusion.** The NuGet snippet clears other package sources (R-UI-018); the scoped npm
  variant routes a scope to trove (R-UI-017).
- **Authorization epoch header.** `Trove-Authz-Min-Epoch` is read only after authentication
  succeeded, and ignored without a credential, so an anonymous caller can neither probe the epoch
  nor make a replica wait (R-API-052). A forged high value costs one coalesced epoch read and
  answers `412` at once ([authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-032). Neither a `412` nor a
  header that passes proves whether a change is stored; the object's `ETag` does.
- **Rate limits across replicas.** The general limits count per caller across all replicas in
  Valkey (R-API-016), so adding replicas does not multiply a caller's budget. Valkey's content can
  raise or lower a budget but never grants access; a Valkey outage falls back to per-replica shares
  (H-43, H-49 in [architecture.md](architecture.md)). The break-glass lockout stays in PostgreSQL.
- **Backups through the API.** The API and UI only read backup runs from PostgreSQL. `web` replicas
  never hold the backup target's credentials, and no endpoint starts, deletes or restores a backup
  (R-API-050, Q-API-10), so neither a hijacked session nor a compromised `web` replica can read or
  destroy backups through trove, and the chart grants trove no Kubernetes permission that could
  start a pod with the backup role's identity.
- **Status payloads.** The system status answers show internal facts (node names, the Valkey
  primary's address, the backup target's bucket and prefix) to `system.read` holders only, and
  never credentials, ACL user names or key material (R-API-038, R-API-050).

## Decisions

Each question below was decided by the development agent from the listed options; the owner reviews the choices at the walkthrough.

### Q-API-1 · OpenAPI generation approach

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Spec-first; generated Go server interface and TypeScript types | `api/openapi.yaml` is written by hand. [oapi-codegen](https://github.com/oapi-codegen/oapi-codegen) generates Go models and the `net/http` server interface; [openapi-typescript](https://openapi-ts.dev/) generates TypeScript types; thin hand-written Angular clients use them | The contract can be reviewed before code exists; drift between document and server, and between document and UI, is a compile error; a missing handler does not compile; routing stays on `ServeMux` (R-ARCH-005) and the UI on `httpResource()` (R-UI-046) | oapi-codegen calls its 3.1 support "initial" (v2.8.0, [release notes](https://github.com/oapi-codegen/oapi-codegen/releases)), so a construct may need an equivalent spelling |
| (b) Spec-first; generated Angular client | As (a) on the Go side; the Angular side is a generated `HttpClient` service layer (for example [ng-openapi-gen](https://github.com/cyclosproject/ng-openapi-gen)) | Less hand-written client code | The generator's output decides how every service looks and is built around observables, while R-UI-046 reads server state through `httpResource()` and signals; one more generator to move in step with every Angular major |
| (c) Code-first | Go types and handler registrations produce the document (for example [Huma](https://huma.rocks/)) | No hand-written YAML; the document cannot lag behind the code | Inverts INV-6's "source of truth": the contract changes as a side effect of code changes; handlers depend on a framework instead of `net/http` |
| (d) Spec-first; types only | Generated Go and TypeScript types; routes and parameter binding written by hand, guarded by the route-parity check of R-API-002 | No dependence on a generator's server code | Parameter parsing and route registration by hand for every operation of Part B; a forgotten handler shows up in CI, not at compile time |

**Choice:** (a) — the hand-written OpenAPI 3.1 document generates Go models and the `net/http` server interface through oapi-codegen and TypeScript types through openapi-typescript, and thin hand-written Angular clients use them.

**Rationale:** For one developer building the whole surface of Part B, compile errors are the cheapest guard against drift, and (a) produces them on both sides while keeping two choices already made elsewhere: `net/http.ServeMux` on the server and signals with `httpResource()` in the UI. (b) would put a generated, observable-based service layer between the UI and those primitives; (c) gives up the reviewable contract INV-6 asks for; (d) costs hand-written parsing for every operation and gains nothing over (a) as long as the generator handles the constructs. The young 3.1 support is contained without hand-written types: a fixture document with every construct the contract uses is generated in CI, and a construct the generator mishandles is written in an equivalent form (`enum: [x]` for `const: x`). Permission enforcement does not depend on the generator at all: the authorization step reads the declarations from the embedded document by matched route pattern, and a route without one stops start-up. The strict-server variant is left out because handlers set `ETag`, `Location`, `Link` and `Retry-After` themselves and stream answers. The development agent revisits this if the fixture shows a construct with no equivalent form, or if the generator's 3.1 line stops moving; the fallback is (d), with the document and the TypeScript side unchanged.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-002 now specifies the generation pipeline (oapi-codegen `models` and `std-http-server` into `internal/api/v1/gen/`, `/files` operations excluded; openapi-typescript into `web/src/app/api/generated/`), the start-up table of authorization declarations keyed by `http.Request.Pattern` that fails closed, the 3.1 construct fixture, and two new acceptance criteria. R-UI-046 names openapi-typescript. The layout changes (`internal/api/v1/gen/`, `web/src/app/api/generated/`, the generator pins) are applied in [architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-003 and R-ARCH-004 (Q-ARCH-1 there).

### Q-API-2 · Is If-Match mandatory on writes?

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Optional unless the owning page requires it | Optional by default; an owning page may require it (permission policies do); the switch `api.require_if_match` makes it mandatory everywhere | Scripts can overwrite without thinking about it | Each owning page has to recognize which of its fields are dangerous to lose; two behaviors to test |
| (b) Required on PUT and PATCH of revisioned resources; `If-Match: *` as the deliberate blind write | One rule for every resource with a revision ETag; 428 without the header; DELETE and delta-style edits exempt | No lost update wherever a full document or a whole array is written; a blind write stays possible but is explicit; the rule is derived from the document, with no switch | Every script that writes configuration sends one more header; curl examples get longer |
| (c) Required only on grant-defining resources | Mandatory for permission policies, CI issuers and identity mappings, and authentication settings; optional elsewhere | Friction only where a reverted change re-opens access | The list is a judgement call that misses cases: a stale write of a virtual repository's `members` (arrays are replaced whole, R-API-013) can put a remote member ahead of the local one again, a dependency-confusion path |

**Choice:** (b) — `If-Match` is required on every PUT and PATCH of a resource that carries a revision ETag, `If-Match: *` is the explicit blind write, and DELETE and delta-style edits are exempt.

**Rationale:** In trove a lost update is a security problem more often than it looks: besides permission policies, the member order of a virtual repository and the conditions of a CI identity mapping decide which package a client receives and who may publish. (a) and (c) depend on someone recognizing each such field; (b) makes the safe behavior the default for all of them, and the UI already sends the header everywhere. The argument against a mandatory header, scripts that overwrite on purpose, is answered by `If-Match: *` ([RFC 9110 §13.1.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110#section-13.1.1)), which keeps blind writes possible and makes them visible in the request. DELETE is exempt because a deletion means to remove whatever version exists; delta edits (`add`/`remove` lists, role bindings, assignments) are exempt because they cannot overwrite another writer's change. A script over the document checks the rule, and dropping the switch leaves one behavior to test. The development agent revisits this if a client tool that matters to the owner cannot send request headers.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-012 states the rule, the exempt list and the 428 answer ([RFC 6585](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6585#section-3)), and gains two acceptance criteria; the configuration key `api.require_if_match` is removed. R-API-002 adds the operation marker `x-trove-if-match`. R-API-013's acceptance criterion and R-API-023's `batch-update` send the precondition. The security notes gain "Lost updates of grants". Pages that own revisioned resources get the 428 answer as a cross-page edit.

### Q-API-3 · Cluster-wide rate limiting

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Revisited on 2026-10-28 after the owner added the Valkey, horizontal-scale, backup and storage-class constraints: the choice moves from (a), per-replica buckets by design, to the new option (e), cluster-wide counters in Valkey with a per-replica fallback, the limiter of [architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-034 (Q-ARCH-17 there); H-43 now covers only the fallback and lost counters.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Per replica, in memory, for every class | Token buckets in each replica's memory, as R-API-016 and the identity and CI pages specified until 2026-10-28 | No shared state and no round trip per request | The cluster-wide budget is the configured value times a replica count that grows with the load and changes with autoscaling; the Service spreads one client's requests over every replica, so the client gets that multiple; the answer depends on the replica a request reaches (INV-18) |
| (b) Shared PostgreSQL counters for unauthenticated classes, per replica for the rest | Login starts, revoke-by-value, the CI exchange and anonymous requests counted in PostgreSQL | A cluster-wide ceiling for callers without credentials | A database write on every unauthenticated request, so a flood lands on the system of record |
| (c) Shared PostgreSQL counters for every class | Every API request updates a counter row | One exact cluster-wide limit | A write per request on the hottest path and row contention on the counter of a busy token; the limiter becomes a denial-of-service lever against PostgreSQL |
| (d) Per replica, sized as cluster limit ÷ live replica count | Each replica divides the configured budget by the replica count of the registry | Approximates a cluster-wide limit without shared state | kube-proxy balances connections, not requests: a client whose keep-alive connection stays on one replica gets 1/n of its budget; small bursts round down to nothing; the limit moves with every scale event |
| (e) Cluster scope in Valkey, per-replica fallback | A sliding-window counter per bucket in Valkey (R-ARCH-034); while Valkey is unavailable, (d) as the fallback | One budget at any replica count and the same answer on every replica; no write on PostgreSQL; Valkey is part of every production topology (INV-12) | One pipelined Valkey round trip per limited request; the sliding window approximates; during a Valkey outage the fallback has (d)'s weaknesses |

**Choice:** (e) — the classes `read`, `write` and `anonymous` count cluster-wide in Valkey through the limiter of R-ARCH-034 and fall back to per-replica shares of the budget while Valkey is unavailable.

**Rationale:**
- The earlier choice rested on two premises that no longer hold. The classes were to protect the
  resources of one replica, and shared counters would have written to PostgreSQL. Under the owner's
  constraints the load exceeds one replica, the replica count follows the load, and the Service
  spreads one client's requests over all replicas. Under (a), a budget of 50 reads per second would
  mean 150 at three replicas and 1,500 at thirty: not a value an operator can set. Valkey is now
  part of every production topology and takes the counter writes off PostgreSQL, which removes the
  reason (b) and (c) were rejected for.
- Replica protection does not need these classes: `server.max_in_flight` stays per replica
  (R-ARCH-005) and is the right unit for CPU and memory.
- The fallback divides by the live `web` replicas, so a Valkey outage keeps the budget near its
  configured value instead of multiplying it, and the identity and CI pages use the same limiter,
  so one rule covers every class.
- Credential guessing is still no argument either way: tokens are 256-bit random values, and the
  break-glass lockout counts in PostgreSQL (R-AUTH-038) because it must survive a loss of Valkey's
  data.
- The development agent revisits this if the limiter's round trip shows up in P-2
  ([architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-027): read classes would then check a local bucket
  first and ask Valkey only near the limit. A per-tenant quota (BEYOND-030, P2) that needs exact
  counts would get a limiter of its own.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-016 is rewritten: purpose (fair share, not replica protection), the limiter names, the sliding window and its fallback at the budget ÷ live `web` replicas, refused requests counting against the window as R-ARCH-034 specifies, `Retry-After` and the `RateLimit` fields with sliding-window values, and acceptance criteria across three replicas with and without Valkey and for a client that ignores `Retry-After`. The earlier statement that the buckets are kept in memory per replica by design is removed. H-43 is narrowed to Valkey outages and to counters lost in a failover; tampering with the counters is H-49 in [architecture.md](architecture.md). The security notes gain "Rate limits across replicas". No configuration key changes; the values are now cluster-wide budgets. Cross-page: none beyond those of Q-ARCH-17 in [architecture.md](architecture.md), which already names R-API-016, this question and H-43.

### Q-API-4 · INV-17's wording and byte transfers on `/files`

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Amend INV-17's wording | INV-17 says: the UI uses only public, documented endpoints (the operations of the OpenAPI document, `/api/v1/…` and `/files/…`, plus the browser sign-in flow under `/auth/…`) and no private UI endpoint | States the purpose, every UI action is scriptable, instead of a path prefix; matches what R-API-002 documents | Touches an invariant |
| (b) Mirror byte transfer under `/api/v1/` | `…/items/content?path=` duplicates `/files` | INV-17's text stays | A second code path for the largest transfers (ranges, digests, streaming) with nothing gained; two URLs for the same bytes |
| (c) Keep INV-17's text and define its reading on this page | R-API-002 says what "public `/api/v1` API" means | No invariant edit | Someone who reads INV-17 alone concludes that the UI's use of `/files` and `/auth` violates it; invariant and page disagree in their words |

**Choice:** (a) — INV-17 is amended to "public, documented endpoints: the operations of the OpenAPI document (`/api/v1/…`, `/files/…`) and the browser sign-in flow under `/auth/…`; no private UI endpoints".

**Rationale:** INV-17 exists so that everything the UI does can be scripted; `/files` is described in the same OpenAPI document and is as scriptable as `/api/v1`, and the UI cannot sign in without the browser flow under `/auth/`, which R-AUTH-005 and R-AUTH-013 own. (b) builds a second byte path for the heaviest traffic only to satisfy a wording; (c) leaves an invariant that its own pages contradict, which is how invariants stop being read. The development agent revisits this only if the UI ever needs an endpoint the document does not describe, which this wording forbids.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-002 refers to the amended INV-17. The invariant text itself is a cross-page edit to [README.md](README.md) (INV-17), with the matching sentence in ADR-028.

### Q-API-5 · Owning page for build information

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A new page `builds.md` with prefix `R-BLD` | Owns the record schema, the mapping of CI job names (which contain `/`) to `{buildName}`, promotion and run retention; uses the build permissions of R-AUTHZ-027 | One owner for one model; [authorization.md](authorization.md) (Q-AUTHZ-8) and [storage.md](storage.md) (Q-STOR-3) reach the same answer | One more page to write before P1 build work |
| (b) Fold it into [gitlab-ci-oidc.md](gitlab-ci-oidc.md) | GitLab CI is the main producer of build records | Close to the producer | Mixes CI authentication with a resource model that changes for other reasons; other CI systems upload builds too |
| (c) Fold it into [operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) | Treat build records as operational data | No new page | Build records have permissions, promotion and retention of their own; operations would own an unrelated model |
| (d) Fold it into [storage.md](storage.md) | Storage already specifies build retention (RET-023, RET-037) | Retention mechanics sit next to the records | Storage would own two models; promotion and permissions are not storage concerns |

**Choice:** (a) — build information gets its own page `builds.md` (`R-BLD`), written before P1 build work starts; until then R-API-042 reserves the paths.

**Rationale:** Build records are a model with their own lifecycle: upload, promotion with copy or move, permissions and retention. Each of (b) to (d) would make a page the owner of two models that change for different reasons, and the three pages that raised the gap all concluded the same. Build information is P1, so the MVP prototype needs none of it; reserving the paths now keeps them from being taken by something else. The development agent revisits this if build information moves to P2, in which case the page waits with it.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-020 names `builds.md` as owner; R-API-042 states the page's scope, that the MVP implements none of it, and that the paths are reserved; R-UI-040 points its acceptance criteria to that page. Adding the page to the page table is a cross-page edit to [README.md](README.md).

### Q-API-6 · Pagination parameter names

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `limit` and `cursor` everywhere | Every list endpoint uses R-API-010's names and its envelope (`items`, `nextCursor`) | Already used by every page except [repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md) and by the job API; one page changes | None beyond that one page's edit |
| (b) `pageSize` and `pageToken` everywhere | Every list endpoint follows the repository list | Familiar from some public API style guides | Every other page, R-API-010, the job API and the UI's list handling change |

**Choice:** (a) — `limit` and `cursor`, with the `items` and `nextCursor` envelope, on every list endpoint.

**Rationale:** Uniform names let the UI and generated clients page through every list with one helper; (a) gets there by changing one page, (b) by changing all others. The development agent would revisit this only if a client ecosystem trove must serve required other names, and none does: package-manager protocols keep their own paging outside `/api/v1/`.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-010 states that the names and the envelope are the same on every list endpoint, with no per-page variants. The repository list's `pageSize`, `pageToken` and `nextPageToken` are a cross-page edit to [repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md).

### Q-API-7 · Syntax of custom methods

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Sub-path verbs everywhere, with reserved names | `POST /api/v1/repositories/batch-create`, `/quick-setup`; any literal segment in a key position is a reserved name of that collection | One form for every action on every page; plain `ServeMux` patterns; the reserved-name rule also fixes literals that already shadow keys elsewhere | Five repository keys become reserved |
| (b) Colon methods for collection actions | `POST /api/v1/repositories:batchCreate`; sub-paths for item actions | Collection actions never share a segment with keys | Two syntaxes for one concept; the shadowing on other collections remains; legal in a path segment ([RFC 3986](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3986#section-3.3)) but unusual in route tables and curl commands |
| (c) A batch resource | `POST /api/v1/repository-batches` with an `operation` field | No verbs in paths | Operations with different semantics (all-or-nothing 200 for create and update, best-effort 202 for delete) behind one operation and one discriminated `oneOf` body; quick setup does not fit |
| (d) Collection actions behind a segment the key grammar excludes | `POST /api/v1/repositories/-/batch-create`; repository keys start with `[a-z0-9]` (INV-5), so `-` can never be a key | No repository key is reserved | An unusual URL shape found nowhere else in `/api/v1/`; it does not help the literals that already sit in key positions (`/users/me`, `/webhooks/deliveries`), so the reserved-name rule is needed anyway |

**Choice:** (a) — every action, on an item or on a collection, is a kebab-case sub-path verb, and literal segments in a key position are reserved names.

**Rationale:** The decisive point is that the collision (b) and (d) avoid for repositories exists anyway on other collections: `GET /api/v1/webhooks/deliveries` makes a webhook keyed `deliveries` unreachable, and `/api/v1/users/me` a user named `me`, because the router prefers the literal. A reserved-name rule is therefore needed whatever this question decides; once it exists, the only advantage of (b) and (d) is that five repository names stay free, and the price is a second URL shape. (c) merges operations whose answers differ in status and atomicity. Declaring the reserved names in the OpenAPI document and deriving the literal siblings in CI turns a silent shadowing bug into a failing check. The development agent revisits this if an import from another system must keep a repository key that collides with a reserved verb; (d) is then the fallback for repositories alone.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-004 now uses the sub-path form for collection actions and adds the reserved-name rule (422 `reserved_name`, `x-trove-reserved-names`, a CI check, an acceptance criterion); R-API-009 lists `reserved_name`; R-API-023 and R-UI-023 use `/batch-create`, `/batch-update`, `/batch-get`, `/batch-delete` and `/quick-setup`. The cross-page edits are the repository paths and reserved keys in [repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md), and the reserved names `me` for users, `test`, `deliveries` and `event-types` for webhooks, and `disable-all` for retention policies on their owning pages.

### Q-API-8 · Stored-secret key-ring status through the API

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

An earlier revision of this page listed `GET /api/v1/system/encryption`; it was dropped because R-ARCH-021 offers key-ring status only through `trove admin secrets status`. This question decides whether the UI and monitoring get that status through the API.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Command line only | `trove admin secrets status`, as R-ARCH-021 specifies | Nothing new to build | Checking a rotation needs a shell in a pod, where the key files themselves are readable; no UI view; nothing alerts when two replicas' rings disagree |
| (b) Read-only status endpoint, metrics and a UI card; re-encryption through the task trigger | `GET /api/v1/system/encryption` with key IDs, counts, canary state and every replica's key IDs; `trove_secrets_*` metrics; the `secrets-reencrypt` task started through `POST /api/v1/system/tasks/{name}/run` and refused while the rings are incompatible | A rotation can be checked and finished without pod access; monitoring can alert on incompatible rings and on values left under a retired key; the API refuses the one step that would break decryption | One endpoint, two metrics and one card to build; replicas publish their key IDs |
| (c) Metrics only | Gauges per key ID on the operations listener | Monitoring without a new API | No UI view; no guarded way to start re-encryption; operators still need a pod shell to finish a rotation |
| (d) Key management through the API | Upload a new key and set the active key through the API | Rotation without touching Kubernetes | Key material travels through the API and must rest somewhere: in PostgreSQL it sits next to the values it protects, in a Secret written by trove it needs write access to Secrets; both break the separation ADR-032 relies on |
| (e) Endpoint and guarded task in the MVP, metrics and UI card in P1 | (b) split by priority | The smallest MVP that still removes the pod shell and guards re-encryption | The metrics and the card read the payload the endpoint already computes, so the split saves little; without the gauge nothing alerts on a mixed-ring cluster, the state in which upstream credentials stop decrypting on some replicas |

**Choice:** (b) — a read-only key-ring status endpoint with metrics and a card on the system status screen, and re-encryption started through the task trigger, which refuses to run while the replicas' rings are incompatible.

**Rationale:** Today an operator follows the four rotation steps of R-HA-027 and checks two of them with `trove admin secrets status`, which in Kubernetes means `kubectl exec` into a pod, a right that also reads the key files. (b) exposes exactly the state a rotation needs (key IDs, counts, which replica holds which key) and nothing secret. It also covers a case the command cannot see: a running replica whose ring lacks a key that another replica has since made active cannot open the values sealed with it. The command sees only its own pod; the endpoint sees every replica through the registry, and the re-encryption task refuses to start in that state. (c) gives alerts but no guarded action; (d) moves key material into the system it protects; (e) saves only two gauges and one card, because both render the payload the endpoint already computes. The whole of (b) is MVP because the key ring and its rotation are MVP (R-ARCH-021, R-HA-027), the per-key counting already exists for `trove admin secrets status`, and the system status screen that shows the card is MVP (R-UI-038). The development agent revisits this when a key source backed by an external key management service arrives (ADR-032 names it as a later option), whose status would extend this payload.

**Applied in the spec:** New requirement R-API-049 (MVP, payload, rules, acceptance criteria), which starts re-encryption as the manual task `secrets-reencrypt` whose job kind carries the same name; R-API-020 lists it; R-UI-038 gains the "Stored-secret keys" card with "Re-encrypt now" and states why the screen is MVP; the security notes gain "Key-ring status without pod access"; the page's Covers list adds HA-016. Cross-page edits: the endpoint, the shared implementation and the job kind renamed from `secrets_reencrypt` to `secrets-reencrypt` in [architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-016 and R-ARCH-021; the replica registry columns, the manual task `secrets-reencrypt` and the two metrics in [operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md); the status check in the rotation steps of [ha-and-helm.md](ha-and-helm.md) R-HA-027; the MVP status of the UI status screen in R-OPS-003 and in [ha-and-helm.md](ha-and-helm.md) R-HA-003 and Q-HA-12, which still call it P1; the HA-016 row of the coverage checklist.

### Q-API-9 · One path for starting, stopping and reading maintenance work

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

The owning pages specified two paths for the same functions: [storage.md](storage.md) starts and stops garbage collection through `/api/v1/maintenance/gc-runs` and refreshes the storage summary at `/api/v1/storage/summary/refresh`, while [operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) starts both through `/api/v1/system/tasks/{name}/run` and reads the summary at `/api/v1/system/storage/summary`.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Domain paths only | storage.md's start, stop and refresh paths; the task trigger refuses these tasks | Each owning page shapes its own API | The system status screen and scripts need a special case per task; two ways to stop work (domain stop and job cancel) |
| (b) Generic paths only | Start through `/system/tasks/{name}/run`, stop through `/system/jobs/{id}/cancel`, results only in job results and under `/system/` | One mechanism, no domain views | Loses the domain view (counts and reclaimed bytes per run, history with filters) that a generic job result serves poorly |
| (c) Generic start and stop, domain read views | Start and stop through the task and job endpoints of R-OPS-019; the owning page keeps read-only views of runs and results under its own prefix | One way to start and stop every task, so "Run now" on the status screen works for all of them; domain data stays with its owner; matches R-API-015's "domain view that references the job" | Two pages change paths |

**Choice:** (c) — every singleton maintenance task starts only through `POST /api/v1/system/tasks/{name}/run` and stops only through job cancel, and owning pages keep read-only domain views.

**Rationale:** Start and stop are the same operation for every task, with the same mutual exclusion and the same 409 when a run is active (R-OPS-019); one implementation serves every task and the system status screen needs no special case. What differs per task is the result, and that belongs to the owning page, which is what R-API-015 already allows. (a) duplicates the trigger per task; (b) pushes domain data into generic job results. The task trigger already takes task parameters (`{"dryRun": true}`), and storage.md models incremental and full collection as two tasks with one schedule each, so nothing is lost; [storage.md](storage.md) reached the same answer in Q-STOR-10. The rule covers singleton tasks only: retention policies run per policy with their own queue, run states and reports (R-STOR-041), which the generic task list does not model, so their run and stop paths stay on [storage.md](storage.md). The development agent revisits this if a task needs a start contract the generic trigger cannot express.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-020 replaces the "until review settles them" paragraph with the rule, its scope (singleton tasks; per-resource actions and retention runs keep their paths) and an acceptance criterion; R-API-040 starts garbage collection (tasks `gc` and `gc-full`, as [storage.md](storage.md) now defines them), the orphan sweep, the scrub and the storage-summary refresh through the task trigger, stops runs through job cancel, lists runs through `GET /api/v1/system/jobs?kind=…`, and keeps `GET /api/v1/storage/summary` and `GET /api/v1/storage/damaged-blobs` as the read paths; R-API-049 starts re-encryption the same way. Cross-page edits to [storage.md](storage.md), [operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) and the GC acceptance criterion of [ha-and-helm.md](ha-and-helm.md) R-HA-002.

### Q-API-10 · Starting a backup from the API or the UI

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

The owner requires a configurable backup job, comparable to GitLab's, that writes a consistent backup to S3 when it runs (INV-19).
