### Q-UI-91 · The endpoint binding in the token forms

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

A token is bound to endpoints through `scope.endpoints` ([endpoints.md](endpoints.md) R-EP-011); a further endpoint accepts only service-account tokens bound to it (Q-EP-10). The forms had no field, so the binding needed the API or `trove admin token`.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Record the gap as decided | The binding stays an API and CLI matter | No change | The customer-endpoint flow of Q-EP-10 needs a bound token per customer; an administrator who works in the UI has no way to issue one |
| (b) A field in both token forms, fed by `GET /api/v1/endpoints`, shown with `endpoints:read` | One checkbox per configured endpoint (inert ones left out); none ticked leaves the token unbound; the selection joins `scope.endpoints` of either scope kind | The list exists and the scope already carries the field; the server still validates every name (`400 invalid_scope`) | A caller without `endpoints:read` cannot bind from the UI |
| (c) A free-text field in the service-account form only | Names typed by hand | No dependency on the list | Typos are found only by the server; the personal form has the same need on an endpoint with other token types |

**Choice:** (b), offering only the endpoints whose accepted token types (`configuration.auth.tokenTypes` of the endpoint list) include the type of the token the form creates: `pat` for a personal token, `sat` for a service account's. The server refuses any other binding with `400` `invalid_scope` (R-EP-011), so the form never offers a token that would work nowhere.

**Rationale:** The API gives the UI what it needs, and the field changes only where a token is accepted, never what it may do. A caller without `endpoints:read` sees no field and issues an unbound token, which is the default of R-EP-011. The development agent revisits this if an endpoint can bind tokens of a user to a different set than the endpoint list shows, or if the list grows beyond what checkboxes carry.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-026, R-UI-029; [endpoints.md](endpoints.md) R-EP-011 is unchanged.

### Q-UI-92 · What "Revoke by value" says after the empty 202

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

`POST /api/v1/tokens/revoke` answers `200` with the token's id and owner to an administrator and an empty `202` to everyone else and for an unknown value (R-AUTH-029, Q-AUTH-6: no existence oracle). The screen built "The token of … was revoked" from a body the `202` does not have.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The same sentence in both cases | "Revoked." | Simple | False for an unknown value; the screen would be the oracle's opposite, a claim the server does not make |
| (b) Name the owner after a `200`, a neutral sentence after a `202` | "The token of alice was revoked." / "The request was accepted. If the value is a token, it is revoked; this answer does not say whether it was one." | Says only what the answer supports; no new oracle | The user without the admin role gets no confirmation that the token existed |
| (c) Show the sentence only for an administrator and nothing otherwise | Silence after a `202` | No wrong claim | A user who pasted a leaked value cannot tell the request arrived |

**Choice:** (b).

**Rationale:** The screen reports the HTTP answer, not a guess about the database. The development agent revisits this if the server's answer for non-administrators changes.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-030.

### Q-UI-93 · How the package page shows NuGet metadata and the listed state

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

R-UI-007 asks for NuGet target frameworks, dependency groups, authors and project URL on the Metadata tab, and R-NUGET-006 gives a version a `listed` flag. `PackageVersion.metadata` is "format-specific, owned by the format page", and the page so far read npm's members only.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The same Metadata tab reads the NuGet members | `dependencyGroups` (a list of `targetFramework` and `dependencies` of `id` and `range`), `authors` (a string or a list), `projectUrl`, `licenseUrl`, `repositoryUrl` and `listed`; a member that is absent is not shown; no branch on the format name | One screen for every format; the format owns the keys; a format that sends none of them shows nothing | The tab knows the key names of two formats |
| (b) A component per format | The page picks a NuGet component by `format` | Each format can lay out freely | Contradicts R-UI-019 (a new format needs no new screen) and puts format knowledge into the UI |
| (c) Add `listed` to `PackageVersionSummary` as well | The versions table shows the state per version | The table is complete | An API change in a generated schema for one format; the list of a version page is a minority path |

**Choice:** (a). `listed: false` shows a banner "Unlisted." above the tabs of the selected version, with the sentence that the version is hidden from search and still downloaded when a project asks for exactly it (R-NUGET-006). The dependencies are grouped by the target framework verbatim as the nuspec declares it (R-NUGET-007), a group without one is "All frameworks", a group without dependencies says so. URLs follow the http and https rule of R-UI-007. The ID is shown as the server serves it, in its original casing.

**Rationale:** The metadata object is the contract between a format's view adapter and the UI, and a tolerant reader costs less than a second screen. The versions table does not carry the state; the version page does, and a reader who looks for unlisted versions opens them from there. The development agent revisits this if users need to see unlisted versions in the "All versions" table, which is option (c) as an additive field.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-007 names the NuGet members the Metadata tab reads; [formats/nuget.md](formats/nuget.md) R-NUGET-007's metadata table is the source of the keys. The view adapter maps the nuspec keys to the members above and adds `listed` (from the version row) and `repositoryUrl` (the `url` of the nuspec's `repository` element); a member it does not send is not shown.

### Q-UI-94 · The NuGet clients and the explanations of their snippets

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Q-UI-70 left the client table of the UI with npm and said that the NuGet clients arrive with the format. R-NUGET-026 names the supported clients: the .NET SDK, nuget.exe and Visual Studio.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Three clients, `dotnet`, `nuget` and `visual-studio`, each with the explanations of its snippets by id | The table gets one entry, `nuget`; `snippetExplanation` knows the ids `dotnet.configure.add-source`, `dotnet.configure.nuget-config`, `nuget.configure.nuget-config`, `nuget.configure.sources-add`, `visual-studio.configure.source`, `<client>.install` and `dotnet.publish`/`nuget.publish` | Matches the clients R-NUGET-026 supports and the catalog's `clients`; an id the server sends without an entry shows the snippet without a sentence | The ids are a contract with the format's setup templates |
| (b) One client `dotnet` | The snippets cover the SDK only | Smallest | nuget.exe and Visual Studio users get no instructions, which R-NUGET-026 and R-UI-019 promise |
| (c) Read the clients from `GET /api/v1/formats` | The UI table disappears | No second list | Q-UI-70 chose the table so the explanations can be translated; the descriptor does not carry them |

**Choice:** (a). Visual Studio has a configure and an install snippet and no publish snippet (the IDE does not push); the setup page shows the Publish tab's "cannot publish" hint for it as for any client without one. The labels are product names and are not translated: ".NET CLI (dotnet)", "NuGet CLI (nuget.exe)", "Visual Studio".

**Rationale:** The explanation texts are the UI's and are translated (R-UI-045); the ids are the stable part of the server's answer (R-API-030). The development agent revisits this when the format's templates use other ids (the explanation would then be missing and the snippet shown without a sentence) or when a further NuGet client is supported.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-018 names the three clients and the snippets the page shows; the table row of Q-UI-70 reads "npm and NuGet".

### Q-UI-95 · What the NuGet browser journey covers

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

R-UI-047 gives each format a browser journey. The npm journey publishes a package through the npm protocol; a NuGet package is a zip with a nuspec, and the journey has no NuGet client.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Repositories, setup, guide, wizard and edit form; no package | The journey creates a local and a virtual repository through the API, checks the three clients' snippets against the repository's `index.json` URL, the guide, the wizard's `deleteMode` and the edit form, with axe in both colour schemes | Runs without a NuGet client; the package page is covered by the component tier and by the NuGet client matrix of the end-to-end suite | The package list and detail with a real package are not seen in a browser |
| (b) Build a nupkg in the test and push it | Zip writing in the journey | The package page is seen too | A zip writer and a nuspec fixture in TypeScript, a second copy of the fixtures of the Go tests |
| (c) Push with the .NET SDK in a container | Real client | Highest fidelity | Needs a container in the browser tier; the matrix does this already |

**Choice:** (a). `web/e2e/tests/11-nuget.spec.ts` is written and runs with the other journeys on the kind stack.

**Rationale:** The part of the screen that depends on the server's rendering (the snippets, the settings schema, the guide) is what a browser journey adds; the package page depends on metadata the component tier fixes. The development agent revisits this when the NuGet matrix publishes a package that a journey can open by name.

**Applied in the spec:** none; [developer/web-ui.md](../developer/web-ui.md) lists the journey.

### Q-UI-96 · cogpit blue as the primary colour, green only for positive status

Status: **Decided by the owner on 2026-11-02.** **Superseded by [Q-UI-128](#q-ui-128--the-references-type-colours-and-measures)**
for the blue: the accent is the reference's blue since 2026-11-06; green still marks a positive status only.

Context: Q-UI-88 took the green of the owner's example screens as trove's one accent, so green marked the current
navigation entry, the primary button, links, the focus ring and a selected row as well as a positive status
(`--trove-status-ok` was the accent green). The owner wants the blue of his other product, cogpit, as the regular primary
colour, and green only for a positive status. cogpit's palettes (`internal/ui/fyneui/theme.go` in guided-traffic/cogpit)
give: dark primary `#4aa8ff` (glow blue) with `#04111f` on it, hyperlink `#7cc4ff`, selection `#22406a`, focus the
primary at alpha `0xaa`; light primary `#0a6fd6` with white on it, hyperlink `#0a62c2`, selection `#cfe2ff`, focus
`#0a6fd6` at alpha `0x99`.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) cogpit's blue as the primary, green for a positive status only | The accent, the link, the focus ring, the selection fills and the navigation's accent take cogpit's values; `--trove-status-ok` keeps its green | The owner's two products share one accent; green has one meaning, "fine", instead of "here", "go" and "fine" at once | Departs from the example screens' green; cogpit's light primary and its translucent focus miss WCAG AA on some of trove's surfaces and need the rule of Q-UI-88 |
| (b) Keep green | Q-UI-88 as built | No change | A positive status and the accent are one colour, so a green mark does not say which of the two it is; not what the owner wants |

**Choice:** (a). Where a cogpit value misses AA on a surface of trove, the rule of Q-UI-88 applies (darkened in the light
scheme, lightened in the dark one, in its own hue):

- The light primary is `#0a62c2`, cogpit's own light hyperlink, for the primary as a whole. cogpit's `#0a6fd6` is 4.9:1
  on white but 4.0:1 on the filled form field (`#e4e7ec`), 4.2:1 on a dialog and 4.47:1 on a hovered row, so a focused
  label would fail; `#0a62c2` is 5.9:1 on white and under white text, 4.8:1 on the field, 5.1:1 on a dialog. One value
  for the whole primary rather than one per use, because Material reads the same `primary` token for the filled button,
  the focused label and the checkbox.
- The dark primary is `#4aa8ff` with `#04111f` on it, as in cogpit: 7.8:1 on the page, 5.7:1 on the field, 7.5:1 on a
  filled button.
- Links take cogpit's hyperlink through a new token, `--trove-link`: `#0a62c2` in the light scheme (the primary itself),
  `#7cc4ff` in the dark one (10.5:1 on the page).
- The focus ring stays a solid 2 px line in the primary: cogpit's light focus at alpha `0x99` is 2.5:1 on white, below the
  3:1 of WCAG 1.4.11.
- `primary-container` is cogpit's selection (`#cfe2ff`, `#22406a`); `secondary-container`, the fill of the selected tree
  item, the current audit row and the active access tab, is cogpit's selected row (`#d6e6ff`, `#183252`); the text on
  both is cogpit's selected-row text (`#0b1a33`, `#f2f7ff`).
- The navigation's accent (`--trove-nav-accent`, and in the dark scheme the current entry's text and fill) is cogpit's
  glow blue `#4aa8ff` in both schemes, because the frame is dark in both: 4.7:1 on the light side bar.
- The Material base palette is `mat.$azure-palette`, whose tone 40 has cogpit's hue of 210° (`mat.$blue-palette` is at
  237°, toward violet).
- `--trove-status-ok` keeps `#1a6e3c` and `#3db064`. Every positive status of the UI already used it and none used the
  accent, so no screen changes its status colour. No other token is green; `web/src/styles/palette.spec.ts` checks that,
  and the contrast of every accent pair, in the unit tier.

**Rationale:** the owner's decision. The contrast adjustments are the rule of Q-UI-88 applied to the new hue; every pair
is in [design-language.md](../developer/design-language.md#contrast-of-the-text-tones-on-the-surfaces-they-sit-on).
The browser tier's axe run has not seen the blue palette yet.

**Applied in the spec:** Q-UI-88 (superseded in part: the accent); R-UI-002 names the accent;
[design-language.md](../developer/design-language.md); [web-ui.md](../developer/web-ui.md#design-tokens).

### Q-UI-97 · The manual's article takes the width of its column; only the prose keeps a measure

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the page of the manual was capped at 52 rem, so on a wide screen its tables sat in a narrow column with the
right half of the screen empty, and the table cells broke inside words ("al / l", "Servi / ce"): the README styles set
`overflow-wrap: anywhere`, which also lowers the minimum width a column may shrink to, and the table was a `display:
block` element that never took the container's width.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Widen the article; prose keeps a wide measure of 110 characters, tables and code use the full width | No cap on the article; paragraphs, lists, quotes and headings are capped at `110ch`; each table sits in a full-width container that scrolls sideways | Tables use the room a wide screen has; prose uses more of it too (the owner asked for the room to be used, 2026-11-02) and stays followable; one rule for every width | 110 characters is above the classic comfortable range of 66 to 90; prose still leaves space to its right on a very wide screen |
| (b) Widen the whole article, prose included | No cap at all | Simplest | Lines of 200 characters on a 2200 px screen are hard to follow |
| (c) A larger fixed cap (for example 80 rem) | Only the number changes | One line of CSS | Still empty space on wide screens and still too narrow for a wide table; the number is a guess |

**Choice:** (a). Rules (the layout is in [package-readme.scss](../../web/src/app/features/packages/package-readme.scss)
and [help.scss](../../web/src/app/features/help/help.scss)):

- The article has no `max-inline-size`; the contents column keeps its 15 rem.
- The help page marks its README `help-readme`; only then are the direct `p`, `ul`, `ol`, `dl`, `blockquote` and
  headings capped at `110ch`. The "On this page" box is capped at 48 rem.
- The finishing pass of `PackageReadmeView` wraps every table in `.readme-table`: full width, `overflow-x: auto`, focusable
  (a keyboard user can scroll it, as with a code block). A table wider than the container scrolls inside it, so the page
  itself never scrolls sideways (phone width included).
- Cells break at spaces only: `overflow-wrap: normal` and `word-break: normal` in `th` and `td`, `overflow-wrap:
  break-word` instead of `anywhere` on the README. Code in a cell does not wrap (`white-space: nowrap`); a long token
  widens the table and the container scrolls. The first column has a minimum width of 9 rem.
- Package READMEs share the component, so their tables take the same rules; only the measure is the help page's.

**Rationale:** the owner asked that the manual use the room a wide screen has (2026-11-02). Tables take all of it; prose
takes 110 characters, wider than the classic measure but still a line the eye can follow back, where a 200-character line
of option (b) is not. Revisit when a manual page carries a table whose first column is long prose (the 9 rem minimum then
squeezes less than it helps), or when the owner wants the prose wider or narrower at the walkthrough.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-050; [manual.md](../developer/manual.md#layout-of-a-page).

### Q-UI-98 · The file browser is two panes with a toolbar and a details header

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the owner called the browser "the worst design I have ever seen" (2026-11-02). It was a loose search form in the
top-left (key, class, format, sort, a search button), one tree row, a "Details" heading far to the right and an empty
screen: no panes, no borders, no height, filters unlike the packages and repositories lists, and no visible way to expand
a node. The design language is Q-UI-88 and Q-UI-96, the lists are Q-UI-68.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Two bordered panes of full height; a compact toolbar and the shared filter panel in the tree pane; a path and an action toolbar above the details | Tree pane `clamp(18rem, 30%, 26rem)`, details pane the rest, both `max(26rem, 100dvh - 13.5rem)` high with their own scroll; filter field narrows as you type, "Filters" opens the shared panel inside the tree pane (class and format as radio groups) with chips, a sort menu, a count; the details header holds the breadcrumb and the actions; a folder's children are the shared data table | Reads as a browser; the filter panel, chips, table and tabs are the ones of the packages and repositories lists, so it is one product; nothing new to learn | The filter panel sits in a 26 rem pane and replaces the tree while open instead of opening at the side |
| (b) The same panes, the shared panel opening to the right of the details | The panel is a third column | Identical to the lists | The tree is 18 to 26 rem, the details are narrow once a panel sits beside them; on 1280 px three columns do not fit |
| (c) A draggable splitter between the panes | The width of the tree is the user's | Long keys and deep paths fit | A separator that is keyboard-operable and remembered per user is its own widget; not needed to meet R-UI-010 |

**Choice:** (a). Details:

- The filter field sends `q` to the address (`replaceUrl`, so typing does not fill the history) 250 ms after the last
  keystroke, and at once on Enter. The server filters (the list's `q`, R-API-025); the screen
  filters nothing itself.
- Class and format are single choices (the list API takes one of each), so the panel offers radio groups; chips remove one.
  Sort is a query parameter (`sort=class`) as before.
- A tree row is a chevron (the expand state, which the old tree never showed), an icon (inventory for a local, cloud for
  a remote, layers for a virtual repository; folder; archive or document for a file), the name, and badges: the format, and
  "cache" on a remote, "disabled" where it is. The class is also in the row's text for assistive technology. A file row
  shows its size.
- A virtual repository expands to its members from the repository document (`virtual.members`), each labelled "resolves
  from" and leading to that repository. A caller who may only read the consumer view does not get the members, and the
  tree says so. The children endpoint is not asked for a virtual repository.
- The selected node is the one data source of the folder table: the tree loads a folder once and the table reads its
  children, with "Load more" in both.
- Upload and New folder need `deploy` and a local repository of the raw-files family (taken from the format's
  `protocolBasePath`), where the old screen offered them wherever `deploy` held and let the server refuse; Delete keeps
  `delete`; Client setup links `/setup?repository=<key>`. No control without a working backend: "Invalidate cache" (R-UI-011,
  MVP) has no client in the UI yet and is left out.
- Narrow content area (under 48 rem, a container query): one pane at a time, the details with "Back to the tree".
- The pattern (two panes, toolbar, panel inside a pane) is in [design-language.md](../developer/design-language.md#the-two-pane-browser).

**Rationale:** the owner's two complaints were structure and the loose form. Panes with borders and their own height give
the structure; the shared filter panel and data table give the likeness to the lists with no new component. A drag
splitter is real work (a keyboard-operable separator, persistence) for a width that a clamp already sets sensibly.
Revisit when a key or path in the tree is regularly cut off, or the owner asks for a resizable tree at the walkthrough.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-010, R-UI-011; [web-ui.md](../developer/web-ui.md); [files.md](../manual/user/files.md).

### Q-UI-99 · The CI screens sit under Identity, and a project's CI screens are the same components under the project

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. **Superseded in part by [Q-AUTHZ-208](authorization.md#q-authz-208--four-project-roles-reader-developer-maintainer-owner)**: the project's CI screens are shown for `ci:read` and for an Owner of the project; the switches and `403 project_switch_off` are gone, and the routes take the project key (`/admin/projects/:project/ci`).

Context: R-UI-035 and Q-CI-26 put the CI mappings with the system administrators and, bounded, with the administrators of a
project, who have no administration entry of their own besides Projects (R-UI-041). The screens needed a place in the
navigation and a shape for the project's copy.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) One entry "CI identity" in the group Identity (`ci:read`); the project's screens are the same components mounted under `/admin/projects/:key/ci` with the project as a parameter | The mapping list, editor, claim tester and issuance list take an optional project key and call the project routes; the project page gets a card that links to them | One implementation of the editor and the tester, so the bounds (no groups, the project's repositories and policies, the name prefix) are the only differences; a project administrator reaches it from the page they already use; the breadcrumb reads Projects > key > CI identity | The components carry a scope parameter |
| (b) Its own group "CI" in the navigation with the issuers, mappings and issuances as entries | Three entries | Short path to each list | CI mappings are principals of the same kind as service accounts and tokens, which Identity already holds; the navigation grows by a group for one feature; a project administrator still needs another way in |
| (c) A separate set of project screens | Copies of the editor and tester for the project | Each can diverge freely | Two editors to keep equal; the evaluation trace and the condition builder are exactly what must not drift |

**Choice:** (a). Routes: `/admin/ci` (issuers), `/admin/ci/new`, `/admin/ci/issuances`, `/admin/ci/:issuer` (tabs through
`?tab=settings|keys|mappings|issuances`, default `mappings`), `/admin/ci/:issuer/test`, `/admin/ci/:issuer/mappings/new` and
`/…/mappings/:mapping`; under a project `/admin/projects/:key/ci`, `…/ci/test`, `…/ci/mappings/new` and
`…/ci/mappings/:mapping`, with the issuer in the query (`?issuer=`), because the issuer name in the path would give the
breadcrumb a step that is no page. The project card is shown for `ci:read` and for an administrator of the project; a switch
that is off answers `403 project_switch_off` on the first read and the screen shows that message alone.

**Rationale:** the editor and the tester are the parts of the feature that carry the rules; two copies would drift. Revisit
when a third tier (delegations to a group, R-CI-023, P1) needs its own screen shape.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-035 (routes and the project card); [web-ui.md](../developer/web-ui.md#ci-identity).

### Q-UI-100 · The bulk revoke counts first, and one issued token opens in a dialog

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: R-CI-020 lets a token administrator revoke the tokens that match `issuer` and at least one of project, pipeline,
job or mapping; the confirmation must say how many tokens it revokes, which the revoke answer only tells afterwards.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Count the active tokens that match the applied filters (the list operation with `active=true`, all pages), name the number in the confirmation, then revoke | Two requests before the write | The number is the one the request revokes, up to a token issued in between; no new API operation | The count is read, not reserved |
| (b) Confirm without a number and report it afterwards | One request | Simple | The confirmation cannot say what it does, against R-CI-020 |
| (c) Ask the API for a dry-run count | A new operation | Exact | Beyond the contract; the work packages are fixed |

The detail of one issuance opens in a dialog over the list, in the system and in the project screens alike (the project's
list cannot call `GET /ci/issuances/{tokenId}`, so the dialog shows the record of the list and adds the usage summary only
where `tokens:read` allows it).

**Choice:** (a), with the dialog. **Rationale:** the confirmation must be truthful, and the existing operations suffice. Revisit
when the API offers a count or when issuances need a linkable address (the audit log linking to one token).

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-035; [web-ui.md](../developer/web-ui.md#ci-identity).

### Q-UI-101 · "Overwrite" of a whole-body replace re-sends the stored record with only the user's changed members

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the mapping editor and the issuer form replace the whole record (`PUT`) with the loaded `ETag`. The shared
conflict resolver was written for merge patches: after a `412` it re-reads the record, compares only the members the user
changed, and "Overwrite" sent the same request again with the new `ETag`. For a `PUT` that request carries the whole stale
form, so a narrowing another administrator made in between (a removed `deploy`, a removed audience, `singleUseSubjectTokens`
switched on) was undone without the dialog ever showing it. R-UI-042 requires that "Overwrite" re-sends only after the
difference was shown; R-CI-002 and R-CI-011 make such a narrowing the thing that must not be lost silently.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The `PUT` body after "Overwrite" is the stored record as read now, with only the members the user changed taken from the form | `overwriteBody` in [ci-common.ts](../../web/src/app/features/ci/ci-common.ts); the resolver hands the stored record to `send(etag, current)` | What the dialog shows (the members the user changed, stored now against yours) is exactly what is replaced; every other member keeps the other administrator's value; no extra screen | A member the user changed that the other administrator also changed is replaced by the user's whole member (a grant list is one member), which the dialog showed as one row |
| (b) Show every member of the full body in the dialog and send the stale form | The diff covers all members | Nothing is hidden | The user is asked to judge members they never touched; "Overwrite" still writes the stale value over the other administrator's narrowing, which is the harm |
| (c) Refuse "Overwrite" for a `PUT` and offer only "Reload" | One button less | Cannot lose a change | The user's edits are lost or copied by hand; the dialog's purpose (R-UI-042) is a choice |

**Choice:** (a). The resolver's `send` takes the stored record as a second argument (`null` on the first attempt); a
merge-patch caller ignores it, a `PUT` caller builds its body from it. The mapping editor builds the stored body through
the form model (`inputFromForm(formFromMapping(current))`); the issuer form takes the members of the stored record and keeps
the list members it leaves out when empty (`allowedAudiences`, `requiredClaims`, `pinClaims`) from the stored record unless
the user had emptied them.

**Rationale:** the safe default for a security-relevant record is that an overwrite replaces what was shown and nothing else.
Revisit when a record gets a `PATCH` (merge patch) operation, which makes the body construction unnecessary, or when the
dialog should compare inside a member (the individual grants of an inline list).

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-042 (the dialog's "Overwrite" text already says "after showing the diff"; this decision fixes
what is re-sent); [web-ui.md](../developer/web-ui.md#ci-identity); tests `ci-editor-screens.spec.ts` and
`ci-issuer-screens.spec.ts` ("Overwrite" keeps the narrowing).

### Q-UI-102 · The bulk revoke is offered only for filters it carries, and the day filters are the local day

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the issuance list filters by issuer, project ID, project path, pipeline, job, mapping, state and a time range, but
the revoke operation (R-CI-020) understands the issuer, the project ID, the pipeline ID, the job ID and the mapping only. The
confirmation counted the tokens of all applied filters, and the request sent a subset: with a project path or a time range
applied it revoked more than it said (Q-UI-100 promises the count is what the request revokes). Separately, the date inputs
were sent as UTC day bounds while the table shows local times.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) "Revoke matching tokens" is disabled while a filter the request cannot carry is applied (project path, issued from or until, state "expired or revoked"), and the note names those filters; count and request use the same members | `unsupported` in [issuance-list.ts](../../web/src/app/features/ci/issuance-list.ts) | The number in the confirmation is the number revoked; the user sees which filter to clear | A time-bounded bulk revoke is not possible from the screen |
| (b) Keep the button, show what will be revoked (the supported filters only) in the confirmation | The text names the ignored filters | The action stays available | The list the user looked at and the set revoked differ; a click-through confirmation revokes tokens the user did not see |
| (c) Add the missing filters to the revoke operation | An API change | Complete | Beyond this fix: the contract and the work packages are fixed |

**Choice:** (a). The day filters become the bounds of the **local** day: `from` is the start of the chosen day in the
browser's time zone and `to` is the start of the day after the chosen one (the API's `to` is exclusive: "issued before"),
both sent as UTC instants.

**Rationale:** a revoke that cannot be undone must act on exactly what it names. Revisit when the revoke operation accepts
the other filters (option c), at which point the note and the `unsupported` list shrink.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-035 (bulk revoke); [web-ui.md](../developer/web-ui.md#ci-identity).

### Q-UI-103 · The claim tester's form view edits the top-level claims as rows and the JSON text is the one source

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: R-UI-036 says the sample is edited "as JSON or in a form view"; the tester had the JSON text area only.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A JSON / Form switch; the form view lists the top-level claims as name and value rows with add and remove; every change writes the pretty-printed JSON, switching back shows it | The text signal stays the only state; the rows are derived when the form view opens | The two views cannot disagree; the evaluate request and the token handling (R-UI-036) are unchanged; a claim is added or removed without touching braces | Nested values are edited as JSON text inside their row |
| (b) A form with one field per sample claim | Fixed fields | Simple to read | Real tokens carry other claims; the sample's claims would be the only ones editable |
| (c) The JSON editor alone | No change | Nothing to build | R-UI-036 names the form view |

**Choice:** (a). A value keeps the JSON type it had: a number typed over stays a number when the text parses as one, an
object or array stays that type, a string stays a string; a row added in the form view is text. JSON that is not an object
(or a token that does not decode) keeps the user in the JSON view with the reason. A pasted compact token is decoded before
the rows are built, so the form view never holds a token either.

**Rationale:** GitLab claims are almost all strings, and the mapping leaves compare text, so a "type" selector per row would
be noise; keeping the type a claim arrived with avoids turning `iat` into a string by an edit of its neighbour. Revisit when
the tester should edit nested claims (a `path` leaf) in rows of their own.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-036 (already names the form view); [web-ui.md](../developer/web-ui.md#ci-identity).

|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A **Mirror** section among the remote settings, and a **Mirror** tab with the status on the edit form (chosen) | Configuration where the remote is configured, status where its other tabs are | One place for one repository; the status sits beside the settings that explain it | A list of every mirror needs the repository list's filter |
| (b) A separate screen for all mirrors | An overview | Comparable at a glance | A second place to configure the same repository |

### Q-UI-105 · Pause and resume are a patch of the document; a pass on request opens its job

| (b) Toggle without `If-Match` | Blind write | One click less | Could overwrite another administrator's change of the same document (R-API-012) |

### Q-API-16 · A `limit` above the maximum is clamped

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Clamp | `limit=10000` returns pages of `api.page_size_max` | A client that asks for "as many as possible" works against any installation; the cursor makes the next page cheap | The page is smaller than asked and the client must read `nextCursor`, which it does anyway |
| (b) Refuse | `limit` above the maximum answers 400 | The client learns the bound | Every client hard-codes the bound or retries; the maximum is configuration, so the same call works on one installation and fails on another |

**Choice:** (a). A `limit` that is not an integer of 1 or more is 400 `malformed_request`.

**Rationale:** R-API-010 gives the maximum as a configuration value, so a client cannot know it; pages are defined by `nextCursor`, not by their size. The development agent would revisit this if a list appears whose callers need to know that they got fewer items than asked.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-010 reads "default 50, maximum 500" as a clamp; implemented in `ParseList` ([http-api.md](../developer/http-api.md)).

### Q-API-17 · The body of an idempotent answer is the database's rendering, and a refusal is stored in a second transaction

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Write the answer from the stored `jsonb` | The first answer and every replay send the text PostgreSQL renders for the stored body (`response_body::text`) | The first answer and a replay are byte-identical on every replica, as the acceptance criterion says ("identical bodies") | Member order and spacing differ from the handler's own rendering |
| (b) Store the handler's bytes in a `text` column | The replay sends exactly what the handler wrote | Handler rendering is kept | `response_body` is `jsonb` in the data model of R-API-014; a column change |
| (c) Compare semantically | Replay renders `jsonb` as is; first answer is the handler's | No change | Bodies are equal as JSON, not as bytes; a client that hashes the body sees two values |

A 4xx outcome has a second question: the change must be rolled back and the refusal stored.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (d) Savepoint | The operation runs under `SAVEPOINT`; a refusal rolls back to it and the row is completed in the same transaction | One transaction | A transaction-mode pooler is fine with savepoints, but every helper and store has to be savepoint-aware |
| (e) Second transaction | The change transaction rolls back; the refusal is inserted in a new one with `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE … WHERE expired` | Simple; the change is never half-applied | A duplicate that was waiting on the first transaction may run the operation itself before the refusal is stored (it gets the same refusal) |

**Choice:** (a) and (e).

**Rationale:** The criterion asks for identical bodies, which only (a) guarantees without changing the table. Two concurrent first requests that both end in a refusal each answer the same refusal, so (e) cannot produce two different outcomes for one key. The development agent would revisit (e) if an operation can refuse after a side effect outside the transaction.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-014 is implemented as written; the data model is unchanged.

### Q-API-18 · An unknown or duplicate member of a body is 400, although it lists a field

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) 400 with `errors[]` | Status 400, code `malformed_request`, `errors[0].pointer` names the member (`errs.WithBadRequest`) | R-API-003's criterion says exactly this; the body could not be read as the resource | `errs.Error.Status` maps "Invalid with fields" to 422, so the kind alone does not say it |
| (b) 422 `validation_failed` | A parsed body with a bad member is a validation problem | One rule for "errors lists fields" | Contradicts the criterion and R-API-009's table (`malformed_request` is 400) |

**Choice:** (a). Member names are compared exactly, unlike `encoding/json`, so `Name` for `name` is unknown.

**Rationale:** The spec fixes both the status and the code. A value of the right shape that fails a rule stays 422 `validation_failed`. The development agent would revisit this if clients need case-insensitive member names.

**Applied in the spec:** none (R-API-003, R-API-009 already say it); `errs.WithBadRequest` is the mechanism.

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |

| (a) Capabilities, and `authenticated` plus a handler check where the caller started the resource | `settings:read` for tasks and the key-ring status, `settings:write` to run a task; jobs are `authenticated`, and the handler grants all jobs with `settings:read` and the caller's own otherwise (R-API-015) | Uses the M0 forms; R-API-008 allows a handler check where the decision depends on the resource | The declaration alone does not say who may call jobs |

### Q-API-22 · Every operation documents `429`

| Option | What it means | For | Against |

| (a) `429` in every operation | The response `TooManyRequests` is referenced by all operations; a test fails on an operation without it | The validation against the document (E1.6) holds for the answer the stage can give anywhere; R-API-002 asks for "every possible 4xx" | A repeated reference |

### Q-API-23 · A job the caller may not see answers 404

|---|---|---|---|
| (a) 404 | `GET /system/jobs/{id}` and `cancel` for a job another principal started answer like a missing one | A caller learns nothing about jobs of others | An administrator-only job looks like a missing one to a user |
| (b) 403 | The job exists but is not yours | Clear | Leaks that the ID exists |
