### Q-API-28 · A missing `If-Match` is 428 by one rule, and a write keeps its epoch through an idempotent replay

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Two behaviors of the shared conventions showed when the first resource with a version header and an epoch used them. The first is
the rule for a missing `If-Match`; it replaces what Q-API-24 and Q-API-32 said separately, and [Q-API-42](#q-api-42--one-mechanism-for-a-missing-if-match-and-one-stale-error) applies it to every resource.

| Question | Options | Choice |
|---|---|---|
| The document marks `If-Match` required on `PUT` and `PATCH`, and the generated wrapper answers a missing required header with 400 before any handler runs. R-API-012 says 428 | (a) Mark the header optional in the document and let each handler answer 428. (b) Keep it required and map the wrapper's missing-`If-Match` error to the 428 problem in `bindError` | (b): the document keeps saying the header is needed (a client generated from it sends it), one place answers it for every resource, and the problem is the 428 of `Precondition.Require`. A handler does not check the header again |
| `Trove-Authz-Epoch` is raised by the change log in a hook just before `COMMIT`, after the operation returned its outcome, yet an idempotent create stores its outcome (R-API-014) and a replay must carry the epoch of the first answer | (a) Leave the header out of a replay. (b) Read the epoch in the operation by locking the epoch row early. (c) Let an outcome complete itself after the commit hooks: `Outcome.Finish` runs in a hook registered after the operation's own, before the outcome is stored | (c): (a) loses what a client that lost the first response needs; (b) takes the epoch row before the policy rows and can deadlock with a writer that takes them in the other order. Every idempotent create that changes authorization data uses it through `finishEpoch` ([Q-API-44](#q-api-44--one-header-name-and-one-setter-for-the-authorization-epoch)) |

**Rationale:** both keep the convention in the shared package and add nothing a resource has to remember. The development agent would revisit (c) if a second use shows that a resource needs to change the status after the hooks, which `Finish` allows but no one needs; it would revisit the binder mapping if the code generator offers a hook for required headers.

**Applied in the spec:** none; [http-api.md](../developer/http-api.md) lists both.

### Q-API-24 · `If-Match` is an optional header in the document

Status: **Superseded** by [Q-API-28](#q-api-28--a-missing-if-match-is-428-by-one-rule-and-a-write-keeps-its-epoch-through-an-idempotent-replay) and [Q-API-42](#q-api-42--one-mechanism-for-a-missing-if-match-and-one-stale-error). The development agent had declared the header inline and optional on the first two operations that used it (`PATCH /settings/auth`, `PATCH /users/me/preferences`) and let the handler answer 428; the binding was mapped in the meantime, so those operations reference the shared required parameter like every other one, and no inline `If-Match` parameter is left on a `PUT` or `PATCH`.

### Q-API-25 · The identity resources have no revision

Status: **Reversed** by [Q-AUTH-50](identity-and-authentication.md#q-auth-50--users-groups-and-service-accounts-carry-a-revision-so-does-the-authentication-settings-row). It had decided that users, groups and service accounts carry no revision and that a merge patch is last-write-wins (the gap H-135). R-API-012 asks `If-Match` for every `PUT` and `PATCH` of a mutable configuration resource, and an administrator editing a group concurrently with another is the case it exists for, so the three resources and the authentication settings now carry a revision, and their `PATCH` requires `If-Match` like every other resource. The merge-patch semantics of this block (a member the patch names is written, an absent one stays, `null` resets, a read-only member is ignored) are unchanged. Membership edits stay exempt: they send a delta (R-API-012).

### Q-API-26 · Preferences without a row

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

R-API-021 gives `user_preferences.revision` as the ETag, and a user who never saved preferences has no row.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Create the row at the first sign-in | The provisioner writes it | `GET` always finds a row | The login area writes a table it does not own |
| (b) Defaults at revision 1, the first write inserts revision 2 (chosen) | `GET` without a row answers the defaults and `ETag: "1"`; a `PATCH` with `If-Match: "1"` or `*` inserts the row | No write on the sign-in path; the `If-Match` is checked in the writing transaction | A revision 1 without a row |

**Choice:** (b).

**Rationale:** most users never change a preference. The development agent would revisit this if the preferences grow a column that a
reader must not see as a default.

**Applied in the spec:** none.

### Q-API-32 · A missing If-Match is 428 even where the generated binder reads the header

Status: **Folded into** [Q-API-28](#q-api-28--a-missing-if-match-is-428-by-one-rule-and-a-write-keeps-its-epoch-through-an-idempotent-replay), which states the rule once: the document keeps the header required and `bindError` answers the binder's error with `precondition_required`.

### Q-API-33 · The /files/ operations are in the document, outside the generated interface and outside the authorization step

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

R-API-002 puts `/files/…` in the document, tagged `files`, excludes the tag from the generation and covers it with the route-parity check.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Generate them like the others | The wrapper binds `{path}` | One mechanism | A path parameter of the generator is one segment; the body would be bound as a request body type; the step of the management API would decide before the handler |
| (b) Document them, generate nothing, compare the routes (chosen) | `exclude-tags: [files]`; `Document.FileOperations()` holds them; `CheckRoutes` compares the patterns `… /files/{repoKey}/{path...}` with the document's `{path}` in both directions; `apitest` looks the route of a `/files/` answer up with a single-segment path | R-API-002 as written; the answers are validated against the document like every other | The declarations of the files operations are read by the files handler's own decisions, not by the shared step |

**Choice:** (b).

**Rationale:** The handler is the raw path of R-ARCH-011; it decides per coordinate and streams. The development agent would revisit this if a second raw family appears.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-002 reads unchanged.

### Q-API-34 · The representation of a repository: read-only members and the warnings

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

R-REPO-009 returns "the stored document plus warnings", R-API-003 says a body obtained by GET can be sent back.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Warnings in a header or an envelope | The document stays as stored | The representation is the document | A write answer differs in shape from a read; the "request type is the response type" rule breaks |
| (b) Read-only members in the same object, ignored on input (chosen) | `lifecycle`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `lastActivityAt` and `warnings` (writes only) are members of the representation; the input drops them before the strict decode | One type for GET, POST, PUT and the base of a PATCH | A client cannot tell a read-only member from an unknown one by the strict decode; it is told by the document (`readOnly: true`) |

**Choice:** (b).

**Rationale:** It is what the conventions of R-API-003 ask. The development agent would revisit this if a read-only member must be refused rather than ignored.

**Applied in the spec:** The schema `Repository` in api/openapi.yaml.

### Q-API-40 · Recent authentication is enforced by the shared authorization step

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

R-API-007 lists the operations that need a recent interactive authentication when called with a session, and the document marked a few of them with `x-trove-recent-auth: true`; only the token and settings handlers checked it, each in its own way.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Each handler checks | `requireRecentAuth` stays a call in the handlers | Nothing to change | An operation that declares the extension and forgets the call is open (the exposure rule writes were, H-165); the table of R-API-007 is not what runs |
| (b) The shared step, after the permission (chosen) | `Operation.RecentAuth` is read from `x-trove-recent-auth` at load; `authorize` calls `requireRecentAuth` once `decide` allowed the caller; a declaration other than `true` refuses start-up | One mechanism; the document is what runs; a caller who may not act gets 403, not an invitation to sign in again | An operation decided inside its handler (`authenticated: true` with an own check, such as token creation) answers 401 before its own 403 |
| (c) The shared step before the permission | Check first, decide second | A stale session never reaches the evaluator | Tells a caller without the permission to sign in again, and the audit event of the denial is lost |

**Choice:** (b). The declaration is on every operation of the table that exists in this build: creating and rotating a token (`createToken`, `rotateToken`, `createServiceAccountToken`), changing the authentication settings, creating, replacing, patching and deleting a permission policy, binding and unbinding a role, deleting a repository, and the four writes of exposure rules. The rows that name operations of later milestones (approving a command-line login, CI issuers and mappings, applying configuration as code) take the declaration with those operations; `TestR_API_007_DocumentDeclaresRecentAuth` lists the set, so a new declaration or a missing one is a deliberate edit. A token is not asked (R-API-007): its scope bounds it. With no session store the step answers 503 instead of passing.

**Rationale:** the question of R-API-007 is "does the document say it", and a rule that the document states must not depend on a handler remembering. The development agent would revisit the 401-before-403 order for the handler-decided operations if a client is shown to leak information through it (the answer names no resource, so none is known).

**Applied in the spec:** none; R-API-007 reads unchanged. Closes H-165.

### Q-API-41 · The request log learns the principal through the request-scoped holder

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

The request log (R-OPS-010) writes `principal`, `principal_type`, `principal_id`, `token_id` and `auth_method`, and recorded `"principal":"anonymous"` even for authenticated management-API requests: the log stage is outside the authentication stage (R-ARCH-005 fixes the order), so it cannot receive the principal from the stage's return value, and nothing set the per-request facts it reads after the request.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Move the log stage inside the authentication stage | The order of R-ARCH-005 changes | The record has the principal as a value | A request refused before the stage (421, 503 server busy, a panic) is not logged; the order is a contract |
| (b) The authentication stage fills the holder (chosen) | `observability.RequestInfo` is the mutable holder the log stage put in the context before the request; `app.authenticate` calls `recordPrincipal` after a successful authentication, and the log stage reads the holder after the request | Nothing moves; the facts exist for every outcome, including a 401 after the stage | The composition root is the one place that knows both packages |

**Choice:** (b). The values follow the log vocabulary of R-OPS-010: `principal_type` `breakglass` for the break-glass administrator (the kind is `break_glass`), `auth_method` `nuget_apikey` for the NuGet API key (the method is `api_key`), `token_id` only for a token credential. An anonymous caller and a request the stage refused keep the record's defaults (`anonymous`, `none`). `TestR_OPS_010_RequestLogRecordsThePrincipal` drives the chain order with the holder, and the E1.5 integration test finds the principal in the stream.

**Rationale:** a holder in the context is the idiom the record already uses for the handler, the address and the host. The development agent would revisit this if a second stage needs to publish facts, and would then give the holder a typed setter per stage.

**Applied in the spec:** none; R-OPS-010 reads unchanged.

### Q-API-42 · One mechanism for a missing If-Match, and one stale error

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

The rule for a missing `If-Match` was written in three decision blocks (Q-API-24, Q-API-28, Q-API-32) and implemented three ways: the shared required parameter with the binder mapping, an inline optional parameter whose handler answered 428, and an inline parameter without `required` on the `DELETE` operations. A stale tag was rendered by five different constructors.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Keep the variants | Each resource decides | Nothing to change | A new resource picks one; the document and the behavior drift |
| (b) One declaration and one error (chosen) | A `PUT` or `PATCH` that requires the header declares `x-trove-if-match: required` and references the shared `IfMatch` parameter; a `DELETE` references the shared `IfMatchOptional`; `bindError` maps the binder's error to the 428; `errs.Stale(what, current)` is the one 412 with `currentEtag` and the cause `errs.StaleRevision`; `errs.AnyRevision` is the one value for the blind write | The document is what runs; a handler cannot forget the check | The domain packages import `errs` for the constant, which they already do |

**Choice:** (b). `TestR_API_012_OneMechanismForAMissingIfMatch` reads the document: every `PUT` and `PATCH` either requires the header with the shared parameter alone or is on the list of exemptions (membership deltas, role bindings, file content), and documents the 428; `TestR_API_012_MissingIfMatchIs428` sends every such operation without the header through the generated wrapper. The domain returns the cause and the extension itself (`repository`, `authz`, `token` settings, the principal manager), the handler adds nothing, and `Failed` is the same error for a handler that compares in memory before it calls the domain. A tag the server never issued is revision 0, which no row has, so it answers 412 with the current tag.

**Rationale:** one declaration in the document and one answer in code is what R-API-012 states ("there is no switch to turn the rule off"). The development agent would revisit the exemption list if a new resource edits a collection member by member without a delta endpoint.

**Applied in the spec:** none; Q-API-24 is superseded, Q-API-32 folded into Q-API-28, Q-API-25 reversed ([Q-AUTH-50](identity-and-authentication.md#q-auth-50--users-groups-and-service-accounts-carry-a-revision-so-does-the-authentication-settings-row)).

### Q-API-43 · The revision of an identity resource is in the ETag, not in the body

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

The policy shows its revision as `version`, the repository as `version`, an exposure rule as `revision`, and each also sends it as the `ETag`. The identity resources (users, groups, service accounts) and the authentication settings gain a revision (Q-AUTH-50), and a body member would be a fourth name or a fifth copy.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A `revision` member in the body | The ETag and the body say the same | A client reads it without the header | A write answers a member the client must not send back; a name for the fourth time |
| (b) The ETag only (chosen) | `GET` and the write answers carry `ETag: "<revision>"`; the representations have no revision member | One place; a body obtained by `GET` is a valid `PATCH` body without a read-only member to ignore | The three older resources keep their member names |

**Choice:** (b) for the new ones. The older members (`version` of a policy and a repository, `revision` of a rule) stay: renaming them changes a contract that the interface screens already read.

**Rationale:** the ETag is the concurrency token (R-API-012), and a representation that repeats it can only disagree with it. The development agent would revisit this if a client cannot read response headers (a browser behind a proxy that strips them), and would then add `revision` to all representations at once.

**Applied in the spec:** none.

### Q-API-44 · One header name and one setter for the authorization epoch

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

`Trove-Authz-Epoch` was written by `authz.HeaderEpoch` in the policy handlers and by a second constant in the endpoint handlers, and the exposure rule create gave its epoch to the first answer only (a replay carried none).

**Choice:** `authz.HeaderEpoch` is the one name, `setEpoch` the one setter for a plain answer, and `finishEpoch` the one `Outcome.Finish` for an idempotent create: the change log raises the epoch in a hook just before `COMMIT`, `Finish` runs after that hook and before the outcome is stored, so a replay carries the epoch of the first answer (Q-API-28). The exposure rule create uses it like the policy create. The endpoint integration test sends the same create twice and compares the epochs.

**Rationale:** a client waits for a replica to reach an epoch it was given (R-AUTHZ-032); a replay that lacks it breaks that wait. The development agent would revisit this if a third kind of write returns an epoch in the body instead.

**Applied in the spec:** none.

### Q-API-75 · How deeply a JSON request body may nest

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

The strict decoding of R-API-003 walks a body token by token to find duplicate members. `encoding/json`'s token reader has no
depth limit, and a body of nothing but `[` (1 MiB fits on the anonymous `POST /api/v1/tokens/revoke`) made the walk hold one
frame and one pointer string per level: memory in proportion to the square of the body's length.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) No bound, an iterative walk | Pointers built only on error | No new rule | The decoders behind the walk (`encoding/json` into `any`, the merge patch) still recurse per level |
| (b) 64 levels (chosen) | A deeper body answers 400 `malformed_request` with `errors[0].code` `depth`; the walk is iterative and builds a pointer only for an error | Bounded work for every body, before any decoder runs; no document of the API comes close | A fixed number |
| (c) A configuration key | `api.max_body_depth` | Adjustable | A knob nobody needs |

**Choice:** (b) (`maxBodyDepth` in `internal/api/v1/decode.go`).

**Rationale:** the deepest document of the API (a repository's configuration) nests fewer than ten levels. The development
agent would revisit the figure if a document needs more.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-017 (a bullet).

### Q-API-156 · The tag of a repository read follows `lastActivityAt`

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

`lastActivityAt` is a member of the repository representation (Q-API-34) and is written by the activity buffer without a new
`config_version`. The read tag was the revision only, so a conditional read after a download answered 304 and the client kept a
stale `lastActivityAt` under a tag that is strong (R-API-012, RFC 9110 section 8.8.1).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Exclude `lastActivityAt` from what the tag validates | Document it | No change | The tag is strong for a representation it does not describe |
| (b) Take the member out of the single read | Only the list shows it | The tag is exact | The detail page of the UI shows it |
| (c) Let the activity bump the revision | | The tag is exact | Every editor's `If-Match` fails once a minute |
| (d) Add the activity time to the read tag (chosen) | `"<revision>.<microseconds>"`; writes strip the suffix and compare the revision | The tag is exact and a download is no conflict | Two tags for the same revision; a tag taken from a read is not the tag a write answers |

**Choice:** (d), in `repositoryETag` and `repositoryPrecondition`. The 412 `currentEtag` and the write answers carry the plain
revision tag.

**Rationale:** the client treats a tag as opaque, so a longer one costs nothing, and the concurrency control stays on the revision.
The development agent would revisit it if another resource gets a volatile member; then the suffix becomes a shared helper.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-012.

### Q-API-157 · The API conventions own the merge patch, the domain receives it as a function

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: RFC 7396 was implemented twice, in `internal/api/v1` (R-API-013, decoding numbers as `float64`, so an integer above 2^53
lost its last digits and two different large values compared equal in the immutable-member check) and in `internal/repository`
(R-REPO-011, with `UseNumber`, a duplicate check and an object check). The repository service needs the merge inside its row lock
and its `If-Match: *` semantics.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The API owns it, the domain receives a function (chosen) | `v1.MergePatch` is the one implementation; `repository.Service.Patch` takes a `Patcher` (`func(current []byte) ([]byte, error)`) and applies it to the stored document under the row lock | One merge; the domain keeps the lock and the `*` semantics; the convention stays with the API | The service API takes a function |
| (b) A leaf package both import | `internal/mergepatch` | Neither area depends on the other | A third home for an API convention |
| (c) Read, merge and replace in the handler | The handler reads the document, merges, calls `Replace` | No function parameter | A patch with `If-Match: *` becomes a lost update or a 412 |

**Choice:** (a). The merge keeps every number as its literal (`json.Decoder.UseNumber`) and refuses a patch with a duplicate
member or nesting deeper than 64 levels (Q-API-75). That the patch is an object is checked where the body is read
(`ReadMergePatch`), not in the merge: the merge is RFC 7396 as written, and a non-object patch replaces the target, which the
appendix-A examples of the RFC require and the conventions test keeps. `CheckImmutable` compares numbers by literal for the same
reason. The 400 of a patch that cannot be read is `malformed_request` with the pointer of the member (`duplicate`, `syntax`,
`type`); `invalid_document` stays the field code of a stored-document problem without a pointer (Q-REPO-84).

**Rationale:** the merge is part of how the API reads a request, so the API owns it; the transaction is part of how the domain
writes, so the domain owns that. The development agent would revisit this if a second area outside the management API needs to
merge a patch; then the merge moves to a leaf package (b).

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-013 (a bullet).

### Q-API-158 · The shared step begins the index only for an operation that decides; a handler that decides begins it itself

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: Q-AUTHZ-159 gives a request one index in a holder (`edge.Access`). Of the operations of the management API, the ones
declared `public` or `authenticated` never decide in the step, and several of them decide in the handler (the repository read and
list, the permission checks).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Begin for every operation | The step takes the index before any declaration | Every handler finds a holder | `ping`, `version`, the problem catalogue and every `authenticated` read answer 503 `authz_stale` while the index is unconfirmed, which they never did |
| (b) Begin for the forms that decide; a handler that decides begins itself (chosen) | A capability, a role and an action declaration begin with the repository of the action form as a key and store the holder; a handler of any other declaration calls `Begin` through the same `Access` and passes the context it derives to everything after | No new refusal for an operation that decides nothing | Two places begin; a handler must pass the derived context |
| (c) A lazy holder | The step stores a holder that begins on first use | One place | `edge.Access` has no lazy form; a context cannot be changed by a callee |

**Choice:** (b). `Beginner` is the optional third method of `v1.Access`: `Begin(ctx, permission, keys...)` returns the holder, or
none for a permission the access opens without a decision (`system.bootstrap_anonymous_read`, Q-AUTHZ-16), so that bridge keeps
answering while the index is stale. `edge.Resolve` returns the stored holder, brought up to the keys the handler learns, or
begins one for a request that reached the handler without the step. Two questions stay outside it, both documented as
exceptions: the rate-limit exemption of administrators, which runs in a chain stage before the step, and the effective
capabilities of `GET /api/v1/authz/me`, for which the decision point offers no `…On` form yet.

**Rationale:** one request, one index is a consistency property, and a refusal that an operation did not have before is a
regression. The development agent would revisit this when the decision point offers `EffectiveOn` and the chain stage can store a
holder; then the step begins for every operation that is not public and the handler's own `Begin` goes.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-008 (a bullet).

### Q-API-159 · What the package list, the version list and the version details carry

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

R-API-029 named the operations and a package example (`id`, `format`, `name`, `description`, `latestVersion`, `keywords`, `repositories`, `updatedAt`) but not the members of a version, the sort fields, or what the list screen of R-UI-006 shows beyond the example. The UI (the shared list table of Q-UI-68, the package page of R-UI-007) is written against the contract, so the members have to be fixed before the read model exists.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Only the example's members | List: the eight members; versions and details by the format page | No decision now | The list cannot show first created, versions and downloads; every format page would invent its own version shape; the UI could not be written against a contract |
| (b) One summary shape for list, lookup and read; a version summary for the list and a version for the details; the format-specific part in `metadata` | `PackageSummary` adds `createdAt`, `versionCount`, `downloadCount`; `PackageVersionSummary` and `PackageVersion` as in the OpenAPI document; `hasReadme` on the version; sort by `name`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt` | One shape per concept; the table of R-UI-006 is fed by the list alone; a version page needs two calls (summary, details) and a README call only when `hasReadme` | Counts and dates are aggregates over the visible versions, which the read model must compute in SQL for every page |
| (c) A `fields` or `expand` parameter | The client asks for what it needs | Small answers | Sparse field selection is not offered in v1 (R-API-011); two representations to test per resource |

**Choice:** (b). Every aggregate (`latestVersion`, `repositories`, `versionCount`, `downloadCount`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`) is computed from the versions the caller may read, so a hidden version leaks neither its number nor its existence (R-API-029). `latestVersion` is the highest visible stable version, or the highest visible pre-release while none is stable. The sort fields are `name`, `createdAt` and `updatedAt` with their descending forms, because the screen's sortable columns are exactly those; the version list sorts by `-publishedAt` (default), `publishedAt`, `-version` and `version`, the last two by the format's version precedence, which the page needs to find "the latest stable version" without reading every version. `hasReadme` exists so that the page chooses its default tab, and requests the README, with the details alone. The package-ownership data of R-UI-007's Owners tab stays with its own work (R-API-048, P1).

**Rationale:** The list screen of the owner's design reference shows first created, versions and downloads, and the API can give them at no extra call; leaving them out would have meant a request per row. Version precedence is the one place where the client cannot do the work itself: a list of 400 versions comes in pages, and sorting a page does not find the maximum. The development agent revisits this when the first format with a different version model (Maven coordinates, container tags; API-094, API-109, API-110) needs a member that does not fit `PackageVersion`; the answer would be a member in `metadata`, not a new shape.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-029: the operations table (sort values), the version details and version list members, the package example and the sentence on `createdAt`, `versionCount` and `downloadCount`; `api/openapi.yaml`, block `M2 packages`.

### Q-API-160 · The client setup answer: credential modes, tabs and snippet ids

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

R-API-030 described the endpoint in prose: `?client=`, the placeholder `{{token}}`, the environment reference with `credentials=env`, snippet `id`s, and rules for quoting. The UI needs three further things: a way to ask for snippets without any authentication line (an anonymous caller; the install panel of R-UI-009), the grouping of snippets into the tabs of R-UI-016, and the lifetime for the token the dialog creates.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `credentials` takes `placeholder`, `env` or `none`; each snippet names its tab, file and language; the answer carries `tokenTtlSeconds` | The contract of the OpenAPI document | The UI groups, labels and downloads without knowing any format; one request per choice; the lifetime comes from the configuration key the spec already names | Three modes to implement per template |
| (b) The UI strips authentication lines itself | Server sends only the `placeholder` form | One mode fewer | The UI would parse client syntax (ini, yaml, xml), the one thing the server owns (R-API-030); any change of a template breaks the stripping |
| (c) The UI knows the tab of each snippet by its `id` | A table in the UI | A smaller answer | A new snippet needs a UI release; a format page could not add a snippet alone |

**Choice:** (a). Snippets have `id` (`<client>.<tab>.<name>`, stable), `tab` (`configure`, `install`, `publish`), `fileName` (null for a command), `language` and `content`. Besides the snippets the answer holds `registryUrl` (with its trailing slash), `endpointPath` (the scheme-less form that is npm's credential key), `username`, `publishTarget` and `tokenTtlSeconds`. The explanation of each snippet is the UI's, translated per `id` (R-UI-045); an `id` the UI does not know shows its snippet without a sentence. The permission declaration is the action form `read` on the repository, so a caller who may not read it gets the `404` of a missing repository (R-AUTHZ-016); the publish snippets and `publishTarget` follow the caller's `deploy` on the target and are absent otherwise.

**Rationale:** (a) keeps the one rule of R-API-030 that matters for security: the server never sees or sends a token, and the browser's only operation is replacing a literal. `credentials=none` is what lets the install panel of R-UI-009 stay free of credentials by construction. The development agent revisits this when NuGet's `nuget.config` and the .NET CLI snippets arrive and need a member that does not fit (a per-snippet `scope`, for example).

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-030: query and answer description, the three credential modes, `publishTarget` and `tokenTtlSeconds`; R-UI-009 (`credentials=none`).

### Q-API-161 · An operation of the published contract that is not built answers 501 `not_implemented`

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

The UI of the packages area is built before the package read model and the format contract exist. The generated server interface forces a handler for every operation of the document.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Leave the operations out of the document until they are built | The UI is written against a hand-made type | No stub | The document is the contract (R-API-002); the UI types could not be generated; the two halves would diverge |
| (b) Document them and answer `501` with the problem code `not_implemented` | `internal/api/v1/packages_api.go` | The UI is generated from the real contract; a stub is visible and cannot be mistaken for an empty result; the route check of R-API-002 stays whole | One more status in the document for these operations |
| (c) Answer an empty `200` | An empty list | The screens render without an error state | An empty list is a lie: it says "no package" for an installation that has packages |

**Choice:** (b). The stub writes the problem document of R-API-009 itself, because `internal/errs` has no kind for 501 and no finished operation answers it; `not_implemented` is not an error code of the catalog and the UI shows "This server does not provide this function yet." for it. Each stub is replaced by its implementation, not extended. The smoke test of R-API-002 accepts exactly this answer for documented operations and no other 5xx. The seven operations carry `501` in their responses (`#/components/responses/NotImplemented`); the response goes when the last stub does.

**Rationale:** A stub that is honest is cheaper than a hand-made type that drifts. The development agent revisits this when the work package that implements the operations lands: the stubs, `NotImplemented`, the `501` references and the smoke test's exception are deleted together.

**Revisit (done):** the seven operations are implemented; the stubs, `notImplemented`, `codeNotImplemented`, the `501` responses and `#/components/responses/NotImplemented` of the document, the exception in the smoke test of R-API-002 and the UI's message for `not_implemented` are deleted.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-029 (the sentence on `501` until the read model exists).

### Q-API-162 · Permission declarations and the reserved name `lookup` of the package operations

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

The `x-trove-permission` declaration of an operation is enforced before its handler (R-API-008). The package operations are not about one repository: a package is visible when any of its versions is, and the answer is filtered in SQL (R-API-029).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `{public: true}` and the filter in the handler | The repository list pattern | The decision is per version, which only the read model can make; anonymous callers work where anonymous read is on; the answer for a caller who may see nothing is an empty list or a `404` | The declaration alone says nothing about the filtering; a missing filter would be a leak that the declaration cannot catch |
| (b) `{authenticated: true}` | Any signed-in principal | Simple | Anonymous read (R-UI-004, R-API-029 "anonymous where allowed") would not work |
| (c) A capability such as `packages:read` | A new system capability | Visible in the document | A capability that grants nothing by itself: the decision is still per repository and package (INV-9); it would only add a second place to keep in step |

**Choice:** (a) for the six package operations, and the action form `read` on `path.repoKey` for the client setup operation. `lookup` is a reserved name of `{packageId}` (R-API-004): `GET /api/v1/packages/lookup` is a literal next to the key, so the parameter schema lists it in `x-trove-reserved-names`, which the document check demands; package identifiers (`pkg_…`) can never be `lookup`.

**Rationale:** The same reasoning as for `GET /api/v1/repositories`: the declaration admits the caller, the read model filters, and a hidden package is a `404` identical to a missing one. The implementation test is therefore the one of R-API-029's second acceptance criterion (a caller who reads only one repository sees only its versions), and it belongs to the work package that writes the read model. The development agent revisits this if a package operation gains a write form (ownership, R-API-048), which gets an action declaration on its repository.

**Applied in the spec:** none; the declarations are in the OpenAPI document.

### Q-API-163 · The version details, the README and their tags

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

R-API-029 states that the README answer is `404` when the version has none. The page needs to know whether to ask, and a README is the largest answer of the area.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Ask and treat a `404` as "none" | No flag | No new member | A request per version page that fails by design; a console error in the browser for every package without a README |
| (b) `hasReadme` on the version details | The page asks only when it is `true` | No failing request; the default tab is known with the details | A member the read model must keep true; a `true` that is followed by a `404` (the README was removed between the two calls) is handled as "none" |
| (c) Inline the README in the details | One call | Fewer calls | Every version call carries up to 1 MiB; the tag of the details would change with the image policy |

**Choice:** (b). The details and the README carry strong `ETag`s and honour `If-None-Match` (R-API-012); the README's tag covers the source hash, the renderer version and the hash of the external image origins, the three inputs of the cache row in R-API-029, so a changed origin list changes it. The README answer is `{contentType: text/markdown, html, truncated, externalImagesBlocked}`; `contentType` names the source, the HTML is always sanitized HTML.

**Rationale:** A failing request by design is noise for the operator and for the user's console; the flag costs one boolean. The UI treats a `404` for a README it asked for as "none" anyway, so a stale flag is harmless. The development agent revisits this when README extraction for NuGet (`<readme>` file) differs enough that the flag cannot be computed from metadata alone.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-029 (the version details and the README answer).

### Q-API-164 · A package id is derived from the format and the normalized name

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

R-API-029 names `id` (`pkg_01JBQ6V7S3K9` in the example) and addresses a package by it. The generic package rows are per repository (`packages (repo_id, name)`), so the package of the API, which spans repositories, has no row of its own: the same name in `npm-local` and `npm-team` is one package of the view and two rows of the store.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A table of package ids | A new table, an id per (format, name), written on the first publish | Ids that look like the example | A write path in every format's publish for the sake of a read model; an id that a restore or a second installation does not reproduce; a row whose lifetime follows no repository |
| (b) A hash of format and name | `pkg_` and a digest | Fixed length | Not reversible, so every request with an id needs a table that maps it back |
| (c) The format and the name, encoded | `pkg_` and the lower-case base32 of `<format> NUL <name>` | Needs no table; the same on every replica, after a restore and on a second installation; resolves by decoding | Not short (a 214-character name is a 350-character id); anyone who knows the name can compute the id |

**Choice:** (c). `view.ID` and `view.ParseID` (`internal/packages/view/id.go`); the alphabet is `[a-z2-7]`, inside the pattern `^pkg_[0-9A-Za-z]+$` of the document. The id is opaque to clients and is no secret and no capability: it names a package, it does not grant the right to read it. An id that decodes to a package the caller may not read answers the `404` of an id that names nothing, so the id reveals nothing that the name did not. A string that does not decode is the same `404`.

**Rationale:** An id that needs a table needs a write in every format, and the view is a read model. The length is the price; names are bounded (npm: 214 characters) and the id travels in a path segment. The development agent revisits this when a format has names above what a path segment carries (Maven coordinates, container image names): the id then becomes a digest with a lookup row written by the same code that writes the package.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-029 (what an id is).

### Q-API-165 · The visibility filter is decided per repository and passed into the statement

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

R-API-029 requires that every aggregate of the list counts only versions the caller may read and that the filter runs in SQL. What a caller may read is decided by the grant index in memory (grants with package and path patterns, the token scope, `content:bypass`, the endpoint's exposure rules with version ranges), not by a table PostgreSQL could join.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) List, then filter | Read the packages and their counts, then drop what the caller may not read | Simple | A count includes hidden versions; the version number of a hidden latest version leaks through the aggregate; the page sizes are wrong |
| (b) Decide every version in Go, count in Go | Read every version row, ask the decision point per row | Always right | A list of ten packages reads every version of the installation |
| (c) Classify the repositories, pass the classification as data | Per repository: all (every package and version of it may be read), none, or rows (decide row by row); the statement takes the keys of the first group and the readable rows of the third | The common case (a reader of whole repositories) is one array of keys; the per-row work is limited to repositories where a grant or a ceiling narrows | Needs a classification that is exactly as strict as the decision point, and a bound on the rows decided in Go |
| (d) Mirror the grants into a table | A materialised grant table joined in SQL | The database does the filtering | A second copy of the decision point; it must follow the exposure ranges of every format |

**Choice:** (c). `authz.ReadScoper.ReadScopeOn` (`internal/authz/visible.go`) returns a `ReadScope` for the request's index: `Shape(key)` is `ReadAll` only when an unrestricted read grant (or `content:bypass`) holds, the token scope does not narrow and the endpoint exposes everything; `ReadNone` for a repository the index does not know, a virtual one (it holds no rows; it shows its members' rows) and one without a read grant; `ReadRows` otherwise. `MayRead(repo, package, version)` is `DecideOn` without the audit event and the denial counters. `view.Service.Scope` lists the versions of the `ReadRows` repositories (at most `DefaultMaxRows`, 200 000; more answers `400`, never a partial set), asks `MayRead` of each and passes the keys of `ReadAll` and the readable `repo, package, version` triples to the statements of `package_view.sql` as arrays. A test (`TestR_API_029_ReadScopeAgreesWithTheDecisionPoint`) checks the classification against `DecideOn` over every subject, endpoint, repository, package and version of a fixture. A repository with include or exclude patterns is never read whole: its versions are decided row by row, with the patterns (`Topology.Admits`) in front of the grant. A virtual repository is shown in a version's `repositories` only when the caller may read it and one of its members holds the version.

**Rationale:** (c) makes the filter part of the statement that counts, so no aggregate can include a hidden version, and keeps the cost proportional to what a narrowed caller can see. The bound turns "too broad" into a refusal that says so. The development agent revisits this when an installation has callers with package-narrowed grants on repositories with more than 200 000 versions: the per-row decision then moves into the statement as a compiled pattern set.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-029 (the visibility rule and its bound); [security: permissions](../security/permissions.md).

### Q-API-166 · The format reaches the view data through an adapter on its data port

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

The package list shows a description and keywords, the details show licenses, the metadata of the format and the README. npm writes no generic attributes for them: they are in `npm_versions` (the manifest, the README, the deprecation) and `npm_packages` (the dist-tags). The generic rows give names, versions, counts, times, sizes, downloads and files.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Attributes set at publish | `OnCommit` writes description, keywords, licenses into `package_versions.attributes` | The generic query reads everything; no adapter | A copy of the manifest in a second place that every edit path must keep equal (deprecate, the tombstone replay, a restore); the README and the metadata do not fit; data the format already holds twice |
| (b) A `ViewAdapter` on the format contract that reads through the format's data port | `Format.View()` returns `Compare`, `Prerelease`, `Describe`, `Find` and `Withheld`; npm implements them in `internal/formats/npm/view.go` over `internal/formatdata/npm/view.go`; `internal/formathost` bridges to the domain package `internal/packages/view` | One source of truth; R-ARCH-008 holds (no SQL in the format, the statements are in the data port); the format also owns the order of its versions and what a pre-release is; a format without an adapter has no package screens and fails nothing | One more method on the contract (it is frozen only at the end of M3, Q-ARCH-213); the adapter is asked in batches |
| (c) Generic SQL over the format's JSON | The view reads `npm_versions.manifest` itself | No contract change | The core would know npm's tables; the second format breaks it |

**Choice:** (b). `formats.ViewAdapter` (`internal/formats/view.go`): `Compare` and `Prerelease` order the versions (SemVer precedence for npm; the core never compares version strings); `Describe` reads description, keywords, licenses, the README flag, the metadata and, when asked, the README for versions, with the visible set of the package so that the dist-tags name no hidden version; `Find` answers the `q` and `keyword` filters over the format's data (the core intersects the ids with what the caller may read); `Withheld` lists the stored versions the format does not serve (npm: tombstoned, R-NPM-047), which the view never counts. `Validate` refuses a format with a view and no package names. `Base.View()` is nil.

**Rationale:** The metadata of a version is the format's; copying it into generic attributes would make every writer responsible for two copies. The adapter keeps the read model free of any format and gives a second format one place to say what its packages look like. The development agent revisits this when the batch reads of a list page show up in a profile: the adapter then gets a summary table maintained in the publish transaction.

**Applied in the spec:** [architecture.md](architecture.md) (the format contract, `View`); [formats/npm.md](formats/npm.md) (the view); R-API-029 (the members that come from the format).

### Q-API-167 · The README is rendered on the server on demand and not cached yet

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

R-API-029 puts the README renderer on the server and sketches a table `package_readme_cache` (source hash, renderer version, image policy hash, HTML). R-UI-008 sets the limits: the source at most `ui.readme.max_source_bytes`, the HTML at most 1 MiB, the rendering at most two seconds.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Render on demand, tag from the inputs | The strong `ETag` is a hash of the source, the renderer version and the hash of the origin list; a request that holds the tag costs no rendering | No table, no invalidation; a changed policy changes the tag without a migration | A client that sends no tag pays a rendering every time |
| (b) The cache table now | Render once per (version, inputs) | One rendering per README | A table written on a read path, a job that prunes it, a migration, and a row per README per policy |
| (c) Render at publish | The HTML in the version row | No rendering on read | The renderer version is then a data migration |

**Choice:** (a). `readme.Renderer` (`internal/packages/readme`) is goldmark with the GitHub-style extensions and raw HTML, bluemonday with the allowlist of R-UI-008, and a pass over the parsed result for what an allowlist cannot say: the links (an absolute `http`, `https` or `mailto` address keeps its target and gets `rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer"`; a fragment stays; anything else is reduced to its text), the images (an `https` image of a listed origin stays, an image of trove's own origin or a relative or other source is dropped, every other becomes a link "External image: <alt>" and is counted), disabled checkboxes, and the heading anchors (Q-UI-76). A source above the limit is cut; an HTML above 1 MiB is re-rendered from a proportionally shorter source; a rendering above two seconds is abandoned for the escaped text; each sets `truncated`. A list of origins that names an origin of the installation is refused at start-up. The cache table of R-API-029 is not built: its three inputs are the parts of the tag, and the table is added when a profile asks for it (H-298).

**Rationale:** The browser keeps the answer by its tag; the server renders for a first view and for a changed policy. The development agent revisits this when README requests dominate the CPU of a replica, or when the abandoned renderings of H-298 show up in a profile: the table then holds the HTML and the abandoned work is bounded by it.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-029 (the data model block is marked as not built), R-UI-008 (configuration, the origin check).

### Q-API-168 · Client setup: templates produce the structure, the API produces the credential mode, the package and the quoting

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

R-API-030 asks for three credential modes (`placeholder`, `env`, `none`), the package of an install snippet, shell and XML quoting, and addresses from the configured base URL. The npm templates of R-NPM-041 are `text/template` over `SetupData`, which has no credential field, and always spell the credential as `${TROVE_TOKEN}`.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Every template implements the modes | Three variants per snippet | Each format is in control | Three copies of every file template; every format re-implements quoting |
| (b) The API rewrites the rendered text | The template spells the token as the literal `formats.SetupTokenRef` and the package as `formats.SetupPackageRef`; the API replaces the first by the placeholder or the configured variable (`ui.client_setup.token_env_var`) or drops the lines that hold it, and the second by the quoted package | The modes and the quoting exist once; a template stays one text; `RequiresAuth` is cleared for `none` so that an always-auth switch goes with the credential | The template and the API share two literals |
| (c) The UI strips and substitutes | The server sends the `env` form | Nothing on the server | The UI would parse client syntax (Q-API-160) |

**Choice:** (b). The templates also get the functions `shell` and `xml` for values they place in a command or in XML. A package name or version above 256 bytes, with a control character or in the shape of a token (`trv_(pat|sat|cit)_`) is refused with `400`, so that the answer cannot echo a token it was handed; every snippet is checked against the shape again before it is sent. The addresses are built on the configured base URL of the endpoint the request arrived on; without one the operation answers `503`, because an address from the `Host` of the request would end in a file the user copies. `requiresAuth` of the templates is true unless an anonymous caller on the same endpoint may read the repository. The publish tab is rendered only for a caller who holds `deploy` on the publish target (the repository itself when local, the deploy target of a virtual one, none for a remote one) and `publishTarget` names it. The snippet id is `<client>.<section>[.<name>]`, with `-scoped` appended to the name of the scoped variant of a configure snippet. The npm templates contribute configure and install snippets (R-NPM-041); the publish and CI snippets of R-UI-017 are not templates yet, so the publish tab is empty for npm until they are (the API renders them where a format supplies them). The npm publish templates arrived with Q-API-180.

**Rationale:** The mode and the quoting are the security-relevant part of the operation and belong in one place with one test (`TestR_API_030_*`, the integration tests over every client, mode and caller). The development agent revisits this when the first format needs a credential in a place that is not a line (NuGet's `nuget.config` element): the literal then becomes a typed marker.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-030 (clients, `503` without a base URL, token refusal, the publish tab); [formats/npm.md](formats/npm.md) (the templates).

### Q-API-136 · One rule for the top-level code of an error

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Four areas answered a duplicate create with three codes (`already_exists`, `conflict`, `repository_exists`) and a 422 under the
code of its first or only violation; the contract tests carried overrides for the repository resource.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Per-area codes | Each page documents its own | Specific at the top | One client rule per resource |
| (b) The convention's codes (chosen) | Duplicate create: 409 `already_exists`. A 422 with fields: `validation_failed`. A body that cannot be read or names an unknown member: 400 `malformed_request` with the pointer. Resource-specific codes live in `errors[].code` | One rule | The specific code is one level down |

**Choice:** (b), with `reserved_name` (R-API-004) as the one top-level 422 code besides `validation_failed`, and `idempotency_key_reused`
(R-API-014). The query filters of the policy list that name nothing (`unknown_principal`, `unknown_repository`) answer 422
`validation_failed` with the parameter name as the pointer.

**Rationale:** codes are a stable contract (R-ARCH-025); a client matching on the top-level code needs no knowledge of the
resource. The development agent would revisit this if a client needs the specific code at the top.

**Applied in the spec:** the 409 and 422 rows of R-API-009; [Q-REPO-84](repositories-and-proxy.md#q-repo-84--a-violation-answers-422-validation_failed-a-body-error-400-malformed_request);
the codes of the policy and role-binding operations (R-AUTHZ-021, R-AUTHZ-022, R-AUTHZ-023) read as codes in `errors[]`.

### Q-API-137 · A refused idempotent request is stored in the transaction that claimed the key

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

R-API-014 stores a 4xx outcome so that a retry gets the same answer. The refusal was stored in a second transaction after the first
rolled back, so a concurrent duplicate that waited on the claimed row could claim it and run the operation again.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A second transaction (as before) | Roll back, then store | No savepoint | A waiting duplicate re-executes |
| (b) A savepoint around the operation (chosen) | A refusal rolls back to the savepoint, drops the hooks the operation registered (`meta.TxState.Discard`), stores the refusal on the claimed row and commits | The duplicate finds the stored answer | A refusal now commits a transaction |

**Choice:** (b). The short lock wait of the claim (`lock_timeout`) is restored to the session value right after the claim, so the
operation does not run under it.

**Rationale:** the claim and the answer become one commit. The development agent would revisit this if an operation needs the
transaction to fail as a whole.

**Applied in the spec:** none (R-API-014 already says a stored 4xx outcome is replayed).

### Q-API-138 · A CORS preflight is answered before authentication

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

A browser sends a preflight without credentials. The preflight stage sat after authentication (stage 7), so an endpoint that
refuses anonymous requests answered 401 and every cross-origin call failed.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Keep it in stage 7 | As before | One stage | R-API-018 cannot hold |
| (b) A preflight stage between stage 5 and 6 (chosen) | `Chain.Preflight` answers the preflight of an allowed origin on an API path with 204 and passes everything else on | Opens nothing else; the actual request is authenticated | The preflight is not counted by the rate limits, only by the in-flight limit |

**Choice:** (b).

**Rationale:** the answer is constant and carries no data. The development agent would revisit this if preflights need a limit of
their own.

**Applied in the spec:** none (R-API-018 already requires the preflight to be answered).

### Q-API-169 · The package protocols have rate-limit classes of their own

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the general classes of R-API-016 limited `/api/v1/` and `/files/` only, and the class an endpoint applies (R-EP-015) is empty on the default endpoint. A caller with a token could therefore send unlimited package requests to the default endpoint: one upstream request per invented name through a remote repository, and full publish attempts that cost a spool and a validation each (S-4).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Three more classes for `/api/<format>/`, with buckets and budgets of their own | `package_read` 200/s burst 1000, `package_write` 10/s burst 50, `package_anonymous` 20/s burst 100 | A lockfile install does not use up the management budget of its token; the same stage and fields as the other classes; no endpoint needs configuring | Three more keys |
| (b) The existing classes for the package protocols | Same buckets | No new keys | One `npm ci` of a few hundred tarballs exhausts the token's management API; the read budget of 50/s is too small for installs |
| (c) Give the default endpoint a default endpoint class | R-EP-015 limits the whole endpoint | No new classes | The UI and the management API of the default endpoint share that budget; a default of `""` is what R-EP-001 documents |

**Choice:** (a). `isPackagePath` (`/api/` below which `/api/v1/` is not) selects the classes in `internal/api/v1/ratelimit.go`; the configuration is `api.rate_limits.package_read`, `package_write` and `package_anonymous`.

**Rationale:** the limit is for fairness and for the cost of a request, and a package request costs more than a management read. The read budget admits 1,000 requests in a burst because an install asks for every tarball of its lockfile at once; npm retries a 429 with `Retry-After` in any case. The development agent would revisit the budgets with the measurements of the performance run, and the path rule when host-root bindings (R-EP-006) serve package routes at `/`: the classification must then follow the route, not the prefix.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-016 (the classes, the configuration, the acceptance criterion).

### Q-API-170 · The package list cursor carries the normalized name

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the list statement sorts and compares keyset positions on the normalized name, and the cursor carried the display name. For a format whose display name differs from its normalized name (a case-preserving format), `Newtonsoft.Json` was compared bytewise with `newtonsoft.json`; because `N` is below `n`, an ascending page repeated rows and a descending page skipped rows. npm passes `name, name` today, so the fault was dormant.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `view.Package.Key` holds the normalized name, and the cursor is built from it | The cursor carries what the statement compares | Correct for every format; one field | The view model has a field the API does not show |
| (b) The statement compares the display name | The cursor stays | No new field | The order would no longer be bytewise on the name the format normalizes, and the unique key of a package is the normalized name |

**Choice:** (a).

**Rationale:** the keyset must be taken from the same column the order is. The development agent would revisit the choice only if a sort by display name is wanted by users.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-029 (the order and the cursor).

### Q-API-175 · Two guide operations, rendered on the server

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: R-UI-049 needs the guide of a repository and the guide of a class before a repository is chosen. The text is the format's (Q-ARCH-235) and must use the installation's addresses and the caller's rights.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `GET /api/v1/repositories/{key}/guide?client=` and `GET /api/v1/formats/{format}/guide?class=&client=`, sections rendered to sanitized HTML on the server | Two operations, one answer shape | One renderer and sanitizer (R-UI-008); the server fills addresses, target and credential mode like R-API-030 | Two operations to document |
| (b) One operation that takes the raw Markdown templates, rendered in the browser | `GET /api/v1/formats/{format}/guide-templates` | One operation | A Markdown renderer and its sanitizer in the browser, a second rule set; the browser fills addresses |
| (c) Fold the guide into the client setup answer | `client-setup` grows sections | No new operation | The setup answer carries the token modes; a guide must never carry one (Q-API-176) |

**Choice:** (a). The repository operation needs `read` on the repository; the format operation is public like `GET /api/v1/formats`. Sections are filtered by the class and the client, ordered by topic, and a section that renders to nothing is left out, so a format writes conditional sections (an anonymous reader, an endpoint without rules) as templates.

**Rationale:** The server already owns the addresses, the caller's rights and the sanitizer; the browser binds HTML it can finish (Q-UI-71). The development agent revisits this if a guide must be shown where the management API is not reachable (a static export of the documentation).

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-053, R-API-020, R-API-022.

### Q-API-176 · A guide references the credential and never holds it

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the client setup offers three credential modes (R-API-030), one of them a placeholder the browser fills with a token (Q-UI-74). A guide shows the configure snippet too.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `env` for a signed-in caller, `none` for an anonymous one; the snippets go through the setup's renderer | No placeholder, no token mode | A guide can be copied, cached, printed without holding a secret; its snippet equals the setup page's default | A reader who wants a token goes to the setup page |
| (b) The guide offers the three modes | The setup page's choice | One page for everything | The token would live in a second component (R-UI-043) |

**Choice:** (a). The reference `${TROVE_TOKEN}` in a section's text is rewritten by the same function as a snippet's (`${<ui.client_setup.token_env_var>}`, or the line is dropped for an anonymous reader), and every answer is checked for the shape of a token before it is sent.

**Rationale:** The guide is reading; the token stays with the one page built for it. The development agent revisits this if the setup page and the guides area merge.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-053.

### Q-API-177 · The formats answer names each format's clients

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: R-UI-049 must offer a new format without a new screen. Q-UI-70 kept the clients of the setup page in a UI table and named (b), the descriptor, as the revisit for NuGet.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `clients: [{id, displayName}]` in each format descriptor of `GET /api/v1/formats` | From `Descriptor().Clients` | The guides area needs no table; a format with clients is a format with a guide (kit check 8) | A required member more in the catalog |
| (b) The guide answer lists the clients | Ask the guide first | No catalog change | The page needs a client to ask for a guide: a circle |
| (c) A UI table, as for the setup page | `clients.ts` | Exists | A new format needs a UI release |

**Choice:** (a). npm's display names are the labels the setup page used ("Yarn Berry (2 and later)", "Yarn Classic (1.x)", Q-NPM-67), so both pages read the same. The setup page keeps its table for now, because its explanations of the snippets are translated per snippet id (Q-UI-70); moving it onto the member is the revisit of Q-UI-70 at NuGet.

**Rationale:** The client list is a fact of the format; the catalog is where the UI reads the format's facts. The development agent revisits this with Q-UI-70.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-022, R-UI-049.

### Q-API-178 · The guide renderer is the README renderer with a bound of its own

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: R-UI-008's renderer cuts a source at `ui.readme.max_source_bytes`, which an operator may set as low as 1 KiB, because a README is untrusted content. npm's troubleshooting section alone is about 9 KiB.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A second instance of the renderer with a fixed 256 KiB bound and no image origins | Same code, same sanitizer, `PackageServices.Guides` | A guide is never cut by a setting meant for untrusted input; one sanitizer | One more instance at start-up |
| (b) The README instance | One instance | Nothing new | An operator's README limit cuts the guide |
| (c) No sanitizer for trusted text | Render only | Cheaper | A format's text would reach `innerHTML` with one layer less; the browser layers stay but the rule of R-UI-008 is broken |

**Choice:** (a). The guide carries no images: an image becomes a link, as for a README without listed origins.

**Rationale:** The bound protects the server from input; a format's own text is not input, but sanitizing it costs nothing and keeps one rule for every HTML the UI binds. The development agent revisits this if a format's guide needs images.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-053.

### Q-API-179 · What a guide names

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: a guide of a virtual repository explains members and the deployment target; the members and the target are configuration (`repositories:read-config`), and a reader of the repository may hold neither that nor `deploy`.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The guide explains the order and the deployment target generically, names the target only to a caller who may deploy there, and never lists the members | As `publishTarget` of R-API-030 | Reveals nothing the client setup does not; a config reader sees the members on the same screen | The guide of a virtual repository is less specific |
| (b) List the members the caller may read | Specific | The caller can read those repositories | Membership is configuration the consumer view withholds |

**Choice:** (a). Both operations need a configured base URL and answer `503` without one, like R-API-030; the guide of a format writes `<repository>` for the key and is as public as the format list, so it says nothing about any repository.

**Rationale:** A guide must not become a way around the consumer view. The development agent revisits this if the consumer view gains the members.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-053; H-321.

### Q-API-180 · Publish snippets address the repository the caller chose

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the npm format had no publish templates, so the Publish tab of the client setup page was empty for every npm repository and, for a virtual one, said it had no deployment target even when it had one (the UI fake served snippets the server did not, so no spec noticed). R-UI-017 wrote the publish registry as the URL of the deployment target. A client sends its credential to the registry whose URL the credential line is keyed to (R-NPM-041), and the configure snippet keys it to the URL of the selected repository.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The publish snippet names the selected repository | `npm publish --registry …/api/npm/npm-all/` for a virtual repository; it forwards the publish to its deployment target (R-REPO-021) | The credential line of the configure snippet matches the URL, so the snippet works as shown; no second credential line; the target key need not be shown to the template | The snippet does not show the target; the page shows `publishTarget` next to it |
| (b) The snippet names the deployment target | `npm publish --registry …/api/npm/npm-local/` | Shows where the package lands | The credential is keyed to the virtual repository's URL, so the client sends none to the target and the publish answers 401 unless a second credential line is added |

**Choice:** (a). The templates need no new field of `SetupData`; the API renders the publish templates for a caller who holds `deploy` on the publish target, and `publishTarget` names that target. The CI snippets of R-UI-017 stay outside the templates. The UI fake renders what the server renders (the fake served a GitLab CI snippet and the target URL before).

**Rationale:** a snippet that is correct only with an added credential line is not correct. The development agent revisits this if the template data gains the second credential line, or if the owner wants the snippet to show the target.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-030, R-UI-017, [formats/npm.md](formats/npm.md) R-NPM-041. Code: `internal/formats/npm/setup.go`; `web/src/app/api/testing/fakes-packages.ts`. Tests: `TestR_API_030_NpmPublishSnippets`.

### Q-API-184 · The UI redirect reads the session cookie itself to find the stored locale

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: R-UI-045 puts the user's stored locale before `Accept-Language`. `webui.Options.Preference` exists for that, but the
composition root did not set it, so a signed-in user with a stored German locale who opened `/ui/` got the browser's language
(found on 2026-11-01). Setting the option is not enough: the authentication stage accepts the session cookie only on the paths of
R-AUTH-001 item 3 and ignores it on `/ui/`, so the principal of a `/ui/` request is anonymous.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The redirect peeks at the session itself (chosen) | `Preference` reads `__Host-trv_session`, resolves it with the read-only `Store.Peek` (the lookup, the freshness gate and the deadline check of `Validate`, without its writes and without filling the session cache, Q-AUTH-185), reads the stored locale of that user | Nothing else changes: the stage still ignores the cookie on `/ui/`; the same lookup and deadlines as everywhere else, so an ended or forged cookie names nobody; a redirect writes nothing: it does not extend the idle deadline, end an expired session or end the break-glass sessions of a disabled account | One session validation and one read of `user_preferences` per request for a locale-less UI path, which is a redirect, not a page |
| (b) Let the stage accept the session cookie on `GET /ui/` | `sessionAllowed` returns true for the UI shell | The principal is there for any later UI code | An invalid cookie would answer `401 session_expired` for the UI shell, the dead-cookie lock-out of Q-AUTH-177 |
| (c) Keep a `locale` cookie the UI sets | The redirect reads a plain cookie | No lookup | A second source of truth next to the preference, and a cookie that stays after the user changes the preference elsewhere |

**Choice:** (a). `Validate` touches `last_seen_at`, ends expired sessions and ends break-glass sessions where the account is disabled, and a redirect to a page must do none of that, so `Peek` exists for it. The function is bounded by two seconds, which holds for the request that starts a shared lookup too (Q-AUTH-181); a failing session store or database, an unreadable row, a user without a
stored locale and a locale the build does not serve all fall back to `Accept-Language`. A replica without a session store (the
shell profile) sets no preference function.

**Rationale:** a redirect that costs one cached session lookup and one indexed read is cheap, and (b) would bring back the lock-out
that Q-AUTH-177 removed. The development agent would revisit this if the redirect of `/ui/` showed up as a hot path, then with a short
cache keyed by the session hash.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-045 (locale choice and acceptance criteria). Code: `Store.Peek` in `internal/auth/session/store.go`, `internal/app/ui_locale.go`, `startClient` in
`internal/app/app.go`.

### Q-API-185 · The ETag of the authentication settings follows the status, and a write takes only the revision

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the ETag of `GET /api/v1/settings/auth` was the revision of the settings row, and `If-None-Match` was answered before the read-only
status was computed. The status changes without the row (a lockout, a provider's discovery document, and now the state of the break-glass
password), so a client holding the tag was told `304` about a status that had moved.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The tag is `"<revision>-<digest of the status>"`; a write reads the revision only (chosen) | The status is computed first; `PATCH` takes the number before the first `-` of the `If-Match` | A moved status is a new tag; the tag from a `GET` still works as `If-Match`, whatever the status did meanwhile | A client sees tags that change without a write |
| (b) Never answer 304 | Drop the conditional GET | Simple | The screen polls the document |
| (c) Include the status in the write's precondition | `If-Match` fails when the status moved | Strict | A lockout would make a save fail with 412 although no setting changed |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the revision is the precondition of a write, the digest only the validator of a read. The development agent would
revisit this if the status held per-replica values that differ between replicas (the discovery state does), then by leaving those out of the digest.

**Applied in the spec:** R-AUTH-040 (read), `api/openapi.yaml` (`getAuthSettings`). Code: `settingsETag` and `settingsRevision` in
`internal/api/v1/authsettings_api.go`.
