the preferences operations use.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The package that owns the preferences exports the read (chosen) | `v1.PreferredLocale` over `loadPreferences`; the redirect calls it | One reading of the table, with its defaults (a user without a row has none) | The composition root imports one more function of the API package, which it already imports |
| (b) A second statement | As built | None | Two readings of one table that can drift |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** a change of the preferences table or of what "no stored locale" means is made once. The development agent would
revisit this if preferences moved into a package of their own. **Applied in the spec:** R-API-021, R-UI-045. Code: `PreferredLocale` in
`internal/api/v1/preferences_api.go`, `uiPreference` in `internal/app/ui_locale.go`.

### Q-API-187 · The token reference has one spelling per shell

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the API rewrote one literal, `${TROVE_TOKEN}`, by the credential mode. A `nuget.config` value and a cmd command expand `%NAME%`, PowerShell `$env:NAME`; a POSIX `${NAME}` there is text. `credentials=env` for NuGet would otherwise write a reference that the client does not expand.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Three literals, `SetupTokenRef`, `SetupTokenRefWin`, `SetupTokenRefPS`; the API rewrites each into the same variable in its own syntax (chosen) | A template spells the one its file or shell expands | Modes and quoting stay the API's; a template stays one text; `none` drops the line with any of them | Three literals instead of one |
| (b) The API chooses the syntax by the template's language | One literal | Fewer constants | A `nuget.config` is `xml` and a Windows batch file is `cmd`; a language does not say who expands; the mapping hides in the API |
| (c) A template function `{{tokenRef}}` | The template calls the API | Explicit | A template would execute with a function that returns what the API then rewrites, and the kit could no longer read the template text for a credential |

**Choice:** (a). The kit (check 8) does not count any of the three as a credential; `placeholder` writes `{{token}}` for each.

**Rationale:** the literal in the template text is what the kit scans. The development agent revisits this when a client needs a fourth syntax.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-030. Code: `internal/formats/setup.go`, `internal/api/v1/setup_snippets.go` (`applyCredentials`), `internal/formats/formattest/checks.go`. Tests: `TestR_API_030_EachShellGetsTheTokenReferenceItExpands`, kit check 8 cases in `kit_test.go`.

### Q-API-188 · The format chooses how a version follows the package in an install snippet

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: `substitutePackage` wrote `package@version`, which is npm's syntax. `dotnet add package X --version 1.2.3` and `Install-Package X -RequiredVersion 1.2.3` take the version as an option.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `SetupTemplate.VersionSpec` with the placeholder `<version>`; "" keeps `@<version>` (chosen) | The template states the form | npm templates stay as they are; the package and the version are quoted each on its own inside the option | One more field |
| (b) Two placeholders in the template text, `<package>` and `<version>` | The template places both | No field | Without a version the option text stays in the command; npm's templates change |
| (c) The API knows the clients | A switch on the client ID | No field | Shared code that names a format's clients |

**Choice:** (a). Without a version the package stands alone. The kit refuses a `VersionSpec` on a template that is not an install template, does not place `<package>`, or whose spec does not place `<version>`.

**Rationale:** the syntax of a client's option is the format's knowledge. The development agent revisits this when a snippet needs the version without the package.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-030, R-ARCH-008 (`SetupTemplate`). Code: `internal/formats/setup.go`, `internal/api/v1/setup_snippets.go` (`substitutePackage`), `internal/formats/formattest/checks.go` (`versionSpec`). Tests: `TestR_API_030_TheFormatChoosesHowTheVersionIsAttached`, kit check 8.

### Q-API-189 · Setup templates may be PowerShell or cmd, each with its own quoting

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: `Lang` was `shell`, `ini`, `xml` or `yaml`, and `shell` meant POSIX quoting. The NuGet snippets include PowerShell and cmd commands, in which a POSIX-quoted package name is not safe.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Languages `powershell` and `cmd` with a quoting function each, also offered to templates (chosen) | PowerShell: single quotes, `'` doubled; cmd: double quotes, `"` and `%` doubled, line breaks dropped | A substituted value cannot break out of the command in either shell | Two more quoting functions to keep correct; cmd cannot quote everything (a line break is dropped, not carried) |
| (b) POSIX quoting everywhere | One function | Nothing new | Wrong in both shells: `'a b'` is not one argument in cmd |
| (c) Refuse every value outside the safe set in those languages | A 400 | No quoting | A legitimate id or version never needs it, but the refusal belongs to the request validation, which does not know the template's language |

**Choice:** (a). The package and the version of a NuGet request are IDs and versions of a fixed alphabet, so the quoting is a second line of defence there, as it is for npm.

**Rationale:** quoting by the language the snippet is shown in. The development agent revisits this when a value outside the alphabet can reach a cmd template.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-030. Code: `internal/api/v1/setup_snippets.go` (`powershellQuote`, `cmdQuote`, `quoterFor`). Tests: `TestR_API_030_PowerShellAndCmdValuesAreQuoted`.

### Q-API-190 · The NuGet settings are a typed member of the repository document, and the format enums follow the registry

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

NuGet registers its format with the class `local` alone (Q-NUGET-28), and the four enums `FormatName`, `LocalFormatName`, `RemoteFormatName` and `VirtualFormatName` are generated from the registry (R-ARCH-010).

|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `NugetSettings` beside `NpmSettings`, `Repository.nuget` refers to it, the equality test runs per format, and the enums list `nuget` where the registry does (chosen) | `nuget` is in `FormatName` and `LocalFormatName` and in neither of the other two until its classes exist | The create form offers NuGet for a local repository only; the generated clients carry the member; a setting added to one statement without the other fails the test | A hand-written schema per format |
| (b) `nuget` in all four enums | The enums are final | None | The create form would offer a class the service refuses, and `TestR_ARCH_010_PerClassFormatEnums` fails |
| (c) An untyped `nuget` object | `additionalProperties: true` | Nothing to keep in step | The generated clients lose the member's type and the equality with the registered schema is not checked |

**Rationale:** the development agent revisits this when the remote adapter lists the class `remote` (the enum, the member's `forwardSearch` description and the test then need no edit beyond the enum).

**Applied in the spec:** R-REPO-004 already states the rule; none. Code: `api/openapi.yaml` (`NugetSettings`, `Repository.nuget`, the format enums), `internal/api/v1/format_settings_test.go`, `internal/repository/document.go` (`Settings.NuGet`, `formatMembers`). Tests: `TestR_ARCH_008_NugetSettingsSchemaEqualsTheOpenAPIMember`, `TestR_ARCH_010_PerClassFormatEnums`, `TestR_NUGET_007_TheNuGetMemberOfADocument`.

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: Q-API-189 gave the setup templates the languages `powershell` and `cmd` for their quoting. The `language` of a `ClientSnippet` is an enum of the OpenAPI document (`ini`, `yaml`, `json`, `shell`, `xml`, `text`) and the NuGet snippets use both new values. R-ARCH-025 fails the compatibility check for a value added to a response enum, and for an enum that becomes extensible, against the last release (oasdiff `response-property-enum-value-added`, `response-property-became-not-enum`).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Report `powershell` and `cmd` as `shell` (chosen) | The template keeps its language for quoting; the answer says `shell` for every command line | The enum stays; no client written against the last release meets an unknown value | A client cannot tell PowerShell from a POSIX shell by the field; the snippet id (`dotnet.configure.powershell`) and the content say it |
| (b) Add the values to the enum | The document lists them | Exact | Fails R-ARCH-025 until the next major version |
| (c) Make the enum extensible | `x-extensible-enum` | Future values need no break | The change itself becomes not-an-enum, which R-ARCH-025 also fails |

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-030 (the languages of a template). Code: `internal/api/v1/packages_api.go`, `internal/api/v1/snippet_languages_test.go`.

### Q-UI-106 · How the UI's downloads and uploads reach `api` after the cut

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: ADR-155 asked whether the UI calls a `packages` or `files` route with the session cookie, and if it does, that the
call is served through `api`. Verified in [web/src](../../web/src/app): the upload and the folder creation are
`PUT /files/{repo}/{path}` with the session cookie and the CSRF header ([files-api.ts](../../web/src/app/api/files-api.ts),
`upload`, `createFolder`), and the Download buttons of the browse screen and the package page navigate to the `downloadUrl`
of the item or the version file ([browse.html](../../web/src/app/features/browse/browse.html),
[package-detail.html](../../web/src/app/features/packages/package-detail.html)), which is a `/files/` URL or a package
protocol URL such as `/api/npm/npm-local/@team-a/ui/-/ui-1.4.0.tgz`. After the cut the edge sends those paths to `packages`,
which evaluates no session cookie (R-EP-010).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Session-only content routes on `api`, `GET`, `HEAD`, `PUT /api/v1/repositories/{repoKey}/content/{path}`, running the `/files/` transfer through the same item store; `contentUrl` on items and version files (chosen) | The UI downloads and uploads through `api`; clients keep `downloadUrl` | No session reaches `packages`; one transfer implementation; token clients cannot move bulk traffic to `api` (a request without the session answers `404`); the UI still builds no content URL itself | A second path for the same transfer to test; `api` pods need a spool for the UI's uploads; a protocol URL opened in the browser asks for a credential, because the cookie no longer counts there |
| (b) Signed short-lived download links that `packages` checks | `api` issues a signature for the session's principal, `packages` verifies it | Downloads stay on `packages` | A credential type of its own with expiry, replay and revocation rules; uploads still need a path through `api` |
| (c) The edge routes requests that carry the session cookie to `api` | A header or cookie match at the edge | No URL change | Not portable (an implementation-specific match in the Gateway API, none in a plain Ingress); a misrouted request falls through to `packages` silently |
| (d) `packages` evaluates sessions on `/files/` and package downloads | The old behaviour on those paths | No change | Puts the session store into `packages`, which ADR-155 excludes |

**Choice:** (a). An upload through the content route is bounded by `ui.deploy.max_upload_bytes` on the server (it was a check
in the browser only), which sizes the `api` spool (R-HA-029, R-HA-035).

**Rationale:** the trust cut stays a property of the roles, the transfer stays one implementation, and the rule that the UI
assembles no content URL holds because the API hands it `contentUrl`. The development agent would revisit this when the content
origin of [architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-029 (P1) is built: package content shown in the browser then loads from that
origin, and `contentUrl` points where that requirement says.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-025 (the routes and their rules), R-API-029 (`contentUrl`), the links to package content of the
UI baseline, R-UI-012 (uploads); [endpoints.md](endpoints.md) R-EP-010; [architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-001 (what
`api` builds); [ha-and-helm.md](ha-and-helm.md) R-HA-029, R-HA-035 (the `api` spool).

### Q-UI-107 · How the status screen groups replicas after the cut

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: R-UI-038 groups replicas by role (`web`, `worker`) and states drain safety per group (Q-UI-7). After the cut there are
three roles, pools of each, endpoint pools, and during the upgrade across the cut the role `web` beside the new ones.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A group per role (`api`, `packages`, `worker`, and `web` or `all` while one is live), a sub-group per pool with its own counts and drain safety (chosen) | Roles first, pools inside | Drain safety is a property of a Deployment, which a pool is; the upgrade window shows both shapes | A longer screen with many pools |
| (b) A flat group per Deployment | Every pool its own group | Simple | Hides which pools belong to one role; the role's totals are lost |
| (c) Groups per role only, pools as a column | Short | Compact | A pool with one ready replica on one node looks drain-safe inside a healthy role |

**Choice:** (a). The screen is served by `api`, so it is never shown with no live `api` replica; it warns when no `packages`
replica is live, which the UI could otherwise not notice.

**Rationale:** the N + 1 rule of R-HA-059 holds per role and pool; the screen shows it where it holds. The development agent
would revisit this if installations run so many pools that the screen needs a filter.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-038 (the groups and their notices); [operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md)
Q-OPS-161 (the role values).

### Q-API-194 · The role members of the replica descriptions are additive, because the role enums are frozen

Status: **Superseded by [Q-ARCH-341](architecture.md#q-arch-341--code-shaped-only-by-the-compatibility-rules-is-cleaned-up-the-cluster-minimum-version-stays)** (owner, 2026-11-06): the three enums list the real roles and `roleName` is gone. The text below is the record of the superseded decision.

Context: Q-OPS-161 makes the registry's role the `--role` name (`api`, `packages`, `worker`, `web`, `all`). Three enums of the
released contract list roles: `answeredBy.role` of the system information, `Replica.roles` and `EncryptionReplica.role`, each
closed at `web`, `worker` and `all`. R-ARCH-025 fails the compatibility check for a value added to a closed response enum
(oasdiff `response-property-enum-value-added`), and for an enum made extensible (`response-property-became-not-enum`); both were
run against the last release (`make compat-check`).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The three enums keep their meaning as a role class, and the exact role is a new member `roleName` (chosen) | `roles` of an `api` or `packages` replica reads `["web"]`; `roleName` reads `api` or `packages`; `Replica.pool` is new too | Additive, so a client written against the last release keeps working and meets no unknown value; `replicas.roles` is a map and takes the exact names | Two members describe one fact; a reader of the registry's JSON example must know that `roles` is the class |
| (b) Add `api` and `packages` to the three enums | The document lists the values of Q-OPS-161 | One member | Fails R-ARCH-025 until the next breaking version of the API |
| (c) Make the enums extensible | `x-extensible-enum` | Future values need no break | The change itself is `response-property-became-not-enum`, which also fails |
| (d) Report `api` and `packages` as `web` and add nothing | No new member | Smallest change | The status screen cannot group by role, the point of Q-UI-107 |

**Choice:** (a). The class is `web` for every role that serves client endpoints (`api`, `packages`, the bridge `web`), `worker`
for `worker` and `all` for the development role (`roleClass` in [internal/api/v1/roles.go](../../internal/api/v1/roles.go));
the handlers set both members when they read the replica source, so the composition root needs no change for the role members.
`pool` is filled by the source (`internal/app/facts.go`), which holds the registry's value.

**Rationale:** the same precedent as Q-API-191 and Q-VULN-74: keep the closed enum, state the new fact in a new member. The
development agent would revisit this at the next breaking version of the API, where one member `role` with the five values is
the cleaner shape.

**Applied in the spec:** R-OPS-003 (the example, the class and `roleName`, the acceptance criterion), R-OPS-004 (`answeredBy`,
`replicas.roles`), R-UI-038 (the groups read `roleName`), R-API-038's acceptance criteria. Code: `api/openapi.yaml`
(`roleName` on `answeredBy`, `Replica` and `EncryptionReplica`; `Replica.pool`), `internal/api/v1/roles.go`,
`internal/api/v1/handlers.go` (`Summarise` keys by `roleName`), `internal/api/v1/encryption_api.go`. Tests:
`TestQ_API_194_RoleMembersOfTheCut`, `TestR_OPS_004_SummaryPerRoleOfTheCut`, `TestR_OPS_004_RingsOfEveryRole`.

### Q-API-195 · The content routes are the files transfer behind a session check, and the UI's upload limit is a configuration key

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: R-API-025 and Q-UI-106 add `GET`, `HEAD` and `PUT /api/v1/repositories/{repoKey}/content/{path}` for the session cookie,
which reaches only `api`. Verified in the code: `PackageFile.path` is the `path` of the live file item of the version
(`PackageViewFiles`) and `PackageFile`'s repository is the one that holds it, so `contentUrl` is built from the pair like
`downloadUrl`; the CSRF check of a session (`session.Store.CheckCSRF`) reads the token header and the origin and never the body, so a
`PUT` that streams its body is checked like one that decodes JSON; `files.Service` reads stored items only and contacts no
upstream, so a path that is not stored answers `404` also in a remote repository. `ui.deploy.max_upload_bytes` did not exist as
a configuration key although R-UI-012 names it.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) One handler: the files handler serves both prefixes through `serve`, and the content routes add the session check and the upload limit (chosen) | `rawfiles.Handler.Content(limit)` registers three routes; the document lists them as operations tagged `files`, kept out of the generated interface because a path of several segments is no generated route | The decision of every request, `Range`, digests, content headers, blocking and statistics are the code of `/files/`, so a caller without `read` gets the same `404`; the document and the route table are compared in both directions | Folder index links and the directory index are those of `/files/` |
| (b) A second implementation in `internal/api/v1` | Generated routes with a query parameter for the path | Fits the generator | A second transfer path that can drift from the first; the path of an item in a query parameter is not what `contentUrl` promises |
| (c) Accept tokens on the content routes too | One route family for everything | Simpler for scripts | Token clients would put their bulk traffic on `api`, which Q-UI-106 keeps off it |

**Choice:** (a). A request whose credential is not the session cookie answers the `404` of an unknown path before the repository
is looked up or an index begun. The routes offer no `DELETE`. A path that ServeMux would redirect (an empty, `.` or `..` segment) is
redirected like on every route of `/api/v1/`; `/files/` answers it `400 invalid_path` because it registers an uncleaned handler for its
whole prefix, and the content routes cannot (the prefix is `/api/v1/repositories/`), which the UI never meets because it encodes
every segment. A `PUT` above `ui.deploy.max_upload_bytes` (default `100MiB`, `0` unlimited) answers `413` through a body reader that
fails at the first read of a declared length above the limit and when a body of unknown length crosses it; the deploy reads the body
only after it decided the caller, so a caller who may not deploy is refused first. The key is the new `ui.deploy` section of
[internal/config/ui.go](../../internal/config/ui.go).

**Rationale:** one transfer path is the property that keeps the two routes equal in authorization. The development agent would
revisit the redirect if a client of the content routes other than the UI appears, and the limit if installations want a per-repository
value (the repository's own `storage.maxUploadSize` still applies underneath).

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-025 (the content row and bullet), R-API-029 (`contentUrl`), R-UI-012. Code:
[internal/api/rawfiles/content.go](../../internal/api/rawfiles/content.go), `internal/api/edge/links.go` (`ContentPath`,
`ItemView.ContentURL`), `internal/api/v1/document.go` (`ContentOperations`), `internal/api/v1/packages_api.go`. Tests:
`TestContentRoutes`, `TestContentRoutesAgreeWithTheDocument`, `TestSplitContentPath`, `TestDescribeItem`,
`TestR_API_029_PackageFileContentURL`.

### Q-API-196 · The mirror's state is the first of seven that holds, and a pass whose job waits in the queue is waiting

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: R-REPO-056 names seven states and says what the three of a pass in progress mean, but a row can satisfy several at once (a
paused mirror whose pass is in progress, a failing mirror whose bound is reached). Verified in the code: a job is `queued`,
`running`, `cancelling` or ended ([internal/jobs](../../internal/jobs/job.go)); a pass that a drain released is the same job
`queued` again with its attempt unchanged (R-REPO-053), and an exclusive enqueue finds a `cancelling` job as active.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Derive the state from the row, the configuration and the job in this order: `off`, `paused`, `failing`, `bound_reached`, `running`, `waiting`, `scheduled`; `running` is a job that is `running` or `cancelling`, any other job or none is `waiting` (chosen) | `mirrorStateOf` in [mirror_api.go](../../internal/api/v1/mirror_api.go) | One answer per row on every replica, no column the engine must keep in step; what an operator must act on (off, paused, failing, the bound) hides nothing behind a pass that is only running | A paused mirror with a running pass shows `paused` while the pass finishes its package |
| (b) `paused` and `failing` only when no pass is in progress | The pass shows first | The UI shows progress while a pause takes effect | A failing mirror that still has a pass in progress shows `running`: the alarm hides |
| (c) The engine writes the state into a column | One source | Cheap to read | A second state that the configuration (mode, pause) changes without the engine knowing; a stale value after a PATCH until the next dispatch |

**Choice:** (a). The pass and its counts are in the document whatever the state is, so a client that wants the progress of a paused
mirror reads `pass`.

**Rationale:** the state is the question "what does this mirror need from me", and the operator-facing conditions come before the
progress. The development agent would revisit the order if the Mirror tab needs "pausing" as a state of its own, which would be a
new member and not a new value of the closed enum (Q-API-191).

**Applied in the spec:** R-REPO-056 (the states). Code: `mirrorStateOf`.

### Q-API-197 · The pass names its job as a job reference, the summary of the last pass has one schema with the stored one, and a summary that cannot be read is none

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: R-REPO-056 shows `pass.job` as `{id, href}` and the last complete pass as a document of eleven members; Q-API-193
named the schemas `MirrorPass` and `MirrorCompletePass`. The engine stores the summary as `mirror_state.last_pass`, a JSON
document ([migration 00040](../../internal/meta/postgres/migrations/00040_mirror.sql)); the migration does not say its members.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `pass.job` is the existing `JobReference` (`id`, `kind`, `state`, `href`), `null` once the job row is removed; the schema of the last pass is `MirrorPassSummary`, its members are the eleven of the example and the engine stores exactly them in `last_pass`; a summary that is missing, `null` or not a document with an `outcome` shows as `null` (chosen) | One schema for what the job API already returns; the UI links the job and reads its state without a second request | The client sees `kind` and `state` too: two members more than the example | The status never fails for a stored document it only shows |
| (b) A schema of two members | Exactly the example | A second job-reference schema | The UI cannot tell a running job from a queued one without reading it |
| (c) The id only | Smallest | — | The `href` is the contract of R-API-015 |
| (d) Answer 500 for a summary that cannot be read | Loud | The engine's mistake is seen | A status that cannot be read hides the failing mirror that the operator opens it for |

**Choice:** (a). The name of the schema is `MirrorPassSummary`, which replaces the name `MirrorCompletePass` of Q-API-193; nothing
was published under it. `docs/developer/mirror.md` states the members of `last_pass` for the engine.

**Rationale:** the job reference is the one way the API names a job (R-API-015), and the Mirror tab needs the state of the job to
tell a pass that runs from one that waits. The development agent would revisit (d) if the engine's tests do not pin the stored
shape; a decoder that falls silent is only as good as that test.

**Applied in the spec:** R-REPO-056 (the example), Q-API-193 (the name). Code: `buildMirrorStatus`, `decodeLastPass`.

### Q-API-198 · The run enqueues first, so that the exclusive key answers whether a pass is queued or running, and writes the request after it

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the run must answer 409 `mirror_pass_running` naming the job, record the request in `mirror_state.pass_requested_*`, enqueue
the pass and write `mirror.pass_requested`, atomically. Verified in the code: `jobs.Queue.Enqueue` inserts under the dedup key and,
when an exclusive job of the key is queued, running or cancelling, returns that job with `Created: false`; the refusal outcomes below
500 of an operation behind an `Idempotency-Key` are stored and replayed, so their transaction commits.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) In one transaction: enqueue; when the job exists, answer 409 with it and write nothing; else record the request and the event (chosen) | `enqueueMirrorPass` | The key decides, so two concurrent requests cannot both create a job; a refusal that commits under an idempotency key has written nothing | The job exists before its request is recorded (both commit or neither) |
| (b) Look for a queued or running job first, then enqueue | A query of the job table | Reads like the spec | A race between the look and the insert; a second statement that repeats the key's logic |
| (c) Record the request first, then enqueue | Spec order | — | A 409 behind an idempotency key commits the request of a pass that was not started |

**Choice:** (a). The other refusals (class, mode, pause) are answered before the transaction from the repository read of PostgreSQL
(Q-REPO-164), so they write nothing either.

**Rationale:** the exclusive dedup key is already the definition of "one pass per repository at a time" (R-REPO-053), and the API
asks it instead of reimplementing it. The development agent would revisit (b) only if the job queue stopped returning the existing job.

**Applied in the spec:** R-REPO-056 (the run). Code: `enqueueMirrorPass`.

### Q-API-199 · The two operations decide their permission in the handler, a refused reader is hidden by the decision on read, and a project administrator runs on the manage it holds

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. **Superseded in part by [Q-AUTHZ-208](authorization.md#q-authz-208--four-project-roles-reader-developer-maintainer-owner)**: the project right is the role, not a switch; the Maintainer and the Owner of the repository's project hold `manage` through their role and run a pass, the Owner reads the status, and `project_switch_off` and `projectAdmin: manageRepositories` are gone.

Context: R-REPO-056 admits for the status `repositories:read-config`, `manage` or an administrator of the repository's project, and for the
run `repositories:write-config`, `manage` or an administrator of the project with `manageRepositories`. The declaration forms
(R-API-008) express one capability, or one repository action; Q-OPS-155 decides such a disjunction in the handler under the
declaration `authenticated`. Verified in the code: the decision point answers a refused `manage` with 403 whatever else the caller
holds, and 404 only for a refused `read` ([internal/authz/decide.go](../../internal/authz/decide.go), `refusal`, R-AUTHZ-016); a
project administrator holds `manage` on every repository of its project, whatever the project's switches say (Q-AUTHZ-183,
`grantedBy`).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Decide in the handler: the capability, the project right, then `manage`; a caller refused on `manage` who cannot read the repository and is not a configuration reader is answered by the decision on `read`, 404 when the repository hides its existence; a configuration reader is answered 403 (chosen) | `requireMirrorReader`, `requireMirrorWriter` | Every row of the table is one branch; a `manage` holder without `read` is no stranger; the answer for a hidden repository is the bytes of a missing one | A caller refused on `manage` costs two decisions, which the denial dedup window of R-OPS-015 keeps from doubling the events |
| (b) Declare `repositories:write-config` with `projectAdmin: manageRepositories`, as the upstream test does | The shared step decides | Nothing to write | The table's `manage` is lost: a team lead with `manage` on one remote could not run its pass |
| (c) Require the project's switch from a project administrator even though it holds `manage` | A second check on top of the decision | The switch means the same for a run as for a write | The decision point already gave `manage`; to ask the grant's source (`project:<key>`) would couple the API to how a grant came about, and the run changes no configuration |

**Choice:** (a). A project administrator with `manageRepositories` off may therefore run a pass; the 403 `project_switch_off` of an
update does not occur on the run. The switch gates what changes a configuration (R-AUTHZ-026), and the run changes none: it asks the
engine for what the settings already allow.

**Rationale:** the table of R-REPO-056 is the union of three rights, and the engine already makes the third include the second for
project administrators. The development agent would revisit (c) if the owner wants a run, which causes background download volume,
to need the project's switch (gap [H-531](../security/delegated-administration.md#h-531--a-run-can-be-requested-as-often-as-a-pass-ends)).
The cache entry list (R-REPO-032) decides the same disjunction with the decision on `manage` alone and so answers 403, not 404, where
the caller cannot read the repository; it is not changed here.

**Applied in the spec:** R-REPO-056 (the permissions), R-API-022. Code: `requireMirrorReader`, `requireMirrorWriter`, `hiddenOr`;
[delegated-administration.md](../security/delegated-administration.md).

### Q-API-200 · The format descriptor's `mirror` is a required boolean read from the catalog

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: R-UI-021 lets the wizard offer the mirror only for a format whose remote can discover; the catalog fact is `Entry.Mirror`
(set by `formats.Register` from the optional lister interface, ADR-152). The descriptor of `GET /api/v1/formats` is built from
`formats.Descriptor`, which does not carry the fact.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A required boolean `mirror` in `FormatDescriptor`, read from `catalog.Default()` by the format's name; false for a format the catalog does not know (chosen) | `mirrorFact` | One source for the repository model and the UI: the model refuses `mode: mirror` by the same fact, so the wizard offers exactly what the save accepts; an addition to a response, which the compatibility check allows (R-ARCH-025) | A client that validates strictly and has no `mirror` member in its copy of the schema |
| (b) An optional member, absent when false | Smaller document | — | Every other member of the descriptor is required; the UI would test for presence |
| (c) A new member of `Descriptor` | The format declares it | — | A second statement of a fact that the registration derives, which can drift from it |

**Choice:** (a).

**Rationale:** the UI must not hold a list of mirrorable formats (R-UI-021), and a fact that the model enforces is the one to offer.
The development agent would revisit (c) never: the fact is derived from the adapter's interface so that it cannot be declared
without being implemented.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-021, R-API-022. Code: `ListFormats`, `mirrorFact`.

### Q-UI-108 · A pool without a live replica is named by its pool, because the registry does not say which queues it claims

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: R-UI-038 asks for "No live replica claims the queues `<queues>`" for a worker pool. The replica registry holds the pool
name (`pool`) and no queue list, and a pool without any registry row is not known to the screen at all.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The warning names the pool: "No live replica in the pool `<pool>`" (chosen) | Shown while every row of the pool is `lost` | Needs no new data; the operator knows the pool and its queues from the values | Does not repeat the queues; a pool whose rows were pruned (24 h) shows nothing |
| (b) Add the pool's queues to the registry and the API | A column and a member | The text of the requirement | A migration and a contract change for a message; the registry would hold configuration |
| (c) No pool warning | Only the role-level warnings | Nothing to build | An empty pool, the case that matters, would go unnoticed for 24 h |

**Choice:** (a). The warning appears on the sub-group of a pool whose replicas are all lost; the role-level notices of `worker`
and `packages` (no live replica) are unchanged.

**Rationale:** the loss of a pool's last replica is visible for as long as its row exists, which is what the screen can know. The
development agent would revisit this if the API gets the pool's queues for another reason.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-038 (the pool notice). Code: `web/src/app/features/system/system-status-model.ts` (`roleGroups`).
Tests: the specs `system-status-model.spec.ts` and `system-status.spec.ts`.

### Q-UI-109 · The Download links use `contentUrl`; "Copy download URL" keeps the protocol URL

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: Q-UI-106 lets the session cookie download and upload through the content routes of `api`. The file browser and the
package screen show a Download link and the browser a copy button for the address.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The link is the `contentUrl` of the item or version file; the copy button copies `downloadUrl` (chosen) | Two addresses, each for who uses it | The link works with the session on `api`; the copied address is what a token client can use on `packages` | None found |
| (b) Both use `contentUrl` | One address | Simple | A copied relative route that a token cannot use |
| (c) Both keep `downloadUrl` | No change | None | The link would need the session cookie on `packages`, which ignores it (R-ARCH-001) |

**Choice:** (a). The upload and the folder creation of the deploy dialog build their URL in one place, `contentPath` of
`web/src/app/api/files-api.ts` (R-UI-001); a file above `ui.deploy.max_upload_bytes` is refused by the dialog before it starts and
by the server with `413`.

**Rationale:** the UI never assembles a protocol URL (R-UI-001). The development agent would revisit this when a content origin
(R-ARCH-029) serves the downloads.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-012, R-UI-001's links rule, R-API-029. Code: `web/src/app/api/files-api.ts`,
`features/browse/browse.html`, `features/packages/package-detail.html`. Tests: `files-api.spec.ts`, `browse.spec.ts`,
`package-detail.spec.ts`.

### Q-UI-110 · The status screen groups by the replica's role and shows a role it does not know after the known ones

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the registry names one role per replica (`roles`, Q-ARCH-341); the screen keeps a group for a role it does not know.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The group of a replica is its role; a role other than `api`, `packages`, `worker`, `web`, `all` is a group after them (chosen) | The screen hides nothing | A further role, or a registry of a newer release, never disappears from the screen | The screen has no text for such a role beyond its name |
| (b) Group by the class in `roles` | No new member needed | Works with the old data | `api` and `packages` would be one group `web`, which Q-UI-107 rejects |
| (c) Drop unknown roles | Only the known groups | Tidy | A running replica would be missing from the screen |

**Choice:** (a). The groups `api`, `packages` and `worker` always exist; `web` and `all` only while a replica reports them. A
sub-group heading is shown when a role has a pool, or more than one sub-group.

**Rationale:** an operator must see every replica the registry lists. The development agent would revisit this when a fourth role
exists.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-038. Code: `system-status-model.ts` (`roleOf`, `roleGroups`). Tests: `system-status-model.spec.ts`.

### Q-UI-111 · During the upgrade across the cut the UI falls back to `/files/` against a replica of the old shape

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: in the first step of the upgrade across the cut (R-HA-064) a UI bundle from a new pod can reach a `web` replica of the
previous release, which has no content route (Q-UI-106) and lists no `contentUrl`.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Links take `contentUrl`, else `downloadUrl`; an upload or a new folder repeats its PUT once on `/files/` when the content route answers 404 `not_found` (chosen) | The old replica serves `/files/` with the session cookie | No step of the upgrade breaks the browser journey | One more request on that 404 |
| (b) No fallback | The UI uses the content routes only | Simpler | Uploads fail and Download links vanish until step 2 |
| (c) Pin the UI to the old routes until step 2 | A value switches the routes | Exact | A setting that exists for one upgrade |

**Choice:** (a). Only the unknown-path code `not_found` triggers the repeat; `repository_not_found`, 401, 403, 409 and 413 are
answered as they are, so the fallback never turns a refusal into a second attempt.

**Rationale:** the upgrade must keep the UI working in both steps. The development agent would remove the fallback once no supported
upgrade starts from the shape before the cut (R-ARCH-025).

**Applied in the spec:** R-HA-064 (the browser journey). Code: `web/src/app/api/files-api.ts` (`putWithFallback`), `browse.html`,
`package-detail.ts` (`fileHref`). Tests: `files-api.spec.ts`, `browse.spec.ts`, `package-detail.spec.ts`.

### Q-UI-112 · The repository wizard asks for the format first

Status: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-05.

Context: the wizard started with the class (local, remote, virtual) and offered the formats of that class second. Some features
are technically impossible for some formats (a format may lack a class, may have no settings for a class, and only some formats
can mirror a remote), so what the later steps offer depends on the format, not the other way round.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Class first, then the formats that implement it (as before) | The first question is what kind of repository | Familiar from the first prototype | The format decides what is possible afterwards, so the first answer limits nothing and the second is limited by it |
| (b) Format first, then the classes of that format (chosen) | The first question is which package type the repository serves | The choice that limits everything after it is the first one; the class step can say what the format cannot do | A user who thought in classes first answers a different first question |

**Choice:** (b), by the owner.

**Rationale:** some features are technically impossible for some formats, so the format is the first choice.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-021 (the steps, the class step's rule and its acceptance criteria). Code:
`web/src/app/features/repositories/repository-wizard.ts` and `.html`. R-UI-023 (quick setup) is unaffected.

### Q-UI-113 · A class the chosen format does not implement is shown disabled, with the reason

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Hide it | The class step lists only the format's classes | Nothing to explain | A user who looks for a virtual repository of a format without it cannot tell whether trove lacks the feature or the format does |
| (b) Show it disabled with one sentence (chosen) | The card stays, cannot be chosen, and says "NuGet does not implement the class Virtual." | It teaches what the format cannot do, which is the reason the format comes first; the sentence is the description of the disabled radio, so assistive technology reads it | Three cards where one would do |
| (c) Show it enabled and refuse at the end | The server's 422 decides | No client logic | The user finds out at the last step |

**Choice:** (b). The reason names the format and the class and is the same sentence for every format; the descriptor says which
classes exist, not why one is missing, so the UI does not invent a cause.

**Rationale:** (a) removes the one piece of information the reordered wizard is able to give. The development agent would revisit
this when a descriptor carries a reason per missing class; the sentence then uses it.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-021. Code: `repository-wizard.html` (the class step), `repository-wizard.ts` (`supports`,
`unsupportedReason`). Test: `repository-wizard.spec.ts`.

### Q-UI-114 · The format tiles are a listbox of `@angular/aria`; the icon is the one of the package list

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Native radio inputs in cards, as the class step | `input type=radio` in a label | Native arrow keys in every direction, no library | The grid is a picker of one of many with a filter; a radio group announces every tile as a group member even while filtered |
| (b) A single-choice listbox of `@angular/aria` (chosen) | `ngListbox` with `ngOption` per tile, explicit selection, horizontal orientation, one tab stop | The WAI-ARIA pattern for choosing one of many, filtered; R-UI-001 names the listbox for such widgets; a tile is not a form control | Arrow keys move along the row (Left and Right, on to the next row), not up and down; typeahead, Home and End work |
| (c) Buttons with `aria-pressed` | A toggle per tile | Simplest markup | One tab stop per tile (a long tab path), no arrow navigation |

**Choice:** (b), with `selectionMode="explicit"` so that moving over a tile does not change the format (a change resets

the icon is the owner's logo where its terms allow it (Debian, NuGet, OCI) and `inventory_2` elsewhere, rendered by
`<trove-format-icon>`; it is still the same function as the list's.*

**Rationale:** the wizard now has a picker of one of many that a filter shortens, which is the listbox pattern. Keyboard users move
with Left and Right, Home, End and typeahead, and the filter shortens the path. The development agent would revisit (a) if the
owner or a screen-reader user finds the missing Up and Down arrows a loss; the tiles then become radios in a CSS grid.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-021. Code: `repository-wizard.html`, `repository-wizard.scss`, `shared/format-icon.ts`. Tests:
`repository-wizard.spec.ts` (the keyboard and selection specs).
