### Q-UI-117 · The Mirror section: where it sits, what it writes, who may change it

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Question | Options | Choice |
|---|---|---|
| Where | The class-specific step and a tab of the edit form; a step of its own | The class-specific step of the wizard (under the access settings and the format's settings), and a tab **Mirror** on the edit form of a remote of a format with `mirror: true`. The status of Q-UI-104 is a later addition to the same tab |
| What shows | Always every member; the members in mode `mirror` only | The mode always; the members in mode `mirror` only, so the default view is two cards |
| What a create writes | Every member; what differs from the default | Nothing in mode `pullThrough`; in mode `mirror` the mode and the members that differ from their defaults (R-REPO-050) |
| What an edit patches | A diff that may drop `remote`; a structural diff | The mode and the mirror object are always part of the compared document, so a merge patch carries only the changed members and a member set back to its default is cleared with `null`; the rest of `remote` (the URL, the credentials) is never part of the patch |
| Project administrator | Hide; read-only | The caller without `repositories:write-config` sees the section read-only except **Paused** and **Turn off** (the mode back to `pullThrough`), and cannot choose mode `mirror` (Q-REPO-142; the server answers `422 mirror_restricted` for anything else) |

**Rationale:** a member written only where it differs follows Q-UI-80 and keeps a stored document equal to what the user decided;
the structural diff is what makes a patch of one member safe on a document whose other `remote` members the form does not edit. The
development agent would revisit the "members in mode `mirror` only" view if operators ask to prepare the settings before turning the
mode on.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-021. Code: `mirror-settings.ts`, `repository-model.ts` (`remoteOf`, `mirrorOf`), `repository-wizard.*`,
`repository-detail.*`. Tests: `mirror-settings.spec.ts`.

### Q-UI-118 · The unbounded-mirror notice is an early warning with the server's rule

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) No client check; show the server's `mirror_unbounded` after the save | Only the server speaks | One rule in one place | The user learns after the last step |
| (b) A notice under the mode that applies the bound rule of R-REPO-052 to the entered include patterns and the storage limit, while the server still decides (chosen) | `refused` (the format's well-known upstream) or `warned` (any other), in the words of the server | The user sees the refusal before it happens and what removes it | The rule is written twice (`Bounding` in `internal/mirror/discover`, `boundsMirror` in `mirror-settings.ts`) |

**Choice:** (b). The wizard has no upstream field, so a create takes the format's default upstream and the notice treats it as the
well-known one; the edit form compares the stored URL with the format's `defaultUpstreamUrl`. The server's answer at `/remote/mode`
is shown at the mode as well.

**Rationale:** an operator who chooses mirror for the public npm registry should not discover the bound requirement from a 422. The
development agent would revisit the duplicate rule if the catalog serves the rule's inputs.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-021. Code: `mirror-settings.ts` (`boundsMirror`, `unbounded`). Test: `mirror-settings.spec.ts`.

### Q-UI-119 · The status sits above the settings on the Mirror tab and is read only while the tab is open

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) One tab: the status above the settings; the panel exists while the tab is open and reads the status every 5 s while a pass is in progress (chosen) | `GET …/mirror` when the tab opens, again every 5 s in the states `running` and `waiting`, after a pause, a resume, a run and a save, and never in the other tabs | What is going on comes first, the settings that explain it follow; no request for a tab nobody looks at; a finished pass stops the polling | A status that changes more slowly than 5 s is up to 5 s old |
| (b) The status below the settings | The same on one tab | The settings stay at the top where an administrator who edits expects them | The state, the one thing an operator comes for, is under a screen of fields |
| (c) A tab of its own for the status | Two tabs | Each tab is short | Two tabs for one repository's mirror, and the form's tab and the status's tab say different things about one state |
| (d) No polling; a **Refresh** button | The status is read when asked | No requests | An operator who watches a pass reloads by hand |

**Choice:** (a). The panel shows when the repository is stored in mode `mirror`; a form that has only just chosen the mode says that the status comes after the save.
The interval is the 5 s of the jobs screen (`JOBS_REFRESH_MS`); the polling stops with the panel because the panel is created by the tab (`matTabContent`).

**Rationale:** the status answers "is it working", the settings answer "why". The development agent would revisit (b) if administrators report
that they scroll past the status to reach the settings, and the interval if the status read becomes expensive on installations with many open tabs.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-021 (the bullet and the acceptance criterion). Code: `mirror-status.ts`, `repository-detail.html`. Tests: `mirror-status.spec.ts` (polling start, stop, refresh), `mirror-tab.spec.ts`.

### Q-UI-120 · Pause, resume and run follow the permission of Save; the status follows the one of the form

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. **Superseded in part by [Q-AUTHZ-208](authorization.md#q-authz-208--four-project-roles-reader-developer-maintainer-owner)**: the buttons show for whoever may save the repository, `repositories:write-config` or the role `owner` in its project; `manageRepositories` is gone, and an Owner without `repositories:write-config` keeps the read-only Mirror section of Q-REPO-142.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The buttons show for whoever may save the repository (`repositories:write-config`, or `manageRepositories` of its project, R-AUTHZ-026); the status shows for whoever sees the form (chosen) | `SessionStore.canWriteRepositories(project)` decides Pause, Resume and the run buttons | It is the permission of the API for a patch and for the run ("as an update", R-REPO-056); the UI already knows it, and a project administrator, who holds `manage` on the project's repositories, gets the buttons (Q-API-199) | A grant of `manage` on one repository through a policy, without the capability, is not known to the UI: such a caller sees no button and uses the API |
| (b) Show the buttons to everyone and let the server answer 403 | No decision in the UI | Never wrong about a grant the UI cannot see | A button that fails for most readers |
| (c) Ask the server first (a probe) | An extra request per screen | Exact | A request to learn what a refusal teaches |

**Choice:** (a). The status needs `repositories:read-config`, `manage` or the administration of the project, and the edit form shows the document to exactly those callers, so a
caller who sees the tab may read the status; a 403 or 400 of the status is shown in the panel as the error it is.
A project administrator pauses and resumes (the server's `mirror_restricted` lets `paused` through, Q-REPO-142), and the Mirror section stays read-only for them except **Paused** and **Turn off** (Q-UI-117).

**Rationale:** the same rule as every other write on the form keeps the screen consistent. The development agent would revisit it when the session
carries the per-repository grants of the caller (R-AUTHZ-010), which would let (a) see a `manage` grant.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-021. Code: `repository-detail.html` (`canChange`). Tests: `mirror-tab.spec.ts` (three callers), `mirror-status.spec.ts`.

### Q-UI-121 · Pause is a patch of its member alone; a run answers with the job or with the reason

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) **Pause** and **Resume** patch `remote.mirror.paused` with the loaded `If-Match` and keep the other unsaved edits; a 412 settles like a save; **Run** shows the job and treats its 409s as answers (chosen) | The document's revision protects the pause (Q-UI-105); the form keeps its draft | The button does what a script does (INV-17); an edit in progress is not lost, nor saved by accident | The form's own **Paused** checkbox and the button are two ways to one member; both read the same stored value after the button |
| (b) Pause saves the whole form | One save | One code path | A click on Pause saves unfinished edits |
| (c) Pause as the form's checkbox only | No button | One way | The status panel shows the state but cannot act on it |

**Choice:** (a). After the patch the stored document is the new baseline and only the `paused` member of the form follows it. A 412 reads the stored
document: when it already says what the user asked (another administrator paused, or a retried write committed) nothing more happens; otherwise the conflict dialog of
R-UI-042 shows the difference and **Overwrite** sends the pause with the new `ETag`, **Reload** takes the stored document. **Run a pass now** posts `{"full": false}`
with a fresh `Idempotency-Key` and **Run a full pass** `{"full": true}`. The 202's job and the `job` of a `409 mirror_pass_running` are shown the same way: the sentence
("A pass is queued." or "A pass is already queued or running.") with its id and state and a link to the jobs screen filtered by the kind `mirror-pass`, because that screen has
no route per job. `mirror_off`, `mirror_paused` and `not_applicable` are shown in words at the buttons; every other failure is an error notice. The panel reads the status again after each.

**Rationale:** a refusal that the server's own state explains is information, not a failure. The development agent would revisit the link when the jobs screen gets a route per job (it would
open that job) and the double path for pause if the checkbox is dropped from the section.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-021, R-REPO-056 (the UI line). Code: `repository-detail.ts` (`setMirrorPaused`, `takeStored`, `handlePauseError`), `mirror-status.ts` (`run`, `runError`). Tests: `mirror-tab.spec.ts` (pause, resume, 412 three ways), `mirror-status.spec.ts` (202, each 409, 400).

### Q-UI-122 · The upstream settings: where they sit, what the URL field holds, what is written

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Question | Options | Choice |
|---|---|---|
| Where | In the access step with the format's settings; a step of its own; the General tab | The class-specific step of the wizard, above the format's settings (so the Mirror section, which depends on the URL, follows it), and a tab **Upstream** on the edit form, for every remote repository whether its format can mirror or not |
| What the URL field holds | Empty with the preset as a placeholder; the preset as the value | The wizard starts with the preset as the value, so "Test connection" and the review show what is used; an empty field means the preset; a format without a preset starts empty and needs the address (the server answers `422` at `/remote/url` otherwise) |
| What a create writes | Everything; what differs from the preset and the defaults | The URL only when it names another upstream than the preset (compared as the server normalizes it), the authentication members only for an authentication other than none, a period only when it differs from the format's default, `availability` only when offline; nothing at all of `remote` when none applies (Q-UI-80) |
| What an edit patches | Whole objects; members | The URL always as entered, so a patch never depends on how the server reads a removed URL; `cache` and `availability` are always present as objects on both sides of the merge patch, so a member set back to its default is `null` inside the object and the members the form does not edit (`storeArtifacts`, `failureThreshold`, ...) are never nulled |
| The mirror's bound notice | The format's well-known upstream; the URL entered | The URL entered, or the preset while it is empty (Q-UI-118 compared the stored URL or assumed the preset) |

**Rationale:** a remote of a private registry, the case that needs a URL and a credential, is what a mirror is most used for; the form shows what the repository will do. The development agent would revisit the
split of the wizard's step if it grows past what one page carries once the extra hosts, the limits and the integrity members get fields.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-021. Code: `upstream-settings.ts`, `repository-model.ts` (`upstreamOf`, `initialUpstream`, `remoteOf`), `repository-wizard.*`, `repository-detail.*`, `mirror-settings.ts` (`upstreamUrl`). Tests: `upstream-settings.spec.ts`.

### Q-UI-123 · The password is write-only: typed, sealed by the server, never read into a field or shown

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The field starts empty; typing sends `{"value": ...}`; an empty field keeps what is stored; **Remove the stored password** sends `null`; the request shown on screen carries a placeholder; no draft stores it (chosen) | R-REPO-033 as the API states it: a read shows `{"set": true}` or the reference, never the value | A secret exists in the page only while it is typed; a save of another member cannot blank it | An administrator cannot see what is stored, which is the point |
| (b) Send `{"set": true}` back with every save | The document as read, sent back | Symmetric with the API's wording | The form would carry a member that is not a setting of the user's |
| (c) Show a masked placeholder in the field | Dots for the stored value | The user sees that there is one | A placeholder that looks like a value can be saved as a new password |

**Choice:** (a). A stored `secretRef` reads as a reference: the hint says so and the field replaces it only when a password is typed. The request body and the `curl` of the review and of the **API** tab show
`<the password>` instead of the value; the drafts kept across a sign-in (R-UI-042) never hold it; and **Test connection** uses only a typed password, because an unsaved test cannot refer to a stored one
(`{"set": true}` is `422 invalid_secret` there), which the page says.

**Rationale:** R-UI-043 keeps secrets out of storage and logs; the API already gives the shape. The development agent would revisit the removal
checkbox if the API grows an operation to rotate the stored secret.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-021 (the criterion). Code: `repository-model.ts` (`upstreamOf`, `maskSecrets`), `upstream-settings.ts`, the draft handling of `repository-detail.ts` and `repository-wizard.ts`. Tests: `upstream-settings.spec.ts`.

### Q-UI-124 · Test connection probes the unsaved section and shows the answer in words

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `POST /api/v1/upstream-tests` with the format and the section as the form would write it, with the URL it would use; the result inline, in words, and gone when a setting changes (chosen) | What the repository would do, before it exists | Works in the wizard, where nothing is saved; the same call on the edit form shows the unsaved state | The edit form's test cannot use the stored password |
| (b) The saved repository's test (`POST …/upstream-test`) on the edit form | The stored section, with the stored secret | Uses the stored password | Cannot test a change before it is saved; a second code path |
| (c) A test only after the create | One path | Simple | The wizard cannot tell the user that the URL is wrong |

**Choice:** (a). The verdict is a sentence ("The upstream answered.", "The upstream answered and refused the credentials.", "The upstream could not be reached.", "The upstream answered with an error.")
with an icon, and green only for an answer with an accepted or no credential and a status below 400; the facts follow: the HTTP status, whether the credentials were accepted, the duration, the certificate
(subject, valid until) and the reason with its code (`dns_error`, `tls_untrusted`, `egress_denied`, `offline`, ...). The offline switch is part of what is tested, so an offline repository's test says `offline`, as the server does.
A refused test (403, 422) is an error notice.

**Rationale:** the section is what the user is about to save; the test of the saved one is the API's. The development agent would revisit (b) for the edit form when the API's unsaved test accepts `{"set": true}` of a stored repository.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-021. Code: `upstream-settings.ts` (`test`, `outcome`), `repository-model.ts` (`upstreamTestBody`). Tests: `upstream-settings.spec.ts`, journey `14-mirror.spec.ts` (F-54).

### Q-UI-125 · The sign-in screen stands alone, and ?auto_sign_in=false waives the automatic sign-in

Status: **Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06.**

The sign-in screen showed the navigation sidebar of the shell, none of whose entries can be used without a session, and it
did so only when it was reached from a guarded route: opened directly at `/ui/login`, the shell stayed hidden, because the
session was never asked for. The owner asked for a sign-in page without the menu, laid out as one column (a form, then the
providers below "or sign in with"), for the automatic sign-in at the provider to be a chart setting, and for a URL parameter
that waives it even when it is on.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `/login` and `/logged-out` carry `data: { bare: true }`; the root component renders none of the shell around such a screen, and none at all before the first navigation has ended (chosen) | The screen alone, in the middle of the page | The same screen whether opened directly or reached from a guard; nothing that cannot be used is shown | Two forms of the frame in one template |
| (b) Hide only the sidebar while no session is known | Top bar stays | Smaller change | The top bar's theme and sign-in controls are as useless before a sign-in; the direct/guarded difference stays |
| (c) A second root component for the screens without a session | Clean split | No condition in the shell | Two bootstraps or a router-level layout switch; the outlet moves and a screen is created twice |

**Choice:** (a). The router outlet stays in one place, so a screen is created once; a navigation that is cancelled (a
guard's redirect) does not decide the frame, the one that ends does. With anonymous access on, an anonymous visitor keeps
the sidebar on every other screen, because there its entries work.

The sign-in screen is one column of at most 25rem: the wordmark, the heading, the break-glass form when it is offered
(labels above the fields, a primary "Sign in" across the column), then the providers. Below the form a provider is a
neutral button with its display name under a divider "or sign in with"; without the form each provider is a primary
button "Sign in with <name>". "Continue without signing in" closes the column when anonymous access is on.

`?auto_sign_in=false` replaces `?local=1` with the same meaning: no redirect to the single provider of `autoRedirect`, and
the break-glass form shown whether or not `auth.break_glass.show_on_login_page` offers it. Only the value `false` waives
the redirect. `?local=1` is not kept as a second name: the installations so far are the owner's, and two parameters for
one switch would both have to be documented and tested. The automatic sign-in itself is `auth.login_page.auto_redirect`
(R-AUTH-009), which the chart already passed through; `values.yaml` now shows it as
`config.auth.login_page.auto_redirect`, and `values.schema.json` types it as a boolean, so Helm refuses another value
instead of a replica failing at start-up.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-004 above, R-AUTH-009 and R-AUTH-014 in
[identity-and-authentication.md](identity-and-authentication.md). Code: `app.ts` (`bare`, `shell`), `app.html`,
`app.routes.ts`, `features/login/login.ts`, `features/login/logged-out.ts`, `_shell.scss` (`.bare`, `.bare-panel`),
`deploy/helm/trove/values.yaml`, `values.schema.json`. Tests: `app.spec.ts`, `login.spec.ts`, journey `01-sign-in.spec.ts`.

### Q-UI-126 · trove's own controls in place of Angular Material

Status: **Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06.** Built: the sign-in screens, the shell and the admin dashboard first, then
every other screen, the dialogs, tabs, checkboxes, menus and the tooltip, and the Material theme last
([Q-UI-153](#q-ui-153--the-last-material-controls-become-small-shared-pieces-on-the-cdk-and-angulararia)); `@angular/material`
is no dependency of `web/` any more.

The owner asked to leave the look of Angular Material for the design language of the sign-in page he showed: flat
controls, labels above the fields, a primary button in the accent, neutral grey secondary buttons. Measured on
2026-11-06: the forms were already native (147 `input`, `select` and `textarea` elements with trove's own classes against
4 `mat-form-field`); Material remained in the buttons (253 uses in 81 files), the dialogs (28 files), the checkboxes (12),
the tabs (5), the menus (3), the tooltip (2), and the top bar and sidebar. `@angular/cdk` and `@angular/aria` were
already dependencies.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Replace Material: trove's own classes for the controls (`_controls.scss`), the behaviour of the composite widgets from the CDK (dialog, menu, overlay) and `@angular/aria` (tabs), screen by screen; `@angular/material` leaves `package.json` at the end (chosen) | The look is trove's alone | Full control of the look; no ripple, state layer or MDC structure to fight; a smaller bundle; focus trap, keyboard handling and ARIA still come from the Angular team's packages | Every template with a Material control changes; the dialogs move to the CDK's API |
| (b) Restyle Material through its tokens and overrides | Templates stay | Fewer changes | The ink bar, the state layers and the dialog structure stay visible; every Material release can move the overrides; `main.scss` already carries many |
| (c) Only the sign-in screen and the shell | Small | Quick | Two design languages side by side until the rest is decided |

**Choice:** (a), in this order: the control styles and the sign-in screens first, then the buttons of every screen, the
shell (top bar, sidebar, menus, tooltip), the dialogs, the tabs and checkboxes, and last the Material theme, whose
`--mat-sys-*` tokens give way to trove's. The colours stay those of Q-UI-88 and Q-UI-96 (cogpit's blue as the accent,
green for a positive status only); the controls take them from tokens of their own (`--trove-control-*`,
`--trove-accent-fill`, `--trove-btn-*`), so they no longer depend on Material.

The controls: one height (32 px) and radius (6 px) for buttons and fields; buttons `btn-confirm` (the accent), `btn-default`
(white with a hairline in the light scheme, filled grey in the dark one), `btn-tertiary` (text only), `btn-danger`,
`btn-icon`, with `btn-block` and `btn-sm`; text fields, selects and areas with a 1px outline of 3.2:1 and 3.4:1 (WCAG
1.4.11) and a semibold label above; native checkboxes and radios in the accent; a solid focus outline for every control.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-044 (contrast and focus unchanged), R-UI-046; R-UI-001's component-library bullet and the
density sentence of R-UI-002 name the result. Code: `_tokens.scss`, `_controls.scss`, `_dialog.scss`, `shared/ui/`; every
screen. Documented in [design-language.md](../developer/design-language.md#controls) and
[web-ui.md](../developer/web-ui.md#controls).

### Q-UI-127 · The admin area has a sidebar of its own behind an Admin button, and the shell takes the reference's frame

Status: **Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06.**

The owner asked for the administration to be separated from the rest of the navigation, entered through an Admin button
of the top bar that only its users see, and for the shell to take the structure and look of the reference he showed:
a top bar and a sidebar on one fill, the content as a panel set into them, the breadcrumb trail on top of the panel, and
a sidebar that collapses away instead of shrinking to icons.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Two areas, one sidebar each: `/admin/…` shows the admin area's entries under the title "Admin area", every other route the content's; an Admin button in the top bar for every caller with `SessionStore.hasAdminArea()` (chosen) | The two kinds of work apart | The sidebar holds what belongs to the task at hand; the admin entries no longer push the content's down; the same rule as before decides who sees the admin area | One more click from a content screen into an admin screen |
| (b) Both areas in one sidebar, the admin area folded | One sidebar | No extra click | The separation the owner asked for is not there |
| (c) A separate admin application | Clean split | Independent | Two shells to maintain, a reload between them |

**Choice:** (a). The button reads "Admin" with a wrench icon and leads to `/admin`, whose guard opens the first admin
screen the caller may use (repositories, or projects for a project administrator); the logo leads back to the start page.
Who sees the button is who saw the Administration area before (any capability, or the administration of a project,
Q-AUTHZ-181), so nothing new is shown or hidden.

The owner's corrections of 2026-11-06, after the first draft: the Admin button keeps the reference's default button, at the
controls' full height and in the neutral fill, inside the admin area as well (the draft had made it small and tinted it in
the accent while the area was open; `aria-current` alone marks that now). And the link to the manual reads
"Documentation" next to its icon, not a bare "?". Below 768 CSS px both labels give way to their icons and remain the
links' accessible names. The breadcrumb bar is as high as the reference's: 40 px with its hairline, as measured on the
owner's instance (the owner had asked for 48 px "like GitLab"; 48 px is the reference's top bar, Q-UI-128).

The frame: one fill for the top bar and the sidebar (since Q-UI-128 the reference's `#ececef` and `#28272d`; light grey
`#f1f4f8` before, where the frame had been navy), the content as a panel on the page's fill with rounded corners, and the
breadcrumb trail as a bar on top of it. The top bar holds the mark and the name, the repository search in
the middle, then the project filter, the Admin button, the Documentation link, theme and the user's round badge; the name is in the badge's
accessible name and on top of its menu. The sidebar's title is the area's name; its entries are pills, the current one
tinted in the blue with its text in a deep or pale step of it and heavier (Q-UI-128; a bar in the accent before). "Collapse sidebar" at its foot hides it where it is pinned (the choice is
stored per principal, as the folded groups are), and "Open navigation" in the top bar brings it back; below 1024 CSS px it
is a drawer over the content with a backdrop, closed by Escape, the backdrop or a link. This replaces the icon rail of
Q-UI-68. The top bar, the sidebar and the menus are no longer Angular Material's (Q-UI-126): the menus are the CDK's
(`cdkMenu`, radio items for the theme and the project filter), the drawer traps the focus with `cdkTrapFocus`.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-002. Code: `app.html`, `app.ts`, `core/navigation.ts` (`areaOf`, `area`),
`core/nav-state.ts` (`collapsed`), `_shell.scss`, `_tokens.scss` (`--trove-nav-*`, `--trove-search-*`,
`--trove-brand-*`), `shared/brand/trove-mark.ts`. Tests: `app.spec.ts`, `app.projects.spec.ts`, `palette.spec.ts`.

### Q-UI-128 · The reference's type, colours and measures

Status: **Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06.**

Context: in the review of the shell the owner found the Admin button harder to read than the reference's and asked for
the reference's colours, then, in its admin area: "Ich will dass du das Design (auch Schriftgröße) von hier übernimmst".
The reference is his own GitLab (19.0.1), which he opened in a browser window the development agent could read. Asked
whether that raises a legal problem: the values (colours, sizes, radii) are taken and written into trove's own tokens;
GitLab's design tokens and component library are MIT-licensed (`@gitlab/ui`), its font is OFL-1.1, and no code, name or
logo of GitLab enters trove.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The reference's values in trove's tokens: colours of both schemes, the type, the measures of the frame, controls, cards and lists; a pair that misses WCAG AA is moved in its own hue (chosen) | trove looks like the reference's admin area | One look across the owner's tools; values measured, not guessed; R-UI-044 holds | trove's own colour (cogpit's blue, Q-UI-96) goes |
| (b) Only the type and measures, cogpit's colours kept | Half the reference | trove keeps a colour of its own | Not what the owner asked |
| (c) GitLab's stylesheet or component library itself | Its CSS in trove | Exact | Its CSS carries GitLab's class names and EE parts under GitLab's own licence; a second component system next to Q-UI-126 |

**Choice:** (a). The font, one decision of its own (owner, 2026-11-06): the reference's "GitLab Sans" is Inter with the
`cv05` form of the lower-case l; trove ships Inter (`@fontsource-variable/inter`, OFL-1.1) with `cv05` switched on, so
the look is the reference's without its name in trove (the options were GitLab Sans itself, or the system font as before).

What was measured, and where it went (the values per scheme are in [design-language.md](../developer/design-language.md#the-two-schemes)):

- Type: 14 px on 21 px at weight 400 for text and controls, 12 px for small text, sidebar entries at 425 and the current
  one at 500, headings at 600 with -0.01em tracking: page titles in the heading-1 size (24 to 30 px by the window's
  width), section titles in heading-2 (21 to 25 px).
- Frame: `#ececef` / `#28272d` around panels of the page's fill, 16 px round, 8 px from the window's right and bottom
  edge, no border; the sidebar 240 px wide, its title in the current entry's text colour, entries 28 px high and 8 px
  round with a 16 px icon in a 24 px box, the current one tinted in the blue (`#1f75cb` at 16 % / `#68a8e8` at 25 %) with
  its text `#0a335c` / `#cae0f7`; the breadcrumb bar 40 px with a hairline, its text 12 px; the search field 12 px round.
- Controls: 32 px, 8 px round, label weight 400; the default button white with a grey hairline / `#89888d` at 40 % without
  one, which makes the Admin button on the dark frame 7.0:1 where it was a fill barely set off from the frame; the confirm
  button `#1f75cb` / `#63a6e9`; menus white / `#28272d`, 8 px round.
- Cards: a strong fill (`#ececef` / `#3a383f`) 12 px round with 4 px inside, the title on it, the content on the page's
  fill 8 px round, rows with 12 px above and below and a hairline between.
- Lists (measured on the reference's Admin → Users): page titles at 30 px confirmed; tables without a frame on the page's
  fill, 16 px in every cell, the head at weight 600 in the heading colour between two hairlines, a hairline under every
  row; tabs with the current label at weight 600 over a 2 px line in the focus ring's blue (`#1f75cb` / `#428fdc`).
  Material's buttons and tabs, which most screens still use (Q-UI-126), are themed to these measures.
- Statuses (owner, 2026-11-06: "Status auf GitLab Standard umstellen"): a status is the reference's badge, a pill 20 px
  high with 12 px text and a 12 px icon, pale with deep text in the light scheme and full with near-black text in the
  dark one (success, warning, danger, info, neutral); every status of trove (an icon and a word with `.ok`, `.warn` or
  `.bad`) is drawn as one, and the outlined tags of the screens became neutral badges. The content width stays the
  panel's (owner, the same day), where the reference centres a 1280 px column.
- Top bar, compared side by side with the reference at 100 % zoom: the Admin button 88 × 32 px with 14 px text, the
  avatar 32 px, 8 px between the actions.
- Links (owner, 2026-11-06, one decision of its own): underlined in running text, so a link there is not told apart by
  colour alone (R-UI-044, WCAG 1.4.1: the link blue is 1.5:1 against the text); in a table or a key-value list, where the
  column or the row says what is a link, underlined only under the pointer and on focus, as the reference shows them.
  The other options were the underline everywhere (as before) and nowhere (as the reference, which fails 1.4.1 in
  running text).
- Moved for WCAG AA (R-UI-044): the accent as text and focus ring is `#2f68b4` / `#66a8ea` (the confirm blue is 4.0:1 and
  4.49:1 on a filled field); the search field's outline is `#858489` / `#737278` (the reference's hairlines are 1.7:1
  against the frame, WCAG 1.4.11 asks 3:1).

- Icons (owner, 2026-11-06): Material Icons in the outlined variant, line icons like the reference's (the same font package
  and ligature names; the reference's own icon set was not taken, it is part of its identity).

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-002 (the breadcrumb bar). Code: `web/angular.json` (the font), `_icons.scss` (the outlined icons), `main.scss` (Material's
palette and type, the body, the page title), `_tokens.scss`, `_controls.scss`, `_shell.scss`,
`features/system/dashboard.scss`, `_list-screens.scss` (the data table), `features/audit/audit-log.scss` (the link button
in its table), the badges in `_controls.scss` (the screens' own tag styles removed). Tests: `palette.spec.ts` (the new surfaces: the
default button on the frame, the hover of the top bar and the menus, the search field, the card; the tab line; each
badge's text and icon on its pill; the positive badge is the one other green).

### Q-UI-129 · The project is the context of the content, chosen from your projects

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-06**, proposed to the owner with the membership of
[Q-AUTHZ-207](authorization.md#q-authz-207--a-user-or-group-is-a-member-of-a-project-with-a-role-and-the-role-grants-the-projects-repositories),
which he chose. Built (T-7).

Context: every repository belongs to exactly one project and is addressed inside it (Q-AUTHZ-206, Q-REPO-212), and a user is a
member of few projects, typically one to five; the platform team and the administrators see many. Today the project is a
filter of the top bar (R-UI-041), offered to administrators and project administrators only.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The project as context (chosen) | The start page lists your projects; a project's screens live under `/projects/<key>/…` with a sidebar of the project (packages, browse, repositories, members, settings) and a project switcher at its top (recently visited, search); the top bar's project filter goes; the admin area keeps its lists over all projects | The address and the sidebar say which project you are in, as the reference shows a project; few projects make a short start page | Every content route moves under the project |
| (b) The project as a filter, as today, for everybody | The content screens stay global and filter by the chosen project | Fewer route changes | A repository's address contains its project (Q-REPO-212), the screens would not; the filter hides where you are |
| (c) A project picker at sign-in | One project per session | Simple | Switching projects means signing in again or a mode; most users work in more than one |

**Choice:** (a). A user with exactly one project starts in it; with several, on the list. A repository, package or file is
always shown inside its project; the admin area's lists name the project in a column.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-002 (the side bars, the project switcher), R-UI-003 (the route table), R-UI-020, R-UI-021,
R-UI-041 (the start page, no project filter); the preference `projectFilter` of R-API-021 is removed (API, OpenAPI, column). Code:
`web/src/app/core/project-context.ts` (the project of the URL, the projects of the caller, the recent ones),
`core/navigation.ts` (`projectEntries`), `features/projects/` (`project-context.routes.ts`, `projects-home.ts`,
`project-switcher.ts`, `project-settings.ts`, `project-members-page.ts`, `project-list-pages.ts`), the content routes
below `/projects/:project`, `GET /api/v1/packages?project=`. Tests: `app.projects.spec.ts`, `app.routes.spec.ts`,
`core/breadcrumbs.spec.ts`; journeys 02, 03, 08, 09, 10, 12, 13 and 15 of `web/e2e`.
