Das gleiche gilt für alle anderen Repositorie typen, nur das die Darstellung zwischen den Typen natürlich deutlich abweichen kann."

Context: the repository screen of R-UI-020 was the settings, and the content a reader wants was in the packages list and the file tree of R-UI-010, across which a reader had to assemble what one repository holds and how to pull from it.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `/repositories/{key}` is the content, the settings move below it (chosen) | The route of a repository is what it holds | What the owner asked; a link to a repository from anywhere shows what is in it | Every link to the settings had to move |
| (b) A second route for the content, the settings stay | `/repositories/{key}` keeps the settings | No link moves | A click on a repository still lands in the settings |

**Choice:** (a). The sub-decisions the owner did not make, taken by the development agent and open to change at the walkthrough:

- The client setup is a tab of the page, not a section below the list and not a dialog: it stays on the page without pushing the list down, and a token created in it dies with the tab (R-UI-043, R-UI-016).
- The open findings of an item were summed over its versions in this repository, with the highest open severity and the count as the row's badge; since the owner's task of 2026-11-12 the row shows the grade of the item's latest version ([Q-VULN-154](vulnerability-scanning.md#q-vuln-154--a-package-is-graded-by-its-latest-version), R-UI-094).
- Debian has no vulnerability adapter today, so its page has no column of findings and says so in one sentence; OCI images are scanned since R-VULN-033 (`vulnerabilityScanning` of the format catalog); the column appears the day an adapter exists, and the digest of a tag and the counts need no other change.
- The digest of a version in the list comes from the format's existing `metadata.digest` behind `include=digest`, not from a new format contract member: only the OCI screens ask for it, so no adapter pays for it otherwise.
- A remote OCI repository lists the tags its cache holds ([Q-OCI-215](formats/oci.md#q-oci-215--the-tags-of-a-remote-are-listed-from-its-cache-entries-by-a-database-view-not-from-version-rows)); the words that differ are Q-UI-217.

**Rationale:** the screen follows the mental model the owner named (images, tags, vulnerabilities, how to pull), and it reuses what exists (the install snippets of R-API-030, the client setup of R-UI-016, the list API of R-API-029) instead of a parallel set of format screens.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-052 (new), R-UI-003, R-UI-006, R-UI-020, R-UI-041, R-API-029, [R-VULN-020](vulnerability-scanning.md#r-vuln-020--findings-api); [web-ui.md](../developer/web-ui.md); [repositories.md](../manual/user/repositories.md). Code: [repository-content.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/repository-content.ts).

**Open:** none. A remote OCI repository's cached images were the open item; they are listed since Q-OCI-215. Vulnerability counts for OCI are those of the image scanning of [vulnerability-scanning.md](vulnerability-scanning.md).

### Q-UI-217 · The content page of an OCI remote uses the words of a cache: Fetched, and a note that names what is listed

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the list API serves the tags of a remote OCI repository since [Q-OCI-215](formats/oci.md#q-oci-215--the-tags-of-a-remote-are-listed-from-its-cache-entries-by-a-database-view-not-from-version-rows),
so the page of R-UI-052 needs no second component. Its words were written for a repository that is pushed to: the time column is **Pushed**, the empty text says to
push an image, and an OCI remote carried a note that nothing is listed.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The same components, the words follow the class: **Fetched**, an empty text that says to pull an image, one note that names what is listed (chosen) | `contentShapeOf(format, class)` returns the words of a cache for an OCI remote | One table of words stays the only per-format code (R-UI-052); the time is what the API's `publishedAt` is for a remote (R-OCI-036) | A second set of words for one format and class |
| (b) The words stay those of a local repository | Nothing changes | No code | "Pushed" for a time nobody pushed; an empty text that tells a reader to push to a cache |
| (c) The generic remote note ("Only what clients have fetched is listed here.") | The note of the other formats | One text | It leaves out the mirror pass, which fills the cache without a client |

**Choice:** (a). The note reads "Only the tags this repository has cached are listed here: those clients have pulled and, in mirror mode, those a pass has fetched."
The empty text reads "This repository has cached no images yet. Pull an image through it with your client.", with **Set up client**
under it (fix wave 2 of T-21). The version table keeps its
columns; the column of the findings is shown when the format is scanned, as for a local repository. No styling is added.

**Rationale:** the screen should not call a fetch a push. The development agent would revisit it if the page gains a "checked" time from the entry's validation,
which would be a second column beside Fetched.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-052, Q-UI-216. Code: [content-shape.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/content-shape.ts), [repository-content.html](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/repository-content.html). Tests: `R-OCI-036` in [repository-content.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/repository-content.spec.ts).

### Q-UI-220 · The form of a service-account token offers the administrator choice for an account that holds the role

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: [Q-UI-213](#q-ui-213--the-token-form-names-what-a-token-can-be-in-three-choices-and-only-an-administrator-is-offered-the-first) left the form of a service-account token without the administrator choice because the form did not know the account's role. The API accepts `{"inherit": true, "admin": true}` for an account's token from an administrator, and the token carries power only while the account itself holds the role ([R-AUTH-024](identity-and-authentication.md#r-auth-024--token-scopes)); an account is bound to the role directly, never through a group (R-AUTH-019), and a project's account holds no system role (R-AUTHZ-026).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Offer the choice when the caller is an administrator and the account holds the role now (chosen) | The record states it (`ServiceAccount.isAdmin`, [Q-AUTH-209](identity-and-authentication.md#q-auth-209--a-token-and-a-service-account-state-whether-the-owner-holds-the-administrator-role)); the choice is offered for an instance-wide account with `isAdmin` | Only a choice that takes effect; the account page also names the role in its details | One more field on the account |
| (b) Offer it for every instance-wide account to an administrator | No new field | The creator may prepare a token for an account that is bound to the role later | The token is inactive from the first minute and the list says so; a choice that does nothing now invites the mistake the token form was reworked to avoid |
| (c) Do not offer it; `trove admin token create --scope-file` stays the way | Nothing changes | No work | The owner's installation has an account that administers, and its token cannot be made in the screen |

**Choice:** (a). The choice sends `{"inherit": true, "admin": true}`, as the personal token's does. A project's account is never offered it (its page shows no role line), and a caller without the administrator role is not offered the form at all (R-AUTH-027). **Rationale:** the form promises only what the token will hold. The development agent would revisit (a) when roles are bound to accounts through a group, which R-AUTH-019 forbids today.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-026, R-UI-029. Code: `TokenManager.offerAdmin`, `ServiceAccountDetail`.

### Q-UI-221 · The token administration marks administrator tokens whose owner no longer holds the role

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the profile's list of the caller's own tokens already said **Administrator rights inactive** by comparing with the caller's role; the token administration (R-UI-030) lists other people's tokens and did not know the role of each owner ([Q-UI-213](#q-ui-213--the-token-form-names-what-a-token-can-be-in-three-choices-and-only-an-administrator-is-offered-the-first), "Not covered").

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The token record carries `ownerIsAdmin`, every list marks an administrator token whose owner is no administrator (chosen) | One field, filled in one query per page of tokens ([Q-AUTH-209](identity-and-authentication.md#q-auth-209--a-token-and-a-service-account-state-whether-the-owner-holds-the-administrator-role)) | The same mark on the profile, the user's and the account's lists and the administration; nothing is computed in the browser from a role it cannot know | The API answer grows by a boolean |
| (b) The administration asks the user list for the roles of the owners on the page | One request per owner or a filtered list | No change of the token record | A second call that needs `identities:read`, which a holder of `tokens:read` alone lacks; a race between the two answers |

**Choice:** (a). The notice is the existing one; the table no longer takes the owner's role as an input. **Rationale:** the fact belongs to the record the notice is about. The development agent would revisit it if a list of tokens grows to a page size where one extra query per page costs measurably.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-029, R-UI-030. Code: `TokenTable.adminInactive`. Tests: `Q-UI-221` in [token-admin.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/tokens/token-admin.spec.ts).

### Q-UI-222 · Which settings pages are one column now, and what a section's save button is called

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the style guide ([Settings pages](../developer/ui-style-guide.md#settings-pages), [Q-UI-215](#q-ui-215--settings-are-fields-in-one-column-and-everything-that-folds-is-animated)) moved the project's settings to one column and listed the other settings pages as still to move. Five pages carry settings: the authentication and the general settings, a service account, a group, and the repository's settings; user, profile, endpoint, issuer and policy pages are detail or editor pages with their own structure.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Move the four pages whose form is a short list of fields; leave the repository's settings and the user page (chosen at first; the user page, the endpoint, issuer and policy pages and the lists of the group page followed in [Q-UI-223](#q-ui-223--the-user-the-endpoint-and-the-service-account-and-group-lists-follow-the-guide) and [Q-UI-224](#q-ui-224--the-policy-editor-and-the-issuer-page-keep-their-structure-and-lose-the-cards-and-the-delete-in-the-header)) | General and authentication settings, service account and group follow the guide; the others stay on the list of the style guide | Each moved page is complete and tested; the repository's settings are a tabbed editor of 300 lines with a stored-document view and a move dialog, which needs its own design | Two screens still show the old card |
| (b) Move all five and the user page | Everything follows the guide | No page left over | A tabbed editor cannot be a column of three sections without deciding what its tabs become; done in one change it would be decided in haste |
| (c) Move nothing until the owner shows the reference's repository settings | Wait | No guess | Four pages that are plainly a list of fields stay behind |

**Choice:** (a), with these rules for a page with more than one save button: the label is **Save changes** and carries the group in a visually hidden suffix, `Save changes (banner)`, so that two buttons of one page have two accessible names; the group's save sends only the members of its group (the authentication settings are one document with one ETag, and saving the token lifetimes never carries an unsaved edit of the anonymous switch); a group that holds a state which must not be missed opens by itself (the maintenance mode while it is on). **Rationale:** a name that is the same on every button cannot be told apart by a screen reader or a browser test. The development agent would revisit the suffix if the owner prefers section titles in the visible label.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-026, R-UI-031, R-UI-033, R-UI-025. Code: `GeneralSettings`, `AuthSettings`, `ServiceAccountDetail`, `GroupDetail`. The group page keeps the creation time as a read-only field (the style guide asks for a value that cannot change to be one, and does not ask for it to go; it was dropped by mistake in the first change and restored in [Q-UI-223](#q-ui-223--the-user-the-endpoint-and-the-service-account-and-group-lists-follow-the-guide)); the service-account page keeps it under Details.

### Q-UI-223 · The user, the endpoint and the service-account and group lists follow the guide

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: [Q-UI-222](#q-ui-222--which-settings-pages-are-one-column-now-and-what-a-sections-save-button-is-called) left the user page, the endpoint page and the lists on the group and service-account pages as cards. The coordinator asked for all of them except the repository's settings.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Fields in place, facts that cannot change as read-only fields, the lists as sections (chosen) | User: display name and email edited in place with **Save changes** (disabled until a change), ID and origin read-only fields, **Details**, **Identities**, **Groups**, **Sessions** and **Advanced** (disable or enable, unlock, delete) as sections, the tokens and the roles between them. Endpoint: base URL, exposure and surface as read-only fields at the top, the rest of the configuration in a section, the rule table below. Group: members, roles and policies are sections, **Members** open. | The same rules as the pages already moved; nothing a screen showed is lost | The Delete of a user and the disable are one section further away than a button row |
| (b) Keep the lists as cards beside the moved fields | Mixed look on one page | Smaller change | A page with a column of fields and boxes under it |
| (c) Show the endpoint's configuration as a collapsed section only | One section | Short | The base URL and the exposure mode, which a reader looks for first, would be hidden |

**Choice:** (a). The user's attribute note stays: name and email come from the identity provider and are replaced at the next sign-in; the fields are read-only for a caller without `identities:write` and for the break-glass account. The endpoint's configuration comes from the configuration file and is read-only, as before. **Rationale:** the guide asks that a value that cannot change is a read-only field and that no key-value list holds what could be fields; a table or a list of rows is content and stays a table. The development agent would revisit the endpoint's split if the owner wants the whole configuration closed.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-024, R-UI-025, R-UI-026, R-EP-017. Code: `UserDetail`, `EndpointDetail`, `GroupDetail`, `PrincipalRoles`. Tests: the `Q-UI-223` cases in [users.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/users/users.spec.ts) and [endpoints.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/endpoints/endpoints.spec.ts).

### Q-UI-224 · The policy editor and the issuer page keep their structure and lose the cards and the delete in the header

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the policy editor has a table of contents, a sticky preview and a review dialog before the save; the issuer page has tabs for settings, signing keys, mappings and issued tokens. Neither is a page of settings groups the way the project's settings are, and the guide says nothing about a table of contents, a preview or tabs of different objects. They still showed cards and put a destructive action beside the main action (the policy's save bar, the issuer's header).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Keep the structure; the groups are sections, the delete is under **Advanced**, the read-only issuer is read-only fields (chosen) | Policy: **General** at the top without a title, **Principals and actions** and **Repositories and patterns** as sections that are open at first (the table of contents opens the one it jumps to), **Advanced** with **Delete policy** last. Issuer: the Settings tab is a column of fields with **Save changes** (**Create issuer** when new), **More settings** as a section, **Advanced** with **Delete issuer**; the other tabs lose their card; an issuer of the configuration shows its settings as read-only fields | The rules of the guide hold; the editor keeps what makes it usable | The delete of an issuer is only on its Settings tab |
| (b) Collapse every group of the policy editor | Closed by default, as a settings page | Same as the others | The groups are the document: a closed group hides what the policy grants, and the table of contents would open it |
| (c) Redesign both | A new layout | Might be better | Needs the owner's reference; not decided here |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** a destructive action belongs at the end under its own sentence (the guide), and a group of fields is a section, not a box. The tabs of the issuer hold different objects (settings, keys, mappings, tokens), unlike the repository's settings, whose tabs are the groups of one document and wait for the owner's reference ([Q-UI-222](#q-ui-222--which-settings-pages-are-one-column-now-and-what-a-sections-save-button-is-called)). The development agent would revisit it if the owner wants the policy's groups closed at first.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-027, R-UI-035. Code: `PolicyEditor`, `IssuerDetail`, `IssuerCreate`, `IssuerForm`. Tests: the `Q-UI-224` case in [policy-editor.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/permissions/policy-editor.spec.ts), the issuer cases of [ci-issuer-screens.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/ci/ci-issuer-screens.spec.ts).

### Q-UI-225 · A format shows its owner's logo where the owner's terms allow it, else the neutral glyph

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.
It supersedes option (a) of [Q-UI-178](#q-ui-178--oci-gets-the-cube-icon-and-the-package-page-takes-its-type-icon-from-the-same-function-as-the-list),
[Q-UI-201](#q-ui-201--debian-gets-the-archive-box-icon) and the "font icons only" part of
[Q-UI-1](#q-ui-1--component-library) for the icon of a format, on the owner's word of 2026-11-11: the Material glyphs for
the formats look terrible, he wants the registries' original logos, which may usually be used.

Context: `formatIcon` returned a ligature of the icon font: `extension` for NuGet, `view_in_ar` for OCI, `unarchive` for
Debian, `terminal` for Ansible Galaxy and `inventory_2` for the rest. It decides the icon in the package list's type column
and its "Recently viewed" list (R-UI-006), on the package page's type badge (R-UI-007) and on the wizard's format tiles
(R-UI-021). A logo is a trademark and a copyrighted drawing; whether a product may show it beside the ecosystem it serves
is its owner's decision. The development agent read each owner's terms on 2026-11-11:

| Format | Mark and official source | Copyright licence | What the owner's terms say about this use | Shown | Conditions trove follows |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `deb` | Debian Open Use Logo without label, `openlogo-nd.svg` from [debian.org/logos](https://www.debian.org/logos/) (page modified 2020-10-05) | LGPL-3.0-or-later or, at the user's option, CC BY-SA 3.0; © 1999 Software in the Public Interest, Inc. | [Trademark policy](https://www.debian.org/trademark) (modified 2026-06-10): Debian's marks may "describe or advertise your services or products relating to Debian"; the logos "can be used as part of a page describing your products or services", not as part of a product's own logo; scaling keeps the proportions; acknowledge SPI's ownership prominently and disclaim affiliation. The logos page asks, as a wish, that the image link to debian.org | Yes | The owner's file unchanged, proportions kept (`object-fit: contain`), always beside the format's name and never as trove's branding; CC BY-SA 3.0 chosen, attribution, ownership and non-affiliation in the notices and the README (Q-UI-227). The image is no link: it sits inside a row link and a listbox option, where a second link would break both |
| `nuget` | NuGet logo, `nuget.svg`, and the owner's white variant `nuget_96_mono_w.png`, from the NuGet project's media repository [NuGet/Media](https://github.com/NuGet/Media) | CC BY 2.0 ("all content in this repository unless stated otherwise") | No logo or trademark guideline of the NuGet project or of the .NET Foundation, whose project NuGet is, was found. nuget.org's terms (Microsoft, January 2025) say Microsoft's logos and product icons need an express licence; Microsoft's trademark list (FY27Q2) does not name NuGet ([H-878](#h-878--the-owner-and-the-terms-of-the-nuget-mark-are-not-published)) | Yes | The owner's files unchanged; CC BY 2.0 attribution (the project, the source at its commit, the licence, no changes) in the notices; the mark only names the NuGet format |
| `oci` | Open Container Initiative icon, `oci-icon-color.svg` and the owner's white variant `oci-icon-white.svg`, from [opencontainers/artwork](https://github.com/opencontainers/artwork) | Apache-2.0 (the repository's licence) | The Linux Foundation's [trademark usage](https://www.linuxfoundation.org/legal/trademark-usage): official versions only, no colour variations, nothing on top of the logo, never more prominent than the user's own name, no implied endorsement, a trademark notice; a logo in "any commercial or marketing context" other than those the page permits needs written permission ([H-877](#h-877--the-oci-logo-rests-on-a-non-commercial-use-under-the-linux-foundations-terms)) | Yes | The official files unchanged, the owner's white variant on the dark scheme, smaller than and beside the format's name; "Open Container Initiative®" and "OCI™" notices and the Apache-2.0 text next to the files |
| `oci` | Docker's whale, [Docker trademark guidelines](https://www.docker.com/legal/trademark-guidelines/) | — | Docker's logos "may be taken only from Docker's product sheet or from Docker's service screen shot following authorization"; to indicate compatibility only the word marks, "not logo marks", may be used | No | — |
| `npm` | npm logo, [npm Logos and Usage](https://docs.npmjs.com/policies/logos-and-usage) (last changed 2025-05-20) | — | "The npm Logos signify us, or a special relationship with us, and you may use them only with our permission"; the logos "may not be used to refer to the project, service, or company in a nominative sense" | No | The neutral glyph; the word mark with "npm is a registered trademark of npm, Inc." in the notices |
| `ansible` | Ansible's mark and the Ansible Galaxy logo, [ansible/logos](https://github.com/ansible/logos) and Red Hat's [trademark guidelines](https://www.redhat.com/en/about/trademark-guidelines-and-policies) | CC BY-SA 4.0 (the logos repository) | "Any use of the Ansible logos and marks without Ansible approval is prohibited"; Red Hat's guidelines give no permission for a Red Hat logo without a separate written agreement | No | The neutral glyph |
| `generic` | none: plain files have no brand | — | — | — | The neutral glyph |

Community sets such as Simple Icons (CC0) offer drawings of such marks, but CC0 covers the drawing and not the trademark,
and every mark that is shown has an official file, so no community file is used.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The owner's logo where the owner's terms allow this use, the neutral glyph elsewhere (chosen) | Debian, NuGet and OCI show their logos; npm, Ansible Galaxy, the generic format and every format the UI does not name show `inventory_2` | The owner's wish wherever an owner allows it; no mark is shown whose owner reserves it | npm, the commonest format, keeps a glyph, and the set mixes logos and a glyph |
| (b) Every format's logo | npm's and Ansible's logos too | The look the owner asked for | Two owners say "only with our permission"; showing their marks is a use they reserved |
| (c) Ask npm, Inc. and Red Hat first, glyphs until they answer | Requests by the owner | A complete set later | Holds back the three logos that are allowed today; a request is the owner's to send |
| (d) Keep the glyphs of Q-UI-178 and Q-UI-201 | No change | No licence question | What the owner rejected |

**Choice:** (a). OCI shows the Open Container Initiative's mark, not Docker's: the type column reads "OCI (Docker)", but
Docker's terms admit its logo only after its authorization, and the format is the OCI image and distribution specification,
which Docker's tools implement. The neutral glyph is `inventory_2`; `terminal` and `extension` are gone with the other
format glyphs. `formatIcon` stays the one function that decides; it returns either a logo (the file, the file for the dark
scheme or none, and whether the mark stands on a plate, Q-UI-226) or the glyph.

**Rationale:** the owner's request holds wherever the owner of a mark allows the use. Where an owner says "only with our
permission" (npm, Red Hat for Ansible, Docker), a product that installations run cannot rest on nobody objecting, and the
name beside every icon (R-UI-006) carries the meaning anyway. The development agent revisits this when npm, Inc. or Red Hat
grant permission (the owner can ask through [npm's contact page](https://www.npmjs.com/contact) and trademarks@redhat.com),
when an owner's terms change ([H-879](#h-879--an-owners-terms-can-change-after-the-day-they-were-read)), and when trove is
offered commercially (H-877).

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-001 (the icon bullet), R-UI-006, R-UI-007, R-UI-021; the notes on Q-UI-1, Q-UI-114, Q-UI-178
and Q-UI-201. Documented in [ui-style-guide.md](../developer/ui-style-guide.md), [design-language.md](../developer/design-language.md)
and [web-ui.md](../developer/web-ui.md). Code: [format-icon.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/format-icon.ts),
[web/public/formats/](../../web/public/formats/NOTICE.txt). Tests: the `Q-UI-225` cases in
[format-icon.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/format-icon.spec.ts), [package-list.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/packages/package-list.spec.ts),
[package-detail.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/packages/package-detail.spec.ts) and
[repository-wizard.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/repository-wizard.spec.ts).

### Q-UI-226 · A logo is an image of the owner's file, and the dark scheme shows the owner's light variant or a plate

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: Q-UI-1 excluded SVG icon registration (a security bypass for every URL, banned by R-UI-046, and a Trusted Types
policy the CSP does not list), and `@angular/material` is no dependency since Q-UI-126. trove's theme is its own: `data-theme`
overrides the system's scheme, and an `<img>` sees only the system's. Measured against the dark surfaces (`#18171d`,
`#28272d`, `#1d283e`), Debian's red (`#a80030`) reaches 1.9:1 to 2.3:1, NuGet's blue (`#004880`) 1.6:1 to 1.9:1 and the
OCI navy (`#262261`) 1.0:1 to 1.3:1; on the light surfaces each is 6.9:1 or more.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) An `<img>` of the owner's file under `web/public/formats/`, in a small component; where the owner has a variant for dark grounds, both images, switched by trove's scheme; else a light plate behind the mark in the dark scheme (chosen) | `<trove-format-icon [format]>` | The file is the owner's, byte for byte (its SHA-256 is in the notice), so "unchanged" is checkable and an update is a copy; no bypass, no new CSP source (`img-src 'self'`); the switch follows trove's theme through CSS | OCI and NuGet load the hidden variant too; files of `web/public` are revalidated, not cached as immutable |
| (b) Inline SVG in a component | The paths copied into a template | One theme mechanism, no request | A transcribed logo is a modified copy, checked by eye; NuGet's light variant is a PNG; the paths ship in the scripts |
| (c) An icon registry | Material's or a registry of its own | One icon API | A security bypass for every URL and the Trusted Types gap of Q-UI-1 |
| (d) CSS background images | `url()` in a stylesheet, hashed by the build | Immutable caching | No element to carry an empty `alt`; the build renames the owner's file; the same scheme switch |

**Choice:** (a). `formatIcon` returns the file, the dark-scheme file or none, and the plate flag; `FormatIconView`
(`<trove-format-icon>`) draws a square of one em, so each place sets the size it had: 20 px in the list and "Recently
viewed", 16 px on the badge, 32 px on a tile. In the dark scheme OCI shows its owner's white icon and NuGet its owner's white
variant, which NuGet publishes as PNG only (96 px covers a 32 px tile at three device pixels per CSS pixel); Debian
publishes none and stands on the plate `--trove-logo-plate` (`#ececef`, 6.6:1 for the swirl; transparent in the light
scheme). No mark is recoloured. The switch is `.logo-on-light` and `.logo-on-dark` in `_icons.scss`, under
`:root[data-theme='dark']` and under `prefers-color-scheme: dark` without `data-theme='light'`, the conditions of the
tokens' `color-scheme`. Every place shows the format's name as text beside the icon, so a logo has `alt=""` and the glyph
`aria-hidden="true"`: the accessible name of a type cell, the badge and a tile is the display name, said once. The files are
served at trove's origin without the page's CSP, so a spec refuses scripts, event handlers, foreign objects and references
outside the file in every SVG that `formatIcon` names.

**Rationale:** the licence and trademark conditions of Q-UI-225 ask for the owner's unchanged file, which (a) ships as it is
and (b) and (d) do not; (c) is what Q-UI-1 excluded. The plate and the owners' light variants keep a mark visible in the dark
scheme without recolouring it, which the Linux Foundation forbids ("should not be displayed with color variations") and no
other owner invites. The development agent
revisits this if NuGet publishes an SVG for dark grounds, if the request of the hidden variant shows in a measurement, or if
an owner asks for the logo to be a link.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-001 (the icon bullet). Code: [format-icon.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/format-icon.ts),
[_icons.scss](../../web/src/styles/_icons.scss), [_tokens.scss](../../web/src/styles/_tokens.scss) (`--trove-logo-plate`),
`package-list.scss`, `package-detail.scss`, `repository-wizard.scss`. Tests: the `Q-UI-226` cases in
[format-icon.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/format-icon.spec.ts) and [palette.spec.ts](../../web/src/styles/palette.spec.ts),
`spokenText` in [axe.ts](../../web/src/app/testing/axe.ts).

### Q-UI-227 · The logos' owners, sources and licences travel with the notices, and the README says they imply no endorsement

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: CC BY-SA 3.0 (Debian) and CC BY 2.0 (NuGet) ask for attribution and the licence's address, Apache-2.0 (OCI) for its
text; Debian asks that SPI's ownership be acknowledged prominently and that affiliation be disclaimed; the Linux Foundation
asks for a trademark notice; npm asks materials that refer to npm to say "npm is a registered trademark of npm, Inc.". The
UI's third-party notices are `/ui/<locale>/3rdpartylicenses.txt` (Q-UI-144), linked from the Installation card of the
system status.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `web/public/formats/NOTICE.txt`, served next to the logos and appended by `build:embed` to the notices, plus a paragraph in the README (chosen) | One section per logo (file, SHA-256, source at its commit, owner, licence, trademark line) and the sentence that no owner is affiliated with or endorses trove; the build fails without it | The notice travels with the files and with the notices of the build; the README is the project's front page, where Debian's "prominently" is met | Two places say the same in different lengths |
| (b) Only in `3rdpartylicenses.txt` | The text in `build-embed.mjs` | One place | The logo directory carries no notice of its own; the README says nothing |
| (c) A line in the UI | A footer or an about panel | Seen by every user | The UI has no footer, and the logos stand beside the names they denote |

**Choice:** (a). The Apache-2.0 text ships as `formats/oci/LICENSE.txt`, the artwork repository's file unchanged.
**Rationale:** each licence wants its notice where the files go, and a build that drops the notice must fail like one that
drops Inter's licence (Q-UI-144). The development agent revisits (c) if an owner asks for a statement inside the product.

**Applied in the spec:** none beyond Q-UI-225. Code: [NOTICE.txt](../../web/public/formats/NOTICE.txt),
[build-embed.mjs](../../web/scripts/build-embed.mjs), the README's licence section. Tests: `TestR_UI_001_ThirdPartyNotices`
([notices_test.go](../../internal/webui/notices_test.go)), the `Q-UI-227` case in
[format-icon.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/format-icon.spec.ts).

### Q-UI-228 · A level is chosen in a radio group of three, each with its icon and a sentence

|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A radio group of Private, Internal, Public, each with GitLab's icon (a lock, a shield, a globe) and one muted sentence; an option that cannot be chosen is disabled with its reason (chosen) | The control of the owner's GitLab "Visibility level"; the style guide's rule for three exclusive choices | The reader sees all three and what each means; a disabled option says why; the same control on four screens | Takes vertical space |
| (b) A select | Compact | One line | Hides the alternatives and their meaning, against the style guide's rule for three choices |

**Choice:** (a), one shared component `trove-visibility-level` in `web/src/app/shared/ui/`, used by the general settings, the project,

that builds it.

exactly this control. The development agent records no revisit condition.

| (b) A column "Visibility" | Explicit | Readable as text | A column in every list for a value of three states |

### Q-UI-233 · The visibility of a project is a section of its settings page, closed by default, with its own save

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A settings section **Visibility** whose one-sentence summary names the level (chosen) | The page keeps the name and the description open at the top; sections fold | The page rule of Q-UI-215 and Q-UI-222: a group with a save of its own is a section; the summary tells the level without opening it | One click to change it |
| (b) The group in the open form next to the name | One form, one save | Visible at once | The level is saved by its own operation with its own confirmation; one save for two requests would send the name along with a cascade |

**Choice:** (a). The group is read-only with "Only an administrator of trove sets the visibility of a project." for everyone without `projects:write`, the Owner included.

### Q-UI-234 · The start page asks the API for the memberships, and a caller redirected into its only project is a signed-in one

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: R-UI-054 lists the caller's projects first, then the others its level admits, and a filter "Your projects" (`membership=true`). The start route used to send a caller with one project into it.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The context holds the whole list; the memberships come first by `role`; the filter reads `membership=true` from the API while it is on; only a signed-in caller with exactly one visible project is redirected (chosen) | The anonymous subject also lists the public projects | The filter is the API's; an anonymous visitor reaches the list instead of being sent into a project it does not know | One more request while the filter is on |
| (b) Filter the list in the browser by `role` | No request | Fewer requests | Not the parameter the spec names; the answer is the same only while the list is complete |

**Choice:** (a).

**Rationale:** The server owns the meaning of membership. The development agent records no revisit condition.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-054, R-UI-057.

### Q-UI-235 · Lowering a project lists a repository when its artifacts or its wiki are above the new level

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: R-UI-054 asks for a dialog that lists the repositories that will be lowered with their levels.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) From the project's repository list, every repository whose artifacts or wiki level is above the new level, one line each: the key, its levels and the level it ends at (chosen) | The list the server will lower, computed from what the screen already reads | The administrator sees the cascade before it happens; the answer's `lowered` is counted afterwards | A repository changed meanwhile can differ from the preview; the answer's count is the truth |
| (b) Only the count | No list | Short | The acceptance criterion names the repository in the dialog |

**Choice:** (a); the dialog says so plainly when no repository is above the new level.

**Rationale:** The preview is a convenience, the server's `lowered` is authoritative. The development agent records no revisit condition.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-054.

### Q-UI-236 · A new repository and a new project start at the level the screen can name, and a caller who cannot read the default leaves the level to the server

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the default level is read with `settings:read`; a project Owner creating a repository, or a caller with `projects:write` only, cannot read it.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|

| (b) Always omit the level at create | The server decides | Simple | The review step could not show the level the repository will get |

**Choice:** (a).

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-054, R-UI-055, R-UI-056.

### Q-UI-237 · The levels of a repository are not part of its edit form, and the project header carries the level icon in the switcher

| (b) The levels in `RepositoryForm` and the one Save changes | One save | Fewer states | Raising a level would travel with unrelated edits; the spec asks for its own save |

### Q-UI-270 · In the repository list the column grows to the address; the list's region scrolls sideways when it must

Status: **Replaced by [Q-UI-300](#q-ui-300--in-a-list-every-address-field-has-one-width-the-lists-longest-address-up-to-what-the-other-columns-leave)** (the owner's task T-21 of 2026-11-12: the list showed a field of a different width in every row
and scrolled sideways at about 1540 px). Kept for its record; nothing in the UI follows it any more.

Context: the list is `<trove-data-table>`: a bordered region that scrolls in both directions (`.table-scroll`, `overflow: auto`)
with a sticky header; the address was capped at 24 ch with an ellipsis. The longest realistic addresses are
`https://trove.k8s-main.wds18.de/api/npm/npm-internal/` (53 characters) and `trove.k8s-main.wds18.de/docker-hub-remote` (40);
at 0.875rem monospace (about 8.4 px per character) the field is about 450 px plus the 32 px button.

| Option | What happens | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The column grows to the field; the region scrolls sideways if the columns are wider than the panel (chosen) | The field is as wide as its address, nothing scrolls inside it | The address is readable at a glance, as the owner asked; the region already scrolls | A very long address widens the table |
| (b) A fixed-width field (about 24 ch) that scrolls inside itself | Every row has the same field | The table keeps its width | The address is cut again; the reader scrolls each field to read it: the defect the owner reported |
| (c) A fixed width, the address wraps | The address breaks mid-word | No sideways scroll | An address is not prose; a break inside a URL reads wrongly and is not one selection |

**Choice:** (a). The cell does not wrap (`white-space: nowrap`), the field's width is `calc(<length>ch + padding)` plus the
button with `max-inline-size: 100%` so that the fields of other screens stay inside their containers, and the address column
has no maximum. The description column keeps wrapping, so it gives room before the address does.
**Rationale:** the owner's report is that the address must be readable; (a) is the only option in which the reader does not
act. The development agent revisits it if installations produce addresses over about 80 characters and the list needs more
than the panel in the common case; (b) with a 60 ch field is then the fallback.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-065, R-UI-066. Code and tests: [client-address-work-packages.md](../projektplan/client-address-work-packages.md).

### Q-UI-271 · On a narrow viewport the field scrolls inside itself and keeps the button attached

Status: **Replaced by [Q-UI-300](#q-ui-300--in-a-list-every-address-field-has-one-width-the-lists-longest-address-up-to-what-the-other-columns-leave) and [Q-UI-301](#q-ui-301--a-field-alone-on-its-line-fills-the-line-up-to-a-measure-of-70-characters)** (the owner's task T-21 of 2026-11-12: the list showed a field of a different width in every row
and scrolled sideways at about 1540 px). Kept for its record; nothing in the UI follows it any more.

| Option | What happens | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The input shrinks (`min-inline-size: 8rem`) and scrolls its text inside; the button stays attached and visible (chosen) | On a facts list or a wizard step the field takes the room that is left; in the list the region scrolls | The button is never pushed out; no new layout | The reader scrolls inside the field to read the end |
| (b) The button wraps below the field | Two rows | Full field width | The button is no longer joined to the field, the one thing the owner described |
| (c) The address wraps in a text area | Several lines | Whole address visible | Not the GitLab field; a text area is for text |

**Choice:** (a). The component is `display: inline-flex`, the input `flex: 1 1 auto; min-inline-size: 8rem`, the button
`flex: none`. There is no breakpoint; the same rule holds from 320 px up (R-UI-044 reflow).
**Rationale:** it is what the reference does, and select-on-focus puts the end of the address one key away (End). The
development agent revisits it if the owner's walk on a narrow screen shows addresses that need a second line.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-065.

### Q-UI-272 · An address field holds one address; multi-line snippets stay code blocks, and the Bastion address becomes a field

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What happens | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The field is for one address only; snippets, commands and guide text keep their code blocks (chosen) | Seven call sites (R-UI-066); the Bastion address, today a `<code>` in a sentence, becomes a field below the sentence | One meaning per control; a field cannot hold several lines; the reference's clone field is one URL too | Two copy looks on a page (field for an address, block for a command) |
| (b) Snippets of one line become fields too | A one-line registry command is a field | Uniform copy look | The line is a command, not an address, and the same snippet is several lines with another client: the shape would change with the data |
| (c) Addresses in the guide's server-rendered HTML become fields | The UI parses the guide's HTML | Uniform | The UI adds format knowledge to server text, which R-UI-049 forbids |

**Choice:** (a). What is out of scope is named in R-UI-066.
**Rationale:** a field says "this is the thing to put into a configuration"; a code block says "run or save this". The
development agent revisits (b) if the owner wants the one-line registry command as a field.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-065, R-UI-066. **Replaced in part by [Q-UI-320](#q-ui-320--every-value-to-copy-of-one-line-is-a-field-with-its-joined-copy-button-a-page-shows-one-client-address-and-a-panels-selects-share-one-width)**
(the coordinator, fix wave 2 of T-21): a command of one line is a field too; a command of several lines stays a code block.

### Q-UI-273 · The field is a native read-only input that selects its text on focus, beside the existing copy button

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What happens | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `<input readonly>` plus `<trove-copy-button>` inside `<trove-address-field>` (chosen) | The browser provides scrolling, selection, caret keys, find and a focus stop | Native behaviour, accessible by default, the reference's markup | The address is not in `textContent`; tests read `.value` |
| (b) A `<code>` in an overflow container | Text in the DOM | Tests unchanged | Scrolling a non-focusable box needs `tabindex` and a role; selecting exactly the address is fiddly |
| (c) A new copy button inside the component | Joined look in one place | Full control | A second copy implementation beside `trove-copy-button`, which the rest of the UI uses and tests |

**Choice:** (a). The component sets `readonly`, `spellcheck="false"`, `autocomplete="off"`, `translate="no"` and `aria-label`
from its `label` input, and selects all on `focus` and `click`. It renders `trove-copy-button` with `[label]="copyLabel"` and
the default glyph; the joined look is the component's own stylesheet.
**Rationale:** the clipboard path, the live-region message and the failure alert exist and are tested once. The development
agent revisits it if `trove-copy-button` gains a visible "copied" state for other places; the field then takes it too.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-065.

### Q-UI-274 · The field keeps the fill and border of an editable control, not the grey of a read-only value

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: `.text-input[readonly]` in [_controls.scss](../../web/src/styles/_controls.scss) is a transparent border on the disabled
fill, the look of a value that is shown, not used. The owner asked for "a read-only, bordered field" like GitLab's clone field,
which has the border and the fill of an input.

| Option | What happens | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The component restates border, fill and radius from the control tokens and overrides the read-only rule for itself (chosen) | A bordered field in the control fill | As the reference and as the owner's words | One more variant of a read-only input |
| (b) Use `.text-input[readonly]` as it is | A grey borderless value | No new style | Not what the owner asked; the joined button has no edge to meet |

**Choice:** (a), in the component's stylesheet, with the hover and focus states of `.text-input`; the other read-only inputs of
the UI keep their look.
**Rationale:** the owner's description is the specification. The development agent revisits it if the owner wants every
read-only input bordered.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-065. The style guide's entry: [Address field](../developer/ui-style-guide.md#address-field).

### Q-UI-300 · In a list every address field has one width, the list's longest address up to what the other columns leave

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the owner's task T-21 (2026-11-12). Under Q-UI-270 each field was as wide as its own address and the column had no
maximum: every row's field had another width, and the list scrolled sideways at about 1540 px. The renders of
`make ui-renders` (R-UI-047) showed the same at 1440 px: the description squeezed to a column of single words, the last
activity and the row actions out of view. The requirement: one width per list; the column as wide as the longest address, up
to a cap that keeps the list free of sideways scrolling at 1280 px and wider with its usual columns; the field fills the cell;
a longer address scrolls inside the field, never an ellipsis, the copy button attached. The coordinator's look at the first
renders (2026-11-12) added: the address is the plain user's main value in the list, so at 1440 px an address of the length of
the owner's (`https://trove.k8s-main.wds18.net/api/ansible/test/galaxy/`, 57 characters) is shown whole, and a field shows the
address from its start, never its tail.

| Option | What happens | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The column is `min(longest address, the list's width minus the room of its other columns)`, at least 16 rem; the field fills the cell and shows the address from its start (chosen) | The list passes the length of its longest address (`--trove-address-chars`) and the room its other columns need (`--trove-address-others`, 36 rem in a project, 44 rem in the admin area with its project column); `td.address-cell` computes the width in the field's own monospace face (`ch`) with the padding, the border and the copy button; that width is also the column's least, so the other columns give way first | One width per list by construction; the address takes all the room the list can give it; no measuring in script | The room of the other columns is a number per list, measured on the renders |
| (b) A share of the list's width (26 %, the first version of this decision) | A fixed proportion | One rule for every list | At 1440 px the field showed 28 characters: the host and a few more; the render showed every row as `https://localhost:4200/api/r…` |
| (c) The share, with the field scrolled to the address's end | The rows differ at their end | Distinct rows in a narrow field | The host is cut mid-token (`pi/ansible/…`, `t:4200/api/deb/…`), which reads as broken |
| (d) The column takes what the browser leaves it (`table-layout: auto`, no width) | The browser shares out the room | Adapts to every list | The address column is shrunk first: every field showed `https://loca` in the render |

**Choice:** (a). Measured on the renders (`.out/ui-renders/<kind>/repositories*-<scheme>-<width>.png`, the report's widths): in a
project's list the input is 521 px at 1440 px (62 characters, the 56-character `https://localhost:4200/api/ansible/platform/collections/`
of the seed whole) and 361 px at 1280 px (40 characters); in the admin area's list, with its project column, 393 px and 233 px.
Neither list scrolls sideways at 1440, 1280 or 1024 px, nor at 390 px, where the rows stack (Q-UI-306). The seed's
`platform/collections` stands for the owner's address: 56 against 57 characters.

**Rationale:** the owner asked for one width per list and no sideways scrolling, and the address is what the plain user comes for,
so it gets every pixel the other columns do not need. The development agent revisits the room of the other columns when a list's
columns change (Q-UI-312 would give the plain user the room of the last activity), and the admin area's list if the owner wants its
addresses whole at 1440 px (its project could then be the key's second line).

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-065, R-UI-066. Code: `td.address-cell` in [_list-screens.scss](../../web/src/styles/_list-screens.scss),
the repository list (`addressChars`, `addressOthers`) and the endpoint page. Style guide:
[Address field](../developer/ui-style-guide.md#address-field).

**Revised by [Q-UI-330](#q-ui-330--a-list-takes-its-columns-from-the-job-of-its-kind-of-user-the-important-properties-are-columns-and-the-address-takes-no-more-than-its-share) (2026-11-12):** the address is no longer what gets every pixel the other columns do not need. The column is
the list's longest address up to its share (`--trove-address-share`): in a project's list what is left after the repository's
preferred 20 rem and the least widths of the others, room left over going back to the repository; in a list without a preferred
column 46 characters and what the others leave at their least widths. Never under 10 rem. A longer address scrolls inside its
field from its start, never an ellipsis. The admin area's list and the search results show no field at all.

### Q-UI-301 · A field alone on its line fills the line up to a measure of 70 characters

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the places with one field (the repository page's facts, the wizard's review, the Bastion address of the client setup
and of the guides). The renders showed the consumer view of a repository with its two addresses stacked in two widths, the same
defect as the list's.

| Option | What happens | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The field fills its line, at most `--trove-address-measure` (40 rem: 70 characters at 0.875rem with the padding and the button) (chosen) | Every single field and every stack of fields is one width | One rule; a stack is aligned; an address of up to 70 characters is shown whole | A short address has empty room at the end of its field |
| (b) As wide as its address (Q-UI-271) | The field follows its address | No empty room | Stacked fields differ, as the render showed |
| (c) The settings column's measure, 56 rem | The widest form measure | One measure for forms | At 1440 px a 53-character address fills half of an 896-px field |

**Choice:** (a). Below the measure the field takes the line and scrolls inside, from 8 rem up (R-UI-044 reflow); several fields
of one repository stand one under the other with `--trove-space-2` between them.

**Rationale:** the renders of the repository page in both schemes and at 1440, 1024 and 390 px show aligned fields whose
addresses are read whole at the two wider widths. The development agent revisits the measure if an installation's addresses
are longer than 70 characters.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-065, R-UI-066. Code: the token `--trove-address-measure` in [_tokens.scss](../../web/src/styles/_tokens.scss).

**Unchanged by [Q-UI-330](#q-ui-330--a-list-takes-its-columns-from-the-job-of-its-kind-of-user-the-important-properties-are-columns-and-the-address-takes-no-more-than-its-share):** a field alone on its line is not one of a list's columns; in a stacked row the field takes the row's
width (Q-UI-306).

### Q-UI-302 · The repository list names a repository by key and description in its first column and puts the row's actions in a menu

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: Q-UI-300 needs room at 1280 px. The list had seven columns and four quiet buttons per row (Settings, Browse,
Vulnerabilities, Delete), which alone took about 300 px, and a description column squeezed to single words. The style guide's
rules for lists ([Lists](../developer/ui-style-guide.md#lists)) say that the first column names the thing with a muted second
line, and that a row's actions go into a menu behind `more_vert` named for the row.

| Option | What happens | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The first column **Repository** holds the key and, as its muted second line, the description; the actions are one `more_vert` menu (chosen) | Six columns and a 32-px menu button | What the style guide asks of every list; about 400 px for the address and the other columns at 1280 px | One click more to reach Settings or Delete from the list; the key's own page has them too |
| (b) Keep the columns, give the address less | Fields of about 12 characters | No change of the list's layout | The field is useless at 1280 px |
| (c) Hide columns below a width | Responsive columns | Room at 1280 px | Columns that come and go with the window; nothing in the guide |

**Choice:** (a). The menu offers Settings, Browse, Vulnerabilities (where the format has the adapter) and Delete (for whoever
may delete), as the buttons did; its trigger's name is **Actions for &lt;key&gt;**.

**Rationale:** both changes are rules of the style guide that the list broke, and together with Q-UI-303 they give the address
its share. The development agent would revisit the menu if the owner names one frequent action that should stay a quiet button.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-020 (the row actions are the same; their place is the menu). Code: [repository-list.html](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/repository-list.html).

**Revised by [Q-UI-330](#q-ui-330--a-list-takes-its-columns-from-the-job-of-its-kind-of-user-the-important-properties-are-columns-and-the-address-takes-no-more-than-its-share) (2026-11-12):** the description is the only line under the key; project, format and class are columns. The
admin area's row has one quiet button beside the menu, the copy of the client address, which the menu offers too.

### Q-UI-303 · The repository list's key breaks after a hyphen where it is longer than its column

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the data table kept every key and identifier on one line. A repository key of 51 characters
(`release-candidates-for-the-customer-portal-frontend` in the seed of the renders) is about 390 px wide at 14 px and pushed the
list sideways at 1440 px whatever the address column did.

| Option | What happens | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) In the repository list the key in the first column (`th.wrap-name`) wraps where it must, after a hyphen; identifiers in other columns and the names of other lists stay on one line (chosen) | A long key takes two or three lines in its row | No sideways scrolling from a long key; a short key is unchanged | A long key reads in parts; the lists differ until the audit's wave decides the rule for all |
| (b) The same for the first column of every data table | One rule | Consistent | The package list, with nine columns, squeezed its names into lines of one word at 1440 px in the render: its columns need a decision of their own first |
| (c) Keep keys on one line | Long keys push the list | A key is never broken | The list scrolls sideways, the defect of T-21 |
| (d) Cut long keys with an ellipsis | One line | Even rows | A name that cannot be read, which R-UI-065 forbids for addresses for the same reason |

**Choice:** (a). The other lists keep their names on one line; whether they follow is item UI-A-29 of the audit
([ui-audit.md](../projektplan/ui-audit.md)), with their columns.

**Rationale:** a name is read, an address copied; a wrapped key stays readable and selectable, and the repository list needs the
room for Q-UI-300. The development agent revisits it with the columns of the other lists.

**Applied in the spec:** the data table's styles ([_list-screens.scss](../../web/src/styles/_list-screens.scss)).

**Unchanged by [Q-UI-330](#q-ui-330--a-list-takes-its-columns-from-the-job-of-its-kind-of-user-the-important-properties-are-columns-and-the-address-takes-no-more-than-its-share):** the key still breaks after a hyphen where it is longer than its column, which is now the widest of the
admin area's list.

### Q-UI-304 · make ui-renders renders the working tree through the dev server, signs the three kinds of user in through a provider of the profile, and seeds through the API

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: rule 11 of the plan (owner, 2026-11-12): a UI change is rendered and looked at before it lands, as each kind of user of
R-UI-067. The UI development profile ([web-ui.md](../developer/web-ui.md#local-ui-development)) had the break-glass account only:
without an identity provider no other user can sign in, and the break-glass account cannot hold a token (`break_glass_restricted`)
for the formats' upload routes.

| Option | What happens | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The dev server (`ng serve --configuration local`) in front of one trove of the profile, a sign-in provider of the profile ([test/devidp](../../test/devidp/devidp.go)) that signs in `sam`, `priya` or `ada` without a password, a seed through the management API as the break-glass account and through the formats' routes with the power user's token (chosen) | The renders show the working tree as it is, in seconds after a change; the users are real users of trove with real grants | No build of the embedded bundle (minutes) per change; the same login as an installation's (code flow, PKCE, the user created at the first sign-in) | English only and no CSP, the dev server's differences that web-ui.md lists |
| (b) The embedded build (`make web`) served by trove | The installation's bundle | CSP and both locales | A localized production build and a rebuild of trove for every look |
| (c) Sessions written into the database for each user | No provider | Fast | Bypasses the login and ties the tool to the schema |
| (d) The browser sends a token instead of the session | No provider | Simple | The UI decides what to show by the session (`whoami`, recent sign-in), so the screens would not be the user's |

**Choice:** (a). The provider listens on `127.0.0.1:19090` only, starts and stops with `make ui-dev-backend`, and is in the
profile's `trove.yaml` as the provider `ui-dev`; the sign-in screen of the profile offers it beside the break-glass form
(`auth.login_page.auto_redirect: false`). The profile's outbound configuration trusts its CA and allows the loopback addresses.
The scheme is the browser's (`prefers-color-scheme`), which the app follows when no theme is stored, the way the theme button's
"Follow the system" does; the seed clears a stored theme of the three users.

**Rationale:** the tool must show what a user sees, so the users sign in as users do; the dev server makes a render after an edit
cheap enough to be done every time. The development agent revisits (b) for a check of the CSP or of the German build.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-047. Code and documentation: [web-ui.md](../developer/web-ui.md#renders-of-every-screen).

**Revised by [Q-UI-330](#q-ui-330--a-list-takes-its-columns-from-the-job-of-its-kind-of-user-the-important-properties-are-columns-and-the-address-takes-no-more-than-its-share) (2026-11-12):** a picture is judged first by the job of its kind of user (does the most important
information get the most room, and can the properties be scanned column by column) and only then by widths and scrolling, which
the report measures.

### Q-UI-305 · The repository list puts format and class in one cell and shows the date of the last activity

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: after Q-UI-300 and Q-UI-302 the renders showed **Last activity** spending about 250 px on a dash in almost every row
(`– ` in 11 of 12 rows of `platform`), with the full time to the second where there is one, and format and class in two narrow
columns of their own. Every pixel they take is one the address does not get.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) One column **Format and class**: the format, the class with its icon muted under it; **Last activity** shows the date (`Nov 12, 2026`), the full time is its `title` (chosen) | Two columns about 230 px narrower | The address gets the room; the date says how fresh a repository is, the time to the second says nothing more in a list | The time needs a pointer; the header **Format and class** is wider than its cells |
| (b) Leave **Last activity** out when no row of the list has one | The column comes and goes with the data | No column of dashes | Lists of two projects look different; a new activity moves every column |
| (c) **Last activity** behind Details | Only on the repository page | The list is short | The power user's view of which repository is still used is lost from the list |

**Choice:** (a). Whether the plain user sees the column at all is Q-UI-312, for the owner's review.

**Revised in fix wave 1 (2026-11-12):** the header is **Format**, its help names the class under it (the longer header took
the address's room); the last activity is shown to who may change the list's repositories (Q-UI-312) and only while a loaded
row has one, so it is never a column of dashes.

**Rationale:** both changes free room for the address without dropping a fact. The development agent revisits the header if the
owner prefers **Type**.

**Revised in fix wave 4 (2026-11-12):** format and class are no column any more, in the project's list either; they are the line
under the key (Q-UI-328).

**Revised by [Q-UI-330](#q-ui-330--a-list-takes-its-columns-from-the-job-of-its-kind-of-user-the-important-properties-are-columns-and-the-address-takes-no-more-than-its-share) (2026-11-12):** that revision is reversed. **Format** (icon and name, on one line) and **Class** (icon and
name) are columns of their own in both lists and the search results, with the help on **Class**; the last activity is the admin
area's column only.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-020. Code: [repository-list.html](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/repository-list.html).

### Q-UI-306 · Below 48 rem of its width the repository list stacks each row, with the address across the row

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: at 390 px (and at 1024 px with the pinned sidebar, where the list is 712 px wide) the table ran off the right edge, the
address column was out of view and the description wrapped into a tall, narrow column (the coordinator's look at the renders,
2026-11-12).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A list that opts in (`class="stack-narrow"` on `<trove-data-table>`) shows each row as a block below 48 rem of the list's width: the name and its description with the row's menu on the first line, format and class on one line, the address field across the full width, then the cells that carry a value, each with its column's name (`data-label`) (chosen) | A container query on the list region `.list-main` | The plain user's address is whole and wide on a phone; no sideways scrolling; the same markup, the head kept for assistive technology | A second layout to check; a table whose rows are blocks keeps its semantics in Chromium and Firefox, not reliably in older Safari |
| (b) The table scrolls sideways in its region | Today | Nothing to build | The address out of view |
| (c) A separate list of cards for small screens | Two templates | Freedom of layout | Two templates of one list drift apart |

**Choice:** (a), for the repository list first; since fix wave 1 for every list of the data table
([Q-UI-308](#q-ui-308--every-list-takes-its-layout-from-the-data-table-a-column-budget-a-least-width-for-its-name-one-alignment-stacked-rows)),
which names each cell by its column itself.

**Rationale:** the stacked row is the shape the address needs at a narrow width, and a container query follows the list's own
width, also beside the open filter panel. The development agent revisits the 48 rem if a list with fewer columns fits wider.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-020, R-UI-065. Code: [_list-screens.scss](../../web/src/styles/_list-screens.scss) (Stacked rows).

**Revised by [Q-UI-330](#q-ui-330--a-list-takes-its-columns-from-the-job-of-its-kind-of-user-the-important-properties-are-columns-and-the-address-takes-no-more-than-its-share) (2026-11-12):** a stacked row shows format and class each on a line with its column's name; the admin
area's row and a search result have no address field, the copy button stands on the first line. The rows stack below 49 rem
of the list's frame, 48 rem of columns and 1 rem for a scrollbar beside the rows, and every list's least widths sum to at most
48 rem, so no list scrolls sideways before it stacks.

### Q-UI-307 · A page's own actions are buttons at the right end of its header; views of the same thing are tabs

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the renders show four forms of page-level action: a confirm button at the right end of the header (repositories), a
confirm button under the description on the left (permission policies, personal tokens), quiet text links at the right
beside the tabs (**Browse files**, **Vulnerabilities** on the repository page; **All repositories**, **Content**, **Browse**,
**Vulnerabilities** on the repository settings), and a link line under the heading (client setup).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The header's right end holds the page's actions as buttons: at most one `btn btn-confirm` and `btn btn-default` beside it, more in a `more_vert` menu; a link to another view of the same thing (its files, its vulnerabilities, its settings) is a tab of the page; a link up to a list is the breadcrumb (chosen) | One place for actions, one for views | The style guide's anatomy of a page, applied to every page; quiet links stop looking like loose text | The repository page gets tabs **Files** and **Vulnerabilities** beside **Packages** and **Set up client** |
| (b) Keep the quiet links | Unchanged | Nothing to build | Four patterns |

**Choice:** (a). On the repository page (Q-UI-313) the header holds the address field and **Set up client** as its primary
action; **Settings** is a default button for who may change.

**Rationale:** a user finds an action where every other page puts it. The development agent revisits the menu if a page has two
frequent actions.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-067; the style guide's [Anatomy of a page](../developer/ui-style-guide.md#anatomy-of-a-page) already
says it, the screens follow in the fix waves of the audit. Built in fix wave 2 on every screen but the repository settings and the
wizard (planned on T-18's tree) and the vulnerability pages (whose displays another builder replaces): a detail page names its
object in the `<h1>` and its kind as a badge (the user `alice`, the badge **User**); the quiet links up to a list are gone, the
breadcrumb is the way up; a quiet action in a header is a default button; the profile's and the project's create actions
(**Create token**, **Create policy**, **Create service account**) are the header's.

### Q-UI-308 · Every list takes its layout from the data table: a column budget, a least width for its name, one alignment, stacked rows

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: fix wave 1 of T-21 (the coordinator, 2026-11-12) after the renders of Q-UI-300: in the repository list at 1440 px the
first column was about 150 px, so the key `debian-internal-packages-for-bookworm-and-trixie` wrapped to four lines and the
descriptions to three; the cells of one row sat at different heights (the name at the top of its tall cell, format and address
centred); and the room of the other columns was a number the repository list set for itself (`--trove-address-others`). The other
lists had none of it (systemic cause 2 of [ui-audit.md](../projektplan/ui-audit.md)).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The data table owns the layout: a column declares its least width (`TableColumn.width`, on the header cell), one column may be the `fill` column that takes what the others leave (the address, Q-UI-300), every cell is aligned to the top of its row with a control centred on the first line of text, and below 48 rem every list stacks its rows, each cell named by its column (`data-label`, set by the table) and an empty one left out (chosen) | One mechanism for ~30 lists | A list states its columns once; the budget is summed, not measured; one alignment everywhere; every list is readable on a phone | A cell's least width must hold its header, which the list's author checks on the renders |
| (b) Each list keeps its own widths and stacking | As after Q-UI-306 | No shared change | The defects of the audit come back with every list |
| (c) Middle alignment, as before | Cells centred | Familiar | A tall first cell leaves the rest of the row floating, the render's defect |

**Choice:** (a). The repository list declares 16 rem for the repository, 7 rem for the project, 5.5 rem for the format (whose
header is now **Format**, its help naming the class under it), 7.5 rem for the last activity and 2 rem for the menu; the address
is the `fill` column. A list whose rows cannot be read as blocks sets `[stack]="false"`.

**Rationale:** the defects were the same in every list, so the fix belongs to the one component every list uses. The development
agent revisits top alignment if a list's controls are taller than one line of text.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-020, R-UI-065; Q-UI-306 now holds for every list. Code: [data-table.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/data-table.ts),
[_list-screens.scss](../../web/src/styles/_list-screens.scss). Style guide: [Lists](../developer/ui-style-guide.md#lists). Fix wave 2: a column marked `narrow` gives its room to the address below 64 rem
of the list's width (`--trove-list-narrow`); the repository list's Last activity is one, so the admin area's list shows about 48
characters of an address at 1280 px as at 1440 px (UI-A-30). Fix wave 4: the narrow columns and the stacked rows follow the table's
own width (the container `table`, its frame), and the address column's share is of the width of the rows without the scrollbar
beside them (Q-UI-327).

### Q-UI-311 · The start page leads the plain user to a repository and its address in two steps

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the start page (`/`, Q-UI-129) is the list of the caller's projects with key, display name, description, role and counts

### Q-UI-312 · The repository list shows the plain user the repository, format, class and address; activity and maintenance actions are the power user's

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Main columns for every kind: repository (key and description), format and class (the format with its icon and name), client address; **Last activity** only for who may change the repository; the row menu offers the plain user **Browse**, **Set up client** and **Vulnerabilities**, and adds **Settings** and **Delete** for who may change (chosen) | One layout, fewer columns for the plain user | The address column gets the plain user's room; the last activity, a maintenance fact, is where maintainers look | Two column sets of one list |
| (b) The same columns for everyone | Today's set after Q-UI-302 | One set | A column that is a dash in most rows of a reader's projects (the renders: `–` in 11 of 12 rows of `platform`) |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** a reader copies addresses and does not maintain, so the list leaves out what only maintenance uses.
The development agent revisits it if readers ask when a repository was last used.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-067, R-UI-020.

**Revised by [Q-UI-330](#q-ui-330--a-list-takes-its-columns-from-the-job-of-its-kind-of-user-the-important-properties-are-columns-and-the-address-takes-no-more-than-its-share) (2026-11-12):** a project's list is the plain user's, in the same layout for every kind (R-UI-067), so it
shows **Last activity** to nobody; it is a column of the admin area's list, the administrator's job, and a fact of the repository
page's **Details** (Q-UI-313).

### Q-UI-313 · The repository page shows the address and the setup first; its configuration facts are Details, and a reader gets no settings page

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

tab **Set up client** only), and the action **Settings** of the list opening a read-only "Repository settings" page that says "You
may use this repository but not read or change its configuration", followed by the facts, the address fields and the whole guide
of the repository's class, several screens long.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The header holds the key, the description, format and class, the client address field(s) and the primary action **Set up client**; the content tabs follow; **Details** (closed) holds the facts of the class (members of a virtual repository and its deploy target, the upstream of a remote, the layout, created, changed, last activity); **Settings** is offered only to who may change it, and the read-only settings view goes (chosen) | The address on the page the plain user opens | The common job without a tab or a second page; one place for the facts | The read-only settings view's guide moves to the setup tab and the guides, where it already is |
| (b) Keep the read-only view for readers | Today | Nothing to build | A settings page the reader cannot use, and a guide in the middle of it |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the repository page is where the list's key leads, so its first lines are the address and the
setup. The development agent revisits the facts' place if power users miss them in the header.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-067, R-UI-052, R-UI-066 (the consumer view's place of the address is the header). Built in fix wave 1:
the header with the address fields, **Set up client** as the primary action, **Settings** for who may change, **Browse files**
and **Vulnerabilities** in the header's menu, and the upstream or the members as a closed **Details** at the end of the page; the
read-only settings view is still offered (UI-A-06). Fix wave 2: the header holds the first address alone and Details the others
with their labels (Q-UI-320); the setup tab is gone (Q-UI-321); Details is the quiet disclosure (Q-UI-322).
