### Q-UI-316 · The client setup starts from where the user came, and its advanced choices are closed

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the client setup (R-UI-016) is a page of four numbered groups (package type, client, repository, credentials) followed
by the snippets; the renders show the plain user the repository list with the note "You cannot publish" on every local repository
and three credential choices.

| (b) Today's four groups | Unchanged | Every choice visible | Choices already made, and notes about publishing for a reader who cannot |

| (b) Open for power users and administrators, closed for plain users | By kind | No click for the power user | The same screen looks different by role, and a kind is per project |

### Q-UI-320 · Every value to copy of one line is a field with its joined copy button; a page shows one client address, and a panel's selects share one width

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: fix wave 2 of T-21 (the coordinator, 2026-11-12) after the renders of fix wave 1: the repository page's header and the
start page's recently opened repositories showed two address fields without a label (the client address and the address for
downloads by path, `…/files/…`), and the user could not tell which one a client needs; the install panel showed its selects each
as wide as its longest option, and its one-line command as a code block with a copy button beside it, a second look for "copy
this" next to the address field.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) An address and a command of one line are `<trove-address-field>` (the read-only input with its joined copy button); a command of several lines stays a code block with its copy button. The header of the repository page and the start page show the repository's first address only; the further ones are labelled fields in the repository page's Details. The selects of a panel stack and take the panel's width (chosen) | One look for one line to copy; one address where a client needs one | The plain user copies the one address its client takes; the second address says what it is for; the panel's controls line up | A long command scrolls inside its field instead of wrapping |
| (b) Keep Q-UI-272: a command is a code block | Two looks | A command reads as something to run | Two copy patterns on one panel, which the owner's renders called out |
| (c) Both addresses in the header, each with a label | Everything at the top | No click for the download address | The plain user chooses between two addresses at the first glance; the header grows by two lines |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** a user who copies a value should meet one control for it everywhere, and the screen that a plain user
opens for its address should hold the one its client takes. The download address is for scripts that fetch by path, a detail.
The development agent revisits the place of the download address if the walkthrough shows readers of generic repositories copy it
first.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-065 (scope), R-UI-066, R-UI-009, R-UI-052; replaces Q-UI-272 for commands of one line. Built in fix
wave 2.

### Q-UI-321 · A repository's client setup is reached one way: the header's Set up client opens the setup for the repository

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The button opens the client setup page for the repository (`/setup?repository=<project>/<key>`, Q-UI-316); the page has no tabs (chosen) | One control, one page | The same way as the start page's and the list's **Set up client**; the setup page has its **Change** and its closed options; the content needs no tab strip | The user leaves the repository page (the browser's back returns) |
| (b) Keep the tab; the button selects it | Two controls for one place | The setup stays beside the content | Two ways for one job; the tab hides the content |
| (c) Keep the tab, drop the button | The tab is the way | One control | The page's main action is no longer in the header (Q-UI-307); the start page and the list still need the page |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** a job has one way to it, and the way should be the same from every screen that offers it. The

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|

A settings page keeps `<trove-settings-section>` for its groups (chosen) | Two components, one per job | Details stay quiet below the content; a settings page keeps the headings that structure it | Two collapsible components to keep apart |
| (b) `<trove-settings-section>` everywhere, with a quiet variant | One component | One file | One component whose look depends on an input; a reader has to know which look means what |

### Q-UI-325 · The admin area's repository list names project, format and class under the key, so a 57-character address shows whole

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: UI-A-30 after fix wave 2. The measure is the owner's own address, `https://trove.k8s-main.wds18.net/api/ansible/test/galaxy/`,
57 characters: in the field's face (0.875 rem monospace, about 8.4 px a character) with its padding, border and copy button the
field needs about 537 px. The admin area's list at 1280 px is about 937 px wide (the sidebar open). With the columns repository
(16 rem), format and class (5.5 rem), Last activity (7.5 rem) and the menu (2 rem), and each column's padding, the other columns took
656 px, so the field got 281 px; fix wave 2 lets Last activity give its room below 64 rem (`narrow`), which made it 433 px.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A narrower first column there | The key column shrinks to what the address needs | The column of format and class stays | At 1280 px the field needs the others to take at most about 400 px: the key column would be 9.5 rem, and the keys and descriptions of the list wrap to three and four lines |
| (b) Drop Last activity from that list | One column less | Simple | Already gone at 1280 px since fix wave 2 (`narrow`), and still 104 px short there |
| (c) Project, format (icon and name) and class lead the line under the key; the list has no column of format and class; Last activity stays and gives its room below 64 rem (chosen) | Two columns become the key's second line | The field gets about 553 px at 1280 px and about 561 px at 1440 px, so the measure shows whole at both; the key column keeps its 16 rem | Format and class are read in the row's second line, not scanned down a column; the project's own list keeps the column |

**Choice:** (c). **Rationale:** in the admin area the address is what a row is copied for, and project, format and class describe the
repository the way its description does, so they belong under its key. Neither (a) nor (b) alone reaches the measure at 1280 px. The
development agent revisits it if administrators sort or scan the list by format, which the filter panel already narrows to.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-020, Q-UI-300 (revisit). Built in fix wave 3. Since fix wave 4 the project's own list does the same
(Q-UI-328).

**Superseded by [Q-UI-330](#q-ui-330--a-list-takes-its-columns-from-the-job-of-its-kind-of-user-the-important-properties-are-columns-and-the-address-takes-no-more-than-its-share) (2026-11-12):** the owner on the render of this list: "A huge field for copying a path that may not even
be needed gets all the room, and every other important property squeezes itself somehow into the artifact's row." The measure of
this decision, a whole address in the admin area, was the wrong one: the administrator manages repositories. Project, format and
class are columns again, and the address is a copy button in the row.

### Q-UI-326 · The admin area has one group Settings, with a page per topic: General and Authentication

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: fix wave 4 of T-21 (the coordinator, 2026-11-12). The admin area's group System listed **Settings**, which opened the
authentication settings (anonymous access, new users external, token lifetimes, the read-only status of the providers), beside
**General settings** (the public base URL, the visibility, the banner, the maintenance mode). Two entries named settings, one of
them named after the whole: an administrator looking for the banner had to guess which one holds it. The reference's admin area has one
Settings group with a page per topic.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A group **Settings** at the end of the sidebar with **General** (where `/admin/settings` leads) and **Authentication**; System keeps status, audit log and advisory sources (chosen) | One place for what is configured at runtime, a page per topic | Each entry names its topic; the pages planned for P1 (sign-in, storage) join the same group; status and logs stay apart from configuration | One more group heading |
| (b) One page **Settings** with tabs General and Authentication | One entry | Shortest sidebar | Tabs over unrelated topics with a save per section, and a tab that is not the URL's first is harder to link |
| (c) Rename the two entries in System ("Authentication settings", "General settings") | Least change | Nothing moves | Configuration stays mixed with the status and the logs, and two entries still start alike |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** an administrator looks for a setting by its topic, and one group named Settings holds every topic,
as the reference's admin area does. The development agent revisits the order when a third page joins the group.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-002 (the admin sidebar), the route table, R-UI-031, R-UI-033. Built in fix wave 4.

### Q-UI-327 · The filter panel sits beside a list only where the list keeps 71 rem, and a table's columns share its rows' width without the scrollbar

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: fix wave 4 of T-21, the owner's screen (2026-11-12, dark, about 1860 px): the admin area's repository list with the filter
panel open scrolled sideways, the address was cut and **OCI (Docker)** wrapped. Two causes, measured in Chrome with the scrollbars a
desktop with a mouse shows. (1) The address column took its share of the list's width, but a table taller than its region has a
scrollbar beside its rows that takes 15 px of that width: every list with an address scrolled 15 px sideways whenever its rows
scrolled, and the more so the narrower the list was. (2) The panel takes 20 rem beside the list from 52 rem of content width up; at
1440 px a list beside it had 49.6 rem, and the audit log (69 rem of columns), the vulnerability report (62 rem) and the admin area's
project list (54 rem) scrolled sideways, as did each list at any width between 52 rem and its columns' width plus the panel's.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The panel sits beside the list only where the list keeps at least 71 rem there (content of 91 rem and more: from about 1770 px with the sidebar open); narrower, it sits above the list, its categories side by side and its button as wide as its label; the address column's share is of the table's scroll region, which keeps the room of its scrollbar (chosen) | One threshold for every list, the width the lists are checked at | Each list keeps beside the panel at least the 70.5 rem it has at 1440 px without it, the width its columns are made for; above the panel at 1440 px the list keeps its whole width and a usual address shows whole; no list scrolls sideways because the panel is open | At 1440 px the open panel pushes the list down by about two rows of categories |
| (b) A list whose columns do not fit stacks its rows beside the panel | The panel stays on the right | No threshold | A desktop window shows the audit log and the project list as blocks; the address is cut at 16 rem in the repository lists |
| (c) The panel over the list, as a drawer | The list keeps its width | Simple layout | The panel hides the rows it filters, and the list cannot be read while the filters are set |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the lists are built and checked at 1440 px; giving each the same width beside the panel keeps that
check valid for the open panel too, and where there is not that room the list is worth more than the panel's place beside it. The
scrollbar's room is a property of the table, so the fix belongs to the data table, not to a list. The development agent revisits
the threshold when a list needs more than 71 rem at 1440 px.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-002 (list screens), Q-UI-308. Code: [_list-screens.scss](../../web/src/styles/_list-screens.scss). Built
in fix wave 4; the renders open the panel of every list that has one and measure each table at the window's first height, with
the scrollbars shown.

**Revised in the follow-up of fix wave 4 (2026-11-12):** below 91 rem the panel sat above the Filters button that opened it. It
now sits between the button and the list, and in the page's order too (toolbar, panel, list), so it opens where it was asked for
and the keyboard reaches it right after the button; a closed category is as tall as its heading. The audit log's **Action** takes
9 rem and a key longer than that breaks where it must: an action without a name of its own (`vulnerability.source.imported`)
showed its key and made the log 42 px wider than its region at 1440 px.

### Q-UI-328 · The project's repository list names format and class under the key, as the admin area's does

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: fix wave 4 of T-21, the owner's screen (2026-11-12). The project's list kept the column of format and class (5.5 rem,
Q-UI-305) when the admin area's moved them under the key (Q-UI-325). The column is the address's room: at 1860 px beside the
filter panel the address field got about 540 px of the rows' width, and wherever a list's longest address is longer than that
the table stands at its least widths, the column at 5.5 rem, so **OCI (Docker)** and **Ansible Galaxy** broke onto two lines.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Format (icon and name) and class are the line under the key in the project's list as in the admin area's, without the project (chosen) | One structure for both repository lists | The address gets the 120 px of the column: about 660 px at 1860 px beside the panel and about 560 px at 1440 px without it, so the owner's 57-character address (537 px) shows whole at both; a format name never breaks | Format and class are read in the row's second line, not scanned down a column |
| (b) Keep the column, as wide as its longest name on one line (about 7.5 rem) | Format and class stay a column | Scannable by format | The address loses another 2 rem, and the owner's address stays cut beside the panel |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the two repository lists are one screen (R-UI-020), and what Q-UI-325 found for the admin area holds
for a project once the panel is open: the address is what a row is copied for. The filter panel's **Format** and **Class** narrow
the list where a column was scanned before. The development agent revisits it with Q-UI-325.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-020, Q-UI-305, Q-UI-325. Built in fix wave 4.

**Reversed by [Q-UI-330](#q-ui-330--a-list-takes-its-columns-from-the-job-of-its-kind-of-user-the-important-properties-are-columns-and-the-address-takes-no-more-than-its-share) (2026-11-12):** format and class are columns of the project's list again, and the address field has a share
that leaves the repository its preferred 20 rem instead of the room the least widths of the others leave, so the repository,
the format and the class are not squeezed.

### Q-UI-329 · Recently opened is the start page's only: the admin area's repository list leaves it out too

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the follow-up of fix wave 4 (the coordinator, 2026-11-12). Above the admin area's repository list "Recently opened" was a

| Option | What it means | For | Against |

| (a) The admin area's list leaves it out; the start page's section is the one place (chosen) | The list starts with its header and the Filters button | One place and one look for one idea; the admin area is for managing, and a repository is found by the top bar's search or the list's filter | An administrator who reopens a repository from the admin list goes through the start page or the search |
| (b) One small style for every "Recently opened" | A small heading and a line of links above the admin list too | It stays where it was | A second look for the start page's section, and a block above every admin list that the filter does not touch |

### Q-UI-330 · A list takes its columns from the job of its kind of user; the important properties are columns, and the address takes no more than its share

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — the rule is the coordinator's (2026-11-12), after the owner's review of a render;
the columns per list are selected from the options below; the owner reviews them at the walkthrough.

Context: the owner on `admin/admin-repositories-filters-dark-1440.png` (2026-11-12): "This looks like shit. A huge field for
copying a path that may not even be needed gets all the room, and every other important property squeezes itself somehow into the
artifact's row." The coordinator: both had measured the list against the owner's earlier complaint (equal widths, the whole
address, Q-UI-300, Q-UI-325, Q-UI-328) instead of asking what the list is for. The rule from then on: each list gets its columns
from the job of its kind of user (R-UI-067), not from the address field; the most important properties get their own columns;
nothing is packed under the key except the description; the address field never takes more than its share.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Per list, its user's job: the admin area's list (manage) has **Repository**, **Project**, **Format**, **Class**, **Last activity** and a quiet copy button with the address in its name and tooltip beside the menu, which has **Copy client address** too; a project's list (find and copy) has **Repository**, **Format**, **Class**, **Client address** and the menu: the repository prefers 20 rem, format and class keep their least widths, the address field takes the rest up to the list's longest address (one width for every row, a longer address scrolling inside it), and room left over goes back to the repository; the search results (find and open) have the admin area's pattern: **Repository**, **Project**, **Format**, **Class** and the copy button, without a field. In the admin area's list and the search results the repository takes what the others leave at their least widths (chosen) | Columns from the job; the address what the properties leave | Each list is scanned column by column for what its user decides on; the repository gets the most room where the user manages; where the user copies, the address gets every pixel the properties do not need and no more than its whole length; room is left for **Visibility** (T-18) | The admin area copies an address with one click more than a field's text selection; at 1440 px a long address scrolls in a project's field |
| (b) One set of columns for both lists, the address field with its share in the admin area too | One layout | One template | The administrator's list spends 480 px at 1440 px on a value it rarely needs, and the visibility column will not fit |
| (c) As after Q-UI-325 and Q-UI-328 | Properties under the key, the address takes the rest | Whole addresses | The owner's verdict on the render |

**Choice:** (a). Measured on the renders and in Chromium with the scrollbars shown, at 1440 px: the admin area's list gives the
repository 449 px, project 136, format 160, class 112, last activity 152 and the two row buttons 104; at 1920 px beside the open
filter panel the repository gets 609 px. A project's list gives the repository 352 px (its 20 rem), format 160, class 112, the
menu 64 and the address field the rest, an input of 362 px (40 characters) at 1440 px; at 1920 px beside the open panel the input
is 522 px (59 characters, so the owner's 57-character address shows whole), and at 1920 px without the panel 836 px, the seed's
longest address of 96 characters whole. The search results give the repository 641 px at 1440 px and 1121 px at 1920 px,
project 136, format 160, class 112 and the copy button 64 (measured at 1920, 1440 and 390 px). No repository list
scrolls sideways at 1920, 1440, 1280, 1170 to 1090 or 390 px, with the panel open or closed. The least widths: repository 14 rem
in the admin area and the search results, 13 rem in a project, project 6.5 rem, format 8 rem (**Ansible Galaxy** with its icon on
one line), class 5 rem, last activity 7.5 rem (gone below 64 rem of the list), the address field 10 rem (its input keeps 8 rem).
The repository lists' least widths sum to 48 rem, the search results' to 45.5 rem; they stack below 48 rem and 1 rem for a
scrollbar beside the rows. A project's list shows no last activity any more (Q-UI-312).

**Rationale:** a list is read across its rows for the properties its user decides on, so they need columns, and the column that
names the thing gets the room where the user manages. Where the user copies, the address is the list's main value: it takes what
the properties leave, up to its whole length, and nothing it does not need. The development agent revisits the repository's 20 rem
if the walkthrough shows that readers cannot tell addresses apart at 1440 px, and the repository's least width when
**Visibility** joins the admin area's list.

**Revised in the follow-up (the coordinator, 2026-11-12):** the first version capped the field at 46 characters in every list.
At 1920 px beside the open panel the repository column of a project's list was mostly empty (most keys are short) while every
address was cut at 46 characters, although the room was there: the cap was as rigid as the room-taking it replaced. A column now
`prefer`s a width (the data table counts it in `--trove-list-others` and gives it what is left over, every other column keeps its
width), and the list sets the address's share to its longest address.

**Revised in the second follow-up (the coordinator, 2026-11-12), a third case: the search results.** With the project list's rule
the search results at 1440 px gave the address field 31 characters, `https://localhost:4200/api/npm/` on every row, so the field
showed nothing that told the rows apart; with a real host (`https://trove.k8s-main.wds18.net/`, 32 characters before the path) it
would be the same. Judged by purpose: who searches wants to find a repository and open it, and copying is secondary there. So the
search results take the admin area's pattern: **Repository** (key and description), **Project**, **Format**, **Class**, and the
quiet copy button whose name and tooltip carry the address, alone at the end of the row because a result has no menu; no
address field. The repository `prefer`s its least width, so it takes every pixel the others leave and project, format and class
read as tight columns.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-020, R-UI-065, R-UI-066, Q-UI-300, Q-UI-301, Q-UI-302, Q-UI-303, Q-UI-304, Q-UI-305, Q-UI-306,
Q-UI-312, Q-UI-325, Q-UI-328. Code: [repository-list.html](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/repository-list.html),
[search-results.ts](../../web/src/app/features/search/search-results.ts), `prefer` in
[data-table.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/data-table.ts), `td.address-cell`, `td.format-cell` and `td.class-cell` in
[_list-screens.scss](../../web/src/styles/_list-screens.scss). Style guide:
[Lists](../developer/ui-style-guide.md#lists), [Address field](../developer/ui-style-guide.md#address-field).

### Q-UI-331 · An endpoint's rules are the shared data table, and a rule's client address is the row's copy button

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: B4's renders of 2026-11-12. The endpoint page's rule table was a table of its own with eight columns, among them an address
field: with a single rule it scrolled 19 px sideways at 1440 px and 512 px at 390 px. The coordinator: move it to the shared data
table, with a column budget and the stacked row. A rule list is the administrator's (R-UI-067): what each rule exposes and whether
it is on; the address is handed to the consumers now and then.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The shared data table with the admin area's pattern of Q-UI-330: **Rule** (name and description; it takes what the others leave), **Repository**, **Packages and paths**, **Versions**, **Pre-releases**, **Enabled**, and the row's copy button (its name and tooltip the address) beside a menu with **Edit**, **Copy client address** and **Delete**; **Versions** and **Pre-releases** are `narrow` (chosen) | Seven columns, least widths 63 rem; below 64 rem 47 rem | Every property the administrator decides on is a column; the list fits 1440 px and stacks on a phone; the rows act like every other list's | The address is read in the tooltip, not in a field |
| (b) The data table with the address field (`fill`) | The field as in a project's repository list | The address readable in the row | With six property columns the field's least width makes the list wider than 1440 px; the rule would get the least room |
| (c) Fewer columns: packages, versions and pre-releases as one line of facts | Five columns | Room for the field | Three properties packed into one cell, which Q-UI-330 forbids |

**Choice:** (a). Least widths: rule 9 rem, repository 9 (`web-frontend/assets` on one line), packages and paths 8, versions 6, pre-releases 6, enabled 6.5, the row's
two buttons 4.5; with the padding 63 rem, so the list fits from 64 rem; below 64 rem versions and pre-releases give their room and
the rest is 47 rem, so the list fits until it stacks. Where the endpoint does not serve the rule's address, a warning glyph named by
that sentence stands in place of the copy button and the menu offers no copy.

**Rationale:** the page is where an administrator decides what an endpoint exposes, so the rules' properties get the columns; the
address is a value to hand out, and one click on the row's button copies it. The development agent revisits it if the walkthrough
shows that administrators read the addresses on this page.

**Applied in the spec:** [endpoints.md](endpoints.md) R-EP-017, R-UI-066. Code:
[endpoint-detail.html](../../web/src/app/features/endpoints/endpoint-detail.html).

### Q-UI-332 · A token list shows token, scope, expiry, last use and its action; created and created via give way first

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the coordinator's look at the renders (2026-11-12): once the render seed gave the plain user a token, the token table on
an administrator's user page scrolled 107 px sideways at 1440 px: nine columns (description, type, scope, created, expires, last
used, created via, state, actions) without a column budget inside the 56 rem of the page. The same table is the profile's, a
service account's and the token administration's. Who reads a token list decides which token to keep or revoke (Q-UI-330).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) **Token** (description and the hint, which names the type: `trv_pat_…`), **Scope**, **Expires**, **Last used** and at the row's end **Revoke** with a quiet **Rotate** icon where the caller may rotate, or the state of a token that is no longer active; **Created** and **Created via** are `narrow` in an owner's list; the token administration adds **Owner** and the selection and stacks below 64 rem (chosen) | Five columns that decide, two that give way first | No column repeats what another says (the type is in the hint, "Active" is the default filter); every list fits its width or stacks; the action is where the eye ends | **Created** and **Created via** are not visible on a page narrower than 64 rem; **Rotate** is an icon with its name and tooltip |
| (b) The nine columns with least widths | Nothing dropped | Every fact visible | 74 rem of columns: no page shows them without scrolling |
| (c) Details of a row behind a disclosure | Fewer columns | Room | A second click for the facts of every token, and a pattern no other list has |

**Choice:** (a). Least widths: token 8.5 rem (it takes what the others leave), owner 7, scope 9, expires 6.5, last used 6.5,
created 6.5 and created via 5 (`narrow`), the actions 7, the selection 2. An owner's list sums to 47.5 rem, with the narrow columns
to 63 rem; the token administration's to 60.5 rem, so it stacks below 64 rem (`stackWide`). A date shows the day, its `title` the
time.

**Rationale:** the facts that decide whether a token stays are its scope, its expiry and its last use; when and how it was made
explain it and can wait for a wider window. The development agent revisits it if the walkthrough shows that administrators sort
or scan the token administration by creation.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-029, R-UI-030. Code: [token-table.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/access/token-table.ts).

### Q-UI-333 · A page's sections are quiet disclosures, Tokens too, open while there is a token; the profile follows

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the coordinator's look at `admin/admin-user-advanced-advanced-light-1440.png` (2026-11-12): on an administrator's user page
**Tokens** was a large heading over an always-open list, while every other section (Details, Identities, Groups, System roles,
Sessions, Advanced) was a quiet disclosure; a service account's page had the same. The profile was a stack of cards with large
headings and a key-value list, a third pattern.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) **Tokens** is a quiet disclosure like its siblings, open while the owner holds a token; the profile becomes one column: the avatar without a card, the identity as read-only fields, then the quiet sections **Preferences** (open), **Groups** (open while the group claim notice stands) and **System roles** (chosen) | One section style on every page of a person or an account | The pages read alike; a list that has entries is open, an empty one says so in one closed line | The tokens of a user are one click away when there are none |
| (b) The always-open lists of a page under one heading style | Large headings for lists, disclosures for the rest | Lists always in view | Two section styles on one page, which is the finding |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the settings rule of the style guide (one column, quiet sections) is the app's one pattern for the
page of one thing; a section with entries opens by itself, so nothing the reader came for is hidden. The development agent revisits
the open state of **Preferences** if the walkthrough shows that users rather see their groups first.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-024, R-UI-029; R-UI-026 (the service account page). Code:

### Q-UI-334 · A picker is one control from the start, held while its list loads, and a field is as wide as its kind of input

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the coordinator's look at the CI mapping editor (2026-11-12): **Add a policy** was a text field until the editor had read
the whole policy list (paged, 100 per page) and then turned into a select; a user who started typing lost the field. The project's
issuer select showed its first issuer while the form held none, so a project with one issuer could not be saved without choosing
it again. And on `plain/profile-dark-1440.png` the **Language** and **Theme** selects of Preferences differed in width, each as wide
as its longest option; every select of the app did the same.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The policy and group pickers are one text field with suggestions (`datalist`) and **Add** from the start, disabled and saying "Loading policies…" while the list loads; a select that loads its options (issuer, project, repository) is the same select, disabled, its one option saying so (chosen) | One control, one type in every state | A long list stays usable by typing; the suggestions are the platform's; a list that cannot be read leaves the same field for typed names, as before | A suggestion list is less visible than a select's open list |
| (b) A select from the start, disabled while loading | One type, the list in full view | Every policy is one click away | Hundreds of policies in one select; a failed read leaves no way to name one |
| (c) A custom ARIA combobox with a listbox | Full control of the suggestions | Styled suggestions | A widget to build and test for a field the platform already offers; the version field and the claim names use `datalist` too |

For the widths:

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The five widths of the T-21b plan (`field-w-number`, `-duration`, `-bytes`, `-name`, `-full`, tokens `--trove-field-width-*`), every select and picker `name` unless its place fills a line (chosen) | One set for the app, by kind of input | The selects of a column line up; the repository forms of T-21b take the same set, so there are never two | A select with long options (the mapping editor's **Pipelines from other projects**) shows the start of its choice in a closed state |
| (b) Small, medium, large by content length | Three sizes for selects alone | Fits each select closer | A second set of widths next to the plan's, which the plan forbids |
| (c) Every select the width of its column | No classes | Lines up | A two-word choice across the whole page |

**Choice:** (a) and (a). **Rationale:** a control that changes its kind under the user's hands is the finding; the loading state is
the cheapest honest state. The widths are the plan's because consistency across screens is the point and T-21b's repository forms
use the same names. The development agent revisits a select whose closed text the renders show to lose its meaning: it becomes
`full`, not a sixth width.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-035; ui-style-guide.md (Forms). Code:
[name-picker.ts](../../web/src/app/features/ci/name-picker.ts),
[mapping-editor.ts](../../web/src/app/features/ci/mapping-editor.ts),
[claim-tester.ts](../../web/src/app/features/ci/claim-tester.ts),

[repository-wizard.html](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/repository-wizard.html),
[exposure-rule-editor.html](../../web/src/app/features/endpoints/exposure-rule-editor.html),
[_controls.scss](../../web/src/styles/_controls.scss).

### Q-UI-335 · Every text field names the width of its expected input, and a number field is never the column

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the coordinator's look at `admin/project-ci-mapping-new-dark-1440.png` (2026-11-12): **Priority** (a small number) and
**Maximum token lifetime (seconds)** each spanned about 700 px, against the owner's rule of the day that a field for a period in
seconds need not offer room for billions. Q-UI-334 had given the selects their width; every text field still took its column.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `<trove-text-field>` must name its `width` (a required input), a raw input of a form carries the class, the schema-driven settings derive it (`widthOf`), and a lint check fails a number field without a number width (chosen) | The five widths of Q-UI-334 on every field, by the kind of its expected input | The compiler refuses a text field without a width, so a new field is decided where it is written; the check keeps raw number inputs honest | Every text area says `full` |
| (b) A default width (`full` or `name`) with exceptions | Fewer attributes | Short templates | A forgotten field silently takes the default, which is how the finding arose |
| (c) Width by `type` alone | `number` → number width | Automatic | A period in seconds is not a count, and an ID of nineteen digits is neither |

**Choice:** (a). The kinds: a count, a priority, a port or a limit `number`; seconds, a TTL, a period in days `duration`; a byte
count, an ID of up to nineteen digits (a GitLab pipeline or job ID) and a date `bytes`, the nearest width that holds a date and
its picker; a key, a name, a login, an email address or a principal `name`; a URL, a description, a path, a pattern and every list
or text area `full`. A filter panel and a search row give their fields their own width. Read-only fields that show a record (the
profile's identity, an issuer's or an endpoint's configuration) take the width of their value the same way. A schema member's
width comes from its name and schema, since a schema states no unit: `…Seconds`, `…Ttl`, `…Interval`, `…Timeout` a duration,
`…Bytes`, `…Size` bytes, any other number a count, a URL or a string longer than 128 characters the column, any other string a
name; a URL (`format: uri`, or a pattern that starts with the scheme) is one line, never a text area. A field and the button that
acts on it share a row, the button level with the control.

**Rationale:** the finding was a default nobody chose; a required width moves the choice to the place that knows the input. The
development agent revisits a width whose renders cut a common value, by moving the field to the next width, not by a sixth one.

**Applied in the spec:** ui-style-guide.md (Forms). Code: [fields.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/access/fields.ts),
[settings-schema.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/settings-schema.ts),
[mirror-settings.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/mirror-settings.ts),
[field-width-rule.mjs](../../web/scripts/field-width-rule.mjs).

### Q-UI-370 · The grades take cogpit's colours, and S, A and B are the greens of a good grade

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the owner asked for the grades "as we realised it in cogpit"; cogpit's scale runs from a deep teal (S) through green
(A), mint (B), amber (C) and orange (D) to red (E), the same in both of its themes, with a quiet grey for N/A. trove's rule is
that green means a positive status only (Q-UI-96).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) cogpit's colours, as tokens with the same value in both schemes for S to E and a grey per scheme for N/A; S, A and B are allowed to be green (chosen) | The palette test admits the three grade tokens and their rim and ink beside the positive status | The grade looks as the owner knows it; S, A and B are the good end of the scale, so their green is a positive status in Q-UI-96's sense; the letter and the text carry the grade, never the colour alone | Three more greens in the palette |
| (b) cogpit's scale without green: S to B in blue or grey | Q-UI-96 untouched | No exception | Not what the owner asked for; a blue S reads as a link or a selection |
| (c) trove's status colours | Positive, warning, error | Fewer tokens | Three colours for seven grades; C and D look the same |

**Choice:** (a). The bar takes cogpit's severity colours as well; its High is one step deeper than cogpit's (`#c9302a` for
`#d9403a`) so that its white count keeps 4.5:1. **Rationale:** the owner's reference, inside the rule's intent: green still means
"good". The development agent revisits (b) if the owner wants green kept for the status badge alone. **Applied in the spec:**
R-UI-090, R-UI-092; [design-language.md](../developer/design-language.md), `palette.spec.ts`, `_tokens.scss`.

### Q-UI-371 · The shield is an inline SVG whose letter is text, and it is decorative beside its text

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Inline SVG: the crest as a path, the letter as `<text>`, colours from the tokens (chosen) | One component draws every size | Sharp at 16 and 32 px and on any screen density; the scheme's tokens apply; the letter is text in the page's face | A gradient per shield needs its own ID |
| (b) Seven image files | A picture per grade | Simple markup | Two schemes and two sizes mean 28 files, and a token change means new pictures |
| (c) A Material icon (`shield`) with a letter over it | No new shape | One glyph | Not cogpit's crest; the letter does not sit on the icon's optical centre |

**Choice:** (a). Beside its text the shield is `aria-hidden`, so a screen reader hears the grade once; alone it is an image named
**Grade E**. **Rationale:** the owner's shape at every size from one source. The development agent records no revisit condition.
**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-090.

### Q-UI-372 · The bar's segments are as wide as their share, with room for their number

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) cogpit's layout: each segment its number's room first, the rest shared by the shares, each at least 7 % (chosen) | A flex item per segment, `flex: <share> 1 auto` | A count always fits; 843 Unknown is visibly the largest; the bar is as wide as its place | A segment of 1 among 1,000 is wider than its share |
| (b) Strictly proportional | Width = share | Exact | 13 of 1,145 is 1 %: its number does not fit |
| (c) Five equal segments | A table of five counts | Simple | Loses what the bar is for |

**Choice:** (a). A severity without findings stays in the bar, faint, so that the five positions never move. **Rationale:** the
owner's pick in cogpit's lab ("Anteilig"). The development agent records no revisit condition. **Applied in the spec:** R-UI-092.

### Q-UI-380 · The report's list fits at 1440 px: the project is the link of the qualified name, and Fixed in gives way below 64 rem

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

added up to more than the list's 1,128 px; the dashboard had a column **Project** beside **Repository**, whose qualified name names the
project already.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The shared budget (Q-UI-308): the identifier is the name column (14 rem); the qualified name breaks only after its slash; the dashboard's project is the link of the qualified name's first part, which narrows the list as the column's link did; the headers **Package** and **Fixed in** are as short as their cells; **Fixed in** is `narrow` and gives way below 64 rem of the list; the time of **Detected**, which the list sorts by, may wrap; a status's reason may go to a second line (chosen) | The list fits its width at 1440 px and gives way where it is narrower | No sideways scroll at 1440 px; the project is still one click; nothing is lost but a repeated name | The dashboard loses its column **Project** (Q-UI-165); between 64 rem and the width where the rows stack a list with long names can still scroll a little |
| (b) Keep the columns and let the list scroll inside its region | Nothing changes | The column stays | The defect stays |
| (c) Stack the rows from a wider width | The rows become blocks earlier | No column dropped | A list of findings is read as a table; blocks at 1440 px are not a table |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the qualified name `<project>/<repository>` is how trove names a repository outside its project ([Q-REPO-212](repositories-and-proxy.md#q-repo-212--a-repository-is-addressed-inside-its-project-and-no-repository-is-shared)), so a
column that repeats its first part costs the room without adding a fact. The development agent revisits the column if the owner wants
the project as a column of its own. **Applied in the spec:** R-VULN-022 (List, Instance-wide); [Q-UI-165](#q-ui-165--the-security-dashboard-is-the-content-report-mounted-in-the-admin-area-with-its-own-links-project-column-and-search)'s column is replaced by the link.

### Q-UI-390 · Enter in the top bar's search opens a results page of the main area; no search leads into the admin area

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the owner typed "test" into the top bar's field **Find a repository** and pressed Enter, and landed on the admin area's
repository list (`/admin/repositories?q=test`, `submitSearch` of [app.ts](../../web/src/app/app.ts)). His rule of 2026-11-12
([CLAUDE.md](../../CLAUDE.md#product-simple-by-default-details-on-demand)): "A search from the main area ends in the main area. Only a
live suggestion that is marked as a page of the admin area, and shown only to an instance administrator, may lead there." The search
with live suggestions for every reader is the owner's task T-22 ([promt.md](../projektplan/promt.md#owner-task-of-2026-11-12-for-later-a-search-with-suggestions)),
planned now and built after T-18; this is the stopgap until then. The field was shown only with `repositories:read-config`, on the
belief that readers had no list across projects; the list `GET /api/v1/repositories` is open to every caller and filtered by `read`
([repositories_api.go](../../internal/api/v1/repositories_api.go), `visibleRepositories`; found by the planner of T-22).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Enter opens `/search?q=<text>`, a page of the main shell: the matching repositories from the same API (`GET /api/v1/repositories?q=`), each with its key and description, its project, format and class and its client address, the key a link to the repository's page in its project; and a link to the start page's package search for the same text (chosen) | One results page in the main area | The rule holds: nothing on the page leads into `/admin`; the reader sees the repositories in the shared list layout and goes on in their projects; every signed-in user gets the field, because the list answers each caller with what it may read | A page T-22 will extend |
| (b) Enter opens the repository list of the caller's project | The project's own list | A page that exists | The search spans every project; one project's list would drop the others' matches |
| (c) Remove Enter until T-22 | The field does nothing | Nothing leads anywhere wrong | A search field that ignores Enter |

**Choice:** (a). The field is shown to every signed-in user (R-UI-002) instead of only to a holder of `repositories:read-config`;
an anonymous visitor gets it with T-22. The page's address is `/search?q=<text>`, which T-22's results page
(R-UI-098 in [its plan](../projektplan/search-work-packages.md)) extends by
`kind` and tabs. The field offers no suggestions of its own while
typing (no `datalist`, no list of trove's): what a browser may offer is its own form history, which `autocomplete="off"` asks it to
leave out. The start page's package search takes its text from the address (`/projects?find=<text>`), so that the results page can
hand the text over. **Rationale:** the owner's rule, with the least that makes Enter useful until T-22. The development agent revisits
nothing: T-22 extends the page. **Applied in the spec:** R-UI-002; [search-results.ts](../../web/src/app/features/search/search-results.ts).
Revisited by T-22 ([Q-UI-415](#q-ui-415--the-stopgaps-results-page-becomes-r-ui-098s)): the page becomes R-UI-098's, with
`kind` and the tabs Repositories, Packages and Projects; the link to the start page's package search goes with that search
([Q-UI-414](#q-ui-414--the-start-pages-package-search-goes-the-top-bars-field-is-the-one-search)); the field offers suggestions
(R-UI-096, R-UI-097) and shows for an anonymous caller while something is `public`
([Q-UI-400](#q-ui-400--every-signed-in-caller-gets-the-field-and-an-anonymous-one-while-something-is-public)).

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: a stacked list (Q-UI-306, Q-UI-308) kept its head for assistive technology only, clipped to one pixel, so its sort

pipeline of `e2e (vuln)`, 2026-11-12). The same held for every sortable list on a phone. Since Q-UI-327's revision the panel sits
above a list below 91 rem of the content area, so the report keeps its width at 1280 px; a phone still stacks every list.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The head of a stacked list shows its sortable headers as one wrapping row of sort buttons above the blocks, each with its arrow; a header that sorts nothing stays for assistive technology only (chosen) | The headers with `aria-sort` stay visible; the data table and the rows are unchanged | Sorting works at every width, with the same buttons and the same `aria-sort`; one rule in the data table's styles for every list | One row more above a stacked list |
| (b) A sort select above a stacked list | A second control for the same order | The reference's look on a phone | Two controls for one state, kept in step; a new component |
| (c) Narrow the report until it fits beside the panel | Fewer or narrower columns | The report stays a table at 1280 px | Every other sortable list still loses sorting when it stacks |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the defect is the shared rule's, so the fix is the shared rule's; the buttons a reader sorts with
on a wide screen are the ones on a narrow one. The development agent revisits a select if the owner wants the reference's form
on a phone. **Applied in the spec:** R-UI-002 (List screens). Code: [_list-screens.scss](../../web/src/styles/_list-screens.scss) (Stacked rows).
The renders' screen `vulnerabilities-filtered` sorts the report by **Detected** at every width, at 390 px in its stacked rows, and
fails where the button cannot be clicked.

### Q-UI-394 · The runs of an advisory source that is off stay on the screen, disabled, with the setting that turns it on

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

visible and says why ("A disabled option stays visible, muted, and says why"; a disabled destructive action says why next to it),
and the app's pattern for a control the user cannot use is a disabled button described by the reason next to it
(`aria-describedby`, the own account's **Disable** and **Delete**).

|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Disabled, with a muted sentence under the buttons that names the source as off and the setting that turns it on, tied to each of its buttons by `aria-describedby` (chosen) | `vulnerabilities.sources.kev.mode`, `vulnerabilities.sources.osv.mode` | The style guide's rule for an unavailable choice; the administrator learns where the switch is; a screen reader reads the reason on the button | One sentence more while a source is off |
| (b) Not offered | The button leaves while the source is off | Nothing on the screen that cannot be used | The way to turn the source on is not on the screen; the table's **Off** is the only trace |

[vulnerability-sources.ts](../../web/src/app/features/vulnerabilities/vulnerability-sources.ts).

### Q-API-246 · An operation that is allowed while the installation is read-only declares `x-trove-maintenance: allowed`

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context and options are those of [Q-OPS-208](operations-and-observability.md#q-ops-208--the-read-only-mode-is-refused-at-four-places-by-a-default-of-refusal-and-the-banner-write-is-refused-with-the-rest); this block fixes the contract of the document.

**Choice:** the member `x-trove-maintenance` of an operation has the single value `allowed`, is valid only on a method other than GET, HEAD and OPTIONS (the document refuses it elsewhere), and is read into `Operation.MaintenanceAllowed`. The `info.description` of the document states the rule. `GET /api/v1/system/banner` is `public`, `GET /api/v1/system/maintenance` is `authenticated`, both `PUT` operations need `settings:write`. `422` is documented on both `PUT`s.

**Rationale:** the document is the one place that already says, per operation, who may call it (R-API-008), so what stays callable in maintenance belongs next to it. The development agent would revisit the single value if an operation needs "allowed for administrators only".

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-008 (declarations), R-API-037 (the two rows of the settings index now exist). Code: [document.go](../../internal/api/v1/document.go). Tests: `TestR_OPS_024_MaintenanceDeclarationIsValidated`, `TestR_OPS_024_OperationsAllowedInMaintenanceMode`.

| (b) A handler check only | The handler asks the wiki | No document change | Nothing says which operation is wiki; a new operation can forget it |

**Rationale:** R-API-008 puts every operation's authorization in the document; the part of a read is part of it. The development

### Q-API-249 · The project list and the project read are open operations that decide in the handler

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `x-trove-permission: public: true`; the handler lists what the caller's level admits, its memberships and, with `projects:read`, every project; a project it may not see is 404 (chosen) | As `listRepositories` does | One place decides who sees a project; an anonymous caller gets the public projects while a public repository exists and 401 before | The declaration does not tell the rule; the description of the operation does |
| (b) Keep the declaration (`projects:read` or a member) and add a second path for the levels | Two decisions | The declaration is still the rule | A project that a level admits would be reachable by two paths with two answers |

**Choice:** (a). `membership=true` keeps the caller's memberships. A caller without a credential gets 401 while no repository's artifacts
are `public` (the gate of the repository list), and 404 for a project it may not see, as an unknown project answers.

**Rationale:** R-AUTHZ-035 rule 8 makes the level part of who sees a project, and the declaration language has no level.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-047, R-API-057; `listProjects` and `getProject` in `api/openapi.yaml`.

### Q-API-250 · The ETag of the visibility settings is a version of their own row

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `visibility_settings.version`, moved by every change of the default (chosen) | The tag of `GET` is the version; `PATCH` compares it | Stable across replicas, moves only with the default; `publicObjects` is read-only and changes with other writes without moving the tag | One more column |
| (b) A digest of the answer | The tag follows `publicObjects` as well | No column | A `PATCH` fails with 412 whenever any project changes its level |

**Choice:** (a), migration `00073_visibility.sql`. A merge patch without `defaultLevel`, or with the level the installation has,
changes nothing and records nothing, and is still compared with `If-Match`.

**Rationale:** the tag protects the one value the operation writes.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-056, R-AUTHZ-033 data model.

### Q-UI-400 · Every signed-in caller gets the field, and an anonymous one while something is public

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Every signed-in caller, and the anonymous UI (chosen) | The field wherever the shell runs | The owner asked for one search for every user; the anonymous UI exists only while `publicContent`, and the API answers what `public` admits | Anonymous typing spends the `anonymous` class of a client address (bounded by Q-UI-408) |
| (b) Signed-in callers only | No anonymous search | No anonymous load | A visitor of public content finds it only through the project list |
| (c) Only callers that can read something | A probe before the field shows | No empty answers | A request on every screen; an empty answer is a valid answer |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the field is how a reader finds content, and the anonymous visitor of public content is a reader.
The development agent revisits it if the field shows up in `trove_api_rate_limited_total{class="anonymous"}`.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-095.

### Q-UI-401 · Slash focuses the field and is on by default; the preference turns it off

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `/` on by default, off in the profile; Ctrl+K and ⌘K always; an anonymous caller Ctrl+K and ⌘K only (chosen) | The reference's key works at once | The owner asked for the reference's search; WCAG 2.1.4 is met by a way to turn the shortcut off, and the key never acts in a text field | A default that R-UI-044 had the other way |
| (b) `/` only after the user turned shortcuts on (R-UI-015 as written) | Off by default | No surprise for a speech-input user | Hardly anyone finds the preference; the key the owner knows does nothing |
| (c) `/` always | No switch | Simple | Fails WCAG 2.1.4 |

**Choice:** (a). An anonymous caller has no preference to turn `/` off, so it gets the chorded keys only. **Rationale:** 2.1.4
accepts a mechanism that turns a single-key shortcut off, and the preference exists already. The development agent revisits it if a
speech-input or screen-reader user reports the key.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-095, R-UI-044, R-API-021 (Q-API-280).

### Q-UI-405 · "Frequently visited" is kept in the browser, per principal, by visits and recency

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Browser storage per principal ID, ordered by visits halved every 14 days; one store for the recent lists too (chosen) | Per browser | Privacy: the server keeps no record of which repositories a person opens, and nothing to back up, restore or delete when a user leaves; no write per page view against the `write` class (10/s) and the database; no request to show it | A second device starts empty; whoever can read the browser profile reads the names (H-987) |
| (b) A server table of visits per user | Across devices | Follows the user | A navigation history of every user on the server; a write per page view; filtered by read on every use anyway |
| (c) The browser, by recency only (today's recent lists) | Last opened | Nothing new | "Frequently" means more than "last" |

**Choice:** (a). The store replaces `trove.recent-repositories`, which is one key for every user of a browser, and
`trove.recent-projects.<name>`. **Rationale:** the list is a convenience, and a convenience does not justify a record of what people
open. As the owner's brief describes the reference, it keeps the list in the browser too (not checked against its current version).
The development agent revisits it if the owner wants the list on every device.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-096.

### Q-API-281 · The suggestions use the `read` and `anonymous` classes, and `q` is 2 to 100 characters

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The existing classes; `q` of 2 to 100 characters (chosen) | No new budget | The field keeps itself at 8 % of `read` (Q-UI-408); 100 is more than the longest qualified name (32 + 1 + 64) | — |
| (b) A class `search` of its own | A second budget | Isolated | A second budget per principal that a client can spend in parallel |
| (c) No length rule | Any text | Flexible | One character matches almost everything; very long texts cost without use |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the classes exist to bound every read the same way. The development agent revisits (b) if searches
starve the screens.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-060.

## What this does not cover


### Q-UI-240 · An Ansible package has a Documentation tab and a Contents tab; the README tab is its first page

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: task T-19. The owner's galaxy_ng shows, per collection version: Install (description, license, install command, download, requires Ansible), Documentation (search and tree), Contents, Import log, Dependencies, Distributions, and the links Docs site, Website, Issue tracker, Repo. trove's package page (R-UI-007) already has an install panel, a Metadata tab (authors, license, `requires_ansible`, dependencies, links), Files, Repositories and All versions.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) For the format `ansible`: tabs **Documentation** (replaces README), **Contents**, Metadata, Files, Repositories, All versions, and **Import log** on a local repository (chosen) | Install = the install panel, Dependencies = a section of Metadata with links to the packages, Distributions = the Repositories tab, the links = the Metadata tab | Nothing exists twice; the page keeps the layout of the other formats; the new tabs are exactly what trove lacks | Dependencies is not a tab of its own, which the reference has |
| (b) Mirror the reference's tab names one by one | Install, Documentation, Contents, Import log, Dependencies, Distributions | Familiar | An Install tab duplicates the sticky install panel; Distributions duplicates Repositories; the layout of R-UI-007 is a decision of the owner (Q-UI-3) |
| (c) Documentation only | No Contents tab | Smaller | The flat list "what is in this collection" is one click in the reference and cheap here (the tree's data) |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the tabs of the reference that hold information trove does not show yet are Documentation, Contents and the Import log; the rest are shown already, by the
install panel, the Metadata tab and the Repositories tab. **Documentation** is shown when `metadata.docs.state` is not `none` or the version has a README, and is the default tab
then (as README is elsewhere); its first page is the README. **Contents** is a data table (name, type, short description, a link to the page where `hasDocs`), a type filter, and
the count in its tab as a neutral badge; shown with the Documentation tab. **Import log** (local only) lists the import task of this version through `listAnsibleImportTasks`, extended by the optional query
parameters `package` and `version` (the tasks are readable by whoever reads the repository, R-ANS-009), newest first, state as a badge and the messages as text. All tabs are `<trove-tab-group>`
lazy tabs in GitLab's strip (design-language.md, Controls). A `404` of the documentation operations removes the tab without an error message (Q-UI-244). Dependencies is a section of the Metadata tab and the links of the reference are its links ([Q-UI-245](#q-ui-245--dependencies-and-the-links-of-the-reference-are-sections-of-the-metadata-tab-not-tabs-the-documentation-link-is-called-docs-site)). Revisit at the walkthrough.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-007 (the tab list for the format), R-UI-060 to R-UI-064, [R-ANS-026](formats/ansible.md#r-ans-026--package-screens-and-the-deploy-dialog), [R-ANS-036](formats/ansible.md#r-ans-036--the-documentation-operations-of-the-screens-their-rendering-and-the-search).

### Q-UI-241 · The Documentation tab is the file browser's two panes: a tree with a search field, and the page

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Two panes as the file browser (Q-UI-98): the tree pane (`clamp(18rem, 30%, 26rem)`) with the search field in its head, the page pane taking the rest (chosen) | The pattern of design-language.md "two panes" | Already built, specified and in the GitLab style (the wiki sidebar has this shape); each pane scrolls on its own; narrow widths show one pane with a back button | A tab inside a page that has its own two columns (tabs left, install panel right, R-UI-007): the content column is narrower |
| (b) A tree above the page | One column | Simple | The page scrolls away from the tree on long module pages |
| (c) A separate route for the documentation | `/packages/ansible/<name>/docs` | Full width | The page leaves the package page; the version selector and the install panel are lost |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the pattern exists and the owner chose it for hierarchies (design-language.md). The tree's rows are 32 px: the first row is **Documentation** (the README, the other
Markdown files below it as children), then the groups **Modules (8)**, **Plugins (24)** (children by type, each type collapsed at first with its count, expanded when it holds the current page or a search match) and **Roles (n)**, as the reference's
tree is, each group with its count as a neutral badge; an entry is a row with its name (the short description as the tooltip); an entry with `hasDocs` false is muted and labelled "no documentation". The selected row is
`--trove-accent-container`. The page is addressed by the query parameter `doc` of the package URL (`doc=README.md`, `doc=module/check_host_reachable`, `doc=file/install.md`), so a link, reload and back button work, and the tree follows it.
Under 48 rem of content width one pane shows at a time. The tree is a `role="tree"` of links (`aria-current="page"` on the open one), reachable by keyboard; it takes the width of the content container query, not of the viewport (the package
page is two columns from 960 px). Revisit if the owner finds the tab too narrow beside the install panel (then the install panel moves above the tabs for this tab).

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-007, [R-ANS-036](formats/ansible.md#r-ans-036--the-documentation-operations-of-the-screens-their-rendering-and-the-search).

### Q-UI-242 · An entry page shows the plugin's documentation in the order ansible-doc prints it, from the structured answer

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A page head (full name with a copy button, short description, "added in", a deprecation notice), then the sections Synopsis, Parameters, Notes, Requirements, Attributes, See also, Examples, Return values, Authors, each only when it has content (chosen) | The structure of the answer of R-ANS-036 | Familiar to anyone who has read ansible-doc; a section appears only with content; prose is the server's sanitized HTML | A table with nested rows for suboptions is wide |
| (b) The raw `doc_strings` as formatted JSON | Whatever came | Trivial | Not documentation |
| (c) Tabs inside the page (Parameters, Examples, Return) | Fewer scrolls | Compact | A page of 59 KB (nmcli) in four tabs hides what the search matched |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** Parameters is the shared data table (no frame, hairlines): the columns are Name (with `aliases`), Type (and `elements`), Required (a text badge), Default, Choices and Description; a suboption row is
indented by its depth (16 px per level, a "suboptions of <name>" label for the screen reader) and a parameter with suboptions is collapsible with a chevron (open at first, Q-UI-252). Defaults, choices and samples are
text (typed JSON shown as written, a boolean as `true`/`false`). Examples and a sample are a `<pre>` in the same code block control as the README's, scrolling horizontally, with a copy button; there is no highlighting. A deprecated plugin
shows a `warn` badge. A role shows its README only. A page whose entry has `hasDocs` false shows the head and the line "This plugin has no documentation in its source." (generated) or "The upstream sent no documentation for this plugin." (upstream).
Below the page, one muted line says where the documentation comes from ("Generated by trove from the archive, 2026-11-11 09:41" or "Taken from the upstream") and names the repository when the version is in more than one. States: `pending`
("The documentation of this version is being fetched.", with a refresh action), `unavailable` (the reason in words), `none` (no tab). Revisit at the walkthrough.

**Applied in the spec:** [R-ANS-036](formats/ansible.md#r-ans-036--the-documentation-operations-of-the-screens-their-rendering-and-the-search).

### Q-UI-243 · The search field filters the tree through the server and keeps the counts

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The field in the tree pane head sends `q` to `getPackageVersionDocs` after 300 ms of silence and at least 2 characters; the tree shows the matching entries, the groups keep their counts and the head says "5 of 32" (chosen) | R-ANS-036 | Matches descriptions and parameter names the tree does not carry; one matching implementation; the counts of the reference's tree do not jump | A request per search |
| (b) Filter the loaded tree in the browser by name | No request | Instant | Names only; a second matching rule |
| (c) A search page | Results as a list | Room for snippets | Leaves the tab |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the search "inside the documentation" has to find a parameter by what it does, which only the server has. The field is a `text-input` with a search icon and an `aria-label` "Search the documentation"; Escape clears it; the
matches are a live region ("5 of 32 entries"); a search with no match shows "No entries match" in the pane, not an empty tree; the open page stays open while one searches; the query is the URL parameter `q`. Groups with no match are
hidden, groups with matches are expanded. Matching text is not highlighted on the page (no client-side matching). Revisit if the owner wants snippets.

**Applied in the spec:** [R-ANS-036](formats/ansible.md#r-ans-036--the-documentation-operations-of-the-screens-their-rendering-and-the-search).

### Q-UI-244 · The tab follows the wiki check: absent, not forbidden

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `metadata.docs` is absent for a caller who may not read the wiki; the Documentation and Contents tabs are then not shown and no request for them is made; a 404 from an operation removes the tab and says nothing (chosen) | R-ANS-037 | Existence is not revealed (R-API-029); the UI needs no knowledge of T-18's levels | A person who is allowed to read artifacts but not the wiki is not told why the tab is missing |
| (b) Show the tab with "You may not read this wiki" | Explicit | Honest to the viewer | Reveals that documentation exists to a caller who may not know it does |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the seam is one function on the server (R-ANS-037); the client asks nothing about levels. T-18 may decide to show a notice (then this decision is revisited with its model). The README tab of other
formats is unaffected.

**Applied in the spec:** [R-ANS-037](formats/ansible.md#r-ans-037--the-documentation-is-wiki-content-which-routes-documents-and-fields-the-wiki-check-gates), R-UI-007.

### Q-UI-245 · Dependencies and the links of the reference are sections of the Metadata tab, not tabs; the documentation link is called "Docs site"

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Verified in this repository: the Metadata tab shows `Requires Ansible`, licences and tags for the format (`ansibleFacts`, `package-detail.ts`), the generic links (Homepage, Documentation, Source
repository, Issue tracker, from `homepage`, `documentationUrl`, `repositoryUrl`, `bugsUrl` that the view adapter sends) and the dependencies member; the Repositories tab lists the repositories of a version.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Dependencies: a section of the Metadata tab whose entries link to the package page when the installation holds the collection; the `documentationUrl` link is labelled "Docs site" for this format; Distributions is the Repositories tab (chosen) | R-UI-063 | Nothing exists twice; the page keeps the layout of the other formats (Q-UI-3); the link label no longer collides with the new Documentation tab | A tab the reference has is not there |
| (b) A Dependencies tab of its own | Six reference tabs one by one | Familiar | A tab for a list of at most a few entries; the Metadata tab holds the same data today |
| (c) Leave the label "Documentation" | No change | Nothing to do | Two things named Documentation on one page, one a tab and one a link out |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the question the first draft left to the owner is decided: the data already exists on the page, a tab would only move it. Revisit at the walkthrough if the owner wants
the tab.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-063, [Q-UI-240](#q-ui-240--an-ansible-package-has-a-documentation-tab-and-a-contents-tab-the-readme-tab-is-its-first-page).

### Q-UI-246 · The Documentation tab keeps its place in the URL and resets with the version

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `tab=documentation`, `doc=<type>/<name>` and `q` are query parameters; a change of version or repository drops `doc` and `q` (chosen) | R-UI-060 | A page is linkable and survives reload and back; no stale page from another version | A person comparing two versions starts at the README each time |
| (b) Keep `doc` across versions | The same module page of the next version | Comparison | The entry may not exist in the other version; an error state to design |
| (c) State in memory only | No URL parameters | Simple | Not linkable; reload loses the page |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** consistent with `version`, `tab` and `prerelease`, which are already URL state (R-UI-007). Revisit if comparing versions is asked for.

### Q-UI-247 · The Contents tab shares the tree's request and lists in pages of 100

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The Contents table and the tree read the same `getPackageVersionDocs` answer and the table pages client-side in 100s (chosen) | R-UI-062 | One request; the two tabs cannot disagree; the answer is already bounded at 5,000 entries and about 1 MB | Up to 5,000 rows held in the page, shown 100 at a time |
| (b) A list operation with cursor paging | `listAnsiblePackageContents` | Server paging | A fourth operation and a second query for data the tree has |
| (c) No Contents tab | The tree is the list | Smaller | The flat view with types and descriptions of the reference is not there |

### Q-UI-248 · The tree of the Documentation tab is the navigation tree of the keyboard library: a row is a link, a group is not selectable

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `@angular/aria`'s tree in navigation mode: a page is an `<a>` with `routerLink` and `aria-current="page"`, a group is a row that is not selectable and opens or closes on a click or the arrow keys (chosen) | R-UI-060 | The roving tab stop, arrow keys, Home and End, type-ahead and the expand keys come from the library the file browser already uses; a row is a real link, so a modified click opens a new tab; `aria-current` is what R-UI-060 asks for | The treeitem role replaces the link role of the anchor, as the library's navigation mode does |
| (b) The same tree in selection mode, rows as `aria-selected` options | As the file browser | One pattern | A row is no link; `aria-current` is not set; a copied link needs the address bar |
| (c) A hand-written tree | Own key handling | No library coupling | A second tree implementation to keep accessible |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** R-UI-060 names links and `aria-current`; the library has a mode for exactly that, and the file browser's styles (`_browse.scss`) take `[aria-current='page']` as the selected row beside `[aria-selected='true']`. Revisit if the library drops the mode.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-060.

### Q-UI-249 · The package page reads the tree once per version for both tabs, and a search is a second read

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The package page asks `getPackageVersionDocs` when the Documentation or Contents tab is open and keeps the answer for the version; the search asks again with `q`; a version with the state `none` and a README asks only for the README file and shows it without a tree (chosen) | R-UI-060, R-UI-062 | Nothing is requested for a tab that is not open; the two tabs share one answer (Q-UI-247); a refusal (404, 403) removes both tabs, any other failure is an error with a retry | A user who opens Documentation, Metadata and Documentation again does not see a newer tree until the page is reloaded |
| (b) Each tab asks for itself | Two requests | Simple | The tabs can disagree; two reads for one answer |
| (c) The tree is part of the version details | `include=docs` | One request | R-UI-060 forbids it: the details would carry up to 1 MB |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the page announces the documentation in `metadata.docs` (Q-API-263), so the tab list needs no probe; the tree is requested lazily and the Refresh action of the state `pending` reads it again. Revisit if the documentation changes while a page is open.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-060.

### Q-UI-250 · What is open in the tree: Documentation, the group of the open page, and every group with a match

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.
