|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Documentation is open; Modules, Plugins and each plugin type are closed unless they hold the open page; a search opens every group that has a match; what the user opens or closes by hand is kept until the search text changes (chosen) | R-UI-060, Q-UI-241, Q-UI-243 | The tree is short at first (three rows and their counts) and a deep link shows its row; a search shows what it found | A group the user closed stays closed when a link opens a page inside it, until the text changes |
| (b) Everything open | Long tree | No hidden rows | 833 entries of a large collection in one list |
| (c) Everything closed | Short | Quiet | A deep link or a search result is hidden |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** it is the rule of Q-UI-241 and Q-UI-243 written as one function with a map of the user's choices on top. A group that holds one type of its own name (Modules, Roles) lists its entries directly; Plugins lists its types. Revisit at the walkthrough.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-060.

### Q-UI-251 · A search text of one character clears the filter; the field follows the address and writes it without a history entry

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The URL parameter `q` is written 300 ms after the last key and replaces the history entry; fewer than 2 characters write no `q` (the filter is cleared) and the live region says "Enter at least 2 characters to search."; an address that changes `q` from outside (back button, link) is written into the field, an echo of what was typed is not (chosen) | R-UI-060, Q-UI-243 | The back button does not walk through every search; the address always shows what the tree shows; typing a space does not lose the space | One history entry for the whole search session |

### Q-UI-252 · The parameters of a page are open at every level at first; each parameter with suboptions folds on its own

### Q-API-260 · The documentation operations are declared wiki content in the OpenAPI document; the marker follows R-AUTHZ-034

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `x-trove-part: wiki` on the three operations, read into `Operation.Part` by the document validator (the analogue of `x-trove-maintenance`, Q-API-246); where T-18's check runs before the handler it reads this marker, and the handler's call is the second layer (chosen) | R-ANS-037 | One declarative place; the generated document and a test can list every wiki operation | The name is a placeholder until R-AUTHZ-034 fixes its own marker; the development agent aligns them when the two plans merge |
| (b) Only the call in the handler | No marker | Nothing to align | A test cannot list the wiki operations from the document; the gate is invisible in the API description |
| (c) A path convention (`/wiki/` in the path) | Visible in the URL | Obvious | The operations sit under the generic package path (Q-ANS-63) |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the declaration is cheap and makes the seam checkable. Revisit with R-AUTHZ-034's wording.

**Applied in the spec:** R-ANS-036, R-ANS-037; [R-API-029](#r-api-029--packages-versions-and-readme).

### Q-API-261 · The operations take a package and a version and an optional `repository`; the entry and the file are path parameters

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `GET /packages/{packageId}/versions/{version}/docs`, `…/docs/entries/{type}/{name}`, `…/docs/files/{file}`, with `repository` (`<project>/<repo>`) and, for the tree, `q`; `type` is the content type, `name` the content name (letters, digits, `_`, `.`), `file` one path segment percent-encoded (chosen) | R-ANS-036 | The screen already holds the ids; the entry URL is stable and linkable; no cursor needed | The files are addressed by name, so two files of one name cannot exist (they cannot: one directory) |
| (b) Entry id in the query | `?entry=module/x` | One path | Cache keys and logs show the same path for every entry |
| (c) Under the repository (`/projects/.../ansible/...`) | Next to `listAnsibleImportTasks` | Fits the management operations of the format | The package screen is cross-repository and would have to pick the repository first (Q-ANS-63) |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** same as Q-ANS-63; a `type` or `name` that does not match its grammar is 404 (it names no entry), a `q` below 2 characters is 422 `invalid_query`. Answers carry a strong `ETag` over the stored row's version (`built_at` and `generator`) or, for a file, the README rule (R-API-029), and `Cache-Control: no-store` as the README answer.

**Applied in the spec:** R-ANS-036; [R-API-029](#r-api-029--packages-versions-and-readme).

### Q-API-262 · `listAnsibleImportTasks` gains the optional filters `package` and `version`

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The existing operation takes `package` (`<ns>.<name>`) and `version` as filters beside `state` (chosen) | R-UI-063 | The Import log tab of one version is one request; no new operation | The operation is under the repository, so the tab names the repository first |
| (b) A task operation under the package | New path | Fits the screen | A second operation for the same rows |
| (c) The tab filters in the browser | No change | None | Pages through every task of the repository to find one |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the rows are indexed by repository, then time; filtering by name and version is a predicate on a bounded list (the sweep keeps 30 days). An unknown `package` or `version` yields an empty page.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-063, [Q-UI-240](#q-ui-240--an-ansible-package-has-a-documentation-tab-and-a-contents-tab-the-readme-tab-is-its-first-page).

### Q-API-263 · The `metadata.docs` member of the version details announces the documentation, and is absent for a caller who may not read the wiki

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `metadata.docs = {state, source, entries}` for the format `ansible`, built by the view adapter; absent when the wiki check says no (chosen) | R-ANS-036, R-ANS-037 | The page picks its tabs from the details it already reads; no probing request; existence is not revealed | The view adapter asks the wiki check per version of a page of details |
| (b) The UI probes `getPackageVersionDocs` | One more request per page | No details change | A request and a 404 per version view; the tab flickers |
| (c) A field outside `metadata` | New schema member | Typed | A generic schema change for one format |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** `metadata` is the format-specific member by design (R-API-029). The adapter's cost is one indexed read of `ansible_version_docs` per version of the page (batched with `ViewDetails`), and the wiki check is asked once per repository of the page, not per version.

**Applied in the spec:** R-ANS-036, R-ANS-037, R-UI-060.

## What this does not cover


### H-43 · General API rate limits are per replica

Component: the limiter of the management API (R-API-016) on top of R-ARCH-034 in
[architecture.md](architecture.md). Subject: every caller of `/api/v1/` and `/files/`, by token,
session user or client address. Since 2026-10-28 the `read`, `write` and `anonymous` buckets count
cluster-wide in Valkey (Q-API-3), so the configured budget no longer multiplies with the replica
count. What remains is narrower than the heading: counting per replica while Valkey is unavailable,
and counters lost in a failover. Live in the MVP in these cases:

- **Valkey outage.** While a replica cannot reach Valkey, its buckets are local, with the budget
  divided by the live `web` replicas of the registry. If only some replicas lose Valkey, the others
  still count the full budget in Valkey, so a client that spreads its requests gets up to one share
  more than the budget per cut-off replica. After a scale-up during an outage, every replica
  divides by the old count until its next registry read, for at most `system.heartbeat_interval`.
- **Counters lost after a failover.** A Sentinel failover that loses recent writes resets the
  counters it lost, which admits at most one extra window per bucket (R-ARCH-034). A Valkey
  restart without persistence has the same effect. trove's own cache flush leaves the counters
  alone ([operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) R-OPS-047).

Tampering is not part of this gap: whoever can write under trove's Valkey prefix can delete
counters and lift every budget, or raise them and refuse a caller with `429`, and that is H-49 in
[architecture.md](architecture.md), which covers every value trove keeps in Valkey.

What makes it real: a client that wants more throughput than its budget, for example to scrape
package metadata, and that can time its traffic to a Valkey outage or failover. It does not weaken
credential guessing: tokens are 256-bit random values, and the break-glass lockout counts failures
in PostgreSQL (R-AUTH-038), which survives a loss of Valkey's data. Per-replica in-flight limits (`server.max_in_flight`) still protect each replica in
every case.

### H-44 · Credentials displayed in the browser are outside trove's control

A token shown once, embedded in a snippet or copied to the clipboard (R-UI-016, R-UI-029) is readable
by browser extensions with page access, by clipboard managers and history tools, and by anyone
watching the screen. trove reduces exposure (environment-variable references by default,
repository-scoped short-lived setup tokens, no storage, Blob URLs revoked at once), but cannot prevent
capture once the value is on screen or in the clipboard.

### H-45 · Hiding unauthorized resources is not timing-safe

With hiding on, a missing and an unreadable repository, item or package give the same status and body
(R-API-008), but the server takes different code paths, and the response time can tell them apart.
Equalizing response times is not specified; an attacker able to measure many requests can still learn
whether a key or path exists.

### H-319 · A configuration file that holds a token can be committed

Component: the client setup page (R-UI-016) and the guides (R-UI-049). Subject: the projects of users who choose "Create
a token for this setup" or "Use a token I already have". Live today. In those modes the snippets and the downloaded
`.npmrc` or `.yarnrc.yml` hold the token itself, and the project directory is where the guide tells a reader to save a
configuration file. The default mode references `TROVE_TOKEN`, the guide says never to commit a file that holds a token
and to keep such a file in the home directory, and the token of the setup page is scoped to one repository and expires
after `ui.client_setup.token_ttl`; nothing checks a repository of source code. What makes it real: a developer who
downloads the file with an embedded token into a project and commits it. Hardening: a secret-scanning rule for
`trv_(pat|sat|cit)_` in the source-code host (the prefix and the CRC-32 of INV-8 make the token recognisable), and a
shorter `ui.client_setup.token_ttl`.

### H-320 · A guide can state what trove no longer does

Component: the guide text of a format (R-UI-049, R-ARCH-008 `Guide()`). Subject: readers who decide on the guide's
statements, for example that a claimed name never reaches a remote member, which names an audit withholds, or that a
published version never changes. Live whenever a change of behaviour leaves the guide unchanged. The tests pin what can be
pinned (npm: every code of the troubleshooting table and its status against the problem catalog, the notices the
handlers send, the defaults the text names, the snippets against the client setup), not every sentence. What makes it
real: a change to the dependency-confusion rules, the audit forward or the publish rules whose author does not read the
format's guide. Hardening: a change to a requirement that a guide section cites is reviewed together with that section
(the developer pages name the files), and every new fact a guide states gets a test.

### H-321 · An anonymous reader learns the token variable's name from the guide of a format

Component: `GET /api/v1/formats/{format}/guide` (R-API-053). Subject: installations with public content (`publicContent`,
R-AUTH-037); dormant otherwise. The operation is as public as the format list and names `ui.client_setup.token_env_var` in its text and
snippets, besides the base URL that the format list already serves. The name is no secret, but it tells someone who can
read a developer's environment which variable holds a trove token. What makes it real: a `public` repository, a variable
name other than the default, and an attacker with read access to process environments of developer machines or CI
runners, who could read every variable anyway.

### H-877 · The OCI logo rests on a non-commercial use under the Linux Foundation's terms

Component: the format icon of `oci` ([Q-UI-225](#q-ui-225--a-format-shows-its-owners-logo-where-the-owners-terms-allow-it-else-the-neutral-glyph)).
Subject: every installation that holds an OCI repository. Dormant today: trove is an open-source project and is not sold.
The Linux Foundation's trademark usage permits a logo expressly only as a link to the project and for private
merchandise, and asks for written permission for a logo "in any commercial or marketing context"; a project's own
interface that names a format beside its logo is neither permitted nor forbidden in words. trove follows every other rule
of the page (official files, no colour change, nothing on top, smaller than the name, the trademark notice). What makes it
real: trove sold or run as a paid service with the logo in its interface, or a request of the Linux Foundation. Then the
Linux Foundation's written permission, or the neutral glyph for `oci` (one line in `formatIcon`).

### H-878 · The owner and the terms of the NuGet mark are not published

Component: the format icon of `nuget` (Q-UI-225). Subject: every installation that holds a NuGet repository. Live today.
The logo's copyright licence is the CC BY 2.0 of the NuGet project's media repository, which publishes the files for the
community. No trademark guideline for the NuGet name or logo was found from the NuGet project, the .NET Foundation or
Microsoft; nuget.org's terms (Microsoft) reserve Microsoft's logos and product icons, and Microsoft's trademark list (FY27Q2)
does not name NuGet. Not verified: who holds a trademark in the NuGet logo, and whether that holder counts it among
Microsoft's product icons. What makes it real: such a holder stating that the logo needs a licence. Then the neutral glyph
for `nuget`.

### H-879 · An owner's terms can change after the day they were read

Component: the format logos and their notice ([NOTICE.txt](../../web/public/formats/NOTICE.txt)). Subject: every
installation. Live from the day after 2026-11-11, when the terms of Q-UI-225 were read. npm's policy calls itself a living
document, Docker and the Linux Foundation reserve changes without notice, and nothing in trove reads the pages again. What
makes it real: an owner that narrows its terms (Debian, NuGet, the Linux Foundation) while trove still shows its logo, or one
that opens them (npm, Red Hat, Docker) while trove still shows the glyph. Hardening: read the pages of the table in Q-UI-225
again when a format is added and before the first stable release, and record the day in the notice.


### H-980 · Sorting by grade covers the first 1,000 entries of a list

Component: the repository content list (R-UI-094, Q-UI-373). Subject: every reader who sorts a repository's items by grade. Live
from the grades on. Sorting by grade loads the list up to 1,000 entries and sorts them in the browser, because the server has no
sort by grade; a repository with more items sorts its first 1,000 by name and grade, and the worst item may be the 1,001st. The
list says so under the table. What makes it real: a remote repository that caches more than 1,000 packages, and a reader who
looks for its worst one. Hardening: a server sort over a stored grade (Q-UI-373 (b)).
